suggestion.title: Blockchain-Based C2 Beaconing from IoT Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Blockchain C2' as novel evolution—no UC exists despite this being the primary attack innovation. Phrase: 'Adds Blockchain C2'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound TLS/HTTP traffic from IoT device subnets to public blockchain node infrastructure (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Monero RPC ports). Flag DNS queries to blockchain RPC endpoints or wallet service domains originating from non-server IoT assets. Look for process execution establishing persistent blockchain node connections.

suggestion.title: Victim Relay / Proxy Infrastructure Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Victim Relays'—compromised hosts repurposed as proxy infrastructure post-disruption. Phrase: 'Victim Relays After JackSkid Disruption'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised IoT devices or victim machines establishing inbound listening ports and forwarding traffic to external C2. Correlate sudden asymmetric bandwidth patterns (high inbound, high outbound) on previously quiet hosts. Flag processes spawning network tunneling utilities (socat, netcat, plink, chisel) from IoT or low-privilege process contexts.

suggestion.title: C2 Infrastructure Reconstitution Post-Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes response to JackSkid disruption—suggests rapid re-platforming and infrastructure rebuild. Phrase: 'After JackSkid Disruption'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden introduction of new C2 endpoints into command flows within 24-72 hours of known disruption events. Monitor for command retry patterns with fallback logic (primary blockchain C2 → relay proxy → backup infrastructure). Correlate infrastructure changes with campaign timeline data to identify evasion after law enforcement action.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IoT devices (RTSP, Telnet, SSH default creds) establishing outbound connections to known Dysphoria C2 infrastructure post-infection. Flag process spawning or privilege elevation on embedded Linux/RTOS systems. Correlate with failed login attempt patterns preceding successful compromise.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Transaction Monitoring for C2 Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Novel use of blockchain for C2 implies commands or coordination data encoded in ledger; article does not clarify mechanism but detection requires blockchain data ingestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest blockchain transaction feeds for Dysphoria-associated wallet addresses. Flag transactions with unusual metadata fields or high-frequency patterns suggesting encoded commands. Correlate blockchain tx timing with botnet activity spikes detected in network/DNS logs.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Rapid C2 Channel Switching Under Detection Pressure
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to map defense-evasion phase despite article detailing tactical shift post-disruption. Evasion techniques (fallback, channel switching, relay proxying) need explicit detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid succession of C2 endpoint changes (>2 new endpoint groups in <48h) targeting the same botnet cohort. Flag pattern changes in command protocol (HTTP→blockchain→relay chain) within defender-observable window post-disruption announcement.

suggestion.title: Machine Account Creation + Suspicious Certificate Enrollment Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A machine account created through the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota setting is a valid domain principal. This allowed the attacker-controlled chase endpoint...' Correlating account creation with immediate certificate requests from low-privilege users is core detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privileged user creating machine account via default quota, followed within 5 minutes by certificate enrollment request targeting DC accounts. Correlate event 4741 (computer account creation) with certificate request event 4890 or equivalent CertSrv logs.

suggestion.title: Certificate Enrollment with Attacker-Controlled CDC/RMD Attributes
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'cdc (Client DC) identifies the server the Certification Authority should contact' and 'rmd (Remote Domain)' pointing to domain controller. Article: 'systems previously did not verify that the server supplied through the attacker-controlled cdc value was a legitimate domain controller.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificate requests containing cdc attributes that resolve to non-Domain Controller systems or rmd parameters targeting privileged accounts (krbtgt, domain controllers). Cross-validate cdc IP against AD computer object registry.

suggestion.title: Rogue SMB/LSA/LDAP Service Responses to Certificate Authority
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker to run rogue SMB, LSA, and LDAP services, direct the CA to the attacker-controlled system, and return false directory information.' CA audit logs will show connection attempts to non-standard sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CA outbound SMB (445), LDAP (389), or LSA (135) connections to hosts not holding Domain Controller role. Correlate connection timing with certificate requests to identify targeting patterns.

suggestion.title: PKINIT Authentication as Domain Controller from Unauthorized Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The released certighost.py proof-of-concept automates this process by using the certificate to authenticate through PKINIT as the targeted domain controller.' Kerberos pre-auth events will show DC impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PKINIT pre-authentication (AS_REQ) where ServiceName is a domain controller account and source IP does not match DC registry. Cross-reference certificate serial number against AD CS issued certificate log.

suggestion.title: DCSync Replication Request from Non-Replicator Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using the saved Kerberos credentials with Impacket's secretsdump tool to perform a DCSync attack and retrieve the krbtgt account's credentials.' GetNCChanges RPC call will appear in audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GetNCChanges RPC calls (Kerberos replication) from user accounts lacking Directory Replication permissions. Correlate with Impacket process signatures (secretsdump, ntlmrelayx) or Python interpreter spawning suspicious network calls.

suggestion.title: CCACHE File Creation and NT Hash Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'saving the resulting Kerberos credentials to a .ccache file and extracting the account's NT hash.' CCACHE files are unusual outside system library paths; NT hash dumps signal credential dumping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .ccache file creation in user-writable directories. Correlate Python execution (certighost.py) with Kerberos tool activity (klist, kinit) or impacket library imports from process memory analysis.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 as a CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-08-10. Article: 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited.' Baseline detection for all CISA KEV entries is vulnerability scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 affecting FortiOS systems. Flag all matches immediately; cross-reference firmware versions against vendor advisory and track patch deployment status. Alert on any unpatched systems as of patch-due date 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to Fortinet Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Attackers will send malformed or unusual HTTP payloads to trigger the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs on Fortinet management interfaces and web services for requests with unusual structure: oversized headers, null bytes, multi-line injections, or verb+path combinations not matching baseline Fortinet API/UI patterns. Alert on POST/PUT requests to config endpoints preceded by filesystem-level activity.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation on Fortinet Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attacker uses symlinks as post-exploit persistence before attempting HTTP bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet filesystem events for symlink creation/modification in critical directories (/var, /etc, /bin, /usr/bin, admin config paths). Alert on symlinks pointing to sensitive files (admin.conf, credentials, logs) or web-accessible directories. Correlate with unexpected process execution or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access and Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability impact: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Successful exploitation results in theft of configuration secrets or network intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After establishing persistence (symlink) and bypassing patch (HTTP), attacker exfiltrates sensitive data. Detect: unusual egress connections from Fortinet systems to external IPs, large data transfers in compressed/encrypted form, access patterns to admin configuration files, and telemetry showing credential material in outbound traffic.

suggestion.title: Initial Filesystem-Level Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite phase must be detected to prevent the subsequent chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for evidence of prior filesystem compromise on Fortinet systems: failed privilege-escalation attempts, unexpected code execution, buffer-overflow patterns in logs, or file-write anomalies. Correlate timestamp of first filesystem access with later symlink creation and HTTP bypass attempts to confirm attack chain.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Lag for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10.' CISA KEV vulnerabilities are actively exploited; patch lag is the primary risk vector. Federal agencies required to remediate; auditors will track this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Fortinet FortiOS firmware versions against the vulnerable range (infer from vendor advisory) and patch-deployment timestamps. Flag systems with patch not applied by 2026-08-10 as audit-critical. Track variance between scan date and patch date to identify deployment delays.

suggestion.title: Token Scope Mismatch: Public-only Token Accessing Private Repository Write
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vulnerability: 'Gitea checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository, which is the public base repository' — but the token then successfully modifies a PRIVATE PR branch. Detection should look for explicit token scopes (public-only/read-only) performing write operations on private/restricted resources.
log_sources: Web access logs (token principal vs. target repository permission level)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate token metadata (scope: public-only, read-only, etc.) against actual operations performed. Flag when a constrained-scope token successfully executes write operations against private/restricted repositories. Search for API calls where the Authorization header indicates a public-only token but the request modifies private resources.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository PR Update via Public Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Gitea allows a public-only,write:repository token to update a private pull request head branch through a public base repository route.' The attack crosses repository boundaries — updating PR in one repo using a route to another. Detection should identify when a single request modifies resources in a repository different from the one in the URL path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST requests to /api/v1/repos/{X}/pulls/{index}/update where the base repository {X} differs from the head/target repository being modified. Cross-reference the repository owner/name extracted from the URL against the actual target repository in the pull request metadata.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private PR Branch Updates via API
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'can update a private pull request head branch' — direct impact statement. Detection should look for any write operations (branch updates, commits, force-pushes) targeting private PR branches from token/user accounts that should not have such access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git branch update operations (git push, force-push) and API calls to update PR head branches where the initiating user/token has insufficient permissions for the target repository privacy level. Flag if a public-scoped token or low-privilege account modifies private PR branches.

suggestion.title: Exploit of Endpoint Authorization Bypass (CVE-2026-58443 Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is authorization logic flaw: 'UpdatePullRequest() then authorizes the pull request...' against the wrong repository context. Detection should identify when endpoint routing validation is bypassed — tokens authorized for repository A can access/modify repository B through endpoint manipulation.
log_sources: Web application firewall / API gateway logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authorization failures or bypasses by monitoring for requests where the repository context validated at route-level differs from the repository context enforced at the controller/action level. Look for 200/success responses to sensitive operations when initial token scope check should have failed.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2025-68686 is CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild); scanner detection is the first-line hunt for any published CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiOS instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 in scanner output. Pivot on product version ≤ the patched version Fortinet released. Correlate with asset inventory to prioritize external-facing instances (KEV implies public exploitation).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Public-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and T1190 exploitation of public-facing applications; asset exposure hunt is mandatory for KEV entries with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS instances in the environment using DNS, IP inventory, and banner-grabbing. Cross-reference external-facing IPs (via cloud asset inventory, WAF, DNS) to identify publicly-accessible FortiOS instances. Flag any unpatched or version < [remediation release].

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker bypasses patch 'via crafted HTTP requests'; detection of abnormal HTTP to FortiOS admin/API endpoints is the exploitation-phase indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web interface (ports 80, 443, 8080) for HTTP requests with anomalous payloads: null bytes, directory traversal patterns, symbolic link references, or unusual method combinations. Flag requests from external IPs to admin endpoints or APIs known to handle file operations.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass of the patch for symbolic link persistency'; post-exploit persistence via symlinks is a defense-evasion and persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS logs and filesystem audit logs for creation or modification of symbolic links in key directories (e.g., /bin, /lib, config directories, web root). Look for symlinks pointing to unexpected or suspicious targets, especially in persistence-relevant paths (init.d, systemd, cron). Cross-correlate with timeline of HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance — CVE-2025-68686 Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and emphasizes that patch lag is a 'silent killer'; compliance hunt ensures remediation tracking against mandatory deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for FortiOS instances not patched to the remediation release by 2026-08-10. Track version strings from inventory scans; flag any FortiOS version <[remediation version] as non-compliant. Alert on slippage after deadline.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation — Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation via 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass a previous patch. Core attack vector is HTTP-based; pipeline should detect abnormal request patterns targeting FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS devices (port 443/8443) containing request patterns associated with symbolic link bypass attempts or unrecognized request structures deviating from legitimate admin interfaces. Flag UNKNOWN or malformed HTTP methods to known vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' — article does not specify what data (configs, credentials, logs); use case should detect elevated read access or bulk exports of sensitive FortiOS objects (firewall policies, VPN configs, syslog settings).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk reads or exports of sensitive FortiOS objects (policies, user configs, VPN settings) by unprivileged or anonymous sessions, especially following HTTP exploitation patterns. Cross-correlate with indicators of prior filesystem-level compromise.

suggestion.title: Chained Vulnerability Detection — FortiOS Filesystem + CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This is a **chained attack**; detection should correlate filesystem-level indicators (file creation, permission changes, binary modification) with subsequent HTTP exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on systems showing both (a) filesystem-level compromise indicators (unexpected files in /var, /etc, or /bin; permission escalation attempts) followed within hours by (b) HTTP requests bearing hallmarks of CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. Indicates multi-stage attack.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV — FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-10; standard CISA KEV hunt should track exposed FortiOS instances and patch compliance. Template is explicitly referenced in article but pipeline produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiOS instances; cross-check against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2025-68686 presence. Flag unpatched or out-of-support versions. Correlate patch dates against federal due date 2026-08-10 for compliance gap analysis. Check firewall access logs for exposure to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Bypass of Previous Patch — Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline should flag attempts to trigger previously-patched symlink behavior or bypasses of the patch protection itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS logs for failed symbolic link resolutions, requests for paths that trigger symlink handling, or errors suggesting patch-bypass attempts. Look for repeated 403/404 responses to symlink-related paths followed by successful 200 responses (indicating bypass).

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Exposed Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active scanning for exposed FortiOS instances in the wild. Pipeline should generate asset exposure use case to identify and track internet-facing FortiOS devices before they are exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor netflow for inbound connections to known FortiOS default ports (443, 8443, 10000). Correlate with DNS queries resolving to Fortinet domains or HTTPS certificate scanning attempts targeting FortiOS SSL certificates. Flag instances without recent patch indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV listing means active exploitation in the wild. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and generated zero scanning detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management systems for FortiOS instances running affected versions. Cross-reference with patch management to identify systems missing CVE-2025-68686 remediations before federal due date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Exploiting FortiOS Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' This describes the direct exploitation vector requiring HTTP traffic inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS management interfaces and exposed services for malformed requests, unusual path traversal patterns, or headers designed to trigger the symbolic link bypass. Alert on unauthenticated requests succeeding against patched versions.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' — indicates post-compromise persistence via symlink creation. Requires filesystem integrity monitoring specific to this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of symbolic links in FortiOS system directories (especially boot/startup paths). Correlate symlink creation with prior HTTP exploitation attempts or unauthenticated access logs to establish full attack chain.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly named 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Article indicates attacker gains ability to bypass authentication post-compromise, enabling config/credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for large outbound transfers or unusual access patterns to configuration files, administrative logs, or authentication databases. Flag data exfiltration correlating with prior exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation Chain: Prior Compromise + Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before the HTTP bypass succeeds. Pipeline missed the two-stage kill chain entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem modifications (symlinks, unauthorized file creation) with subsequent HTTP anomalies or authentication bypasses. Two-stage temporal pattern indicates active exploitation chain, not isolated scanning activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Failure or Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-08-10 establishes deadline for patch compliance. Detection should flag systems that fail patching or remain vulnerable after deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management for FortiOS systems with failed or pending CVE-2025-68686 updates past the federal deadline. Flag devices running FortiOS versions known vulnerable to the bypass to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article directly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the core persistence technique. Filesystem monitoring for symlink creation/modification is the foundational post-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem events for unexpected symlink creation or modification in system/web directories and config paths. Post-compromise symlinks (especially those linked to sensitive binaries or config files) are high-confidence persistence signals.

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting CVE-2025-68686 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' HTTP request pattern detection is the primary exploit-in-flight indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal FortiOS API/HTTP access patterns. Alert on HTTP requests with abnormal URI structures, double-encoded payloads, or header patterns consistent with patch-bypass attempts targeting symbolic link restoration.

suggestion.title: Detect Unpatched FortiOS/FortiProxy Instances (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry and federal patch due date (2026-08-10) establish this as actively exploited. Asset exposure hunting for vulnerable, internet-facing instances is the primary preventive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and vulnerability scanning systems for FortiOS/FortiProxy instances with missing CVE-2025-68686 patches. Cross-correlate with internet-facing asset registry (via DNS, certificate transparency, or external scan data) to prioritize external exposure risk.

suggestion.title: Detect Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Compromise on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Post-compromise exfiltration of configs, credentials, or traffic logs is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from compromised FortiOS for unusual volume spikes, unusual destinations, or suspicious DNS/encrypted tunnels shortly after initial access indicators fire. FortiOS configs and traffic logs are high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Detect Filesystem-Level Code Execution Pre-Cursor (Prior Vulnerability Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detecting this precursor exploitation is critical early-warning detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected command execution, process spawning, or code injection events on the FortiOS filesystem (OS-level or management interface). Unusual system calls, module loads, or privilege-escalation attempts on FortiOS indicate pre-exploitation of the prior CVE.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents the obfuscation technique: 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This is a testable detection boundary—tags moving between commit hashes in rapid sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect release tags in Action repositories reassigned to commits not on main/protected branches. Alert on sequences where existing semantic version tags (v35, etc.) point to different commit hashes or to commits reachable only through deleted branches, indicating tag-to-commit re-pointing.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article's core finding: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the direct attack surface—the pipeline missed the credential exposure pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow job logs for failures in secret decryption or environment variable injection that result in plaintext credential leakage. Detect regex patterns matching GitHub tokens, API keys, or encryption markers appearing unmasked in public logs.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commits in Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates the technique step-by-step: 'Create a branch and push it up to GitHub... Then, delete the remote branch. You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch.' This is a detection-free obfuscation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commit-then-delete-branch patterns in high-risk repositories (public Actions, widely-used tools). Alert when tags are reassigned to point to commits whose only path exists through deleted branches, or when commits are authored but never appear on any live branch.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack—High-Dependency Repository Write Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the attack surface: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Pipeline missed the core supply chain IOC entirely—the compromised repository.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repositories with high dependency/fork counts (GitHub Actions, SDKs, build tools) for unusual push patterns: commits to ephemeral branches, tag rewrites, orphaned commit authorship, or external URL references in code. Correlate with account geo-anomalies or new collaborator onboarding.

suggestion.title: External Network Requests from CI/CD Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article documents that the attack 'relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This is the detection that *actually caught* the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted domains, particularly those downloading code, scripts, or binaries. Baseline legitimate workflows and flag deviations, especially downloads from newly-registered or low-reputation domains.

suggestion.title: Git Repository Metadata Manipulation—Ref Updates on Critical Tags
suggestion.rationale: The attack required forcing tag re-assignments: 'tag is now associated with the orphaned commit' and then users 'reference that tag and assume that's what we'll be getting.' The pipeline missed this version-pinning attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on force-push operations to public repositories, especially those modifying existing tags or refs. Flag rapid mutations of version tags (semantic versioning tags like v\d+\.\d+\.\d+) that would violate immutability expectations. Correlate tag mutations with commits introducing external calls or credential writes.

suggestion.title: Cross-repository artifact access via HMAC reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'cross-repository artifact read' but none of the hunts filter by repository identity. The vulnerability allows reading artifacts from *different repositories* with the same signed URL structure—this is orthogonal to cross-task exploitation and deserves standalone detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea artifact API endpoints for requests where the repository context embedded in the URL or request parameters differs from the repository associated with the original signed-URL token. Correlate URL repository identity with account's accessible repositories.

suggestion.title: Artifact retrieval outside normal CI/CD task execution windows
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker exploiting signed URLs created *during* a task. Detection should flag artifact downloads initiated from IP/account combinations that are NOT currently executing a Gitea Actions task—this separates legitimate task-internal reads from post-execution exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ArtifactService DownloadArtifact requests with running Gitea Actions job contexts. Flag downloads where the requesting source (IP, account, process) is not an active runner or executor in the accessed repository during that time window.

suggestion.title: HMAC-signed artifact URL parameter tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes URL rewriting that preserves the HMAC—the vulnerability is that URL parameters can be changed (taskID, artifactName) without invalidating the signature. Detect successful requests where URL parameters were modified post-signature, not just reuse across contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log the full URL and signature for each artifact request. Validate signature against the *current* URL parameters; if signature was computed on different taskID/artifactName values, flag as tampering. Requires logging the original signed URL at request creation time.

suggestion.title: Rapid signed-URL reuse across multiple distinct operations
suggestion.rationale: A single signed URL created for one artifact upload should be used once. Article indicates attacker reuses URLs across tasks—if the same sig parameter value appears in requests with different endpoints (UploadArtifact vs DownloadArtifact, or changing operations), this is atypical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each unique signature, count the number of distinct endpoint operations (UploadArtifact, DownloadArtifact) and distinct HTTP methods observed. URLs signed for upload should not be reused for download or vice versa; flag where the same sig appears with >1 distinct operation type.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Fortinet FortiOS with patch due 2026-08-10; pipeline must identify unpatched instances before exploitation. No asset-inventory UC was generated despite 'your scanners say not vulnerable' language in article body implying scanner coverage is insufficient.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Fortinet FortiOS instances that report version < [patched version per vendor advisory]. Cross-reference against CISA KEV due date (2026-08-10) to identify patch lag. High criticality if system is internet-facing or in DMZ.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Exploitation in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and post-exploit bypass of patched vulnerability. No behavioral detection for symlink abuse was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in Fortinet FortiOS critical directories (e.g., /etc, /var/log, /web-root). Correlate with prior compromise events or suspicious file-access patterns. High fidelity if symlinks point to sensitive config files or logs.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Crafted HTTP Patch-Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Zero detection rule for malformed/exploit-pattern HTTP traffic to FortiOS was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for unusual request patterns that correlate with symbolic-link handling—e.g., requests with path traversal sequences, %2e%2e, or encoded slashes targeting web-root or config paths. Pair with failed or unusual POST requests to admin interfaces post-patch publication.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Exposure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No data-exfiltration or information-disclosure detection use case was generated to alert on successful attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk data reads or unusual egress of diagnostic output, certificate stores, VPN credentials, or configuration blobs from FortiOS. Look for large HTTP responses from admin/diagnostic endpoints, unusual DNS queries for data exfil, or high-volume outbound connections post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect FortiOS exploitation via crafted HTTP requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers use 'crafted HTTP requests' to exploit and bypass the patch. Pipeline generated zero use cases to detect this activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for suspicious HTTP request patterns: malformed headers, oversized payloads, unusual method sequences, or requests to administrative endpoints from unexpected sources. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 to detect exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Hunt for prior filesystem-level compromise on FortiOS hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline missed this two-stage prerequisite entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiOS systems with known filesystem-level vulnerabilities or RCE exploits still unpatched. Cross-reference vulnerability scan data with exploitation timelines. Look for filesystem permission changes or suspicious binary modifications preceding CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized information access on FortiOS systems
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; pipeline generated no detection logic for this information disclosure phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS logs for successful authentications from unexpected sources, bulk access to sensitive configuration or credential storage, or data export/backup operations initiated by unauthorized actors. Flag any suspicious information access post-CVE-2025-68686.

suggestion.title: Detect patch bypass attempts on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline missed detection for this specific patch-bypass exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS systems reporting patch status for CVE-2025-68686 and correlate with exploitation attempts. Look for requests matching the pre-patch vulnerability signature succeeding against patched systems. Monitor for patch version mismatches between reported and actual applied levels.

suggestion.title: Track symbolic link persistence mechanisms on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as a persistence technique. Pipeline generated zero hunts for this specific artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS filesystem logs for suspicious symbolic link creation, especially in startup directories, cron jobs, library paths, or authentication modules. Correlate with post-exploitation timelines. Look for symlinks pointing to sensitive FortiOS binaries, configuration files, or credential stores.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Remote Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch... via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero UCs for the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS WAF/HTTP logs for anomalous request patterns targeting known vulnerable URIs. Flag requests with unusual encoding, oversized payloads, or header manipulation techniques designed to evade signature detection of patch-bypass payloads.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article references: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Persistence layer detection entirely missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (via auditd or OS-level FIM) for symbolic link creation/modification in startup paths, config directories, or library paths. Correlate with evidence of filesystem-level compromise preceding the symlink activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Coverage Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10. Article states 'patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Standard UC for any KEV article; pipeline failed to generate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all FortiOS instances against known-patched version for CVE-2025-68686. Identify patch gaps and prioritize remediation to meet federal due date. Distinguish between 'patched', 'not vulnerable per scanner', and 'patch lag' states.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Compromise: Initial Vector + Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Chained exploitation requires detection of both initial breach AND secondary patch-bypass attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for filesystem-level anomalies in FortiOS (kernel module loads, privilege elevation, write to protected paths). Correlate with subsequent HTTP anomalies to T1190 indicators to detect the chained attack pattern.

suggestion.title: Exposed FortiOS Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' implies network-accessible instances. CISA KEV active-exploitation context requires exposed-asset hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all FortiOS deployments; confirm internet-facing instances. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for version/patch status. Prioritize any instance matching vulnerable version range with outbound connectivity.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Remote Code Execution via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests'—explicit exploitation mechanism requiring detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin/public interfaces for HTTP requests exhibiting unusual parameter encoding, multi-part payloads, or header anomalies consistent with CVE-2025-68686 bypass attempts. Baseline legitimate admin traffic to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—core persistence vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories for unexpected symlink creation/modification, especially links traversing outside application paths. Alert on symlink changes outside maintenance windows; correlate with prior exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Fortinet FortiOS Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV guidance: 'worth one quick check across your fleet'—asset-exposure hunt required; article specifies patch due date 2026-08-10
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for FortiOS instances running pre-patch versions; cross-reference against patch baseline. Flag systems lacking documented remediation plans or showing patch-compliance exceptions.

suggestion.title: Patch-Bypass Attempts Against Symbolic Link Mitigation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—evasion pattern on patched systems requires monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For patched FortiOS, monitor for repeated failed symlink operations, alternative path-traversal attempts, or privilege-escalation payloads attempting to circumvent the symbolic-link mitigations.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise in FortiOS Post-Initial Exploit
