suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem compromise events (write access to sensitive paths, symlink creation) with subsequent HTTP requests from the same or proximal source IP on the same FortiOS instance. Alert on timelines where filesystem activity precedes exploitation-pattern HTTP traffic by hours to days, indicating staged compromise.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch-due date of 2026-08-10 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No UC for tracking remediation status or identifying systems still vulnerable post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain continuous inventory of Fortinet FortiOS instances and their patch levels. Flag systems still unpatched after 2026-08-10 as non-compliant. Generate daily reports of at-risk assets and alert SOC on any exploitation attempts (matched HTTP patterns or filesystem activity) against unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific CVE ID and product family with patch deadline 2026-08-10. Pipeline must flag vulnerable versions in asset inventory; 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and CISA KEV status confirm active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query FortiOS instance inventory and vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2025-68686 presence. Correlate with network telemetry showing FortiOS appliances responding to external connections. Flag any version prior to patch release date or where update status is unknown.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the exploitation vector, and 'remote unauthenticated attacker' confirms network-level access path. Pipeline should capture this as initial-access network anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to known FortiOS management interfaces (TCP 80, 443, 8080, 8443). Flag malformed requests, unusual payloads, or request patterns deviating from normal device management baseline. Focus on sources outside trusted administrative networks.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a filesystem-level persistence technique that must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for suspicious symlink creation, especially in startup/autorun paths or config directories. Cross-reference with process execution logs for any FortiOS service loading symlink targets. Flag modifications to filesystem ACLs that would enable persistence without elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Evidence of Prior Product Compromise (Multi-Stage Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Critical attack prerequisite stated in article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This multi-stage nature must inform threat-hunting logic—presence of CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts should trigger review for earlier-stage compromise vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When CVE-2025-68686 exploitation indicators detected, pivot to historical forensics: audit logs for unusual authentication, process creation by FortiOS system accounts, or unexpected service restarts within 48 hours prior. Presence of filesystem-level changes (unapproved binary modifications, config rewrites) indicates compromise window.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' is the vulnerability impact. After initial exploitation, suspect data exfiltration. Network telemetry should flag suspicious FortiOS outbound traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For FortiOS appliances showing signs of compromise or CVE-2025-68686 exploitation, monitor outbound traffic for anomalies: large data transfers to external IPs, DNS queries to suspicious domains, or connections to known C2 infrastructure. Correlate with sensitive data types stored/processed on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Patch Application Compliance and Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patch due-date and the core issue is a 'bypass [of] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Detection must verify patch status AND detect bypass attempts within already-patched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Confirm FortiOS patch application status via device inventory queries. For patched systems, monitor for attempts to trigger the *pre-patch* symlink persistence payload (e.g., old-variant process names, known vulnerable file paths). Flag any process or file behavior matching the published bypass technique from vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Malicious HTTP Exploitation Requests Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch after filesystem compromise. No detection rule for this attack vector was generated despite it being the primary exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS appliances for malformed or anomalous HTTP requests that bypass authentication validation. Track requests containing patterns associated with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts. Alert on any unauthenticated requests that trigger sensitive functionality (e.g., configuration export, diagnostics, file access).

suggestion.title: Fortinet Asset Exposure Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access, implying internet-facing Fortinet devices are at risk. Asset discovery/exposure detection is the baseline hunt for KEV entries but was omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Fortinet FortiOS instances reachable from external networks (WAN ingress, public IPs). Correlate against patch status and deployment date. Flag devices running versions matching CVE-2025-68686 scope that have not received patches by federal due date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem Compromise Precursor Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite attack must be detected before the HTTP bypass is attempted; pipeline generated no detection for this stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS for successful exploitation of known filesystem-level vulnerabilities (pre-compromise stage). Track file permission changes, unauthorized process execution, or configuration modifications on FortiOS appliances. Flag any evidence of filesystem-level access that precedes HTTP-based exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthorized Information Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE is explicitly 'Exposure of Sensitive Information' but no UC for detecting exfiltration, unauthorized API calls, or sensitive data access post-exploitation was included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized access to sensitive information stores (configuration files, encryption keys, credentials, VPN user lists, firewall rules). Detect anomalous API calls, configuration dumps, or data exports from unauthenticated or anomalous source IPs post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Patch Bypass Indicator Removal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed that 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' implies the attacker is actively evading the defense. Detection for patch-bypass or persistence mechanism indicators is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable, downgrade, or circumvent the CVE-2025-68686 patch. Monitor for rollback of security updates, modification of patch validation routines, or re-establishment of symbolic link persistence mechanisms that the patch was designed to prevent.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Vulnerability Exploitation Baseline Detect
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries indicate active wild exploitation; pipeline should flag CVE-2025-68686 as immediately actionable regardless of scanner results. No baseline 'actively exploited KEV' detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automatically alert on any Fortinet FortiOS systems in scope for CVE-2025-68686 that have not been patched by 2026-08-10 federal deadline. Cross-correlate with access logs to detect any unauthorized login attempts or exploitation indicators on these systems.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 and states it is in CISA KEV (actively exploited). 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' establishes urgent asset hunt requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for FortiOS instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference against patch logs to identify unpatched systems. Given CISA KEV status (in-the-wild exploitation), prioritize systems deployed before patch availability and flag for immediate review.

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted HTTP Exploitation Requests Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack method: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web interface logs and HTTP traffic for requests with anomalous payloads targeting information disclosure endpoints. Look for requests that bypass authentication flows, contain path traversal sequences, or attempt to access configuration data without proper credentials. Correlate with known exploit signatures from threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Persistence Abuse Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies persistence mechanism: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem audit logs for symbolic link creation in config, temp, or log directories. Alert on processes attempting to follow symlinks to sensitive files outside expected paths. Correlate symlink creation with timestamps following known compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Core attack objective is unauthorized access to configuration, credentials, or operational data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk reads or exports of configuration files, credential stores, or logs by unexpected processes or accounts. Alert on sensitive file access outside normal administrative patterns. Look for data staging patterns (copying sensitive files to temp directories) preceding network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Detect Chained Vulnerability Exploitation Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article prerequisite: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Describes multi-stage attack chain requiring initial breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances vulnerable to multiple CVEs, especially those affecting filesystem access or remote code execution. Correlate with exploitation indicators for predecessor vulnerabilities. Review threat intelligence for documented exploit chains targeting FortiOS.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Remote Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker using 'crafted HTTP requests' to exploit — no detection use case provided despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS management interfaces (typically ports 443, 8443) containing patterns consistent with CVE-2025-68686 payloads. Correlate with known exploit signatures and monitor for rapid sequences from external IP ranges to admin panels.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the persistence technique — this requires distinct filesystem-level detection absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for symlink creation in system directories, configuration paths, or boot directories. Detect processes with root/admin context creating symbolic links pointing to sensitive FortiOS binaries, config files, or logdirs. Flag symlink clusters in /etc/init.d, /etc/rc.d, or /data directories.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Patch Bypass via Crafted Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—this defense-evasion activity requires explicit detection not provided by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests that attempt to trigger pre-patch behavior in FortiOS after security updates applied (e.g., requests to deprecated endpoints, unusual parameter combinations known to bypass symlink checks). Monitor for version-downgrade attempts or in-memory patching of FortiOS binaries.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes vulnerability 'may allow exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—no detection logic for abnormal information access, credential harvest, or exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes on compromised FortiOS reading from sensitive paths: /data/config, /data/logaudit, certificate stores, credential caches. Correlate file-read activity with outbound network connections to external IPs. Alert on bulk archive creation or encoded data in HTTP POST requests.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Scan: Unpatched Fortinet FortiOS Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal remediation by 2026-08-10—pipeline should emit standard asset-inventory and vulnerability-scan detection but produced nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Fortinet FortiOS instances for CVE-2025-68686 exploitability. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with patch-management logs, firewall exposure logs, and network-accessible asset inventory. Escalate any unpatched FortiOS appliances exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Gitea API token scope boundary violation: public-only token accessing private resources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'public-only, write:repository token' can update private PR branches. This is the privilege escalation vector (T1550.001) but no UC detects token scope misuse. Phrase: 'Gitea checks the token's public-only restriction against the route repository, which is the public base repository' — the bypass happens when token scope doesn't match resource privacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication tokens tagged with 'public-only' scope successfully calling operations on private/internal repositories or PR branches. Requires application-level logging of token scope vs. resource visibility. Flag requests where token policies should have been denied but authorization checks against the wrong (public) repository succeed.

suggestion.title: Gitea PR branch update from public-only authenticated source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes the attack: attacker uses public-only token to update private PR head branch through public repo route. No UC captures the specific combination of public-route + private-target. Phrase: 'update a private pull request head branch through a public base repository route'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/v1/repos/{public-repo}/pulls/{id}/update where the public base repo differs from or does not have visibility into the PR's head branch repository. Requires correlation between request path (public repo) and actual target resource (private head branch). Flag when the authorization context mismatches the accessed resource.

suggestion.title: Gitea unauthenticated or weak-auth API scanning for PR endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1595 (Active Scanning) as reconnaissance phase. UC_101_2 detects authenticated enumeration but misses pre-auth reconnaissance. Phrase: 'Active Scanning' technique mentioned but no detection for initial probing of Gitea API surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated 404/401/403 responses to Gitea API endpoints (pattern /api/v1/repos/*/pulls/*/update) from a single source over a short window, indicating automated scanning for valid endpoints or accessible repositories before exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable FortiOS Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 and lists it in 'Indicators of Compromise' section. CISA KEV artifacts require asset-exposure detection; federal patch due date 2026-08-10 is organization-critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for FortiOS instances flagged with CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference asset inventory to identify which systems require remediation before 2026-08-10. Prioritize internet-facing FortiOS appliances (T1190 exploit path).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is filesystem-level persistence observable after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symbolic link creation targeting FortiOS directories (config paths, binary directories). Look for process chains where compromised process creates symlinks pointing to system/boot startup locations to establish post-exploit persistence.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Pattern to FortiOS Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism: 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Standard web-application exploitation detection required; malformed requests bypass patch checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interfaces (ports 443/8443) for anomalous HTTP requests: malformed headers, unusual request structure, request mutation attempts, or repeated 401/403 responses followed by successful bypass attempts. Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Filesystem Access to FortiOS Internals
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Direct filesystem access is detectable as process behavior anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-standard processes accessing FortiOS configuration/binary directories outside normal operations. Flag processes reading/writing to /opt/fortinet (Linux) or C:\FortiGate (Windows) with unusual parent process chains or privilege contexts.

suggestion.title: Patch Integrity Bypass or Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'bypass the patch developed for...persistency mechanism', indicating attackers can circumvent patch detection/integrity checks. Patches fail to stop exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiOS patch verification fails or reports inconsistency. Flag processes attempting to disable/bypass patch checks. Detect symbolic link persistence remaining active after security updates applied (indicates patch bypass success).

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scan Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary detection method for CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Fortinet FortiOS instances. Flag unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize findings with federal due date 2026-08-10; absence of patch indicates exploitation risk given active wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—this is the persistence vehicle preceding CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS filesystems for symbolic links in unexpected locations (esp. system/config directories). Symbolic links are setup after initial filesystem compromise and signal attacker presence pre-dating this CVE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Pattern Detection (CVE-2025-68686 Patch Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'via crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch.' This is the active exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces for patterns bypassing patch: malformed headers, oversized payloads, path traversal-like syntax, or requests with anomalous parameter combinations. Correlate with post-compromise activity on same asset.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability impact: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' achieved by remote unauthenticated attacker. Detect the information-disclosure outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or anomalous-privilege access to FortiOS sensitive resources: config files, admin panels, backup archives, credential storage. Alert on subsequent egress of large data volumes over HTTP/HTTPS to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Filesystem-Level Access on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite stated in article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Detect this precursor activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiOS process/filesystem activity. Alert on: writes to protected system directories by non-system processes, elevation to filesystem-access privileges, reads of sensitive files outside normal service workflows. Indicates post-compromise persistence setup.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Version Enumeration / Banner Grabbing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must enumerate FortiOS version before targeting CVE-2025-68686-vulnerable instances. Reconnaissance precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect probes targeting FortiOS known paths (/admin, /api/) coupled with version extraction attempts. Flag sequential HTTP/HTTPS requests from single source to multiple FortiOS IP ranges within subnet followed by exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>' and references '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure', yet zero UC was generated. This is the minimum required detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Fortinet FortiOS systems matching CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize internet-facing assets. Verify patch compliance against Federal due date 2026-08-10. Confirm absence of vulnerable version string across monitored FortiOS fleet.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' but pipeline missed persistence detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting filesystem-level compromise on FortiOS, monitor for symbolic link creation in system directories or service startup paths. Flag symlinks targeting configuration files, credential stores, or log directories.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Exploitation Attempts to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation 'via crafted HTTP requests' post-compromise, but pipeline extracted no exploitation detection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, hunt HTTP requests to FortiOS admin interfaces with anomalous payloads (path traversal, symlink references, bypass tokens). Correlate timing with filesystem access anomalies and unusual process execution on FortiOS host.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article's core impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor', but pipeline generated zero detection for information leakage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk reads of configuration files, certificates, credentials, or logs outside normal admin patterns. Pair with network indicators of exfiltration (large transfers to external IPs, suspicious DNS queries from FortiOS process context).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Lag Risk Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10. Pipeline failed to generate compliance baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all FortiOS systems remaining unpatched for CVE-2025-68686 after 2026-08-10. Cross-reference with external asset exposure scans. Escalate internet-facing appliances as imminent compromise risk.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Hunt: Fortinet FortiOS Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due date 2026-08-10. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this operational directive and template reference in source body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for unpatched Fortinet FortiOS instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 (exposure of sensitive information). Correlate vulnerability scanners against patch-management systems to identify instances past the 2026-08-10 federal remediation deadline. Prioritize externally-facing FortiOS appliances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiOS: Symbolic Link Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No detection rule was generated for this specific exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints that attempt symbolic-link path traversal, unusual query parameters targeting file-access APIs, or patterns deviating from baseline FortiOS administrative traffic. Focus on requests following filesystem-level compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Post-Compromise Information Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No detection for bulk data access or exfiltration from FortiOS systems post-compromise was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large data reads, configuration exports, or API bulk-retrieval operations on FortiOS instances following anomalous filesystem access or patch-bypass HTTP requests. Monitor for access to sensitive files (credentials, encryption keys, system configuration) or unscheduled bulk data transfers.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Access to Fortinet FortiOS: Initial Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite attack step was not converted into a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation or suspicious process execution on FortiOS systems leading to unauthorized filesystem access. Monitor for creation of symbolic links in system directories, writes to /etc or /proc, or access to kernel structures that precede the HTTP-based exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and designates this as active KEV. Pipeline produced zero IOC or detection logic for this baseline indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FortiOS or FortiProxy appliance in vulnerability scan results showing presence of CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize by public exposure (Internet-facing); do not discount based on reported patch status—patch lag is endemic in production environments.

suggestion.title: FortiOS/FortiProxy Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and KEV status indicates active wild exploitation. Template section requests standard asset-exposure hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS/FortiProxy appliances accepting unauthenticated connections from untrusted networks (Internet or untrusted VLANs) on common admin ports (443, 8443, 10443). Cross-correlate with CVE-2025-68686 scanner hits to prioritize investigation.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Bypass via HTTP Request
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker bypassing 'the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the core attack vector and requires direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In FortiOS/FortiProxy HTTP/HTTPS logs, detect requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\..), symbolic link references, or administrative endpoint access using crafted query strings. Correlate with post-exploit indicators (lateral movement, data staging) to identify active exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states final impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' and notes attacker must 'have compromised the product via another vulnerability' first. Detect exfiltration phase after initial breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-confirmation of compromise (login anomalies, execution of suspicious processes on FortiOS), detect bulk access to sensitive files (credential stores, config backups, user databases) or exfiltration-pattern outbound connections from the appliance to external IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Status Inventory & Due Date Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10'. SOC must track patch status against regulatory timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiOS and FortiProxy instances. For each, verify patch version against Fortinet security advisories for CVE-2025-68686. Flag any unpatched or outdated instances and escalate to patch management with due date (2026-08-10) for federal compliance tracking.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' Attacker repointed v35 and other existing tags to hide malicious code. Tag reassignments outside normal branch flow are rare and suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor release/semantic version tags in high-dependency repositories for reassignment to different commits (especially commits outside primary branches). Alert when tags move backward in history or point to commits without branch lineage. Cross-correlate tag movement with orphaned-commit creation.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposed in GitHub Actions Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core impact statement: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Secrets normally redacted by GitHub were exposed due to workflow code injected into widely-used Action. Directly observable in job run output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs for credential patterns (AWS key prefixes AKIA, JWT structures, common secret variable names like API_KEY, TOKEN, PASSWORD). Correlate with repository-level encrypted secrets. Alert on plaintext secret appearance in logs, especially at scale across multiple users/orgs using the same Action.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation and Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'orphaned commits and manipulated release tags' as 'key enabling factors.' Attacker created a commit, deleted the branch, then tagged the orphaned commit to activate it downstream. Orphaned commits + tags = unusual pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits reachable via tags but not via any branch (git rev-list --all | git rev-parse --not --branches). Alert when new release/version tags point to such commits. Investigate commits that exist in history but have no branch ancestry, especially recently created orphans.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Widely-Used GitHub Action Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' This is textbook T1195.001. Attacker leveraged compromised access to popular Action (tj-actions/changed-files) to inject malicious code at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor widely-used GitHub Actions (1000+ stars, 10K+ dependent repos) for unusual commits, new committers, anomalous tag patterns, or permission escalations. Alert on write-access grants to high-dependency repos. Track all commits merged to primary branch with focus on external contributors or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Code Download in GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Attack triggered network anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions jobs executing curl, wget, or download operations targeting non-GitHub domains (especially dynamic/suspicious hosts). Alert on shell patterns like curl|sh or wget -O|bash. Correlate external downloads with known-malicious or newly-registered domains. Focus on Actions used by thousands of downstream repos.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Write Access to Critical Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo.' Access vector remains unclear, but unusual permission grants to high-impact repos merit detection. Initial compromise required write-access foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new collaborators, deploy keys, or third-party OAuth applications granted write access to widely-depended Actions. Monitor for out-of-band user additions, unusual access from new accounts, or permission escalations on critical repos. Investigate PAT (Personal Access Token) creation targeting high-dependency projects.

suggestion.title: Gitea artifact HMAC signature applied to request with different repository/task context than signature generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can turn a signed URL for an attacker-controlled artifact into a URL that reads artifacts from another task context while preserving the original HMAC signature.' Need UC detecting signature-URL component mismatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract HMAC signature, taskID, repoID, and artifactID from artifact endpoint requests. Build baseline of valid (sig, taskID, repoID) tuples from legitimate CI job patterns. Flag signatures appearing with taskID or repoID values outside the baseline tuple set.

suggestion.title: CI runner or service account accessing artifacts across unauthorized repositories in single Actions workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'cross-repository artifact read' as core attack. Legitimate workflows have bounded repository scope; detect when one CI job identity accesses artifacts from 2+ repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each CI job identity (service account or runner hostname), track distinct repositories accessed during DownloadArtifact requests. Flag jobs accessing N+1 expected repositories within a single workflow run or within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Artifact modification or upload to previously-readonly task context via signed URL reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cross-task upload-state write.' Need UC distinguishing legitimate initial artifact uploads from subsequent modifications to task-scoped artifacts by foreign contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For UploadArtifact PUT requests, correlate taskID + artifactID + source IP.
