suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploitation Chain: Prior FortiOS Vulnerability → CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' The two-stage attack (initial compromise + secondary exploitation) should be modeled as a kill-chain correlation rule, but pipeline shows no phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances with evidence of prior successful exploitation (e.g., unexpected filesystem modifications, privilege escalation artifacts, suspicious process history) followed by HTTP requests matching CVE-2025-68686 exploitation signatures. Treat as multi-stage attack.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—this is a second-stage persistence technique that requires direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous symbolic link creation or modification on FortiOS systems, particularly in config directories or startup paths. Correlation with failed HTTP requests in the same timeframe raises confidence—attacker may be re-establishing persistence after patch disruption.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly stated: 'via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the bypass mechanism after symlink patching. Must detect HTTP patterns consistent with path traversal or encoding tricks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS instances with unusual path encoding (double-slash, Unicode, percent-encoding), directory traversal patterns (../ sequences), or suspicious parameter inflation. Baseline clean request patterns first.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure to Unauthorized Principals
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly named 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'—need to detect when sensitive data leaves protected contexts (config files, credential stores, policy databases).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for large or unusual reads of configuration files, policy databases, or VPN credential stores. Correlate with HTTP exfiltration patterns or data staging on the filesystem. Alert on any egress of files containing API keys or encrypted credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FortiOS Filesystem-Level Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—this implies prior compromise chain (likely CVE+RCE). Must detect suspicious filesystem activity that indicates execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file enumeration, permission changes, or access to restricted system directories on FortiOS after other CVE exploitation is suspected. Focus on /etc/config, /etc/ssl, and application binary directories. Correlate with web server or process activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to TeamCity Admin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Run OS Commands Without Logging In'—attackers exploit an unauthenticated endpoint. Must detect HTTP POST/GET requests to TeamCity administration paths (e.g., /teamcity/admin, /guestLogin.html) from external or low-privilege sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to TeamCity admin endpoints that succeed (HTTP 200–299) without prior successful authentication event. Baseline legitimate admin access, alert on spike from external IPs or anomalous user agents.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from TeamCity Process
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Run OS Commands.' TeamCity process (TeamCity.exe, teamcityd) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell without prior human action on agent/server indicates exploitation or post-compromise lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation from TeamCity service account spawning interpreters (cmd, PowerShell, bash) with suspicious arguments (encoded strings, base64, network callbacks). Exclude known build configurations.

suggestion.title: Rapid Web Service Restart Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may trigger service recovery, reboot, or log clearing. Detect abnormal TeamCity service lifecycle events (restart, stop/start within minutes) coupled with preceding HTTP activity to admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate TeamCity HTTP 200 responses to admin endpoints within 1–10 minutes of TeamCity service stop/restart events. Alert if no known maintenance ticket or scheduled deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File/Script Creation in TeamCity Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE allows attacker to drop payloads into build output directories. Detect .ps1, .bat, .exe, .jar creation in TeamCity artifact/build paths with timestamps correlating to exploitation HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamCity artifact directories (typically /buildAgent/work, /artifacts) for new executable or script files created outside normal build window. Correlate creation time with HTTP exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Out-of-Band Command Callback from TeamCity Host
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may establish persistence or interactive access via reverse shell or DNS/HTTP callback to C2. Alert on unexpected outbound connections from TeamCity process to suspicious external IPs/domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from TeamCity process (or child processes) to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially on ports 443, 8080, 4444, or DNS queries for newly registered/suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Build Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may be used to inject malicious build steps into CI/CD pipelines to compromise downstream systems. Detect modifications to build config files without corresponding UI admin session or VCS commit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to .teamcity/settings.kts, build configuration XML, or build step parameters not preceded by authenticated TeamCity admin login or corresponding git push event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious tc Command Execution with Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'race into root exploit' via traffic-control subsystem; pipeline generated zero use cases despite mention of unprivileged-to-root escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tc (traffic control) commands spawned by unprivileged users, especially with rapid file descriptor manipulation or system calls that trigger race conditions. Flag if process token privilege level increases post-execution or if child processes inherit root context.

suggestion.title: Kernel Race Condition via inotify/fanotify File Descriptor Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'race condition' in traffic control; common pattern exploited through inotify/fanotify watchers combined with file operations. Pipeline omitted kernel-level exploitation technique detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid inotify_add_watch / inotify_rm_watch syscall sequences from non-root processes, paired with concurrent write/unlink operations on /etc/passwd, /etc/sudoers, or network config files. Flag race-window exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Network Namespace Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'traffic-control' (tc, qdisc) as attack surface; tc operates on network namespaces and netlink interface. Pipeline failed to model detection for netlink-based kernel exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netlink socket operations (NETLINK_ROUTE family) from unprivileged processes, especially crafted qdisc/tc filter additions with unusual callback or classid values that may trigger kernel UAF/OOB conditions.

suggestion.title: Process Privilege Token Elevation via Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'root exploit'; pipeline generated no use case for privilege token changes. Core attack chain is unprivileged→root, not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process token privilege transitions where a process spawned by unprivileged user (UID 1000+) gains UID 0 ownership without sudo/su invocation or credential delegation. Correlate with suspicious syscall volume immediately prior.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Exploit Toolchain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes 'AI helped develop' exploit; pipeline should flag AI code-generation patterns in discovered payloads or implants (e.g., ChatGPT-like variable naming, template-generated shellcode signatures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compressed/encoded payloads with entropy patterns consistent with LLM-generated code (repetitive function preambles, stereotyped error handling). Cross-reference discovered exploit scripts against known AI model output signatures.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of tc Qdisc Command Injection via Malformed Filter Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'traffic-control' as the vulnerable subsystem; no detection use case for command/filter injection in tc operations (e.g., qdisc add, filter add with malformed class/action specs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor tc command-line invocations for suspicious syntax: nested backticks, shell metacharacters in class/filter IDs, unusual action targets (e.g., action bpf with inline eBPF payloads). Correlate with kernel error log spikes.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Impersonation (NightLedger)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The implant masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is explicit persistence/execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SspiCli.dll load attempts from non-system directories, especially when triggered by RPCRT4.dll delay-loading during RPC authentication calls in AppVShNotify.exe context. Detect unsigned or timestomped SspiCli.dll in unexpected paths.

suggestion.title: WebSocket-Based Tunneling Command and Control (BridgeHead/ArcBridge)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling' as primary C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket upgrade handshakes over HTTP/HTTPS to C2 infrastructure. Flag persistent bidirectional WebSocket connections from compromised aerospace/aviation sectors. Correlate WebSocket tunnel establishment with preceding DLL hijacking events.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Spear-Phishing Lures Targeting Defense/Aerospace Sectors
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with recruitment/hiring-themed subject lines and attachments targeting aerospace, aviation, defense, telecom sectors across Middle East/Africa. Flag links to lookalike videoconferencing domains redirecting to file-sharing services. Alert on high-confidence phishing infrastructure impersonating LinkedIn, Indeed, or Zoom.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Third-Party File-Sharing Services Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states lures 'redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services,' indicating secondary delivery mechanism following initial phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads from Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box for archive files (ZIP, RAR) linked from phishing emails. Flag immediate archive extraction and spawning of unsigned executables or DLL loads. Correlate timing with phishing campaign detection.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Capabilities via NightLedger Backdoor (Process Discovery, Screenshot Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies NightLedger enables 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture,' indicating discovery phase commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process enumeration commands (tasklist, Get-Process, ps) originating from AppVShNotify.exe child processes. Detect screenshot API calls (BitBlt, ScreenCaptureAPI) from unusual parent processes. Flag file enumeration (dir, ls, find) chained with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Deployment of BridgeHead Tunneler in Victim Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.' Indicates lateral movement/persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In post-compromise detection, flag BridgeHead tunneler deployment alongside reconnaissance commands. Monitor for WebSocket listener establishment on internal network segments following initial NightLedger compromise. Correlate with aerospace/aviation IP ranges in Egypt and Pakistan.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Process Execution from Network
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'command injection flaw'—exploitation would trigger abnormal process spawning from VeloCloud service context (e.g. `velocloud` user executing `cmd.exe`, `/bin/sh`, or `powershell`). No detection UC generated despite clear RCE attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes created by VeloCloud Orchestrator services (w/ parent: velocloud/orchestrator process). Flag execution of shells, interpreters, or encoded payload runners outside expected maintenance windows. High fidelity signal in enterprise networks where VeloCloud is appliance-only.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud HTTP Request Parameter Fuzzing or Injection Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'command injection'—exploitation involves HTTP parameter tampering. Pipeline missed detection for malformed or special-char-heavy request payloads targeting known VeloCloud API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST/GET requests to VeloCloud admin or API endpoints (e.g. `/api/`, `/rest/`) for command metacharacters: `; | & $ ( ) < > \n \r`. Correlate with 400/500 error responses followed by 200 OK—signature of fuzz→exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from VeloCloud to Rare/Malicious Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker typically establishes C2 or exfiltration channel. Article doesn't specify IOCs but pipeline should infer callback detection for compromised orchestrator appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline VeloCloud network egress (DNS, NTP, vendor update servers). Alert on new destinations with high reputation risk, tor exit nodes, or dynamic DNS. High-value indicator if VeloCloud is air-gapped or restricted-egress in topology.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Service Restart or Crash Following Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Failed injection attempts or exploit edge cases often crash the orchestrator. Pipeline should have suggested monitoring service health events as a leading indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track VeloCloud Orchestrator service crashes, unexpected restarts, or hang events within minutes of suspicious HTTP requests. Combine with failed login spikes or auth errors to triangulate exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Arista VeloCloud Configuration or Credential Export
suggestion.rationale: RCE via command injection likely enables attacker to extract running config, credentials, or customer VPN keys stored on orchestrator. Pipeline missed post-exploitation data exfil use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads of `/opt/velocloud/config/`, `/etc/velocloud/`, or registry hives containing orchestrator secrets. Track unusual tar/zip/scp operations from velocloud process context targeting external IPs or DNS queries for pastebin/data-exfil domains.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication or Privilege Elevation Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: After command execution foothold, attacker typically moves laterally or escalates. Pipeline omitted user/service account creation or sudo/privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new local user creation or `sudo` invocations originating from web service context (velocloud user). Look for `useradd`, `net user`, or service-account password changes coinciding with HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-based C2 Beaconing Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Dysphoria IoT Botnet Adds Blockchain C2' — a novel persistence and evasion mechanism post-disruption. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this core attack innovation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IoT devices performing unusual blockchain network queries or peer-to-peer protocol handshakes indicative of C2 beaconing. Look for DNS queries to blockchain nodes, unusual outbound connections to known blockchain networks (Ethereum, Bitcoin testnet), or patterns of encoded command exfiltration over ledger-based channels.

suggestion.title: Victim Relay Node Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Victim Relays' as post-disruption infrastructure replacement. No use case captures detection of compromised endpoints acting as intermediate C2 nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify IoT or end-user devices exhibiting relay behavior: forwarding unusual traffic patterns to external IPs with low payload variance, establishing persistent bidirectional connections, or spawning child processes that bind to listening ports. Correlate inbound C2 traffic with outbound relay to third parties.

suggestion.title: IoT Exploitation and Dysphoria Botnet Infection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Dysphoria IoT Botnet' but no detection use case for initial compromise or infection indicators. Article body mentions infection post-disruption resilience.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IoT devices (routers, cameras, NAS, industrial controllers) for execution of shell scripts or interpreted code with network exfiltration, credential enumeration (passwd/shadow reads), or privilege escalation attempts. Correlate with known Dysphoria-associated domains, file hashes, or behavioral fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Post-Disruption C2 Resurrection and Network Reconstitution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'After JackSkid Disruption' — a behavioral shift from centralized to blockchain-based relay model. No use case detects rapid infrastructure migration or resurrection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track clusters of previously silent or sinkholed IoT malware nodes suddenly resuming outbound communication with new C2 endpoints, particularly to blockchain networks or peer-to-peer infrastructure. Correlate timing with known disruption events.

suggestion.title: Peer-to-Peer Botnet Mesh Network Formation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victim relays and blockchain C2 as decentralized infrastructure. No use case detects mesh network topology or peer-node enrollment patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify compromised nodes establishing high-cardinality connections to geographically dispersed peers with consistent port sequences, low-bandwidth heartbeat traffic, or packet patterns consistent with distributed hash table (DHT) or gossip protocols indicative of botnet mesh membership.

suggestion.title: Certificate Requests with Non-DC CDC Values
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'systems previously did not verify that the server supplied through the attacker-controlled cdc value was a legitimate domain controller' and attackers 'direct the CA to the attacker-controlled system, and return false directory information for a targeted machine account.' CDC manipulation is the exploit root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AD CS certificate enrollment requests where the Client DC (CDC) attribute resolves to a system not registered as a domain controller in Active Directory, or where CDC IP/hostname maps to non-DC subnets. Cross-reference certificate request timestamps against AD computer object creation time.

suggestion.title: PKINIT Kerberos Auth as Domain Controller from Non-DC
suggestion.rationale: Article states PoC 'authenticate through PKINIT as the targeted domain controller' using certificate and 'the attacker can...perform privileged Active Directory operations.' Direct authentication anomaly indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kerberos TGT requests (AS-REQ) with PKINIT pre-authentication where the requested principal is a domain controller account (CN=DC$) but source IP is not a known domain controller. Alert on certificate-based auth to DC accounts from user workstations or non-DC servers.

suggestion.title: DCSync Replication Initiated by Non-Domain-Controller
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome: 'the attacker can request account secrets, including the krbtgt secret' via 'Impacket's secretsdump tool to perform a DCSync attack.' GetNCChanges replication from unexpected principals is the detection window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Directory Replication Service (DRS) GetNCChanges operations for directory replication requests originating from systems not holding the domain controller role. Alert on replication of sensitive container attributes (cn=krbtgt) requested from non-DC sources with any authentication method.

suggestion.title: Machine Account Creation by Low-Privilege Users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A low-privileged user first creates a machine account, which is permitted under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota configuration' and 'A machine account created through the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota setting is a valid domain principal.' This is the attack entry point and exploit enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected machine account creators (service accounts, admin groups). Alert on machine account creation by end users, service accounts not in authorized groups, or accounts outside network administration organizational units. Flag creation of multiple machine accounts by single user within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Credential Cache Files (.ccache) on Windows Systems
suggestion.rationale: PoC workflow: 'saving the resulting Kerberos credentials to a .ccache file' for subsequent credential reuse. .ccache files are Unix/Linux-native and not standard on Windows, indicating attacker tools like certighost.py or Impacket.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or access of .ccache files on Windows systems, which indicates credential caching via non-native tools (likely Impacket or certighost.py). Correlate .ccache file creation with PKINIT authentication attempts or certificate enrollment activity.

suggestion.title: Rogue LDAP/LSA/SMB Services Responding to CA Requests
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'run rogue SMB, LSA, and LDAP services, direct the CA to the attacker-controlled system, and return false directory information.' These services are the 'chase' mechanism exploitation enabler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LDAP (port 389/636), LSA (port 445 SMB), or NETLOGON services running from user-context processes or on non-standard ports. Monitor outbound connections from AD CS server to non-DC systems on LDAP/SMB ports. Alert on service creation by non-SYSTEM accounts for directory services.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector and 'remote unauthenticated attacker' as the threat actor capability. No HTTP-based detection UC was generated despite this being the primary delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with abnormal patterns (high payload sizes, suspicious headers, or known exploit signatures) targeting FortiOS default paths or admin interfaces. Correlate with FortiOS version detection to scope exposure. Look for 400/401/403 response clustering before successful 200s, indicating reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'. No filesystem-level persistence detection UC was generated despite this being a named attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink creation in FortiOS directories (typically /usr/local, /var/webui). Suspicious patterns: symlinks pointing to world-writable locations, symlinks created by unprivileged processes, or symlinks created post-patch installation. Cross-reference with timeline of prior compromises.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article defines impact as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'. No data exfiltration or unauthorized access UC was generated to detect when exposed information is actually accessed or transmitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS logs for access to sensitive datastores (configs, credentials, certificates) by unauthenticated or unexpected processes. Monitor egress of FortiOS configuration files, SSL certificates, or authentication objects. Alert on unusual volume of log reads or database queries from compromised admin interfaces.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline of 2026-08-10. Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer'. No asset inventory or patch compliance UC was generated despite this being mandatory for federal agencies and critical for any enterprise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all FortiOS instances across the fleet for version/build number against the patched build list published by Fortinet. Flag any instances running vulnerable versions as CriticalUnpatched. Correlate with internet-facing asset registry to identify externally exposed vulnerable FortiOS boxes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Config File Unauthorized Read Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'exposure of sensitive information'. Symlink attacks typically target configuration files. No detection for abnormal config access was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of FortiOS configuration files (/etc/fortios.conf, /data/config, etc.) from unexpected process contexts or UIDs. Look for sequential reads of multiple config files in rapid succession. Alert on symlink resolution attempts targeting credential stores or SSL key materials.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch'—the primary attack vector. No HTTP-level detection hypothesis was generated despite this being observable in access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS appliance HTTP access logs for requests matching known vulnerable patterns—symbolic link bypass indicators, unusual parameter encoding, or version-specific request signatures. Correlate with failed patch verification and unpatched system inventory to identify high-risk exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—no filesystem monitoring or persistence-layer detection use case was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for suspicious symbolic link creation in sensitive directories (config paths, plugin directories, authentication modules). Flag links pointing outside expected directory trees or created by non-admin processes. Correlate link creation with post-exploitation timeframes and failed patch attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Sensitive Configuration and Credentials
suggestion.rationale: CVE's core issue is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—no exfiltration or unauthorized access detection was generated for credentials, config, or encryption keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unauthorized reads of FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, and encryption keys. Monitor API logs for bulk data exports or config downloads from unexpected source IPs. Alert on exfiltration of VPN credentials, admin accounts, or certificate material. Baseline legitimate backup patterns to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unpatched System Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch lag and cites federal remediation due-date (2026-08-10). Template guidance directs asset-exposure hunt, yet no UC was generated despite this being straightforward vulnerability-to-asset correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 against FortiOS asset inventory. Alert on any unpatched FortiOS system detected on internet-facing networks or DMZ. Prioritize systems with historical patch lag; correlate scanner findings with FortiOS version queries and management-plane access logs.

suggestion.title: Pre-Exploitation: Initial Compromise via Secondary FortiOS Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability'—the prerequisite initial-access step was not modeled in kill chain or detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FortiOS exploitation chains typically involve pre-requisite CVEs to gain filesystem/process access. Monitor for exploitation attempts of other known FortiOS vulnerabilities. Cross-correlate authentication failures, HTTP anomalies, and filesystem access patterns to detect multi-stage attack progression leading to CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FortiOS Management Interface Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploit via HTTP and bypass patches to access management interface and sensitive data—no hunting for unauthorized admin console access or lateral movement into management plane was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate admin access to FortiOS HTTPS management interface (ports 443, 10443, etc.). Alert on logins from new/unexpected IPs, access at unusual hours, failed authentication attempts preceding successful login, or bulk configuration exports. Correlate with HTTP exploitation logs and filesystem anomalies to identify post-compromise reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FortiOS Inventory Before Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 2026-08-10 patch deadline; pipeline generated no vulnerability scanner query. 'CISA KEV' + 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate' establishes urgent asset detection need.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for FortiOS versions matching CVE-2025-68686 affected ranges before federal deadline. Alert on unpatched public-facing FortiOS appliances. Track remediation status daily post-detection.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse in FortiOS Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass the patch developed for symbolic link persistency'—attack vector completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS installation directories for suspicious symlink creation. Flag symlinks pointing to /tmp, /dev, or user-writable paths. Alert on access patterns through symlinks that precede data exfiltration or process execution.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Bypassing Symbolic Link Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack uses 'crafted HTTP requests' and involves 'bypass the patch'—direct exploitation vector not reflected in any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS admin endpoints with path traversal, dot-dot-slash sequences, or symlink references in query parameters. Correlate with timestamp of failed authentication attempts followed by successful config/credential access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Disclosure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is defined as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' but no detection for information access/exfiltration was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data transfers from FortiOS to external IPs post-compromise. Monitor audit logs for unauthorized reads of config files, credential stores, or system_info endpoints. Flag unencrypted exfiltration channels.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiOS Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—suggests multi-stage attack enabling lateral movement into protected networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FortiOS compromise indicators with unusual outbound traffic to internal subnets. Alert on port scans, SMB attempts, or credential attacks originating from FortiOS segment post-CVE exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2025-68686 in Fortinet FortiOS with federal patch deadline 2026-08-10. Requires asset enumeration to identify in-scope appliances: 'CVE-2025-68686'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS appliances (via port 443, HTTPS management interface, SSH banners) running vulnerable versions prior to the patch deadline. Cross-reference against FortiOS security advisories for CVE-2025-68686 affected versions. Prioritize exposed administrative interfaces (public-facing).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Filesystem Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Requires detection of symbolic-link creation/abuse in FortiOS directories after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic-link creation/modification in persistence directories (startup scripts, cron jobs, initialization paths). Alert on ln -s or symlink API calls in FortiOS chroot or configuration paths. Baseline legitimate FortiOS symlink operations and flag anomalies post-breach.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation method as 'via crafted HTTP requests' bypassing the symbolic-link patch. Requires detection of malformed or obfuscated HTTP traffic to FortiOS management interfaces: 'crafted HTTP requests'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and analyze HTTP requests to FortiOS management ports (443, 8443, 8080). Flag requests with unusual path encoding (URL normalization bypasses), HTTP method abuse, or malformed headers targeting symbolic-link patch conditions. Correlate with successful authentication anomalies or filesystem activity.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker capability as 'allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch... [via] sensitive information.' Detect unauthorized access to FortiOS configuration, credentials, or system data after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for reads/copies of sensitive files post-breach: /etc/config/* (system config), /etc/passwd (local accounts), VPN credentials, firewall rules. Alert on any filesystem or process reads of these paths by non-admin processes or during off-hours. Correlate with network exfiltration events (outbound data transfer).

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before the FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 exploitation succeeds. Detects the full two-phase attack sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: initial compromise via unidentified vulnerability (filesystem-level access), followed within minutes/hours by crafted HTTP requests and symbolic-link operations. Build correlation rules: failed exploit attempts → filesystem write access → HTTP anomalies. Flag rapid progression through these phases as likely exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Management Interface Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' threat model; asset-exposure hunt for publicly-reachable FortiOS management interfaces. 'Remote unauthenticated' implies network exposure is the precondition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing IP ranges for FortiOS management ports (443, 8080, 8443). Correlate with known DNS CNAME/A records and certificate transparency logs for FortiOS hostnames. Identify publicly-routable FortiOS instances and cross-reference against internal asset inventory; prioritize for immediate access-control review and patching.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors.' Exposed FortiOS instances are the attack surface for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances accessible from the public internet by scanning for expected ports (typically TCP/443 with FortiOS TLS certificates or HTTP/8080 for management interface) and matching vendor signatures. Priority: any exposed instance is at risk given active KEV exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' Direct description of exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to exposed FortiOS management interfaces (8080, 443) with patterns consistent with symlink persistence bypass attempts. Look for sequential requests suggesting payload delivery followed by filesystem access patterns; baseline against known exploit signatures as they emerge.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence technique being bypassed. Filesystem-level persistence is the attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symbolic links in application directories (e.g., /bin, /usr/local/bin, configuration paths). Correlate symlink creation with HTTP exploitation attempts. High-confidence signal: symlinks pointing to world-writable locations or system utilities.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Defense Evasion in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' The bypass is the attack; detection must focus on circumvention of existing protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS that employ obfuscation, unusual encoding, or request patterns designed to evade signature-based patch protections. Look for requests differing significantly from baseline traffic or documented legitimate administrative paths.

suggestion.title: Secondary CVE Exploitation Chain (Filesystem Privilege Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This describes a multi-step breach requiring initial compromise via separate CVE, followed by exploitation of CVE-2025-68686 for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In FortiOS environments, correlate alerts for other exploited vulnerabilities (check FortiOS security bulletins) with subsequent HTTP exploitation of CVE-2025-68686. Chains of multiple CVE exploitation attempts within short timeframes indicate sophisticated post-compromise persistence tactics.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exposure via CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article title and source define the vulnerability as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' The exposure itself is the impact mechanism, not just the persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for unusual data access or transmission patterns post-exploitation, especially access to credential stores, configuration files (containing VPN keys, certificate material), or user identity databases. Correlate with baseline FortiOS traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-08-10; SOC must identify all FortiOS instances and patch status. No inventory hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management DB and vulnerability scanners for FortiOS instances. Cross-reference build/patch version against Fortinet advisory. Flag any system not patched or with unknown version as of 2026-08-10 deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector. Pipeline did not create HTTP anomaly detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP request logs for patterns matching known CVE-2025-68686 payloads (if disclosed); flag requests from untrusted IPs to FortiOS admin interfaces; alert on 400+ HTTP errors from FortiOS appliances that correlate with subsequent system compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass of patch developed for...symbolic link persistency.' No hunt for artifact creation or filesystem anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS appliances, hunt for unexpected symlink creation in critical directories (/bin, /etc, /var). Correlate with prior CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts. Look for symlinks pointing to attacker-controlled paths or unusual target locations.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information' as the ultimate goal. Pipeline ignored the data access/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS logs for unusual read/access patterns to sensitive config files (vpn users, certificates, PSK, admin credentials) following known exploitation windows. Flag bulk data export or config backup events outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Admin Interface Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains unauthenticated access via HTTP bypass after initial compromise. No hunt for admin/management plane anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed vs. successful FortiOS admin logins; flag logins from IPs never seen before authenticating to that appliance; detect login storms or brute-force patterns against admin accounts; cross-reference with CVE-2025-68686 HTTP logs.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails targeting Microsoft 365 credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Kratos kit is 'built to steal Microsoft 365 sessions.' Phishing is the documented initial access vector; pipeline generated zero phishing-detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails with M365/Office 365 branding and urgency language, spoofed Microsoft sender domains, and embedded login URLs or credential-harvesting forms. Flag campaigns targeting bulk user populations with phishing-kit signatures.

suggestion.title: MFA interception and bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'bypass MFA'—this is the kit's core differentiator. No detection logic was generated for MFA challenge interception or replay.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA bypass via: geographically impossible logins within MFA challenge window, repeated MFA rejections followed by successful auth, suspicious MFA method changes, or token replay from non-standard OAuth clients.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Microsoft 365 session creation from phishing-harvested credentials
suggestion.rationale: Kit is designed to 'steal Microsoft 365 sessions.' Compromised sessions will exhibit anomalous login patterns; pipeline did not generate session-anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag M365 logins from unusual geolocations, non-standard clients (legacy auth), or times inconsistent with user baseline. Alert on bulk session creation from single source IP; monitor for mailbox forwarding rules set post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Kratos phishing-kit command-and-control infrastructure blocking
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses dismantlement of Kratos but pipeline extracted zero IOCs: no C2 domains, malware hashes, or redirector infrastructure. These should be flagged for network block and threat-hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block outbound DNS/HTTPS connections to known Kratos C2 and phishing redirector domains. Monitor for malformed SSL certificates, suspicious domain registration patterns, or fast-flux DNS behavior associated with phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Office 365 use of stolen authentication tokens
suggestion.rationale: Stolen sessions mean attackers possess valid refresh/access tokens. Article does not specify detection for token-reuse attacks or out-of-band token abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office 365 operations (mail forwarding, inbox rules, app consent) from API clients that differ from normal user agents. Alert on token age anomalies, cross-region use, or token reuse across multiple devices in short time window.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Remote Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the primary attack vector and requires direct detection coverage for exploitation attempts against internet-facing FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiOS management/application endpoints with suspicious characteristics: directory traversal sequences (../ or ..\ patterns), symbolic link references, or known CVE-2025-68686 payload patterns. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data to identify which systems lack patches.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence in FortiOS Filesystem Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—symlink creation/abuse must be detected as the persistence mechanic after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious symbolic link creation or modification within FortiOS system directories, especially targeting config, binaries, or script locations. Anomalies include: symlinks pointing outside expected paths, symlinks created by unexpected processes, or symlink chains suggesting evasion intent.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Fortinet FortiOS Fleet Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due date 2026-08-10—baseline asset inventory against vulnerable versions is mandatory for this CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS systems and flag those running versions prior to the applicable CVE-2025-68686 security patch. Prioritize systems with internet-facing access. Monitor for sustained patch gaps beyond organizational SLAs and federal remediation deadlines.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via Directory Traversal in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' via crafted requests post-compromise—detection of abnormal sensitive file access and data movement is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting exploitation attempts, hunt for unauthorized access to sensitive files (configuration, credential storage, encryption keys, logs) within FortiOS. Flag exfiltration of configuration backups, admin credentials, or VPN keys to unexpected external IPs or domains. Monitor for large data transfers post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Compromise Chain: Initial RCE → Filesystem Access → Symlink Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—detection must capture the sequential exploitation pattern and privilege escalation within FortiOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple FortiOS vulnerability exploitation attempts within short time windows (hours). Flag sequences where a code-execution or RCE vulnerability precedes symlink creation activity. Alert on process privilege escalation or context switches following initial exploitation.

suggestion.title: Bypass of Security Patches via Evasion Techniques
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—detection of patch evasion attempts and re-exploitation of theoretically-patched systems is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor patched FortiOS systems for exploitation attempts using alternative payloads or evasion tactics (obfuscation, polymorphic requests). Hunt for evidence of patch bypass: symlink abuse on systems reporting patches as applied, or crafted requests designed to evade patch signatures.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is the persistence vector after initial compromise and should be detected via filesystem monitoring for symlink creation in FortiOS config/binary directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system logs and filesystem events for creation or modification of symbolic links in config directories (/etc/init.d, /etc/cron.d equivalent, or FortiOS-specific persistence locations). Correlate with evidence of filesystem-level access following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Requests Exploiting CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch' after gaining filesystem access. Detection should key on HTTP request patterns post-compromise that deviate from legitimate FortiOS API usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to FortiOS management interfaces with suspicious patterns (non-standard methods, malformed parameters, or requests targeting symbolic link traversal paths) from authenticated or previously-compromised sessions. Baseline legitimate admin HTTP traffic and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' then leverages CVE-2025-68686. Detection should correlate initial exploit attempts with subsequent filesystem-level activity and HTTP-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation of known FortiOS pre-auth vulns with subsequent filesystem access (file creation/modification events) and crafted HTTP request patterns. This multi-event correlation separates opportunistic scanning from actual compromise chains.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS Version Inventory with Post-Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article notes patch lag and the symbolic link bypass only affects certain versions/patches. Asset discovery should identify vulnerable FortiOS versions and cross-reference with indicators of compromise (unauthorized symlinks, privilege changes in system logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all FortiOS instances by version/patch level. Flag those missing patches for CVE-2025-68686 due by 2026-08-10. Alert on any of these devices showing filesystem modification events, new symlinks, or suspicious login activity.

suggestion.title: HTTP Bypass Attempts Against Known FortiOS Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically states the attack 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Detection should flag HTTP requests from already-compromised FortiOS systems attempting to exercise the vulnerability despite patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For patched FortiOS systems, alert on HTTP requests matching known CVE-2025-68686 exploit patterns (request structure, parameter names, URI paths historically associated with this bypass). The presence of such requests despite confirmed patches suggests attack replay or new variants.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article centerpiece: 'CVE-2025-68686' is the primary detection artifact and CISA KEV entry point. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for FortiOS instances matching CVE-2025-68686. Cross-reference with network telemetry to identify any exposed FortiOS management interfaces. CISA KEV due-date (2026-08-10) indicates active exploitation—patch lag is critical.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' Describes the exploitation method explicitly. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints containing patterns consistent with patch-bypass attempts (e.g., requests targeting symbolic-link traversal, malformed authentication headers, or requests timing with known exploit POC patterns). Baseline legitimate FortiOS management traffic first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Implies the attacker reactivates or leverages filesystem-level symlink backdoors post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS logs and underlying OS logs for symbolic link creation or modification in critical directories (e.g., /bin, /lib, config paths). Focus on symlinks created post-compromise that might persist privilege or bypass subsequent patches.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Information Disclosure Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' and 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability.' Requires detection of data access post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual data access patterns or bulk reads from FortiOS configuration, credential stores, or logs after a confirmed or suspected breach via CVE-2025-68686. Include API calls requesting sensitive config exports or authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation: Initial Vulnerability + CVE-2025-68686 Chaining
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline did not reconstruct this dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate CVE-2025-68686 exploit attempts with evidence of prior filesystem-level compromise or exploitation of other FortiOS CVEs (common precursors: authentication bypasses, LFI, RCE). Flag any FortiOS instances with known-exploited predecessor CVEs currently patched against 2025-68686.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Verification Post-CISA Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due-date 2026-08-10. After this date, unpatched instances in federal/contractor scope are audit risk. Pipeline did not suggest compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-08-10, run targeted scan for FortiOS instances still missing CVE-2025-68686 patch. For unpatched boxes, establish if they are in federal/contractual scope and generate remediation tickets. Compare patch date against exploit timeline from threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template reference; this is CISA KEV (actively exploited in wild). Federal patch due 2026-08-10. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear actionable guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2025-68686 against Fortinet FortiOS asset inventory. Alert on any unpatched instances, especially externally exposed. Cross-reference CMDB to identify FortiOS products deployed; validate patch status against federal deadline 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed this specific exploitation vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for requests with malformed/unusual patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Baseline normal request signature post-patch; alert on deviations, non-standard HTTP methods, oversized headers, or parameter combinations not seen in patched steady-state.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is explicit persistence technique but pipeline missed T1547 mapping and detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit FortiOS filesystem for suspicious symlink creation, especially in /etc/init.d or other autostart directories. Alert on symlinks created by non-root during/after exploitation windows. Correlate with HTTP request anomalies to establish full attack chain.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Data Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' but pipeline missed information-gathering/exfiltration detection. Article describes data-exposure vulnerability, not just DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk access to sensitive files (configs, credentials, keys) by non-administrative accounts during or immediately after HTTP request anomalies. Alert on unusual outbound connections from FortiOS to non-standard ports/IPs, especially if correlated with sensitive data reads.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage FortiOS Compromise Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline missed multi-stage attack chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate detections: (1) other FortiOS CVE exploitation attempts, (2) filesystem-level access anomalies (failed/succeeded privesc), (3) subsequent HTTP request patterns targeting CVE-2025-68686. Flag clusters of FortiOS security events within 24-48h windows as high-confidence compromise chains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and specifies 'CVE: CVE-2025-68686' for scanner matching. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance and CISA KEV urgency (federal patch due 2026-08-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Fortinet FortiOS or FortiProxy system flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 in active scanner output. CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation; match against all scan results regardless of claimed patch status, as patch lag is the primary real-world risk vector.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Mechanism Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence vector. Pipeline missed this post-compromise persistence technique entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symbolic links in writable directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, config paths, plugin directories). Flag symlink creation by processes running with unexpected privilege levels, especially correlating with prior compromise events. Article notes attacker must first compromise via separate vulnerability at filesystem level.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Attempts Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker exploits via 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch. This is the primary attack delivery mechanism and pipeline generated no HTTP-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP traffic to FortiOS admin console (/admin, /api/v2 endpoints). Alert on malformed requests, unusual URI paths, requests with atypical parameter combinations, or payloads attempting to trigger symlink-related code paths. Flag requests that bypass standard authentication flows or target protected resources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Sensitive Information
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly addresses 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Pipeline produced no detection for exfiltration or unauthorized access to credentials, configs, or routing data post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unauthorized read/export operations on sensitive files: system.conf, certificates, VPN credentials, firewall rules, routing tables, admin credentials vault. Alert on bulk reads, copy commands, or access from unexpected processes or external connections. Correlate with filesystem-level compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Indicators on FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability exploits systems 'via crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline did not generate detection for patched-but-still-vulnerable indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track FortiOS patch level and version. Alert if system reports patched status for CVE-2025-68686 but still exhibits symbolic link anomalies, old binary hashes, or unexpected code path execution. Flag rollback or downgrade attempts that would re-expose the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Malicious Release Tag Redirection to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: "The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit" — GitHub Action tags moved to commits not on main/protected branches is a key obfuscation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for release tag deletions and creations, especially when new tags point to commits not reachable from main/master branches. Correlate tag movements with unusual commit orphaning patterns. Alert when a single commit is retargeted by multiple version tags (e.g., v34, v35, v36 all pointing to same malicious commit).

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection in Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: "Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch... factors added a bit of obfuscation" — commits existing outside branch history enable hiding of malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan repository commit graphs for commits reachable via tags but not from any branch. Flag orphaned commits especially when they appear in widely-used action repositories. Correlate with recent write access and any associated tag operations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: "The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity." External calls from Actions are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution logs for unexpected curl, wget, or network-based download commands pulling from external domains. Baseline typical network behavior per repository and action. Flag new external domains contacted by established actions or unusual network patterns in CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: "attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs" — GitHub secrets should never surface unencrypted in log output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching secret formats (common patterns: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=, token=, password=, oauth_token). Alert on secrets appearing outside expected redaction. Cross-reference with repository secret definitions to identify specific leaked credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Repository Write Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: "An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit..." Direct write access to high-impact repositories is the critical enabler; monitor for privilege escalation or account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual write operations to GitHub repositories used by >1000 downstream repositories (identify via dependency graph). Alert on new collaborators added with write access, unexpected commits from known accounts, or access pattern changes. Correlate with releases and tag modifications.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Trusted GitHub Action Compromise
suggestion.rationale: "About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action... An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo" — compromising a single widely-trusted component cascades to thousands of dependent workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify high-impact GitHub Actions (used by >5000 repositories). Monitor for sudden changes to action code, new external dependencies, or network activity. Track downstream execution of modified actions across dependent repositories. Alert when a single malicious action version affects thousands of workflows simultaneously.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the primary detection mechanism for identifying at-risk FortiOS instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any FortiOS instance detected as vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 in active vulnerability scans. High priority given CISA KEV status and 2026-08-10 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiOS HTTP Exploitation Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch, following initial filesystem-level compromise. Requires monitoring for anomalous HTTP patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual or malformed HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints, particularly POST/PUT requests with executable content or symlink references, following filesystem access indicators.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as part of the bypass mechanism, indicating filesystem-level persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem logs for suspicious symlink creation or modification, particularly in web-accessible directories or config paths. Cross-correlate with preceding filesystem access.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due date (2026-08-10) and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Compliance hunt required before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate all FortiOS instances have received patches for CVE-2025-68686 before federal deadline. Identify instances with patch lag >10 days post-release.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Chain: Dual-Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. Requires correlation between initial compromise and secondary bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate indicators of prior-stage compromise (filesystem access, unexpected elevation, suspicious logs) with subsequent HTTP exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2025-68686 bypass.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Public Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can reach the vulnerability, implying FortiOS instances are internet-accessible. Baseline asset-visibility detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal network ranges for open TCP/443 and TCP/80 responding with FortiOS banner or login page. Correlate with corporate asset inventory to identify unmanaged or non-patched instances. Alert on any FortiOS asset not behind corporate WAF or access control list.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass published patch. Need signature-based detection on request payload anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS management interfaces for malformed headers, oversized payloads, null bytes, or known CVE-2025-68686 bypass patterns. Alert on any successful response (2xx) to anomalous requests targeting `/api/`, `/system/`, or `/admin/` paths.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Artifacts Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker bypassing 'patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Filesystem-level detection required for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation of symbolic links in `/etc/`, `/var/`, or `/usr/` by processes other than `fortid` or `init`. Alert on symlinks pointing to system binaries, cron jobs, or rc.d scripts. Cross-reference with known FortiOS startup sequences to flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Process Anomalies Post-HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite compromises and HTTP exploitation should trigger process creation or privilege escalation. Need behavioral detection for post-exploitation sandbox or fork activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual child processes spawned by FortiOS web services (e.g., `httpsd`, `nginx`, `lighttpd`), especially those invoking shell interpreters (`/bin/bash`, `/bin/sh`) or writing to filesystem paths outside expected directories. Correlate with filesystem audit logs for symlink creation and cronjob modification.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 — Exposed FortiOS Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit exposed instances; pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt. Fortinet/FortiOS devices accessible to internet are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances with internet-accessible HTTP/HTTPS ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443). Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize externally-facing instances where unauthenticated access is permitted. Track patch deployment timeline relative to 2026-08-10 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 — Crafted HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as exploitation vector; pipeline did not generate detection for anomalous request payloads to FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP/HTTPS endpoints for request patterns deviating from baseline admin and API access—unusual headers, binary payloads, encoding anomalies. Alert on sequences suggesting exploitation probes. Correlate with vulnerability scanner activity and patch status.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence — Filesystem Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'; pipeline ignored this defense-evasion persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation/modification in sensitive directories (/etc, /usr/bin, /var, system startup scripts). Alert on process execution chains using symlinked paths. Baseline legitimate symlinks and detect anomalies, especially post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Prior Compromise — Filesystem-Level Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—pipeline ignored this prerequisite stage, missing early-stage intrusion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized filesystem access, privilege escalation to root/system, and unexpected writes to protected directories on FortiOS. Correlate privilege escalation events with subsequent HTTP-based exploitation attempts to reconstruct multi-stage attack chain.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass — Regression Detection Against Prior Symlink Fix
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—pipeline missed regression hunting: are previously-patched exploits being re-exploited?
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts against previously-patched symlink vulnerabilities in FortiOS deployments. Correlate patch-deployment timestamps with subsequent symlink-persistence indicators or HTTP exploitation attempts to detect patch-bypass techniques.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 — Patch Compliance & Federal Deadline Tracking

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously scan Fortinet FortiOS fleet for CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Generate compliance dashboards mapping unpatched instances by business unit. Alert escalation as 2026-08-10 deadline approaches. Cross-reference patch status with internet exposure to prioritize remediation by risk.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt via Crafted HTTP Requests
