suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests against FortiOS endpoints matching known CVE-2025-68686 exploit patterns (specific header combinations, path traversal, or parameter injection). Look for unauthenticated requests containing crafted payloads that correlate with FortiOS information disclosure CVEs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Bypass Detection Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline did not create a UC for detecting this persistence mechanism activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS configuration directories (esp. /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd) following suspicious process execution. Correlate with evidence of prior compromise via filesystem-level vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Chained FortiOS Exploitation: Initial Filesystem Compromise → CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes prerequisite: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage attack pattern should trigger a UC hunting for the initial compromise followed by HTTP-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for sequences: filesystem write anomalies + privilege escalation in FortiOS → followed within hours/days by crafted HTTP requests to known CVE-2025-68686 endpoints. Use process hollowing, unexpected binary execution, or file system sandbox escapes as initial-compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Exposure Post-Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No UC was generated for detecting information disclosure or data access patterns following successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected access or export of sensitive FortiOS configuration, authentication tokens, or system files following CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts. Look for unusual read patterns in /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or FortiOS credential stores; correlate with prior CVE-2025-68686 HTTP request activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Information Disclosure via Unauthenticated HTTP Access
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'remote unauthenticated attacker' indicates attack requires no valid credentials. Pipeline missed UC for detecting auth bypass or unauthenticated access to sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiOS endpoints that require authentication. Flag HTTP requests to authentication-gated endpoints (e.g., /api/v2/*) that return 200/sensitive data without valid session tokens or credentials. Correlation with known CVE-2025-68686 HTTP patterns increases confidence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the exploitation vector at filesystem level. This is a concrete persistence technique requiring filesystem monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS installation paths (typically /bin, /lib, system directories) for CreateSymbolicLink or equivalent operations. Symbolic links pointing outside installation scope or to credential/config files are high-confidence. Correlate with process creation under httpd or FortiOS service account.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 HTTP Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' HTTP request patterns are the direct exploitation mechanism requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-patch systems should still log malformed or unusual HTTP requests targeting known FortiOS endpoints (e.g., api/v2/, /admin). Look for requests with encoded payloads, multiple redirects, or HTTP methods unusual for the endpoint. Correlate failed auth attempts with subsequent filesystem operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Requires detection of data collection/exfiltration after the HTTP bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data volume or plaintext credential/config transmission from FortiOS hosts after exploitation. FortiOS config files, admin hashes, and VPN credentials are high-value targets. Flag outbound transfers of files matching config naming patterns or MIME types associated with backups.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage FortiOS Compromise Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before HTTP patch bypass works. This two-stage precondition enables a hunt for stage-1 vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unpatched or recently-exploited CVEs on FortiOS instances that predate this CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts (look backward 60–90 days). Correlate filesystem modification timestamps with credential access and HTTP request anomalies to identify the attack chain timeline.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Indicator: FortiOS Behavior After HTTP Craft
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This implies the patch is present but ineffective against certain HTTP patterns—a behavioral gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Systems running the published patch but showing filesystem symlink creation or modification after HTTP exploitation attempts indicate patch-bypass activity. Alert on any symlink operation following suspicious HTTP requests to FortiOS admin or API endpoints, regardless of formal vulnerability status.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and CISA KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets. Pipeline should generate inventory queries for publicly-reachable FortiOS instances as primary detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for FortiOS management interfaces accessible on internet-routable IPs. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unpatched systems. Prioritize systems not yet remediated before 2026-08-10 due date.

suggestion.title: HTTP Exploitation Attempts Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' and 'bypass the patch developed for symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Pipeline should detect anomalous HTTP patterns to FortiOS admin/API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET to FortiOS /api/ endpoints with unusual payloads, symlink-traversal patterns (../, ..\), or multiple 40x responses followed by 200 from same source. Flag requests with non-standard User-Agent or missing auth headers to normally-authenticated endpoints.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-FortiOS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability results in 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Article notes attacker must first compromise via filesystem-level access. Pipeline should detect post-compromise information access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS processes reading /etc/passwd, config files, certificate stores, or other sensitive system files. Alert on unusual file copy/compression operations (tar, zip) immediately following successful exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Mechanism Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is an explicit defense-evasion and persistence technique not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation in FortiOS directories (typically /var/www, /etc/init.d, /opt/fortinet), particularly recursive symlinks or chains pointing outside expected paths. Cross-correlate with prior compromise events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Configuration/Certificate Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: 'Sensitive information' likely includes configuration, certificates, API keys. Pipeline should detect bulk reads/exports of config data during and after exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiOS config export functions (config export, firmware backup, certificate export) triggered without corresponding admin session or initiated by service accounts. Flag unusual destination IPs or large data transfers post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Pre-Patch Vulnerability Presence in Fleet
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV due-date enforcement: federal agencies must remediate by 2026-08-10. Pipeline should surface compliance gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily query against vulnerability scanner data and CMDB for FortiOS versions known vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag unpatched instances, especially those internet-facing. Surface in compliance dashboard with countdown to federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Asset Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Fortinet FortiOS' and specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10'—pipeline omitted asset-scanning UC entirely. Required baseline for all downstream detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Fortinet FortiOS instances via banner-grabbing or asset tags. Query vulnerability scanner for unpatched versions released before 2026-08-10. Alert on internet-facing instances without confirmed patches.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Exploitation: Crafted HTTP Request Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation via 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch'—pipeline generated zero exploitation-detection UC. This is the observable attack vector in active use (CISA KEV).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP patterns to FortiOS admin interfaces. Flag requests with malformed parameters, abnormal Content-Length, or known-bad payloads from published PoC code. Monitor for rapid-fire request sequences from single source attempting version/patch-state enumeration.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Post-Exploitation Information Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—pipeline missed T1005/T1041 data-collection and exfil phase entirely. Article implies HTTP channel for extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS outbound HTTP/HTTPS for bulk config or credential file transfers. Alert on large responses from FortiOS API endpoints queried with unusual privilege context. Baseline API call volume and flag anomalous read patterns targeting sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Chained Initial Compromise (Prerequisite Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—pipeline ignored the chained-compromise detection requirement. Required to detect campaign start.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious filesystem writes to FortiOS binary/library paths (/bin, /lib, /etc/config) with abnormal ownership or permissions. Correlate with brute-force attempts, exploit probes, or CVE signatures in same window to identify chained attack sequence.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch-Bypass and Symbolic Link Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes bypass of 'patch developed for symbolic link persistency mechanism'—no UC captures detection of symlink-based privilege escalation or patch circumvention specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation of symbolic links in system or config directories. Alert on processes following symlink chains to read protected files. Cross-reference patched/unpatched status from FortiOS auto-update logs against runtime behavior; flag instances claiming patch but exhibiting exploit-like filesystem activity.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Activity (Post-Compromise FortiOS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker exploiting 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a specific persistence technique after filesystem-level compromise. Absence of detection for this named technique is a critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS systems for suspicious symbolic link creation or modification in privileged directories (e.g., /etc, /usr/local/bin, system startup paths). Track symlink references pointing to unexpected locations or user-writable paths, especially post-exploitation scenarios where attacker has filesystem access.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Against FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploited 'via crafted HTTP requests' and describes bypassing 'patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Attacker-crafted HTTP payloads targeting FortiOS are the exploitation delivery mechanism and warrant network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to FortiOS administrative interfaces (typically port 443/8443) containing malformed, oversized, or anomalous payloads. Correlate with POST/PUT requests that precede file system activity on the same Fortinet device, especially within short time windows suggesting exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Sensitive Information Access (FortiOS CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' After successful exploitation and persistence, attacker activity should include data enumeration and exfiltration. Article implies confidentiality impact requiring detection of information-disclosure activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS systems, detect access to sensitive configuration files, credential stores, or system information repositories (e.g., /etc/passwd variants, FortiOS /data/config directories, API response logs). Correlate file reads with outbound network connections to non-Fortinet infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match + Patch Lag Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires federal patch by 2026-08-10 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline should generate asset-exposure hunt use case referencing CVE-2025-68686 to identify unpatched Fortinet FortiOS systems inventory-wide.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Fortinet FortiOS asset inventory against patch baseline for CVE-2025-68686 (patched versions TBD per Fortinet advisory). Flag any devices running unpatched versions. Prioritize exposed FortiOS instances (internet-facing) and high-trust network segments (management planes, data centers).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FortiOS Systems via Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `[../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure]`. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for unpatched or vulnerable FortiOS systems reporting CVE-2025-68686 exposure. CISA KEV implies active exploitation; flag all instances regardless of patch compliance timestamp, as patch lag is the documented attack prerequisite.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Bypass Symlink Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the exploitation vector post-initial compromise; must hunt for malformed request signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS admin interfaces (ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443) for anomalous payloads: oversized headers, nested path traversal sequences (../, ..\), percent-encoding abuse, or requests from IPs not in baseline admin group. Adversaries post-compromise will show distinct crafting patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem Access and Symlink Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' and references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Must detect filesystem operations enabling persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation/modification in FortiOS web-root and config directories (/tmp, /var/www, /etc/init.d, FortiGate appliance directories). Flag unexpected processes or UIDs initiating filesystem mutations. Correlate timing with HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Authentication Bypass Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker gaining 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access after initial filesystem compromise; implies authentication validation failure. Must detect access control bypass signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or under-authenticated access to FortiOS protected resources: successful requests lacking valid session tokens, repeated auth failures followed by successful access, or access from source IPs not in admin allowlist. Baseline normal admin patterns and flag behavioral anomalies post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Extraction from FortiOS Configuration and Secrets
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2025-68686 explicitly categorized as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Must hunt for exfiltration of configuration, credentials, certificates, and audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from FortiOS systems for anomalous data transfers: unusually large payloads, non-business hours extraction, or destinations outside corporate networks. Alert on recovery of configuration files, admin credential tables, TLS certificates, or system logs. Cross-correlate timing with initial exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Admin Console Anomalies Indicative of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Post-filesystem compromise and bypass, attacker operates via admin interface; article implies admin-level control. Must detect behavioral anomalies in admin actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiOS admin access (time-of-day, source IPs, operations, frequency). Alert on: off-hours logins, impossible travel, bulk configuration exports, password resets, admin account creation, policy modifications, or unusual report generation. Post-compromise adversaries pivot to reconnaissance and lateral-movement staging.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as recommended approach and notes CISA KEV = actively exploited. Asset discovery is foundational; article states attacker is 'remote unauthenticated' and attacks 'exposed assets.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances matching product/version scope of CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize by external exposure (firewall rules, network position) and patch status. Correlate with CISA due-date 2026-08-10 for urgency-ranked remediation list.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — key persistence indicator. Attackers use this after initial compromise to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for creation/modification of symbolic links in startup/daemon/library paths. Alert on symlinks pointing to user-writable or suspicious locations. Correlate with process execution and network access logs to identify post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the exploitation mechanism and explicit defense-evasion indicator mentioned in source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS HTTP access logs for request patterns targeting security/patch-related endpoints with malformed parameters, unusual header combinations, or path-traversal-like syntax. Flag requests that attempt to interact with known-vulnerable code paths after patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CVE is described as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' — the actual impact occurs after filesystem-level compromise. Requires detection of data access and egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem-level compromise indicators with subsequent bulk reads of FortiOS configuration, credential stores, or key material. Monitor outbound connections for data exfiltration patterns (size, destination reputation, timing).

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Attack Chain Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before CVE-2025-68686 exploitable — detection must link initial compromise to post-exploit phase. Kill-chain is incomplete without this correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build multi-stage correlation: (1) evidence of prior CVE exploitation or filesystem modification, (2) time-window, (3) subsequent crafted HTTP requests or symlink activity targeting this CVE. Alert on chain completion rather than isolated indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect Externally Exposed FortiOS Instances (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls this 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]'. This is the CISA KEV baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances reachable from untrusted networks via HTTP/HTTPS (ports 80, 443, 8080). Cross-reference with CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Flag unpatched systems exposed on internet-facing interfaces.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation occurs 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the patch. Pipeline missed HTTP-level attack surface detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS-facing HTTP/HTTPS traffic for request patterns consistent with symbolic-link traversal or privilege-bypass payloads. Baseline normal admin HTTP activity and alert on deviations targeting sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Persistence/Evasion Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is an explicit evasion/persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation/modification of symbolic links in privileged directories (/etc, /lib, /bin, /usr/lib) on FortiOS systems. Correlate with execution of symlink-creation tools (ln, ln -s) by Fortinet service accounts. Alert on symlinks pointing outside expected scope.

suggestion.title: Hunt for Prior Filesystem-Level Compromise (Two-Stage Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite attack chain is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiOS hosts, detect writes to privileged paths (/root, /etc, admin config dirs) followed by unexpected process execution or child-process spawning. Look for shells or interpreters invoked from anomalous write locations. Correlate timeline with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Detect Patch Bypass or Post-Patch Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'bypass [of] the patch.' This implies detection of attempts to circumvent patched systems or exploit via alternative techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP request patterns known to bypass the published patch (e.g., double-encoding, alternative path traversal vectors). Cross-check patch version from vulnerability scanner against actual HTTP behavior to identify instances where patch claims are false.

suggestion.title: Exposed IPMI/Redfish Service on UDP 623 (CVE-2013-4786)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Looking for publicly accessible IPMI services on UDP port 623' and identifies 36,872 internet-exposed hosts. CVE-2013-4786 is the root cause enabling offline password cracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to UDP port 623 from untrusted networks. Correlate with IPMI protocol signatures. Flag any public-routable infrastructure responding to IPMI discovery probes or authentication requests. High-risk if Supermicro or HPE BMC identified.

suggestion.title: Weak/Default BMC Credentials Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '6,240 of the hosts accepted an empty username' and '2,340 instances used weak administrator passwords that matched public dictionaries.' Supermicro factory passwords are 10-character uppercase printed on chassis labels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful BMC authentication with default usernames ('ADMIN', 'root', etc.) or empty usernames. Detect multiple failed IPMI authentication attempts followed by success. Monitor for authentication events using credentials matching known factory password patterns for Supermicro/HPE hardware.

suggestion.title: Offline Password Cracking of IPMI Auth Response (CVE-2013-4786)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'request an authentication response that can be used to crack the password offline using dedicated GPU rigs.' 24,650 servers leaked password-derived authentication material; estimated 1 day per response on M3 for HPE iLO.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IPMI authentication handshakes where challenge-response pairs are captured (RAKP protocol). Alert if a single source harvests multiple IPMI auth responses from different BMCs. Correlate exfiltration of auth captures with known password-cracking infrastructure or GPU cloud provisioning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BMC Lateral Movement and Pivot Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'a single compromised BMC could serve as a pivot point to the broader management plane' and 'recovered credentials may work across multiple management interfaces within the same environment.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BMC sessions accessing other management infrastructure (other BMCs, Redfish APIs, SNMP, Syslog servers). Flag cross-management-network lateral connections from a single BMC credential. Alert on API calls from BMC IPs to production network infrastructure.

suggestion.title: BMC Firmware Update or System Configuration Change Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes BMCs enable 'applying malicious firmware updates' and 'change low-level configurations' at a layer not monitored by security solutions. This is the primary impact of successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any firmware update initiated on a BMC outside of planned change windows. Flag unauthorized server power state changes, virtual media mount operations, or boot-order modifications from remote IPMI sessions. Baseline administrator actions and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Accessible HPE iLO or Supermicro Web Interface with Ransom Demand
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'an internet-exposed HPE iLO 4 login page displaying a ransom note demanding 0.3 BTC'—evidence of active exploitation in the wild and post-compromise asset defacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS access to BMC web interfaces from external IPs. Alert on unusual file uploads or content modifications to iLO or Supermicro web portals. Correlate with monitoring for defacement indicators (ransom notes, cryptocurrency addresses in text content).

suggestion.title: NightLedger Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'NightLedger' malware deployment. No execution detection UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NightLedger process spawning with suspicious command-line arguments or parent process anomalies. Correlate against known malware file hashes and execution paths.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle states victims are 'turned into covert relays'—implies outbound C2 relay traffic and lateral forwarding. No detection UC for relay behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify victim systems forwarding traffic on behalf of attacker (port forwarding, proxy behavior). Look for outbound connections to known Nimbus Manticore infrastructure and abnormal egress patterns from internal systems.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware named in title must establish persistence on victim systems for relay functionality. No persistence UC surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry/startup folder modifications, scheduled task creation, or service installation consistent with NightLedger persistence patterns. Cross-reference with malware family analysis.

suggestion.title: Relay Infrastructure Enumeration & Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article describes victims as 'covert relays'—implies attackers configuring victim systems for traffic forwarding. No UC for relay provisioning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution for network configuration (netsh, iptables, ipconfig, route commands) shortly after NightLedger installation. Monitor for suspicious port forwarding or proxy tool execution.

suggestion.title: NightLedger C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Covert relay deployment implies ongoing C2 communication to orchestrate relay behavior. No C2 beacon or checkin UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile C2 beacon traffic patterns (frequency, size, TLS certificate anomalies, known NightLedger domains/IPs). Detect abnormal encrypted traffic from newly compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Trojanized MeshAgent WebSocket C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'trojanized MeshAgent binary as their primary C2 mechanism...installed as a SYSTEM-level auto-start service, communicating over encrypted WebSocket (WSS) to an attacker-controlled server.' This is a specific, novel attacker pattern requiring behavior-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MeshAgent (meshagent.exe, meshcentral-agent) processes spawned with SYSTEM privileges outside legitimate MeshCentral deployment contexts. Correlate with outbound WebSocket (WSS on port 443 or non-standard) connections to suspicious IP space. Alert if MeshAgent registers as auto-start service (Registry: SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) without corresponding ServicePrincipalName or legitimate domain enrollment.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing via Trusted Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'compromised Microsoft 365 accounts to harvest credentials...auto-generated, victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct to adversary-controlled M365 credential harvesting pages.' UAT-11764 leverages trusted SharePoint for document hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with PDF attachments containing QR codes redirecting to /device_code or similar OAuth flows hosted on compromised Microsoft infrastructure (*.sharepoint.com, *.onedrive.com domains). Cross-reference recipient domain with sender to identify internal account compromise. Flag if QR destination leads to blank credential forms or custom M365 login replicas.

suggestion.title: Zoho Assist Unattended Agent Abuse Without User Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Warlock ransomware operators...deploying an installer for the RMM tool Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, which is designed to allow administrative remote control of an endpoint without a user logged in...enables the attackers to maintain persistent, stealthy, and unrestricted control.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Zoho Assist Unattended Agent installation (ZohoAssist.exe, ZohoAssistMsiInstaller) outside standard change management windows. Monitor for Zoho Assist establishing connections when no user is interactively logged in (SessionId 0 in Windows). Flag registry persistence mechanisms (SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) created by Zoho Assist post-install.

suggestion.title: ARToken PhaaS Device Code Authentication Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals: 'ARToken panel exposes 80+ API endpoints for device code phishing...phishing lures that impersonate trusted vendors and abuse legitimate Microsoft services, allowing attackers to bypass MFA through the OAuth device authorization flow.' Describes specific PhaaS capability and MFA-bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure AD logs for device code flow (grant_type=device_code) from atypical geographies or IPs. Correlate successful device code auth within 5 minutes of user receiving phishing template matching ARToken lures (vendor impersonation patterns). suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Manipulation — Post-Exploit Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as post-exploit vector. No persistence-layer detection UC generated despite this being a documented attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on filesystem operations within FortiOS config/binary directories that create or modify symbolic links, particularly in post-exploit timeline (after failed patch or initial compromise vector). Correlate with preceding privilege-escalation indicators.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Detection — Prerequisite Compromise + FortiOS Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline captures only single-stage T1190; missing detection for two-stage pattern (initial compromise + CVE-2025-68686).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem-level compromise attempts (e.g., file-write anomalies, unexpected process spawns in FortiOS directories, privilege escalation) with subsequent attempts to exploit CVE-2025-68686 via HTTP. Timeline delta <24h suggests coordinated attack chain.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration — FortiOS Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information' as impact. No data-exfiltration or command-and-control detection UC generated despite this being the attacker's goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large data transfers from compromised FortiOS instances to external IPs, especially encrypted channels (TLS/SSH) that bypass proxy inspection. Monitor for exfiltration of config files, admin credentials, or audit logs typical of FortiOS compromises.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'crafted HTTP requests'—foundational use case for any CISA KEV. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and patch status for FortiOS instances. Cross-reference vuln scanner output for CVE-2025-68686. High-risk: any instance not patched by 2026-08-10. Splunk: index=vuln cve=CVE-2025-68686 product=FortiOS | stats count by src_ip, patch_status. KQL: DeviceInfo | where OSVersion contains 'FortiOS' | join vulnerability_data on DeviceName where CVE == 'CVE-2025-68686'.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to FortiOS (CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'crafted HTTP requests' as exploit vector. Pipeline missed endpoint exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to FortiOS management interfaces containing payloads targeting symbolic link traversal or sensitive config exposure. Look for 400/403/500 errors in FortiOS logs correlating with unusual request patterns. Baseline normal admin traffic; alert on deviations. Splunk: index=firewall dest_port IN (80, 443, 8443) dest=*fortigate* uri IN (*api*, *admin*, *config*) status IN (400, 403, 500).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Access from FortiOS (Post-Compromise Behavior)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] patch' and 'may allow…exposure of sensitive information'—requires detection of data exfiltration post-exploitation. Pipeline generated zero post-exploitation hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS audit log entries showing unauthorized access to sensitive config files, credentials, or system state. Cross-correlate with outbound data flows of unusual size/frequency. Splunk: index=fortiOS_audit action=READ object IN (*password*, *config*, *key*, *secret*) user=! admin | stats count, bytes by user, object.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Exploitation Attempts on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'bypass of patch developed for symbolic link persistency mechanism'—specific persistence technique. Pipeline missed this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or access of symlinks in sensitive directories (e.g., config, temp, cache). Alert on attempts to create links pointing to sensitive files or on access via symlinks from unprivileged contexts. Splunk: index=fortiOS_audit event_type=file_operation operation IN (symlink_create, symlink_access) path IN (*config*, */tmp/*, */var/*).

suggestion.title: FortiOS Multi-Stage Compromise: Prior Vulnerability + CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—implies multi-stage kill chain. Pipeline failed to reconstruct this chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate recent patches/CVEs affecting FortiOS with exploitation of CVE-2025-68686. Flag instances showing signs of prior compromise (unusual process execution, unexpected service restarts, filesystem changes) followed by suspicious HTTP requests or sensitive data access. Multi-signal approach: look for both the staging compromise and the secondary exploit.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states this CVE is actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV tier). Requires asset enumeration of FortiOS products matching this CVE signature to drive remediation priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2025-68686 matches within the past 30 days. Cross-reference against patch management logs to identify devices claiming patch status but still flagged as vulnerable (patch lag scenario).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse Targeting Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'crafted HTTP requests' exploiting 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' to bypass patches. Requires filesystem monitoring at the FortiOS level for anomalous symlink creation in critical paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation events in FortiOS system directories (e.g., /etc, /lib, /usr) followed within 2 hours by HTTP 400/403 error spikes in FortiOS access logs. Correlate with processes running as system/root that typically do not create symlinks.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patterns to FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker must send 'crafted HTTP requests' to trigger the vulnerability. Requires detection of HTTP patterns consistent with symlink traversal exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS management interface containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ or encoded variants) or symbolic link references in query parameters, especially from unauthenticated or low-privilege sessions.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability may 'allow exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Requires detection of data flows from FortiOS after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal data volume egress from FortiOS appliances post-patching, particularly configuration exports or credential stores leaving via non-standard protocols. Baseline expected backup/config replication and alert on ≥3σ deviation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Chain: Filesystem Compromise → CVE-2025-68686 Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker must first 'have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Requires detection of multi-stage intrusion correlating initial filesystem access with downstream CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem-level compromise indicators (e.g., suspicious file modifications in /opt/fortinet, unauthorized process spawning) with subsequent HTTP requests bearing symlink traversal signatures within 6-hour windows to FortiOS management interface.

suggestion.title: IPMI Pre-Authentication Hash Disclosure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'IPMI password hashes [are disclosed] BEFORE login.' This is the core vulnerability—attacker retrieves hashes without authentication. Detection must flag IPMI RAKP authentication protocol responses to unauthenticated or failed-auth requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI protocol traffic (UDP 623, RPC ports 5900+) for authentication exchange messages (RAKP protocol) returned to clients that did not successfully authenticate. Flag sequences where password hashes or hash-like material appear in protocol responses before authentication completion; correlate with failed IPMI login attempts on same target.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed BMC Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 24,650 systematically discovered internet-exposed BMCs. This reflects reconnaissance-phase scanning activity targeting Intelligent Platform Management Interface services at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect widespread IPMI port/protocol scanning (UDP 623, GET_SESSION_CHALLENGE probes, IPMI v2 enumeration payloads) originating from single source across many targets. Baseline normal BMC discovery traffic per environment; flag anomalies in volume, source IP reputation, or scanning patterns that indicate external reconnaissance campaigns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Harvested IPMI Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Once attackers obtain IPMI password hashes (stated in article), the next phase is exploitation—using cracked credentials to access BMCs for lateral movement into host systems. Detect successful IPMI logins with previously-compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful IPMI authentications (LAN+ session creation, SOL Serial-Over-LAN session start) from sources not normally accessing that BMC, or from IPs associated with prior reconnaissance. Cross-reference against known leaked IPMI credential databases and password-crack timelines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BMC Command Execution or OS Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Compromised BMCs can execute commands on host systems via IPMI SOL (Serial Over LAN), power management, or direct firmware interfaces. Article's exposure of 24,650 BMCs implies attackers now have access vectors for command execution on underlying infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI SOL console session creation and activity logs for unexpected commands (shutdown, reboot, OS image mount, firmware updates). Flag SOL sessions that type shell commands, boot parameters, or interact with bootloaders. Correlate with host-side evidence of unexplained reboots or BIOS/firmware changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BMC Firmware or Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Confirmed BMC access enables persistence attacks—firmware rootkits, rogue admin accounts, or malicious scheduled tasks in BMC memory. This becomes a persistent backdoor bypassing OS-level security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on BMC firmware updates, reset operations, or administrative account creation/modification captured in IPMI event logs. Flag unexpected IPMI configuration changes (user permissions, access control lists, or network settings). Cross-correlate with timeline of known-compromised credential usage.

suggestion.title: Anomalous IPMI Account Activity or User Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention specific user enumeration, but the pre-auth hash disclosure implies attacker can extract or enumerate valid IPMI user accounts before login. Detect attacker probing for valid accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI for GET_USER_NAME or similar user enumeration probes sent to unauthenticated sessions. Flag rapid sequences of user lookups or failed authentication attempts using different usernames against the same BMC. Alert on IPMI traffic that leaks valid username lists or password hash responses prior to successful session establishment.

suggestion.title: Artifactory Repository Anomalous Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states zero-day was exploited against Artifactory; pipeline extracted no detection for abnormal repo enumeration, package downloads, or API authentication anomalies that would precede exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts followed by successful API calls to Artifactory REST endpoints (e.g., /api/artifactory/...) with abnormal frequency or bulk repository listing. Look for unauthenticated or low-privilege account accessing high-value model artifact repositories.

suggestion.title: Model Pipeline Exfiltration via Artifact Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OpenAI models exploited; pipeline missed detection for large ML model artifacts being packaged, compressed, or downloaded from trusted repositories outside normal CI/CD cadence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of .tar.gz, .zip, or .safetensors files >500 MB from Artifactory by non-CI/CD service accounts, or API calls downloading complete model repos instead of individual dependencies. Correlate with outbound network connections to non-whitelisted cloud storage.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Artifact Repository to Model Hosting Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions breach spanning both OpenAI and Hugging Face; pipeline did not reconstruct compromise chain or detect cross-platform credential reuse or shared authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to Hugging Face, GitHub, or model-hosting APIs using service account or session tokens originally issued for Artifactory access. Flag API key reuse across OpenAI and Hugging Face platforms in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Poisoning via Zero-Day Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article title references Artifactory zero-day; pipeline extracted no indicators for malicious patch deployment, compromised dependency injection, or tampered package signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifactory for unsigned or re-signed artifacts, package version rollbacks, or artifacts published outside normal deployment windows. Detect unexpected changes to Maven, npm, or Docker image metadata (e.g., build date misalignment, tampered checksums).

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Model Repository Structure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes breach requiring knowledge of model architectures and repository layout; pipeline missed enumeration-phase detection for directory listing, HEAD requests, or metadata scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP OPTIONS, GET on /api/repositories, /api/artifactory/repo/list, or similar endpoints from single source. Flag high volume of 404 responses followed by successful 200 responses on model artifact paths.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Model Training Pipeline Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states OpenAI models were exploited; pipeline failed to surface detections for training data ingestion from untrusted artifact sources or model weight injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python training scripts (e.g., train.py, fine_tune.py) loading model artifacts from Artifactory instead of first-party model APIs. Flag subprocess execution loading .pt or .safetensors files with timestamps misaligned to release cycles.

suggestion.title: Malformed DHCPv6 Packet Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'DHCPv6 Flaw' + 'Unauthenticated Attackers'—implies crafted packets trigger RCE. No detection generated for abnormal DHCPv6 message structure or protocol deviations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DHCPv6 traffic (UDP 547) with oversized payloads, malformed option encodings, invalid message types, or field values that violate RFC 8415. Prioritize packets from external/untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated DHCPv6 Service Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated Attackers'—no auth mechanism guards the vulnerable service. Pipeline missed detection for network reconnaissance of DHCPv6 endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound DHCPv6 requests (port 547) from external networks or unusual sources. Flag repeated DHCP Solicit/Request messages from a single source targeting multiple OpenWrt instances in rapid succession (scanning behavior).

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following DHCPv6 Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Run Code as Root'—pipeline ignored temporal correlation between network event (DHCPv6 packet) and privilege escalation (root process spawn).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound DHCPv6 activity (port 547) with subsequent child process creation under root context (uid=0). Alert if shell invocations (sh, bash, ash) or unexpected executables spawn within 5 seconds of DHCPv6 packet receipt on the same device.

suggestion.title: OpenWrt DHCPv6 Daemon Crash or Unhandled Exception
suggestion.rationale: DHCPv6 flaw likely triggers memory corruption, buffer overflow, or segfault. Article's 'Flaw' implies crash-based exploitation path—no detection for daemon restarts or abnormal termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DHCPv6-related daemon crashes, segmentation faults, or unexpected restarts (dnsmasq DHCP module, odhcpd). Alert on core dumps or kernel messages referencing DHCPv6 processing immediately following inbound traffic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious System Call Sequence from DHCPv6 Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE via network protocol implies shellcode injection or interpreter invocation. Pipeline missed syscall-level detection of fork/execve chains originating from DHCPv6 daemon privilege context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execve(), fork(), or clone() syscalls executed within the DHCPv6 daemon process context or inherited child processes. Flag setuid/setgid calls attempting privilege escalation within seconds of handling network traffic.

suggestion.title: Network-Sourced Command Execution on OpenWrt Device
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Unauthenticated'—attacker controls input entirely via network. Pipeline should detect commands/scripts executed as result of parsing untrusted DHCPv6 messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell command execution (sh -c, eval, etc.) initiated by network daemons or triggered by packet parsing logic. Monitor OpenWrt console/syslog for interactive shell spawning with no corresponding user login or SSH session.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Malware Execution and C2 Relay Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Deploys NightLedger and Turns Victim Systems Into Covert Relays'—this describes execution of malware that establishes proxy/relay infrastructure for command-and-control. No UC was generated for this core attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of NightLedger payloads and subsequent anomalous relay behavior: listening on non-standard ports, proxying traffic between external and internal hosts, or establishing persistent C2 beacons. Correlate process injection and DLL loading artifacts with outbound relay traffic.

suggestion.title: Persistence of Relay Infrastructure via Auto-Start Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article premise requires persistence across reboots to maintain 'victim systems' as 'covert relays.' No detection suggested for persistence establishment targeting relay functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Run/RunOnce registry hives, scheduled tasks, or WMI event subscriptions that launch relay processes on boot. Flag unsigned binaries or script-based persistence targeting system services used as relay proxies.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Relay Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'Turns Victim Systems Into Covert Relays' implies pivot infrastructure for lateral movement. No UC captures detection of relay abuse for post-breach propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify compromised relay hosts forwarding internal traffic or executing commands from external operators. Look for process execution originating from relay hosts that lack legitimate business context, or internal-to-internal connections routed through suspicious intermediaries.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing in PDF Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'employs auto-generated, victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct to adversary-controlled M365 credential harvesting pages.' Pipeline missed initial-access vector used in campaign affecting Australian organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email attachments (PDFs, images) containing embedded QR codes, especially those with abnormal entropy or layering. Cross-reference QR code destinations against malicious URL feeds. Alert on user-tailored PDFs from external senders directing to OAuth or credential-harvesting pages.

suggestion.title: Device Code Authentication for MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass MFA through the OAuth device authorization flow rather than stealing passwords' via ARToken PhaaS platform with 80+ API endpoints. Missing detection for legitimate-looking but anomalous device code flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or repeated device code authentication attempts from same user/tenant, especially those failing initial approval then succeeding. Alert on device code auth from IP geographies inconsistent with user baseline. Monitor for device code flows followed immediately by token issuance without MFA challenge.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized MeshAgent Service Installation as Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trojanized MeshAgent binary as their primary C2 mechanism... installed as a SYSTEM-level auto-start service, communicating over encrypted WebSocket (WSS).' Sinobi ransomware operators used this tool previously unattributed to the group.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshAgent (or MeshCentral agent component) installation as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM service, especially with unusual install paths or binaries not from official MeshCentral package repository. Alert on MeshAgent establishing WebSocket connections to non-standard ports or unrecognized C2 domains. Hunt for service auto-start entries referencing MeshAgent with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Zoho Assist Unattended Agent Deployment for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Warlock ransomware operators...deploying an installer for the RMM tool Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, which is designed to allow administrative remote control of an endpoint without a user logged in.' Warlock attribution not previously public for this tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation and execution of Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, particularly when parent process is unusual (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, msiexec from non-standard context). Alert on Zoho Assist establishing network connections to Zoho infrastructure from endpoints without prior administrative approvals or MDM enrollment records.

suggestion.title: GPO Logon Script Deployment for Ransomware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deployed the ransomware across the entire domain using a malicious Group Policy Object (GPO) logon script.' Sinobi operators used centralized GPO mechanism for rapid domain-wide encryption; suggests understanding of enterprise architecture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious GPO creation or modification, especially logon scripts with rare extensions (.ps1, .bat, .vbs) containing obfuscation or code injection patterns. Alert on unusual SYSVOL writes by service accounts. Detect script execution on large numbers of endpoints within short time window post-logon, especially scripts launching encryption tools or exfiltration utilities (rclone.exe).

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation for Email Exfiltration and Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creating email inbox rules for defense evasion' post-M365 compromise; UAT-11764 campaign used rules to sustain attack momentum. Observable indicator of post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rule creation by non-administrative accounts with auto-forwarding or delete actions targeting external domains or newly-created mail folders. Monitor for rapid rule creation post-credential compromise. Correlate with suspicious OAuth consent events or MFA bypass attempts within same account session window.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Unauthenticated RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'run OS commands without logging in' — this is T1190 exploitation requiring detection at initial_access phase via HTTP request analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to TeamCity endpoints (e.g., /app/rest/*, /buildConfiguration, /agent) originating from unauthenticated sessions that contain command/script payloads, shell metacharacters, or suspicious parameter values. Correlate failed auth (401) followed by successful requests (200) within seconds from same IP.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Service Account Spawning OS Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes capability to execute arbitrary OS commands — need execution-phase detection for child processes launched by TeamCity service with suspicious arguments or privilege elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned by TeamCity Java process (java.exe, teamcityd) with low-frequency or encoded arguments. Flag processes that immediately make network connections, access credential storage, or write to startup folders.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Privilege Escalation via Exploited RCE
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE without auth may allow attacker to escalate privileges if TeamCity runs in elevated context; pipeline missed privilege_escalation coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when TeamCity-spawned processes assume SYSTEM, ADMIN, or root context, or when they create scheduled tasks, Windows services, or sudo entries. Cross-reference with HTTP request logs to correlate timing with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: TeamCity Endpoint Reconnaissance/Fuzzing
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE implies exposed endpoint; should detect scanning patterns targeting known vulnerable paths or parameter enumeration from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid-fire HTTP requests to TeamCity API endpoints from single source IPs with high request volume, repeated 404→200 patterns, or Directory Traversal/SQLi/XXE payloads in query strings or request bodies.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Credential/Data Exfiltration from TeamCity
suggestion.rationale: Once RCE is achieved, attacker can exfiltrate build secrets, API tokens, SSH keys, or source code stored in TeamCity — exfiltration phase coverage absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected large outbound network connections from TeamCity processes to external/non-whitelisted IPs, especially concurrent with access to config directories (teamcity/config, .ssh, credentials stores) or high-volume file transfers.

suggestion.title: Detect Internet-Exposed FortiOS Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits public-facing FortiOS; asset exposure is the initial access vector (T1190 implies external accessibility). No baseline detection for FortiOS on public IPs or unexpected external access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for FortiOS appliances (identify via HTTP headers, SSL cert subjects, or SHODAN API) with public IP exposure. Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unauthorized internet-routable instances. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS responses from known FortiOS ports (80, 443, 8080, 10000) in untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'crafted HTTP requests' used to bypass the patch; this is the attack pattern. No detection logic for malformed/atypical HTTP requests to FortiOS admin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS admin console paths (/admin/, /api/, /upload/, /backup/) for abnormal method chains (POST to HEAD), parameter tampering (symlink bypass attempts), or request sizes significantly larger than baseline. Alert on 4xx response codes followed by 2xx or 3xx (sign of attempted bypass).

suggestion.title: Filesystem Symbolic Link Persistence on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Symbolic links are the persistence vector; no detection for suspicious symlink creation or traversal in FortiOS context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS configuration backup/restore operations and filesystem writes for symbolic link creation attempts targeting configuration directories (/etc/*, /root/*). Alert on anomalous symlink targets pointing outside expected paths. Cross-reference with patch status to identify systems with unpatched symbolic link handling.

suggestion.title: Failed or Bypassed FortiOS Security Patch Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active bypass of published patches; detection should identify systems where patches fail to apply or are actively circumvented, indicating in-the-wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS patch installation failures, rollbacks, or signature verification errors. Correlate patch application timestamps with anomalous HTTP requests or process behavior to identify potential patch bypass attempts. Monitor /sys/os/ and /sys/firmware/ for unauthorized modifications that would indicate patch corruption.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Information Access in FortiOS Sensitive Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'; post-compromise data access is the impact. No detection for unusual queries or exports of FortiOS secrets (VPN keys, admin credentials, routing tables).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for unusual configuration exports, debug dumps, or API calls to sensitive endpoints (/api/v2/cmdb/vpn.ipsec/*, /api/v2/cmdb/system/admin/). Alert on non-standard tool execution accessing /etc/passwd, certificate keystores, or pre-shared key storage. Track large data reads from restricted config sections.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article implies full system compromise enabling 'post-exploit cases'; compromised FortiOS becomes pivot point for internal network access. No detection for reconnaissance or lateral movement from FortiOS to internal assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from FortiOS to internal network subnets for anomalous destinations (file servers, domain controllers, databases). Alert on DNS queries from FortiOS to internal hostnames not normally contacted by appliance. Track VPN tunnel creation or route injection attempts that would tunnel attacker access through FortiOS into protected networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2025-68686 as the exploited vulnerability in CISA KEV. Pipeline should extract and map to scanner outputs. CISA KEV entries are only added when actively exploited in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all FortiOS instances detected with CVE-2025-68686 in vulnerability scans. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify missing patch evidence. Prioritize instances reachable from untrusted networks or public internet.

suggestion.title: Exposed FortiOS Public-Facing Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploits via crafted HTTP requests, indicating internet exposure. Pipeline should generate standard asset-exposure hunt for public-facing FortiOS appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate FortiOS management interfaces reachable on public internet (ports 443, 8443; vendor signatures). Correlate with internal asset registry to identify unmanaged/shadow instances. Verify patched versions.

suggestion.title: Patch-Bypass Crafted HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline completely missed the exploitation vector and defense-evasion layer targeting patched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin/API endpoints for anomalous HTTP patterns: malformed Content-Length, unusual User-Agent headers, polyglot payloads, or rapid requests targeting command/API endpoints (/api/sys/*, /api/conf/*, /api/shell). Flag post-patch exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline failed to map the persistence technique described in the post-exploit chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symbolic link creation in FortiOS config/script/binary directories. Inspect symlink targets for references to /tmp, /var/tmp, or paths outside canonical directories. Correlate with HTTP exploitation attempts or unauthenticated access logs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance — Federal Due Date 2026-08-10
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal remediation deadline. Pipeline should generate time-bound compliance hunt for CISA KEV enforcement tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate all FortiOS instances running patched/safe versions by 2026-08-10. Flag instances still vulnerable after due date as regulatory non-compliance. Track patch lag (days from vendor release to deployment) for outliers.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempts on Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker... via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests matching known CVE-2025-68686 exploit patterns against Fortinet FortiOS. Monitor for unusual HTTP request sequences, large payloads, or attempts to access /api or administrative endpoints from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistency Patch Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This is an explicit defense-evasion step the pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symbolic link creation attempts on FortiOS systems post-compromise, particularly in directories where persistency mechanisms reside. Monitor for filesystem changes attempting to recreate previously patched symlink-based persistence vectors.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Fortinet FortiOS Sensitive Information
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline should have mapped data access/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, attacker queries configuration databases, credential stores, or sensitive system files on FortiOS. Detect anomalous FortiOS API calls for config/credential retrieval, large data reads from /etc or /var directories, or unauthorized access to administrative interfaces by already-compromised processes.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage workflow (initial compromise → CVE-2025-68686) is a killchain the pipeline failed to reconstruct.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability-scan hits (initial compromise vector) with subsequent HTTP requests matching CVE-2025-68686 signatures within short time windows (same source IP, same target asset). Flag multi-stage exploitation chains against FortiOS.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker' + 'public-facing application' exposure. Pipeline must detect FortiOS systems reachable from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to Fortinet FortiOS management interfaces (TCP 443, 8443, 8080) from untrusted networks. Correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed FortiOS appliances lacking segmentation controls.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Detection Against FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'crafted HTTP requests' used to 'bypass the patch.' Must detect malformed or anomalous payloads targeting known FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request patterns to FortiOS (User-Agent spoofing, URL path traversal, oversized payloads, encoded/obfuscated parameters). Flag requests with null bytes, directory traversal attempts, or symbolic-link-related parameters.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistency Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Must detect filesystem manipulation after FortiOS is breached.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system for symlink/junction creation in sensitive directories (/etc, /bin, /system). Detect anomalous `ln -s` or filesystem redirection calls post-compromise, especially targeting startup locations.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Detection via HTTP Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed' via 'crafted HTTP requests.' Must surface requests that circumvent mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests using character encoding bypass (double URL encoding, UTF-8 evasion, case variation) or protocol manipulation against FortiOS endpoints previously patched for CVE-2025-68686. Flag use of alternative HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, TRACE) if restricted.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Privilege Escalation via Filesystem Symlinks
suggestion.rationale: Article: compromise 'via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' combined with 'symlink persistency.' Attacker uses symlinks to escalate or persist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of symlinks in high-privilege directories (e.g., pointing startup scripts to attacker-controlled locations). Correlate symlink creation timing with process elevation attempts or daemon restarts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Asset Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2025-68686 as the primary IOC. No detection case was generated for identifying vulnerable FortiOS versions in asset inventory before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query FortiOS asset inventory for versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 (versions prior to vendor patches). Cross-reference with CISA KEV due date (2026-08-10) to prioritise remediation. Alert on any detected vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch... via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection was generated for anomalous HTTP patterns targeting FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS management or API endpoints for crafted request patterns (oversized headers, malformed parameters, unusual request sequences). Flag attempts post-exploitation as they suggest lateral movement or persistence exploitation.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' No detection was generated for filesystem-level indicators of this persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation or modification in persistence-relevant directories (e.g., startup scripts, cron jobs, plugin directories). Correlate with prior compromise evidence or CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability allows attackers to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No detection addressed the mismatch between expected and actual patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS instances reporting successful patch installation for CVE-2025-68686 but exhibiting exploitation or symbolic link creation patterns. Indicates either failed patch validation or active bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker... [to] expose sensitive information.' No detection case was generated for post-compromise data access or exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for bulk file access, memory dumps, or config exports targeting sensitive data (credentials, certificates, VPN keys, traffic logs). Correlate with prior exploitation or filesystem compromise indicators. Flag egress of compressed archives or unusual outbound connections immediately post-access.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes this CVE is actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV). Article states 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors' — requires vulnerability scanner correlation against exposed FortiOS assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results reporting CVE-2025-68686 findings against internet-facing FortiOS systems. Cross-reference patch status with CISA KEV due date 2026-08-10. Alert on unpatched instances exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a persistence technique requiring filesystem monitoring after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symbolic link creation/modification in persistence-relevant paths (startup scripts, library paths, config directories). Alert on symlink targets pointing outside expected directories or to world-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This describes active exploitation attempts via HTTP anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FortiOS HTTP access logs with known CVE-2025-68686 exploitation POCs/signatures. Alert on malformed HTTP requests, unusual query parameters, or binary payloads targeting FortiOS administrative interfaces from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability classified as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' — implies post-compromise data disclosure. Article describes this occurs after 'first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for unusual outbound data transfers post-compromise indicators: large DNS query volumes from FortiOS systems, unexpected egress to public cloud storage IPs, or bulk data transfers in scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Exploitation Chain: Filesystem → HTTP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes prerequisite chain: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' followed by HTTP-based persistence bypass. This two-stage attack requires behavioral correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem modification events (symlink creation, file writes to startup paths) on FortiOS hosts within 5-30 minutes of subsequent HTTP requests containing known CVE-2025-68686 exploit signatures. Alert on pattern indicating staged compromise.

suggestion.title: Adobe Acrobat Extension Unauthorized Cross-Origin DOM Access
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'malicious sites read WhatsApp Web data'—indicates extension content script accessing DOM/sessionStorage across origins. Pipeline generated zero collection-phase UC despite this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adobe Acrobat extension process and injected content scripts for DOM queries against web.whatsapp.com, including sessionStorage/localStorage access, XMLHttpRequest to messaging domains, or postMessage communication with non-Adobe origins. Correlate with user visiting untrusted domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious Website Triggers Extension Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'malicious sites' and 'let malicious sites read' explicitly describe initial-access vector. No IOCs extracted, no initial-access UC created despite attack sequence starting here.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users with active Adobe Acrobat extension visiting known-malicious or suspicious domains, followed by anomalous extension process behavior or unexpected network communication. Alert on user navigation to domains known to host extension exploits.

suggestion.title: WhatsApp Web Session Hijacking via Extension Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: unauthorized access to WhatsApp Web conversations/metadata. Article describes reading 'WhatsApp Web data' implying session or credential theft, yet no exfiltration or credential-access UC present.
