suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exfiltration of WhatsApp Web authentication tokens, session cookies (e.g., wa_web_app_session), or message metadata to attacker infrastructure. Look for HTTPS POST requests from Adobe Acrobat extension context to non-WhatsApp, non-Adobe destinations carrying serialized session data.

suggestion.title: Browser Extension Manifest Permission Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: extension permissions allowing access beyond documented scope. Article indicates flaw in permission model but pipeline suggested zero UC for permission-abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser extension content scripts executing against origins not listed in extension manifest, or accessing sensitive APIs (e.g., storage, cookies) targeting messaging/communication platforms. Flag extensions requesting broad host permissions or wildcard patterns that exceed documented functionality.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Adobe Acrobat Extension Code Injection Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability implies code execution within extension sandbox or insufficient origin isolation. No execution-phase UC despite exploitation of client-side application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adobe Acrobat extension process for memory corruption indicators, abnormal code execution patterns, or injection of third-party scripts into extension context. Track vulnerable extension versions and alert on exploitation indicators such as extension crash reports or unexpected child process creation.

suggestion.title: Malicious DOM Manipulation in Browser Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes data being 'read' from WhatsApp Web—implies malicious JavaScript accessing and exfiltrating DOM/session objects. No defense-evasion or execution UC for in-browser payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injection or execution of malicious JavaScript within Adobe Acrobat extension context that queries DOM selectors for authentication tokens, message content, or user metadata. Monitor for eval(), Function(), or dynamic script injection patterns within extension background or content scripts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers bypass patch 'via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary exploitation vector; pipeline completely missed it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for anomalous HTTP requests with symbolic-link traversal patterns, unusual headers, or abnormal request sequencing. Correlate with HTTP 200/302 responses from FortiOS to external IPs post-exploitation timeframe. Flag any unauthenticated access to sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch Compliance & Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date 2026-08-10. Pipeline missed the compliance/inventory detection entirely despite this being canonical CISA KEV response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB or vulnerability scanner to enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS instances and compare installed versions against patched build numbers for CVE-2025-68686. Alert on any vulnerable instances still present after federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Symbolic Link Persistence Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—pipeline ignored this persistence indicator entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS host filesystem for suspicious symbolic link creation, especially targeting application binaries, shared libraries, or configuration directories. Alert on symlink creation followed by abnormal process execution or file modifications within the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Exposure / Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly defined as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline generated zero data-exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data flows from FortiOS instances containing credentials, configuration files, or backup archives destined for external IPs or untrusted networks. Correlate with prior exploitation attempts or symbolic link creation indicators to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack: Filesystem Compromise → CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline's empty kill-chain missed this two-stage attack pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem compromise signals (unexpected file ownership changes, binary modifications, privilege escalation attempts in FortiOS logs) occurring 6-48 hours before HTTP exploitation attempts matching CVE-2025-68686 patterns. Flag accounts or processes appearing in both phases.

suggestion.title: Authentication Failure Spike & Unauthorized Access Attempts to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploited by 'remote unauthenticated attacker' via HTTP; should generate detection for failed auth attempts and 401/403 response patterns even if exploitation initially fails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on spike in failed authentication or authorization failures to FortiOS management/application interfaces from external untrusted IPs. Combine with request-uri inspection for symlink traversal payloads (../, encoding variants) and suspicious User-Agent strings.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse in FortiOS Filesystem Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—the prior-patch attack vector this CVE bypasses. Symlink creation/abuse is the persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation in /tmp, /var/tmp, or configuration directories. Alert on symlinks pointing to binaries or libraries outside their expected locations. Correlate with process execution originating from those directories.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' post-filesystem-compromise to bypass the patched symlink mechanism. Network-level detection of malformed or traversal-indicative HTTP traffic is necessary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS admin or API endpoints containing path-traversal payloads (../, encoded variants, null bytes, unicode escapes). Establish baseline of legitimate management client user-agents and IPs; alert on deviations paired with suspicious request bodies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Read Access to FortiOS Sensitive Configuration
suggestion.rationale: CVE enables 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—detection must identify file-read patterns on credential stores, config databases, and policy files by unauthorized or anomalous sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for high-volume or sequential reads of /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow equivalents, policy configuration files, or VPN credential stores. Alert on reads outside administrative baselines. Correlate with network exfiltration or data staging.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Coverage Inventory for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal patch by 2026-08-10. Asset-exposure hunt must confirm patched status across all FortiOS instances, prioritizing externally-facing appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all FortiOS appliances for version and patch level via API or direct scan. Flag unpatched instances. Cross-reference with external IP exposure (public DNS, shodan, internet scans). Alert on unpatched + internet-facing + high-risk network zones.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Correlation: Filesystem Compromise Followed by HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates prior 'compromise via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before CVE-2025-68686 is usable. Detection must correlate initial compromise signals with subsequent HTTP-based bypass attempts on same target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of FortiOS exploitation attempts (failed RCEs, command injections, other CVE exploitation). Alert on timelines where initial-access indicators occur within 24–72 hours of crafted HTTP requests or symlink filesystem artifacts targeting the same appliance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Session Access to FortiOS Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: CVE enables 'remote unauthenticated attacker' access post-filesystem-compromise; detection should surface authentication bypass or missing-token patterns in FortiOS HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiOS /api/, /admin/, or /config endpoints lacking valid session tokens, cookies, or authentication headers. Flag sequences of auth-failure logs followed by successful requests from the same source IP within minutes.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation or Modification on FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence method the patch was designed to prevent. This is a clear post-compromise persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS file system logs and system calls for creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (e.g., startup paths, library paths). Anomalous symlinks in post-compromise contexts are a strong persistence indicator after initial compromise via separate vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Bypassing FortiOS Patches
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' This describes the exploitation vector post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with unusual payload patterns, encoding, or parameter manipulation targeting FortiOS endpoints, especially those that deviate from typical administrative or user workflows. Correlate with file system activity indicating symbolic link operations.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Systems Already Compromised via Secondary Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This is the preceding attack stage that enables the CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances that show signs of prior compromise or exploitation (authentication anomalies, unexpected filesystem modifications, presence of known FortiOS exploit artifacts). These are prerequisites for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation and indicate active adversary presence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Version Detection and Lag Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'patch developed for' the persistence mechanism and a federal due date of 2026-08-10. Gap between patch release and applied versions indicates exploitation risk window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference FortiOS device inventory against patch release dates. Flag systems still running unpatched or older versions of FortiOS after the federal remediation deadline. Prioritize systems that have been compromised before (as they are confirmed targets).

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Attempts on FortiOS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'bypass the patch developed for' the vulnerability. This implies attackers testing or exploiting the gap between older and patched versions, or attempting to circumvent patch mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests or commands that attempt to interact with or manipulate the symbolic link persistence mechanism after patches are applied. Look for failed exploitation attempts or requests using obsolete exploitation paths.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—this is the primary persistence vector and requires filesystem-level monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (e.g., /bin, /etc, /var/lib). Correlate with filesystem audit logs showing unusual link creation by processes running as root or fortimanager service accounts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—requires HTTP anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS with abnormal headers, payloads, or encoding patterns that bypass authentication or patch detection. Monitor for requests that attempt to manipulate symbolic link paths or trigger the disclosed bypass.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem-Level Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—requires baseline detection of initial filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate FortiOS filesystem modifications. Alert on unexpected changes to binaries, libraries, or configuration files—particularly in /opt/fortinet, /bin, /lib directories. Cross-reference with exploit database for known FortiOS filesystem-level vulnerabilities.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Application Verification
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-08-10 and article describes 'bypass the patch'—requires verification that patches are deployed and effective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all FortiOS instances for patch application status. For patched systems, verify patch integrity and monitor for rollback. For unpatched systems after federal due date, escalate to high priority. Cross-check patch application timestamps against known exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FortiOS Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' accessing system post-compromise—monitor for authentication bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to FortiOS admin interfaces, API endpoints, or management ports without corresponding authentication logs. Flag sessions that appear unauthenticated yet perform administrative actions. Monitor for rapid-fire failed auth attempts followed by successful access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FortiOS Systems Inventory (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited.' Pipeline generated no inventory/scanning use case. Title/body CVE mismatch (CVE-2025-24472 vs CVE-2025-68686) also unresolved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all FortiOS/FortiProxy instances not patched for CVE-2025-68686 by federal due date 2026-08-10. Query asset inventory and scanner results for version < patch baseline. Prioritize internet-facing instances and correlate against network exposure scans.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as documented attack behavior. No persistence detection use case generated despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for symlink creation/modification in FortiOS system paths (e.g., /etc/rc.d, /etc/init.d, cron.d). Baseline legitimate symlinks and alert on post-compromise anomalies. Cross-correlate with filesystem access logs and HTTP request timing.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection for malformed/anomalous HTTP payloads targeting patched endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP patterns to FortiOS endpoints pre-patch deployment. Post-patch, alert on requests with unusual encoding, oversized parameters, malformed headers, or double-encoding targeting symlink-related functions. Correlate with 403/bypass error responses.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability classified as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' but no collection/exfiltration detection generated. Article implies data access after filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After filesystem-level compromise detected, alert on anomalous access to FortiOS config files, certificate stores, credential vaults. Monitor egress for bulk data transfer or connections to external IPs from compromised FortiOS instances.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Timeline Violation Post Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-08-10. No temporal hunt for systems remaining unpatched beyond deadline, when exploitation risk escalates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FortiOS system still vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686 after 2026-08-10. Correlate patch-deployment logs with asset inventory. Alert on unpatched systems with internet exposure or access from untrusted networks post-deadline.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reversion to Malicious Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker deleting original tags and re-pointing release tags to orphaned malicious commit: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' Pipeline missed this defense-evasion pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository tag modifications on critical/popular Actions. Alert when tags are moved to commits not on main/release branches, especially if commit shas differ from prior tag points. Cross-correlate with repo write-access logs to identify suspicious privilege use.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker created orphaned commits to obfuscate the attack: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch These factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.' Pipeline captured no defense-evasion detection for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits reachable via commit SHA but not reachable from any branch HEAD in repositories with ≥1k stars or ≥100 watchers. Flag if commit authored by account with write permissions but commit never merged to main or released via tag.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secrets Exposed in Plaintext Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this high-impact credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs (especially public repos) for patterns matching GitHub secret format (starts with gh[opsu]_ prefix). Cross-correlate with commits that modify Actions workflow YAML or step output handling. Alert if plaintext secrets detected within 24 hours of unexpected repository code changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attack relied on external network calls that enabled discovery: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Zero network-based detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-canonical CI/CD infrastructure domains. Baseline expected artifact repositories per org, alert on calls to unfamiliar or single-use domains, especially with large payload downloads or POST exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Write-Access Abuse on High-Profile GitHub Actions Repository
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: attacker exploited write privileges on repo with 23k downstream dependents. Article notes: 'the bottom line is that a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Pipeline never surfaced the account-compromise or privilege-abuse angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For repositories tagged as GitHub Actions / widely-used packages, alert on new or unusual user push events, especially commits that introduce external network calls, modify action.yml entry-points, or access repository secrets environment variables. Require secondary approval for deployments to tags on high-impact repos.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Reachability via Tag or Release Asset
suggestion.rationale: Attacker exploited GitHub's permissiveness: orphaned commits remain accessible via SHA and can be re-tagged. Article demonstrates: 'You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch.' Detection gap on persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For public repositories, monitor API calls resolving commits to tag/branch associations. Flag cases where a release tag points to a commit SHA with no branch ancestry or where branch deletion is followed within 24h by tag creation pointing to previously-branched commit SHA.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt (Windmill)
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'arbitrary server files' access without auth. Pipeline missed mapping this to path traversal patterns. Phrase: 'Read Arbitrary Server Files Without Authentication' implies directory traversal or path-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for Windmill endpoints receiving path traversal payloads ('../', '..\', '%2e%2e', Unicode equivalents) in URI or query parameters. Alert on sequences combining directory-traversal syntax with file-read operations (e.g., /api/read?path=../../../etc/passwd).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Access to Windmill APIs
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Without Authentication.' Pipeline failed to surface detection for unauthenticated calls to protected endpoints. Core attack prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to known Windmill file-read or resource-access endpoints (e.g., /api/scripts/*, /api/resources/*) that lack valid authentication tokens, API keys, or session cookies. Correlate with HTTP 200 or 206 responses indicating successful unauthorized access.

suggestion.title: Bulk or Sequential File Read Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file-read vulnerabilities are typically weaponized through enumeration: attacker probes /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, config files, secrets. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection. Phrase: 'arbitrary server files' implies attacker can request unknown/multiple files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of HTTP requests from a single source to Windmill file endpoints requesting progressively sensitive paths (e.g., requests for /api/files?path=config.yaml, then secrets.json, then .env, all within minutes). Flag if response sizes or HTTP 200 counts exceed baseline for anonymous/untrusted users.

suggestion.title: Windmill Version Disclosure or CVE Probing
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted; pipeline should have identified version-specific indicators or CVE reference if present. Attackers typically confirm vulnerability via version header or endpoint response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from Windmill services for version disclosure in Server headers (e.g., 'Windmill/1.x.x'). Alert if versions match known-vulnerable ranges. Also detect probing for CVE-specific endpoints (e.g., requests to deprecated or previously-vulnerable API paths).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of System Configuration or Credentials via File Read
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows reading arbitrary files without auth; implies access to /etc/passwd, config files with embedded credentials, .env, or secrets. Pipeline had zero impact/exfiltration mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Windmill file-read requests targeting known secret locations (e.g., paths containing 'secret', 'config', 'password', 'api_key', '.env', '/etc/') with outbound DNS or HTTP exfiltration. Alert if file contents are echoed in HTTP response bodies or sent to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Windmill Service Compromise via Unauthenticated API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: If arbitrary file read allows access to workflow definitions, scripts, or API keys, attacker can pivot to service manipulation or lateral movement. Pipeline missed this secondary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After unauthenticated file reads, detect modifications to Windmill workflows, job definitions, or stored scripts without corresponding authenticated API calls. Alert on creation of new workflows or jobs immediately following high-volume unauthorized file access from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary exploitation vector for an actively exploited KEV and requires immediate detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for anomalous HTTP requests targeting symbolic link bypass patterns. Establish baseline for normal admin/API traffic and alert on deviations, particularly requests with path traversal sequences, repeated 404→403→200 patterns, or symlink-related error codes.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline missed the persistence layer entirely. This is the foothold mechanism that requires post-exploitation monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected symlink creation in FortiOS startup directories, initialization scripts, or application bootstrap paths. Prioritize symlinks created immediately after suspicious access patterns or within documented exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploitation Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline ignored this chaining requirement—detect the initial filesystem-level compromise that enables the symlink bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate evidence of filesystem-level compromise (file permission changes, unusual access patterns, privilege elevation) with subsequent exploitation attempts. Look for time sequencing where filesystem access precedes HTTP-based bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Public Exposure Baseline
suggestion.rationale: KEV status implies active in-the-wild exploitation against exposed assets. Article mentions 'remote unauthenticated attacker' requiring internet-facing instances. Standard asset-exposure hunt completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiOS instances with public IP addresses or resolvable DNS names. Cross-reference with patch management system to identify unpatched instances before federal due date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass Attempts Post-Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' Post-patch, sophisticated attackers will attempt circumvention. Requires post-deployment detection to catch targeted attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After patch application, monitor for HTTP requests using known edge-case bypass techniques: race conditions on symlink operations, timing windows, or request patterns similar to pre-patch exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline failed to extract this primary IOC and detection driver.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner outputs and asset management systems for FortiOS instances reporting CVE-2025-68686 as unpatched. Cross-reference with device inventory to establish affected appliance locations, versions, and exposure dates.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Indicators on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack exploits 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Pipeline missed this core persistence vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories and web-accessible paths for suspicious symbolic links pointing to sensitive configuration or authentication files. Flag symbolic link creation events following evidence of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Patch Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'bypass the patch...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is a specific exploitation technique requiring HTTP traffic inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for malformed or anomalous request patterns targeting authentication endpoints or patch-related URI paths post-patch deployment. Look for repeated 4xx/5xx responses followed by authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation FortiOS Filesystem Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Defenders must hunt for signs of prior compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem modification events on FortiOS appliances with HTTP request anomalies or authentication failures. Flag unexpected changes to configuration files, web directories, or system binaries that predate patch deployment by hours/days.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Product Inventory and Exposure Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies widespread FortiOS deployment requiring rapid inventory validation. Pipeline should have generated asset-hunt use case per CISA KEV guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS appliances in the environment via asset inventory, banner-grabbing, and certificate transparency logs. Validate patch status and internet accessibility to prioritize remediation for public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 in Vulnerability Scans
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline produced zero use cases; article is CISA KEV (actively exploited) requiring immediate asset hunt. Article states 'CISA KEV only adds CVEs observed exploited in the wild' and 'Federal civilian agencies required to remediate by due date 2026-08-10'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2025-68686 on Fortinet FortiOS appliances. Prioritize Internet-exposed instances and cross-check patch dates to identify systems lagging remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers exploit 'via crafted HTTP requests' to an unauthenticated endpoint. Pipeline missed this initial-access vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with anomalous payloads, excessive special characters, or malformed headers targeting FortiOS appliance paths (e.g., /api/, /admin/, /upload). Correlate with known-exploited FortiOS version identifiers.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Creation on FortiOS Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in post-exploit cases'—this is persistence behavior the pipeline completely ignored. Maps to T1547 or T1574 family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem logs and FIM for unexpected symlink creation in config/startup/library directories. Symbolic links post-exploitation often redirect critical files to attacker-controlled paths to maintain access.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access Attempts to FortiOS Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit'—indicates auth bypass or unauthenticated interface exposure. Pipeline missed auth-related detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiOS admin interface (e.g., 200/302 responses without prior login session). Baseline known-good admin IP ranges and flag requests from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Detect Information Disclosure from FortiOS Config Dumps
suggestion.rationale: CVE classified as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to Unauthorized Actor'—pipeline did not map to collection/exfiltration phases. Article suggests attacker can read config files post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for bulk read operations on FortiOS configuration files (/etc/config/, /data/config/) especially from non-admin processes or during off-hours. Flag any config exports or data staging activities in temp directories.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline output included no compliance-oriented detection. Required for audit/regulator query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously track FortiOS appliance versions against known-vulnerable build numbers for CVE-2025-68686. Flag any instances running unpatched versions and cross-reference patch dates to 2026-08-10 deadline for escalation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states this CVE is 'observed exploited in the wild' (CISA KEV criterion). Scanners will flag FortiOS assets vulnerable to this. Missing from pipeline entirely despite being the primary IOC vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) detecting CVE-2025-68686 in FortiOS instances. Cross-reference asset inventory to confirm exposure scope and patch status.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the exploitation vector: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases, via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed this execution-phase activity entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiOS admin ports (443, 10443). Flag requests with unusual User-Agent strings, malformed query parameters, or requests targeting admin endpoints from unexpected source IPs or geographies.

suggestion.title: Symlink Persistence Detection in FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' exploited post-compromise. This is filesystem-level persistence activity that should trigger collection hunting: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symbolic link creation or modification in FortiOS system directories (e.g., /root, /etc/config). Alert on symlinks pointing outside expected system paths or to suspicious locations, especially if paired with HTTP exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Initial Compromise Detection — Secondary Vulnerability (Unknown)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability.' Pipeline should flag this as a detection gap: the primary entry point is unspecified, but any FortiOS system showing signs of compromise (process anomalies, config changes, unexpected authentication events) warrants immediate forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual FortiOS login patterns (failed auth spikes, logins from new IPs, root access outside change windows), unexpected config file modifications, or process spawning anomalies that predate CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Check — CVE-2025-68686 Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10.' Regulatory/compliance detection case missed entirely. Organizations will be audited on remediation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for FortiOS instances and verify patch version is ≥ remediation level by 2026-08-10. Flag any assets with patch age exceeding 7 days post-due-date; escalate to CISO.

suggestion.title: Information Disclosure Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline should hunt for data exfiltration patterns post-exploitation: unusual egress traffic, config file reads, credential store access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk reads of FortiOS config files (/etc/config/fgt*), access to credential stores, or large outbound transfers from FortiOS systems immediately after detection of HTTP anomalies or symlink creation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch... via crafted HTTP requests'—primary exploitation vector that must be detected in real-time against unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS administrative/API endpoints for abnormal HTTP request patterns: malformed payloads, unusual URI sequences, or rapid retry attempts targeting admin portals. Correlate requests against system patch status; alert if unpatched FortiOS instances receive exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the core post-exploitation tactic: attackers 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—requires filesystem integrity and process monitoring on compromised systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS instances, detect creation/modification of symbolic links in security-sensitive directories (config, scripts, lib paths). Alert when links bypass restrictive permissions or point to writable locations exploitable by FortiOS daemon processes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' as the vulnerability impact. Detection requires behavioral baselining of data movement from FortiOS to external networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unpatched FortiOS instances for unusual outbound traffic following exploitation indicators: unexpected port/protocol combinations, bulk data transfers to non-Fortinet infrastructure, or exfiltration to external IPs outside normal baselines.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Patch Status and Remediation Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline 2026-08-10 and KEV status confirms active in-the-wild exploitation. Vulnerable-system inventory is foundational before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Fortinet FortiOS deployments in scope; verify each system running patched code post-July 27, 2026 release. Flag systems still vulnerable; cross-reference with IDS/proxy logs to detect exploitation attempts against unpatched instances, prioritizing remediation by deadline.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Asset Inventory and Patch Gap Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation in wild (CISA KEV) with federal patch due 2026-08-10. No asset discovery hunt provided. Phrase: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset management systems for Fortinet FortiOS instances running vulnerable versions (prior to the version containing the symbolic link persistency bypass patch). Flag any unpatched instances given active exploitation in the wild and federal remediation timeline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Symbolic Link Creation on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is an explicit persistence mechanism that must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS systems for unexpected symbolic link creation in system directories (e.g., /var/run, startup folders, scheduled task directories). Correlate with prior evidence of filesystem-level compromise. Symbolic links in unexpected locations on FortiOS are strong indicators of post-exploitation persistence.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS Bypass Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline missed HTTP-layer detection entirely. This is the exploitation vector for the bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiOS web logs and WAF logs for malformed or anomalous HTTP requests targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Look for request patterns attempting to bypass path validation or input sanitization (e.g., double-encoded paths, null byte injection, symbolic link traversal attempts). Baseline normal FortiOS admin traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Access to Compromised FortiOS Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article prerequisite: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This multi-stage attack requires detection of the first-stage compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected local shell access, process spawning, or file modifications on FortiOS appliances. Correlate filesystem-level activity (e.g., unusual write access to config directories, binary modification, library injection) with subsequent HTTP activity or symbolic link creation. Filesystem compromise is the prerequisite for CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Output for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability tracking. Article identifies specific CVE identifier requiring scanner correlation and post-scan manual verification given patch bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2025-68686 (Fortinet FortiOS). Perform manual verification on flagged assets: confirm patch status, check for evidence of exploitation attempts in logs, verify no suspicious persistence mechanisms have been installed. Given active exploitation, treat scanner findings as high-priority and validate manually rather than relying on vendor patch status alone.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'via crafted HTTP requests' bypasses patch; this is the core attack vector and requires detection of anomalous HTTP patterns targeting Fortinet management or API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Fortinet FortiOS systems for patterns consistent with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation (crafted payloads, specific URI patterns, or abnormal request sequences). Alert on attempts to bypass existing patches or access sensitive endpoints without proper authentication.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies vulnerability scanning should identify unpatched systems; pipeline template references asset-exposure hunt with version checking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check vulnerability scanner results for FortiOS systems with known-exploited status of CVE-2025-68686. Flag systems running affected versions prior to federal due date (2026-08-10) for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Activity on Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level,' indicating this is a second-stage attack requiring detection of post-compromise persistence or lateral movement on already-breached appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for signs of pre-existing compromise (unauthorized admin accounts, modified system files, suspicious scheduled tasks) on Fortinet appliances. This CVE is exploited post-breach, so pair with prior-compromise indicators before triggering the HTTP-based exploit.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exposure from Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is categorized as 'exposure of sensitive information'; detection should monitor for data exfiltration attempts or unauthorized access to configuration/credential stores following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet appliance logs and network traffic for unauthorized access to sensitive data stores (configuration files, certificates, VPN keys). Alert on data reads followed by unusual outbound connections.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article directly cites CVE-2025-68686 as the vulnerability and states CISA KEV entries are actively exploited. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite explicit CVE mention. Standard asset inventory hunt against vulnerability scanner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for FortiOS appliances (vendor:Fortinet product:FortiOS) in vulnerability scanner results with CVE-2025-68686 flagged as 'exploitable' or patch status older than 2026-08-10 (federal due date). Cross-reference with network ingress logs to identify exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Bypass via Crafted HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'bypass[ing] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline reconstructed zero kill-chain phases despite this explicit attack step, missing detection for post-compromise persistence evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP request logs for anomalous payloads or request patterns targeting config/persistence paths. Cross-correlate with file integrity monitoring for symbolic link creation/modification on FortiOS filesystems, especially post-authentication or in privileged contexts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' after filesystem compromise. Pipeline assigned zero techniques for data collection/exfiltration, missing the adversary's objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthorized reads of sensitive FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, or authentication material post-compromise. Look for access to /etc/passwd, SSL key directories, or admin credential storage paths following lateral movement or privilege escalation on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated FortiOS HTTP Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch,' suggesting access control bypass. Pipeline produced no detection for unauthenticated access to protected endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS management/API endpoints from non-whitelisted IPs with missing or invalid authentication credentials. Correlate request patterns with known FortiOS admin console URIs and look for repeated failed auth followed by successful unauthenticated bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Compromise Chain: Pre-Exploit Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability,' implying a two-stage kill chain. Pipeline produced zero phases and thus missed the foundational compromise step that enables the CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Prioritize FortiOS instances with multiple unpatched vulnerabilities or signs of prior compromise (unusual process execution, unexpected outbound traffic, config drift). Use this to identify high-risk hosts where CVE-2025-68686 exploitation is more likely to succeed.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Public-Facing Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes T1190 via 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and 'public-facing application' context. Pipeline generated no asset-inventory or exposure detection use case despite CISA KEV urgency (patch due 2026-08-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Fortinet FortiOS instances exposed to untrusted networks (public IPs, DMZ, VPN frontends) with CVE-2025-68686 vulnerability scanner feeds. Prioritize instances unpatched as of 2026-08-10 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a distinct persistence layer (T1547.004 / T1574.008) with no corresponding detection use case in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS for symbolic link creation in application / library directories post-exploitation. Correlate filesystem events with failed HTTP exploit attempts. Symlinks to attacker-controlled binaries or configs post-compromise indicate persistence establishment.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Exploit Request Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly named: 'via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated no HTTP-layer detection use case despite this being the initial access mechanism to public-facing FortiOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP request patterns to FortiOS admin / API interfaces. Flag anomalous requests with path traversal, symbolic link escapes, or payload patterns matching known CVE-2025-68686 PoCs once disclosed.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation status requires mandatory patch tracking. Article includes federal patch due date (2026-08-10). No vulnerability management use case generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily correlation: identify Fortinet FortiOS instances with CVE-2025-68686 vulnerable signatures. Alert on instances exceeding patch SLA. Cross-reference with federal compliance schedules.

suggestion.title: Two-Stage Exploit Prerequisite Detection (Filesystem Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This prerequisite suggests reconnaissance, version probing, or lateral movement from prior compromise—no detection use case exists for the setup phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for automated or repeated queries to FortiOS endpoints disclosing version, build, patch status (e.g., diagnostics, /api/v2/cmdb/system/status). Detect scanning patterns preceding exploitation attempts; correlate with internal reconnaissance behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Post-Install Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Compromised npm Packages: @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts Ship an Obfuscated Remote Access Trojan' — pipeline extracted zero IOCs for these package names despite them being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/require operations on @joyfill/components or @joyfill/layouts followed within seconds by unexpected outbound network connections (non-npm registry) from Node.js process. Monitor for connections to non-standard ports or residential IP ranges post-installation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution from Node Modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Obfuscated Remote Access Trojan' — detection should target obfuscated code patterns within node_modules to catch similar payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js executing JavaScript files from node_modules containing characteristics of obfuscated code (high entropy strings, excessive bracket nesting, variable names as hex/unicode escapes, or known deobfuscation tool usage). Correlate with module load events from suspicious packages.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from npm Package Runtime Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT capability implies remote command and control; article lacks specifics but detection should cover C2 patterns from Node.js child processes spawned by npm module initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect persistent outbound connections (TCP/HTTPS) initiated by Node.js processes loading from compromised packages, with regularity suggesting heartbeat or command polling. Look for DNS queries to newly-registered domains (< 7 days old) or IPs with no legitimate npm CDN association.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing or Code Injection from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: RAT functionality often includes process injection to maintain persistence and evade detection; no injection techniques were mapped despite RAT classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process relationships where Node.js spawns unexpected child processes (especially system utilities like powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or svchost.exe) with code injection indicators (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory API calls or equivalent). Flag mismatches between module declared dependencies and spawned processes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomalies and Rapid Version Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often rely on typosquatting or hijacking existing packages; no behavioral detection on package repository patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag packages with abrupt ownership changes, unusual version bumps without changelog, or publish patterns deviating from historical cadence. Correlate compromised package publish timestamp against known breach disclosure dates to identify compromise window.

suggestion.title: New authenticated session from IP mismatch post-redirect injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IdP to redirect the victim's authorization code to an attacker' — attacker now possesses valid auth code and can initiate authenticated sessions. Pipeline missed detection of new successful login for victim user from previously-unseen IP within 1h of failed redirect attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication for user U from IP not in 90-day baseline, within 1 hour of ErrorCode=50011 (redirect mismatch) logged for same user. Increase severity if IP is anonymized, foreign geography, or accesses high-privilege resources within 30min.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated OIDC/SAML endpoint fuzzing with multiple Host header values
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' — initial reconnaissance/injection attempts target Poweradmin auth endpoints. Pipeline missed detection combining: repeated unauthenticated requests to */oidc/*, */saml/*, */logout* from single IP + multiple distinct Host header values in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag 3+ unauthenticated requests to Poweradmin auth endpoints (*/oidc/*, */saml/*, */logout*) from single source IP within 10min window, with 2+ distinct Host header values present. Correlate with 301/302 redirect responses to confirm injection attempt.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation / sensitive app access immediately post-token theft
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains victim's credential via stolen token. Compromise detection post-theft requires detecting victim's account used for high-risk operations (Graph API, SharePoint, Teams, Azure AD Graph) from anomalous IP within narrow token-lifetime window (~1h).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user resource access to high-value targets (msgraph.microsoft.com, SharePoint, Exchange, AAD Graph) from IP cluster not in user's 90-day baseline within 30min of correlated signals (failed redirect + new anomalous session). Flag especially: consent grants, service principal creation, forwarding rules, app registration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated IPMI Hash Extraction Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Disclose IPMI Password Hashes Before Login.' Hash material is retrievable without authentication via RAKP phase 2 capture or similar IPMI protocol mechanics, enabling offline cracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI service port 623 for unauthenticated RAKP or authentication requests that return hash material. Detect IPMI protocol handshakes that leak credential hashes (bcrypt, MD5, or salted formats) in response frames. Correlate with external source IPs to identify reconnaissance of exposed BMCs.

suggestion.title: Port 623 IPMI Exposure and Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '24,650 Internet-Exposed BMCs'—massive surface of IPMI port 623 open to public internet. Detection should identify both unintended exposure and active reconnaissance of IPMI services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to port 623 from public/untrusted IP ranges. Monitor for scanning patterns (e.g., rapid sequential IPMI probes to multiple targets). Detect IPMI service banners or responses to external queries. Correlate exposure with CMDBs to flag unexpected internet-facing BMCs.

suggestion.title: IPMI Default/Weak Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exposed BMCs commonly retain default credentials (ADMIN, IPMI, 12345, etc.). Article's volume (24K+) implies many are unpatched or misconfigured with predictable passwords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI services for successful login attempts using known default account names or weak passwords. Alert on any successful IPMI auth without prior failed attempts, suggesting pre-known credentials. Track login anomalies from unexpected geolocations or times.

suggestion.title: IPMI Lateral Movement via Serial-Over-LAN (SOL)
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials obtained via hash cracking, attackers pivot through IPMI to access host consoles, reboot systems, or modify firmware. IPMI provides direct BMC command and SOL access to target servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IPMI web console or SOL session initiations from external IPs. Monitor for IPMI commands (power cycle, reset, firmware update) issued in unusual sequences or outside change windows. Correlate IPMI login with host-level anomalies (unexpected reboot, privilege escalation, persistent backdoor installation).

suggestion.title: Bulk IPMI Service Enumeration and Credential Testing
suggestion.rationale: Availability of hash material and volume of targets enables large-scale attack orchestration. Attackers will enumerate capabilities and test credentials across the 24K+ exposed BMCs systematically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire IPMI enumeration queries (Get Channel Info, Get Session Challenge) from single or few sources targeting multiple BMCs. Alert on distributed credential testing patterns (N failed IPMI logins across M targets, followed by successes). Identify tooling signatures (e.g., metasploit IPMI modules, custom scanners).

suggestion.title: IPMI Firmware/Configuration Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once BMC compromised via IPMI credentials, attacker can modify firmware, disable security features, install rootkits, or enable persistence mechanisms at the hardware management level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPMI for firmware upload or update commands issued outside maintenance windows. Detect BMC configuration changes (e.g., disabling ACPI power button, modifying alert settings, enabling debug modes). Alert on modifications to IPMI user accounts or access control lists. Track firmware hash changes on production BMCs.

suggestion.title: snap-confine privilege escalation via flaw exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw 'could give local users root' and is marked critical severity. Pipeline did not generate any privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for snap-confine binary execution with privilege-level transitions (UID 0 spawned from non-root parent, or execve syscalls changing effective UID/GID during snap operation). Flag if snap-confine or snap-spawned child processes obtain root credentials without sudo/auth entry. Correlate with snap policy violations in audit logs.

suggestion.title: Unexpected root shell spawning from snap context
suggestion.rationale: Local user exploiting snap-confine flaw to gain root access would manifest as shell spawning under root after snap process invocation. Article describes impact as 'root on default desktop installs.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other shell spawns with PPID chain originating from snap-confine or snap.*, and the process UID is 0 but parent UID is non-zero. Baseline normal snap execution and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: snap-confine binary modification or integrity breach
suggestion.rationale: LPE via snap-confine likely involves either exploiting a code path or tampering with binary/config. Article implies default installs are vulnerable—suggests the flaw is in snap-confine codebase itself, not misconfig.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to snap-confine binary (/usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine), snap policy files, or snap.conf. Detect file-write events from non-privileged users targeting these paths. Compare file hashes against known-good versions for affected Ubuntu releases.

suggestion.title: Snap operation audit-log tampering or suppression
suggestion.rationale: If snap-confine flaw allows privilege escalation, attacker may disable/clear audit logs post-exploitation to cover tracks. Article does not mention this, but common post-exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on auditctl rule deletions or audit log writes from processes spawned by snap operations. Monitor for gaps in auditd event stream coinciding with snap-confine invocation. Flag if audit daemon is restarted after snap execution.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Anomalous HTTP Request Pattern to Bypass Patched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism, via crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS-targeted HTTP requests originating from unauthenticated sources (no successful auth events in preceding 5 minutes). Correlate request patterns against CVE-2025-68686 PoC signatures. Flag requests containing suspicious query parameters, path traversal attempts, or binary payloads sent to known vulnerable endpoints (likely /api/v2/ paths on FortiOS).

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation for Persistence on Compromised FortiOS Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—establishes filesystem-level persistence technique requiring detection but pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symbolic link creation attempts targeting FortiOS configuration directories (/etc/fortiosconfig/, system paths). Alert on `ln -s` or filesystem syscalls creating symlinks to sensitive config files, particularly from non-standard process parents. Correlate timing with prior exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Access to FortiOS Sensitive Configuration Files via Exposed Filesystem Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' requires detection of unauthorized config/credential file access—pipeline produced zero data-access detection use cases.

suggestion.title: Write-Access Modification to High-Dependency GitHub Repositories

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor write-access grants (user addition, PAT creation, SSH key upload) to repositories with >5000 dependents. Alert on first-time access from new identities. Investigate any PAT or SSH key created immediately before suspicious commits.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Modified Action Version Tag Points to New Commit

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of GitHub Actions pinned in organization workflows. Monitor for version tag reassignments in upstream Action repos. When tag commit SHA changes, compare commit diff for additions related to external calls, log manipulation, or secrets access.

Alert especially on symlinks pointing to parent directories or world-writable paths. Correlate timestamps with prior failed authentication attempts or HTTP exploitation alerts.

Alert on anomalous admin commands or spawned processes occurring shortly after HTTP 400/401 response clusters. Detect creation of scripts or binaries in unexpected system directories post-compromise.

Alert on external connectivity to ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443. Correlate with inbound HTTP exploitation attempts. Verify security groups/ACLs restrict access to trusted admin LANs.
