suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires hostile JavaScript executing in browser context with capability to call extension APIs. Article phrase 'malicious sites' confirms third-party script execution as vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web pages served from non-Adobe domains whose inline or externally-loaded JavaScript successfully calls adobe.extension.* or chrome.runtime.connect() APIs, or reads/writes to extension background page objects. Flag when Content Security Policy violations correlate with extension API calls.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Same-Origin Policy Bypass via Extension Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: WhatsApp Web data theft without explicit DOM access indicates SOP bypass via extension context. Detect when non-messaging-domain requests successfully access web.whatsapp.com resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XMLHttpRequest/fetch calls originating from HTML pages on external attacker-controlled domains that successfully reach web.whatsapp.com API endpoints or IndexedDB storage. Correlate with absence of browser SOP warnings or bypass of CORS headers via extension background script.

suggestion.title: Detect installation of compromised @joyfill npm packages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts as compromised packages in public npm registry; pipeline extracted zero package IOCs. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install or yarn add operations for @joyfill/components or @joyfill/layouts from public npm registry. Correlate with deployment systems and developer machines. Confirm compromised versions via package manifest timestamps post-disclosure.

suggestion.title: Detect obfuscated code execution within node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'obfuscated remote access trojan'—pipeline did not generate detection for obfuscated code execution (T1027), which is the core attack technique after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js runtime for execution of base64-encoded, gzip-compressed, or otherwise obfuscated strings in require() chains or eval() patterns. Flag suspicious child processes spawned from node_modules/@joyfill subdirectories or from require() of these packages.

suggestion.title: Detect RAT command-and-control communication from Node.js processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a remote access trojan; pipeline missed C2 detection logic. RATs must phone home; network-based detection is critical. Article should specify C2 indicators if available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of network destinations contacted by legitimate @joyfill packages. Alert on anomalous outbound connections (non-RFC1918 addresses, high-entropy domains, command-protocol patterns, beaconing behavior) from Node.js or child processes post-installation.

suggestion.title: Detect persistence installation by npm package code
suggestion.rationale: RATs universally establish persistence; article likely describes persistence techniques but pipeline generated no detection. Supply-chain malware typically plants scheduled tasks, registry keys, or startup scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU RUN keys, scheduled task creation (Win32_ScheduledJob, Task Scheduler), and file writes to Startup folders during or immediately after @joyfill package installation. Cross-reference parent process to npm/Node.js.

suggestion.title: Detect privilege escalation attempts from npm package context
suggestion.rationale: RATs frequently attempt privilege escalation; pipeline did not propose detections for escalation techniques (T1134, T1547, etc.) that malicious npm code would employ.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UAC elevation prompts, token impersonation attempts, or WMI/COM elevation patterns originating from Node.js processes or child processes spawned by @joyfill code. Correlate with package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: Detect system reconnaissance commands from npm-spawned child processes
suggestion.rationale: RATs perform discovery (T1049, T1082, T1087); pipeline did not propose detection for reconnaissance activity that typically follows successful initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of whoami, ipconfig, tasklist, systeminfo, net commands or their PowerShell equivalents as child processes of Node.js. Flag unusual combinations or rapid execution consistent with automated discovery scripts.

suggestion.title: SFTP file access operations following goshs connection from non-standard port
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SFTP accepts connections without password' and implies file transfer via SFTP after auth bypass. Need detection for successful SFTP sessions followed by file read/write operations. Article provides no file-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SFTP SSH handshake completion (successful auth, possibly with empty password signature) on non-standard ports (e.g., 2222) with subsequent file I/O operations from the SFTP process. Flag if source is external or privileged-access tool.

suggestion.title: goshs process invoked with -b flag containing empty username or password segment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the vuln config: `-b 'admin:'` (empty password after colon) and earlier CVE as `:pass` (empty username before colon). The regex in UC_4_2 covers this, but a complementary hunt for command-line argument parsing of the `-b` flag itself would catch missed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on goshs/goshs.exe process creation where ProcessCommandLine contains `-b` followed by pattern matching `<username>:` (no password) OR `:<password>` (no username), excluding processes with `-fkf` flag.

suggestion.title: goshs configuration file creation or modification with empty-credential basic auth
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions vulnerability config passed via `-b` flag; if config is persisted to file (e.g., `.goshs.conf`), detect file write/modification events with empty credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of goshs config files (common patterns: `.goshs.conf`, `goshs.yaml`, `goshs.json`) where file content contains `-b` flag with empty username or password segment, or direct config key `basic_auth` with null/empty password value.

suggestion.title: SSH service fingerprint mismatch: goshs SFTP variant detected via banner or protocol anomaly
suggestion.rationale: goshs is a lightweight SFTP server with distinct SSH banner and protocol behavior; network detection can identify unexpected/unauthorized goshs instances. Article does not mention network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SSH connections with Server Banner containing 'goshs' or exhibiting SFTP-only protocol behavior (no interactive shell) from unexpected/unauthorized hosts or listening on non-standard ports (e.g., 2222).

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Unauthenticated Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Exploited SmartConsole Flaw Allowing Full Admin Access'—implies unauthorized access to management console, the critical initial vector for this vulnerability chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole for authentication bypasses or HTTP requests to /web/index.html and /smartconsole endpoints that succeed without valid credentials. Flag requests using known exploit patterns or from unexpected source IPs/ASNs.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation via SmartConsole Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly states 'Full Admin Access'—post-exploitation, attacker will create privileged accounts for persistence. Yet pipeline generated no detection for unauthorized admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new administrative user creation in SmartConsole outside normal provisioning windows, especially following suspicious authentication events or during off-hours. Flag accounts with implicit trust relationships to managed security appliances.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole API Abuse for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SmartConsole with admin privileges enables unrestricted access to managed Check Point gateways via REST API (/web_api/v*). Pipeline missed detection for command-and-control via management plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole REST API calls for unusual patterns: bulk policy deployments, gateway configuration changes, rule insertions, or API authentication from new user agents/IPs. Correlate with newly-created admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Security Policy Deployment via SmartConsole
suggestion.rationale: With admin access, attacker modifies firewall rules on all managed appliances. Headline implies 'full admin access' includes policy control—this is an impact vector the pipeline completely ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy pushes that disable logging, add overly-permissive rules (e.g., allow-all to specific IPs), or modify inspection profiles on bulk appliances. Flag policy changes occurring outside change windows or by recently-provisioned admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Firewall Gateway Compromise via SmartConsole Chain
suggestion.rationale: SmartConsole admin access enables compromise of all downstream Check Point appliances. Article's 'full admin access' directly threatens managed gateway security posture—no lateral movement UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for configuration synchronization events from SmartConsole to gateways that contain suspicious commands or policy rules. Alert on unexpected gateway restarts, certificate changes, or firmware updates initiated from compromised SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Version Scanning and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation, attackers enumerate SmartConsole versions to confirm vulnerability presence. Article states 'patches exploited'—implies active reconnaissance phase missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to SmartConsole endpoints that probe for version info (/web/help/about, JS version strings, default paths). Flag rapid version enumeration attempts from single source IP followed by exploitation patterns within 24–48 hours.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Scanner Validation Against KEV
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable" because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet' — scanners may miss the known-exploited status or patch-bypass logic. Needs active validation against CISA KEV confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when FortiOS devices are reported 'patched' against CVE-2025-68686 but are still exposed to the known-exploited form (patch bypass via symlink persistence). Compare scanner output against CISA KEV publication date (2026-07-27) to identify lag.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symlink Persistence Mechanism Filesystem Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' and 'at filesystem level' — post-compromise attackers will create or manipulate symlinks to bypass patched HTTP handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (especially /etc, /var, /tmp) for symlink creation or modification correlated with HTTP daemon restarts or crafted HTTP requests. Symlink targets pointing to sensitive config or system paths warrant escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management/Web Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and 'via crafted HTTP requests' as the exploitation vector post-compromise — malformed or unusual HTTP patterns bypass the patched symlink check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS web/management ports (80, 443, 8443) from external IPs that are malformed (oversized headers, null bytes, unusual path traversal attempts, symlink-escape sequences) without authentication headers. Correlate with symlink filesystem events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Information Disclosure Post-Compromise via HTTP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' through the patch bypass — successful exploitation results in data exfiltration from config files, logs, or system state accessible via symlinks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large reads or exfiltration of sensitive FortiOS files (/etc/system.conf, /etc/passwd, /var/log/*, certificate stores) following patched HTTP daemon activity or after symlink creation. Monitor for encoded/compressed data staging on the filesystem.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypasses via Known Symlink Escape Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' — the patch itself is known; look for HTTP payloads that work around it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match HTTP request payloads against known PoC patterns for CVE-2025-68686 symlink bypass (e.g., double-URL encoding of ../../../, null-byte injection, symlink-race conditions). Correlate payload attempts with 404/403 responses followed by 200 OK responses on sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Fileless FortiOS Post-Exploitation via Memory-Mapped Symlinks
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — once inside, symlink abuse may enable memory-resident persistence without disk artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FortiOS HTTP daemon (e.g., httpsd) opening symlinked files or mapping them to memory; correlate with /proc/<PID>/maps changes or unusual system calls (openat, readlink, mmap) that re-read symlinked config files at runtime.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild; 'CVE-2025-68686... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Federal patch due 2026-08-10. Vulnerability scanner data is primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS appliances (FortiGate, FortiManager, etc.) missing patches for CVE-2025-68686 via vulnerability scanner output or asset inventory. Cross-reference with patch dates post-2026-08-10 federal deadline. False positives: scanner false negatives on patched builds.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—persistence vector used post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem (via sysmon, auditd, or FortiOS CLI logs) for suspicious symbolic link creation in system directories or config paths. Look for unusual .lnk or symlink references in /etc, /opt, or application directories post-compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests Targeting FortiOS Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' after filesystem-level access—exploitation delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS management ports (443, 8080, 10443) with malformed headers, oversized payloads, or unusual URI patterns. Correlate with failed auth attempts or file-modification events on same system within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Filesystem Modification on Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'—behavioral detection post-initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect filesystem writes to FortiOS system binaries, config files, or boot-level paths by non-admin processes or unexpected service accounts. Escalate if modification timestamp post-dates known vulnerability exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Compliance Drift Post-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-10 is audit trigger; 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Regulatory compliance reporting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-2026-08-10: identify FortiOS instances still missing CVE-2025-68686 patches. Flag as audit-reportable non-compliance. Cross-check against CISA KEV due-date tracker to identify remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Public-Facing Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can exploit 'public-facing application' — this is T1190 in practice. Pipeline missed explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances for HTTP requests to management interfaces from external sources. Baseline normal admin access patterns and alert on spike in authentication failures or unusual source IPs. Focus on unauthenticated access attempts to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Bypass via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'crafted HTTP requests' used to 'bypass the patch' — this is the core exploitation technique. Pipeline failed to operationalize this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests with suspicious payloads targeting FortiOS HTTP handlers. Look for requests with unusual character encoding, path traversal patterns, or oversized headers that may bypass WAF/IDS signatures. Correlate against known CVE-2025-68686 PoC patterns.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — this describes T1547/T1574 persistence, not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation or modification of symlinks in sensitive directories (config, bin, lib paths). Detect symlink→external paths. Alert on symlinks created within 10 minutes of exploit indicator (HTTP 403→200 pattern or authentication log anomalies).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit FortiOS Sensitive Information Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker seeks 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' after initial breach — requires post-exploit monitoring for data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting initial compromise or patch bypass, hunt for access to sensitive config files (passwd, config.db, certificates) via unusual process or user context. Monitor for syslog exfiltration, unusual outbound TLS connections from FortiOS appliance, or config file reads by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Prior Compromise Detection — Filesystem-Level FortiOS Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — this multi-stage attack requires detection of initial filesystem compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect first-stage compromise by monitoring FortiOS OS-level file writes to protected paths (root-level binaries, config directories) by processes running as non-root or via unusual execution chains. Correlate with kernel logs for privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Patch Non-Compliance and Bypass Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context: article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and attackers exploit already-patched vulnerabilities. Detection must confirm patch presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all FortiOS instances for presence of the CVE-2025-68686 patch. Correlate patch status against HTTP attack attempts — if unpatched instance receives crafted HTTP requests, escalate immediately. Detect attempts to patch downgrade or patch-bypass via integrity checks.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FortiOS Inventory — CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet.' CISA KEV implies active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-08-10 creates hard deadline for remediation hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for FortiOS versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag any external-facing instances not patched before 2026-08-10. Escalate based on CVSS and network exposure.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Management/API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS. This malformed HTTP traffic signature must be monitored at proxy/WAF/network-edge layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests to external FortiOS admin/API endpoints for malformed payloads, oversized parameters, null bytes, or path-traversal patterns. Correlate with auth bypass (401→200 transitions) or 5xx errors.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Symlink abuse is direct persistence indicator post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for creation/modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (init, cron, startup, config paths). Alert on ln -s or symlink() syscalls in restricted locations. Correlate with prior compromise timestamps.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Compromise Activity (Pre-CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' This two-stage attack requires hunting for prior access: file upload, path traversal, or command injection that preceded HTTP exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate timeline: hunt FortiOS logs for file writes to unexpected paths, unsigned binary execution, privilege escalation attempts, or known CVEs (path traversal, arbitrary file write) exploited in weeks before detection of CVE-2025-68686 activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiOS Gateway
suggestion.rationale: A compromised firewall/gateway is network-critical pivot point. Post-breach lateral movement to internal assets must be monitored to limit blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag anomalous outbound traffic from FortiOS management/data planes to internal subnets post-compromise (SMB, RDP, LDAP, DNS queries to internal resources). Alert on new sessions to high-value targets (AD, exchange, databases).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection via Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2025-68686 as the indicator and explicitly references the asset-exposure hunt template. CISA KEV status means active exploitation; standard asset-exposure rule applies directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Fortinet FortiOS systems reporting vulnerable versions matching CVE-2025-68686 in scanner output. Cross-reference with patch due date 2026-08-10 for compliance tracking and urgency prioritization.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiOS Admin/Config Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'via crafted HTTP requests'—this is the exploitation vector. Requires monitoring for HTTP patterns that attempt to bypass the patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS management interfaces for malformed requests: unusual encodings, oversized payloads, POST/PUT to config endpoints with suspicious headers, path traversal indicators (../, encoded equivalents), or requests containing filesystem-level special characters.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Critical Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—direct indicator of post-exploitation persistence attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS config directories, web root, or module paths. Establish baseline of authorized symlinks and flag new ones outside maintenance windows, especially those pointing to sensitive files or system utilities.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FortiOS Credentials and Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—direct impact. Monitor who/what accesses credential stores post-detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads of FortiOS configuration files (config.sys), credential vaults, VPN secret storage, and admin user databases. Flag access patterns that do not match baseline (non-admin processes, HTTP handlers, scheduled tasks accessing these files).

suggestion.title: Bypass of CVE-2025-68686 Patch via HTTP Evasion Techniques
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—indicates active evasion. Detect requests that successfully evade patch protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests employing alternate encodings, request smuggling, chunked transfer encoding tricks, or filesystem-level escape sequences designed to reach code paths supposedly protected by the CVE-2025-68686 patch. Correlate successful exploitation with symlink creation or credential access.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerable Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates hunt for exposed FortiOS instances: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...#asset-exposure]'. Pipeline generated zero use cases. Article explicitly references Fortinet FortiOS product and CVE-2025-68686.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances exposed to internet via port 443/80 scanning, banner grabbing, or vulnerability scanner results. Use vendor identification string matching in proxy logs, IDS/IPS signatures, or active network discovery. Correlate against CVE-2025-68686 patch status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt (Crafted HTTP Requests)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests'. Pipeline failed to create detection for this exploitation vector despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS instances (identified via product discovery) for malformed or anomalous HTTP requests targeting known exploitation paths. Flag requests with unusual header combinations, path traversal patterns, or symlink-related payloads. Correlate with post-compromise filesystem access patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Filesystem Persistence Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'filesystem level' compromise as prerequisite. Pipeline missed detection for persistence artifacts left behind post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt FortiOS systems for symbolic links created in unexpected locations (especially web-accessible directories), unusual file ownership changes, or suspicious .so / binary modifications in system paths. Cross-reference against patched vs. unpatched asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Sensitive Information Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor'. Pipeline generated no detection for the information disclosure phase despite it being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unauthorized read access to sensitive FortiOS files (e.g., config archives, VPN credentials, encrypted keys) by correlating filesystem audit logs with HTTP request logs. Flag exfiltration of large config files or repeated access to credential stores on CVE-2025-68686 affected instances.

suggestion.title: Pre-Requisite Vulnerability Chain Leading to CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'. Pipeline failed to model the prerequisite compromise as part of the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each FortiOS instance, cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results to identify other active CVEs or unpatched services that could serve as initial entry point. Prioritize instances with multiple vulnerabilities present. Model attack chain as: [initial CVE] → [filesystem access] → [CVE-2025-68686 exploitation] → [info disclosure].

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request to FortiOS Sensitive Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism... via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the active exploitation vector and should be a first-order detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin/API endpoints for HTTP requests with atypical patterns: path traversal sequences, unusual HTTP methods, malformed headers, or parameters that bypass validation. Correlate with Fortinet OS version to flag unpatched targets. Baseline legitimate admin and automation traffic first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation in FortiOS Config/Data Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' as the underlying post-exploit technique being bypassed. Direct filesystem monitoring for symlink creation is the persistence hunting signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation (ln -s, mklink, or API equivalent) in FortiOS critical directories: /var/lib, /var/etc, /opt/fortinet, /var/log. Filter out maintenance symlinks (config backups, log rotation). Correlate with prior filesystem access from non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Must detect access to FortiOS secrets post-compromise: keys, credentials, VPN configs, traffic logs stored at filesystem level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor read access to /var/log (traffic/auth logs), /var/etc/admin_* (admin hashes), /var/etc/certs (private keys), /var/etc/vpn (VPN configs) from non-FortiOS-service processes. Alert on bulk exfil patterns (multiple files read in short window from single process).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates scanner-based detection. Article specifies CVE-2025-68686 and federal patch-due date 2026-08-10. Any unpatched FortiOS in scope is a critical alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) for CVE-2025-68686 matches. Alert on High/Critical findings on externally-facing FortiOS instances. Cross-reference with patch management system to confirm remediation status and prioritize by patch gap (due date: 2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Filesystem Access Followed by Anomalous HTTP Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: compromise (filesystem-level access) → then HTTP-based exploitation. Detecting the correlation between filesystem modifications and subsequent crafted HTTP requests is the two-stage exploit signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate (a) filesystem-level write/create events in FortiOS system dirs with (b) anomalous HTTP requests to FortiOS endpoints within 5-30 minutes. Baseline: legitimate admin changes to FortiOS config are typically via CLI or API, not raw filesystem writes. Alert on write→HTTP correlation, especially if source is non-admin process.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Admin/API Access from Non-Standard Clients
suggestion.rationale: Prior compromise required for exploitation. After initial breach, attacker must interact with FortiOS remotely—likely via REST API or admin interface. Look for authentication from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS admin interface (port 443, /admin path) and REST API (port 443, /api/v2) for login attempts and API calls from IPs not in baseline (datacenter IPs, known mgmt networks). Alert on failed auth attempts followed by successful access (brute force hypothesis). Flag API calls from automated tools not in change-mgmt system.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'—requires scanning FortiOS versions across the fleet. Zero detection UCs for patch-status validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset DB for FortiOS appliances. Flag instances with version/patch dates prior to 2026-08-10. Cross-reference against CVSS score and device exposure (internet-facing). Alert on unpatched FortiOS in federal/critical-infrastructure networks.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Bypass Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'bypass the patch…via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection for malformed/adversarial HTTP patterns targeting the patch mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS web interface (typically port 443/8443) for HTTP requests with atypical structure: oversized headers, null bytes, path-traversal sequences, or symbolic-link references in URI. Alert on repeated requests to /api or config endpoints from unauthenticated sessions, especially post-IPS/vulnerability-scan activity.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—no detection for filesystem artifacts created after initial compromise. This is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS /var, /tmp, and /proc for symbolic links to auth binaries, config parsers, or credential stores. Alert on ln -s or symlink syscalls from non-standard processes outside change-management windows. Correlate with prior filesystem write events and HTTP request anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Sensitive Data Access from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker'…'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No detection for unauthorized data reads/exfiltration without valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS audit logs for file reads from /etc/passwd equivalents, VPN config dirs, certificate keystores, and credential vaults. Alert on data access without valid admin session, especially followed by outbound HTTP/HTTPS to non-Fortinet IPs. Correlate with prior symlink-creation events.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vulnerability Exploitation Chain (Initial CVE → FortiOS Filesystem Access → CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' No detection for the two-stage attack pattern.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Exposed Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploit 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV implies active scanning. Detection should identify FortiOS assets accessible from untrusted networks via network scanning or configuration review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances responding to HTTP requests from external sources. Look for HTTP User-Agent patterns typical of FortiOS or known scanner signatures attempting to fingerprint the product.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers bypass the patch 'via crafted HTTP requests.' Detection should capture malformed or anomalous HTTP request patterns targeting FortiOS services post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for FortiOS endpoints showing unusual request patterns: non-standard HTTP methods, oversized headers, special characters in URL paths, or Content-Type mismatches. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or suspicious parameter values.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Abuse on FortiOS Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and 'bypass' of that mechanism, indicating attacker creates or manipulates symbolic links post-compromise. Detection should alert on filesystem operations related to symlink creation in critical directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for symlink creation or traversal attempts in FortiOS configuration or binary directories. Look for processes spawned by admin or system accounts that reference /proc/self/fd or similar symlink paths, and cross-reference with post-exploitation timeframes.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerability Confirmation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article implies patched versions exist. Detection should confirm whether endpoints have been patched or remain vulnerable by querying vulnerability scanner data or native FortiOS version enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match FortiOS product inventory against CVE-2025-68686 patch baseline. Flag any instances running versions known to be vulnerable or with patch date before federal due date 2026-08-10. Cross-correlate with network segmentation rules.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit HTTP Admin API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker must first compromise FortiOS 'via another vulnerability' then bypass patch via HTTP. Detection should identify anomalous admin API calls post-initial-compromise, such as credential changes, policy modifications, or data exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiOS admin console (/admin, /api/v2/cmdb) from non-approved source IPs, especially those without valid session cookies or with reused tokens. Correlate with successful authentication only to admin accounts, and look for config modification events immediately after.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism ... via crafted HTTP requests' but pipeline provides no HTTP-level detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS web interfaces (ports 80, 443, 10000, 8443) for HTTP requests with suspicious or malformed parameters consistent with patch-bypass attempts. Correlate against device version to identify unpatched instances. Flag requests deviating from normal administrative traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch Compliance and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10 for compliance audits, but pipeline provides no asset-inventory or patch-status use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability-management and CMDB systems for Fortinet FortiOS instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag instances in internet-exposed or DMZ segments. Alert on instances not patched by 2026-08-10 federal due date to support regulatory compliance workflows.

suggestion.title: Symbolic-Link Persistence Detection on Fortinet Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and notes 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — establishing post-exploitation persistence requirement absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem logs and file-integrity systems for creation of symbolic links in web-accessible directories (/var/www, /usr/local/share/fortiweb) pointing to config or credential storage. Alert on link creation outside normal administrative hours or by non-privileged processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Extraction of FortiOS Sensitive Information Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' but pipeline contains no detection for unauthorized config access, credential theft, or exfiltration following compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk extraction of FortiOS administrative credentials, VPN configurations, firewall rule sets, or system logs following filesystem-level compromise indicators. Monitor for subsequent anomalous outbound connections over non-standard ports from affected device IP space.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation Attempt — Anomalous HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'crafted HTTP requests' as the attack vector and that exploits target FortiOS admin interfaces. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this explicit attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS /admin, /api/, and /cgi-bin endpoints for POST/PUT requests with unusual payloads (e.g., path traversal patterns, symbolic link references, or requests from non-standard User-Agents). Flag patterns matching known FortiOS exploitation frameworks targeting this CVE.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistency — Post-Exploitation Filesystem Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism' but no detection for symbolic link creation or filesystem persistence was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of symbolic links pointing to FortiOS system directories (/etc, /root, /usr/bin) or temporary paths. Correlate with prior CVE-2025-68686 exploitation indicators to confirm post-compromise persistence setup.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Information Disclosure — Sensitive Config File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'may allow...bypass...unauthorized actor' to access sensitive info; impact is information disclosure but no detection for reading protected config or credential files was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS for read access to sensitive paths (e.g., /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow variants, FortiOS config backups, VPN credential stores) following anomalous HTTP activity. Flag processes spawned by web services (fortishell, httpd) reading files outside normal operational scope.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Remote Access — Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote unauthenticated attacker' and bypass of existing security controls; no detection rule for authentication-bypass patterns generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiOS admin endpoints with missing or malformed authentication headers, or requests that succeed despite 401/403 responses to prior requests from same source. Track bypass success rates by source IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Prerequisite Compromise — Multi-Stage Attack Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' No correlation rule for detecting this prerequisite initial compromise was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of FortiOS vulnerability scans flagging other pre-2025-68686 CVEs. Create hunt for systems with active exploitation indicators (failed RCE attempts, webshell paths) followed within 48h by 2025-68686-specific HTTP patterns; indicates staged attack.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Status Verification — Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article notes federal due date 2026-08-10 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'; no use case for identifying unpatched FortiOS versions in fleet inventory was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset inventory for FortiOS instances with versions < fixed build (requires Fortinet advisory for exact version ranges). Cross-reference with network telemetry to identify which systems accept inbound HTTP/S on admin ports; prioritize remediation for internet-facing assets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2025-68686 as the actively exploited CVE with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-10. Pipeline must detect vulnerable FortiOS versions via scanner fingerprint, HTTP header disclosure, or patch-status cross-check against asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances running vulnerable versions via vulnerability scanner exports or HTTP responses disclosing version strings. Cross-reference asset inventory to flag systems not remediated by 2026-08-10 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' Attackers create symlinks in FortiOS filesystem to maintain foothold after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink creation (ln -s calls) in FortiOS protected directories (/usr/local/fortisandbox, /etc/fortigate, /var/cache/forticlient). Flag symlinks pointing to writable temp directories or scripts. Monitor for post-exploit symlink overwrites of system binaries.

suggestion.title: Patch Bypass HTTP Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism via crafted HTTP requests.' Must detect polymorph requests circumventing input validation patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed HTTP requests to known-vulnerable FortiOS endpoints (e.g., /upload, /api, /admin) with special character encoding, multi-stage payloads, or boundary-bypass patterns. Correlate with POST/GET responses indicating patch-bypass success (symlink creation side-effects, file disclosure).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote unauthenticated attacker' exploiting 'public-facing application.' Must detect unauthorized access to FortiOS management interfaces without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to FortiOS admin/API endpoints (ports 80, 443, 8080, 10443) from external IPs returning 401/403 authentication failures. Flag sequences of requests probing multiple endpoints without auth headers or with invalid tokens pre-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information' after 'prior filesystem level' compromise. Detect abnormal access to configuration, credential, or API-key files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads on sensitive FortiOS config paths (/etc/fortiweb.conf, /etc/fortisandbox.conf, /etc/passwd, /var/log/authlog) from unexpected processes or UIDs. Correlate with prior symlink-creation or patch-bypass signals. Flag exfiltration attempts (curl/wget) of config file contents.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Privilege Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level,' indicating lateral privilege escalation from restricted process context to system/root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process fork/exec sequences escalating from sandboxed FortiOS services (fortisandbox, fortiweb daemons) to root-level actions. Flag access to /proc/*/mem, ptrace calls, or kernel module loading from unprivileged contexts. Monitor setuid/setgid bit abuse on FortiOS binaries.

suggestion.title: Compromised NPM Package Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts are compromised; no use case for detecting installation of known-bad npm packages in package.lock or npm install logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn install, and pnpm install processes for package manager invocations installing @joyfill/components or @joyfill/layouts. Cross-reference against threat feed of compromised package names and versions. Flag installations on development and CI/CD systems.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution from Node Modules
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Obfuscated Remote Access Trojan'; pipeline missed T1027 defense-evasion indicator for obfuscated payloads embedded in node_modules during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or JavaScript engine executing heavily obfuscated code from node_modules directory. Look for suspicious eval(), Function constructor, or atob() chains originating from installed dependencies. Flag high entropy strings being decoded at runtime.

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Communication from Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT payload; no detection for outbound C2 communication initiated by Node.js or application processes loading compromised npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTPS or DNS queries from node.js processes against known RAT C2 infrastructure. Monitor for long-lived connections or periodic beaconing patterns from application entry-points that depend on @joyfill packages.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: RAT typically requires code execution and reverse shell capability; no use case for detecting shell spawning from npm-installed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.js or npm processes spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with command-line arguments. Correlate parent process tree to installed packages. Flag child_process module calls with network-suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Package Lock File Modification Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often alter lock files to persist across dependency updates; no detection for tampering with package-lock.json or yarn.lock after initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json and yarn.lock for suspicious hash mismatches or version downgrades matching known-compromised package releases. Detect modifications to lock files immediately following npm install or package manager invocations.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Obfuscated Dependency Payloads
suggestion.rationale: RAT payloads typically enumerate system info and running processes; no detection for discovery commands embedded or scheduled via npm post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag post-install scripts or require-time code execution that invokes system discovery commands (whoami, hostname, netstat, tasklist, ps, etc.) without legitimate build-time justification. Correlate with @joyfill package installation.

suggestion.title: ClickHouse database error logs from malformed/injected SQL
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers inject 'arbitrary SQL by using trailing backslash'—successful injection will either execute or generate database errors. Pipeline missed application/database log detection. Article phrase: 'allows arbitrary SQL execution' implies backend logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query ClickHouse system.query_log for syntax errors or unexpected query patterns (e.g., UNION, OR 1=1) originating from HTTP requests. Correlate with escapeValue() stack traces or process memory analysis showing backslash bypass logic triggered. High-confidence signal if error occurs immediately after HTTP request containing backslash-quote in parameter.

suggestion.title: @hypequery/clickhouse process communication anomaly detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes escapeValue() function vulnerability—monitoring the vulnerable library's function calls or memory behavior during exploitation would detect injection in-flight. Missing: dynamic analysis of the vulnerable code path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process executing @hypequery/clickhouse or Node.js with embedded hypequery when receiving HTTP requests with backslash-quote patterns in parameters, followed by unexpected child processes (sqlclient, curl to external IPs, base64 encoding tools) or high volume of database queries in short window. Correlate HTTP request timestamp with process execution within 100ms.

suggestion.title: Version mismatch: @hypequery/clickhouse <2.0.2 still running post-patching
suggestion.rationale: Patch available (2.0.2+), but article states 'versions prior to 2.0.2 who pass user-controlled input'—many orgs delay patching. Missing: detection for unpatched systems still in production after advisory release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package manager logs or process execution for @hypequery/clickhouse binary/module load with version <2.0.2 post-2026-07-28 (advisory date). Cross-reference against patch deployment logs. Flag if system is internet-facing (has public DNS, listening on 0.0.0.0, exposed via CDN/LB).

suggestion.title: POST-exploitation: data exfiltration via SQLi result tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'allows arbitrary SQL execution' but provides no hunts for successful exploitation outcomes. Attacker would exfiltrate data via injected SELECT statements tunneled through HTTP response or error messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP responses >10KB or unusual Content-Type (application/octet-stream from JSON API) correlating with database query errors or long query execution time. Detect SELECT INTO OUTFILE patterns in HTTP requests or error messages. Flag if response contains CSV/JSON data structure matching database schema.

suggestion.title: WAF/IDS bypass indicators: double-encoding and normalization evasion
suggestion.rationale: The pipeline's UC_2_2 assumes URL encoding consistency, but sophisticated attackers will use double-encoding (%255c), mixed case (%5C vs %5c), or unicode normalization to bypass pattern matching. Article doesn't mention evasion, but a critical SQL injection warrants it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed HTTP requests (403/406 from WAF) to same endpoint followed by successful request (200) with different parameter encoding. Flag if single source cycles through >5 different encoding variants of backslash-quote pattern within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable @hypequery/clickhouse dependency in npm shrinkwrap/package-lock.json
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies package & version; runtime detection only catches active exploitation. Missing: pre-deployment/build-time detection of vulnerable dependency in source code repositories and artifact repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package-lock.json / yarn.lock / shrinkwrap.json in all code repos and CI/CD artifact repos for @hypequery/clickhouse version <2.0.2. Alert on pull requests adding or keeping the vulnerable version post-2026-07-28. Cross-ref against deploy logs to identify running instances.

suggestion.title: WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite:T header targeting existing file
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states MOVE with 'Overwrite: T' performs explicit RemoveAll on destination—this header presence is the attack signature. Searching for MOVE requests carrying Overwrite: True against existing destination paths is precise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebDAV MOVE/COPY requests with Overwrite: True header sent against a goshs server (identify via banner or HTTP Server header). Correlate with file access logs to confirm destination existed pre-request and was deleted/overwritten post-request.

suggestion.title: goshs version running without patch for CVE-2026-64863 or CVE-2026-50138
suggestion.rationale: Article references two CVEs, indicating this is a known vulnerability with a patch. Detection should identify goshs versions vulnerable to this bypass, not just --no-delete flag presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify goshs process with version < [fixed version] running with --no-delete flag. Query against process inventory or EDR Process telemetry for Version field. A baseline should include goshs binaries with hash signatures of vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Destination header rewrite in WebDAV MOVE to exfiltrate/modify unintended files
suggestion.rationale: WebDAV MOVE allows specifying a Destination header distinct from the path being moved. Article describes 'MOVE deletes source file...and with Overwrite: T it additionally performs RemoveAll on destination'—an attacker could exploit this to delete files outside their intended scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all WebDAV MOVE/COPY requests and compare the request path with the Destination header value. Flag when Destination points to a different directory or filename than the request path, especially if the destination previously existed (check access logs for pre-move activity).

suggestion.title: goshs listening on web port without authentication + --no-delete but accepting MOVE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes running with '--w --no-delete' (likely -w for web mode). Lack of authentication coupled with disabled DELETE but enabled MOVE creates the bypass condition. Detection should identify this configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify goshs processes listening on HTTP/HTTPS (port 80, 443, or common alternate web ports) with --no-delete flag in command line AND WebDAV protocol active (detect via OPTIONS request support or presence of WebDAV-specific headers in responses).

suggestion.title: Source file present before WebDAV MOVE, absent after (file deletion via protocol)
suggestion.rationale: The attack succeeds when MOVE destroys the source file while --no-delete is supposed to prevent it. A precise signature is: file enumeration shows file exists, WebDAV MOVE succeeds, file no longer exists at original path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WebDAV access logs (MOVE/COPY requests) with file system audit logs or directory listing snapshots. Flag when a MOVE request succeeds (201/204) but the source path no longer contains the file immediately after (requires file listing or audit log confirmation of deletion).

suggestion.title: goshs process spawned with -sftp and -b flags simultaneously
suggestion.rationale: The article emphasizes the combination of `-sftp` and `-b 'admin:'` in a single invocation. A process-creation detection that correlates both flags on the same cmdline strengthens initial-access detection. Article: 'Start goshs v2.1.3 with `-b 'admin:' -sftp`. No `-fkf`.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation of goshs/goshs.exe where the command line contains both `-sftp` and `-b` flags in sequence, indicating SFTP listener with basic authentication enabled. Exclude processes with `-fkf` flag (the published fix). This is the tell-tale sign of vulnerable configuration.

suggestion.title: Comparison of goshs instances with and without -fkf flag presence
suggestion.rationale: The article explicitly states that CVE-2026-40884 was incompletely fixed and that adding `-fkf` is the mitigation. A compliance-style hunt should track which goshs processes lack this protective flag. Article: 'CVE-2026-40884 blocks the empty-username variant... The empty-password variant bypasses that fix.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all goshs/goshs.exe process invocations across the estate. Flag any that include `-sftp` and `-b` but LACK the `-fkf` flag. This identifies unpatched/misconfigured listeners vulnerable to CVE-2026-62325 and the prior CVE-2026-40884.

suggestion.title: Credential submission to SFTP listener (empty-password or empty-username auth attempts)
suggestion.rationale: If SFTP auth logs or SSH logs capture the actual authentication exchange, empty-password or empty-username login attempts (via SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST or similar) to port 2121 would be direct evidence of exploitation. Article narrative: 'SFTP accepts connections without password' and 'empty-password variant'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt SSH/SFTP protocol-level auth attempts where username field is populated but password field is empty, or vice versa. Focus on connections to goshs listener ports (2121 if default). This may require SSH daemon or SFTP client logs on the network segment.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploited SmartConsole Flaw Allowing Full Admin Access' — pipeline did not capture the privilege-escalation attack path or exploitation detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Check Point SmartConsole processes and services for abnormal elevation of privileges, failed-then-successful authentication transitions, or privilege grants from unauthenticated context. Alert on successful admin-level operations following exploitation attempts or from non-standard service accounts.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Public Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Exploited' (past tense, active threat) — pipeline missed detection for inbound exploitation attempts or post-exploitation reconnaissance of SmartConsole endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to Check Point SmartConsole management interface (port 4434 default or variants) from unexpected source IPs, with payloads indicating SQL injection, path traversal, or deserialization attack patterns matching known SmartConsole CVEs.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Check Point SmartConsole Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is about a patch release — pipeline should have extracted vulnerable and patched version identifiers for software inventory baselining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Check Point SmartConsole installations via process/service introspection, registry keys, or file paths. Compare installed versions against CVE advisory patch baseline to identify vulnerable deployments requiring immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Unauthorized Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Full admin access is the impact — pipeline should surface detection for new admin accounts or permission escalations post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new SmartConsole admin accounts, elevation of existing account roles to admin, or unexpected permission grant operations following authentication anomalies or exploitation activity on the SmartConsole host.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability impact is management-plane compromise — pipeline should flag reconnaissance for other Check Point infrastructure or downstream policy querying.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole processes for outbound enumeration of gateways, firewalls, or internal Check Point services post-exploitation. Flag network sweeps or policy-enumeration API calls from the compromised SmartConsole.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2025-68686 as the CISA KEV entry and states it is actively exploited in the wild. Standard asset-hygiene hunt for any critical KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiOS instances in your environment and correlate against scanner output for CVE-2025-68686 presence. CISA KEV items are confirmed-exploited; patch lag is a primary risk factor.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a persistence technique used post-initial-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation or modification in critical system directories. Flag unusual symlink targets pointing to binaries or startup mechanisms. Correlate with file integrity monitoring for unauthorized changes.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Anomalies Against FortiOS Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass the symbolic-link persistency patch. This is the exploitation mechanism after initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to FortiOS web interface (typically TCP 80/443, 8080, 8443) containing path traversal sequences, crafted URI encoding, or abnormal parameter values. Baseline normal admin access patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage FortiOS Exploitation: Initial Compromise + HTTP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before the HTTP-based bypass. This is a multi-stage kill chain requiring correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate indicators: (1) successful initial exploit against FortiOS (CVE unknown but likely a pre-auth RCE or auth bypass); (2) followed by filesystem modifications; (3) followed by abnormal HTTP requests to same FortiOS instance. Timeline should be hours to days.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploitation requires the device to be reachable from the internet. Asset exposure hunt is canonical for public-facing application exploits (T1190).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiOS appliances (via DNS, certificate transparency, shodan-style indexing) that are exposed to the internet. Cross-reference against your asset inventory for unaccounted or unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Audit for CVE-2025-68686
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries include federal remediation due dates (2026-08-10 in this case). Compliance hunting is mandatory for regulated environments and SOC baselining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and patch-management systems for FortiOS version and patch level. Flag any instance older than the patched version or where last patch date is before the CVE advisory date.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Vulnerable Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker bypasses patch 'via crafted HTTP requests' — this is the primary exploitation vector that must be detected in network logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to FortiOS management or API endpoints (typically ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443) with malformed headers, oversized payloads, or unusual request patterns that do not match legitimate admin/automation traffic. Focus on requests arriving at unpatched FortiOS instances within your environment.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration/Data Access Post-FortiOS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' — need to detect unauthorized access to secrets, configs, and credentials typically stored on FortiOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On compromised FortiOS systems, detect unusual file and process activity targeting credential stores, configuration files (/etc/config, /etc/passwd, SSL keys), and log files. Correlate with network exfiltration immediately following exploitation.

suggestion.title: Filesystem-Level Persistence and Symlink Traversal Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' and mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' — detection must cover first-stage filesystem abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of suspicious symlinks, executable placement in startup directories, and unexpected file ownership changes on FortiOS systems. Symlink traversal attempts (reading/writing outside intended directories) are a key bypass indicator for the patched vulnerability.

suggestion.title: FortiOS System Information Discovery Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Following initial filesystem compromise, attacker will enumerate system state; article describes prior compromise scenario requiring discovery of vulnerable FortiOS instance state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance queries on compromised FortiOS systems: process enumeration (ps, netstat), network scanning (nmap, curl to local services), and queries to system files (/proc, /etc). These precede the HTTP-based exploitation phase.

suggestion.title: HTTP Status Anomalies and Error Responses from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Crafted HTTP requests targeting the patch bypass will generate atypical responses; article implies requests that evade newly-deployed mitigations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FortiOS HTTP response patterns and alert on high-volume requests returning 400-level errors, timeouts, or unusual response sizes. Attackers retry exploit payloads; clustering of failed attempts followed by success indicates active exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Cross-Check
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable' — detection should verify scanner accuracy against actual running FortiOS versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference your vulnerability scanner results for FortiOS systems against the CVE-2025-68686 patch dates and Federal due-date (2026-08-10). Identify discrepancies: systems flagged as patched but running vulnerable versions, or systems not scanned recently. Prioritize manual verification of critical FortiOS assets.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Hits on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2025-68686 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV implies active exploitation. Pipeline generated no vulnerability-scanning detection despite explicit instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanners and patch management systems for positive detections of CVE-2025-68686 on FortiOS appliances. Flag any systems showing 'vulnerable' status and verify patch status against federal due date (2026-08-10).

suggestion.title: Detect Crafted HTTP Requests to FortiOS Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker...via crafted HTTP requests.' This is the primary exploitation vector and should generate network-based detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual or malformed HTTP requests to known FortiOS appliances (identify by User-Agent, Server banner, or asset tags). Correlate with requests attempting to access /api or admin endpoints from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Symbolic Link Manipulation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This describes persistence/privilege escalation activity pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystems (via EDR or SIEM syslog collection) for symbolic link creation/modification in persistence-relevant directories (/etc, /lib, system startup paths). Correlate with prior unauthorized filesystem access or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Sensitive Information Exposure from FortiOS
