suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2025-68686 as bypassing 'the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' This Defense Evasion technique allows re-establishing persistence despite prior patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symbolic link creation or modification in FortiOS configuration directories (/etc/fortisandbox, /etc/fortimgmt paths, or similar) and FortiOS binary directories. Post-compromise, attackers will recreate symlink persistence to maintain access despite patch.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access in FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article impact is explicit: 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Monitor for exfiltration or abnormal access to FortiOS secrets after exploitation.
log_sources: File access logs (config files, certificates, keys)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful exploitation (crafted HTTP request + symbolic link bypass), attacker will access sensitive data: admin credentials, VPN configurations, SSL certificates, API keys stored in FortiOS config. Hunt for unusual access to /etc/fortisandbox/*, /etc/fortimgmt/*, or FortiOS configuration database files from unexpected processes or users.

suggestion.title: Check Point SmartConsole Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'Authentication Bypass' in SmartConsole; pipeline extracted zero detection logic for this primary attack vector. Expected to find reference to PoC exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SmartConsole management interface HTTP/HTTPS requests with malformed or missing authentication headers, particularly POST requests to login endpoints. Flag requests originating from non-expected source networks or those containing known bypass payloads if disclosed in PoC analysis.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SmartConsole Admin Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass should lead to unauthorized privileged access; article title implies 'Public PoC' means exploitation is practical and likely to spawn admin sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SmartConsole admin console sessions established without corresponding successful credential validation events. Look for API tokens or session cookies issued without prior authentication challenge completion or from anomalous network locations.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Remote Code Execution via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Critical severity and PoC release suggest remote code execution risk once auth bypass is achieved. No RCE detection logic in empty pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SmartConsole server process (wdAdmin, FwM) for unexpected child process creation or remote PowerShell/bash invocation following authentication bypass timeframe. Flag command-line activity originating from SmartConsole service context performing system administration tasks.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Policy Download for Lateral Movement Staging
suggestion.rationale: Management console access typically enables policy exfiltration and network reconnaissance; article implies admin-level access post-bypass, yet no collection/discovery use case present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SmartConsole policy or object export/download operations initiated immediately after session establishment, especially exports of gateway configurations, user lists, or network topology that could inform lateral movement.

suggestion.title: SmartConsole Gateway Rule Modification Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised SmartConsole can be weaponized to disable security controls; no persistence/defense-evasion UC generated despite critical severity and likely attacker objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall rule, access control policy, or logging configuration changes made via SmartConsole shortly after suspicious authentication or session anomalies. Include changes that disable logging, weaken rules, or exempt attacker IPs.

suggestion.title: Exposed API Token Reuse Across Services
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exposed Credentials Across Four Services' — pipeline should detect when single compromised token/key authenticates to multiple disparate cloud/SaaS platforms in short timeframe, indicating automated credential abuse
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events where same token/API key successfully authenticates to 3+ distinct services (Hugging Face, AWS, GitHub, etc.) within 1 hour. Correlate failed login attempts preceding success. Exclude known service-to-service integrations and automation accounts.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Credential Testing Pattern
suggestion.rationale: OpenAI Agent used credentials suggests automated tool testing multiple endpoints — pipeline should detect characteristic agent behavior: rapid sequential auth attempts, consistent user-agent patterns, machine-generated access patterns across services
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bursts of API/login attempts from single source with identical user-agent (esp. agent/automation signatures), targeting multiple service discovery endpoints or account enumeration APIs within minutes. Correlate source IP, token fingerprint, and request timing deltas.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exposed Service Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Breach describes exploitation across four services — pipeline should detect when credentials sourced from one compromised service (e.g., Hugging Face) are weaponized against unrelated services, often with time-lag between compromise and lateral movement
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication failures from stolen credential set against Service A with later successful authentications to Services B, C, D within 24–72 hours. Flag if source IPs, geolocation, or request patterns diverge from historical baseline for compromised credential holder.

suggestion.title: Cross-Service OAuth/Token Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: OpenAI agent compromise likely involved token theft (T1528); article mentions 'credentials' plural — pipeline should detect when single OAuth token or refresh token is replayed across multiple 3rd-party integrations or service boundaries
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor token grant/use logs for single token/session used to authenticate to >2 unrelated service scopes/audiences. Flag token reuse from different IP/device/user-agent than initial grant context. Correlate against OpenAI API logs and agent orchestration logs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Service-to-Service API Call Chain
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should detect when compromised OpenAI API key is used to programmatically invoke other service APIs (aws, github, hugging face) via agent commands, creating telltale call chain across service audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where OpenAI API call logs show agent prompt/completion referencing external service credentials or actions, followed immediately by auth/API activity in those target services. Correlate prompt content keywords (e.g., AWS, GitHub) with downstream service logs.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Agent Inference API
suggestion.rationale: If agent was used to extract or validate stolen credentials by testing them live, pipeline should detect API calls to token validation endpoints, password reset confirmations, or account enumeration queries
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag agent API calls (via OpenAI platform) that invoke credential validation, account lookup, or token-check endpoints across multiple services. High cardinality in target services, low cardinality in returned data. Correlate with failed auth events on same services.

suggestion.title: Git Hook File Creation in Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'plant a Git Hook'—attackers write .git/hooks/* files to persist execution. No detection rule addresses this file-system signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new or modified executable files under .git/hooks/ (pre-commit, post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge). Hook creation by non-admin users or outside normal CI/CD should trigger. Correlate with repository write events.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawned by Git Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article mechanism: 'run shell commands' via hook execution. When git daemon or git pull triggers, child processes launched outside expected git operations (commit, merge) signal hook exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by git.exe/git daemon with suspicious parent lineage or command payloads (curl, PowerShell, bash -c, nc). Establish baseline of legitimate hook commands; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Gitea Configuration or Repository Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Git hooks are stored in repository metadata (.git/hooks/). Article does not detail *how* repository writers gain permission to modify hooks—suggests ACL bypass or Gitea-specific configuration flaw. Missing detection for unauthorized hook configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on changes to .gitconfig, .git/hooks/ permissions, or Gitea repository settings that enable hook execution. Detect modifications by non-admin authenticated users or outside expected workflows.

suggestion.title: Hook Execution Triggered by Git Clone/Pull/Merge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Hooks execute on git operations. Article scenario: repository writer plants hook, another user clones/pulls, hook fires. Must detect hook firing, not just creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate git clone, pull, merge, or checkout events with subsequent unexpected process spawning (shell, curl, powershell, etc.). Baseline should show minimal child process creation from git operations in normal environments.

suggestion.title: Gitea Service Running Under Elevated Privileges Executing User-Supplied Hook Script
suggestion.rationale: RCE impact depends on Gitea service privilege level. If Gitea runs as root or system user, hook execution escalates to full system compromise. Article does not specify but 'RCE' suggests full system access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell or command-line processes spawned by Gitea service (git daemon child processes) executing with elevated UID/GID. Cross-reference against Gitea process privilege level at startup.

suggestion.title: Android RAT Command & Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat found on '170 servers' and describes active RAT infrastructure—RATs require persistent C2 channels to exfiltrate data and receive commands. No UC generated despite this being core RAT behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Android devices establishing outbound connections to suspicious or newly-registered domains, unusual port combinations (high-numbered ports for C2), and encrypted traffic volumes inconsistent with normal app behavior. Flag APK families contacting multiple unrelated C2 endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious APK Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'source code circulates' implying active malware distribution. Pipeline missed detection for initial compromise vector—installation of malicious APK.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK installation bypassing Google Play Store verification, installation from sideloaded sources, or matching known Flying Eagle APK signatures/hashes. Flag devices with installation events preceded by phishing or credential-theft indicators.

suggestion.title: Excessive Permission Requests in Installed APK
suggestion.rationale: Android RATs characteristically request broad permissions (camera, microphone, contacts, location, call logs) for surveillance. Article emphasizes RAT capability but no behavioral detection on permission abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK manifests requesting combinations of CAMERA, RECORD_AUDIO, READ_CONTACTS, READ_CALL_LOG, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION simultaneously. Cross-reference against whitelisted apps; legitimate apps rarely need all five. Trigger on runtime permission grants for high-risk combinations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Mobile Device via RAT
suggestion.rationale: RATs are designed for data theft—article's mention of '170 infected servers' implies active data collection campaigns. Pipeline generated no exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data access patterns: bulk reads from /data/data/, repeated access to credential stores, camera/microphone activation without user interaction, keystroke capture libraries loaded. Correlate with outbound C2 traffic to catch exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Packed Malware Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Source code circulation suggests attackers are actively obfuscating variants to evade static analysis. Pipeline missed defense-evasion phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK files with stripped or obfuscated class names, packed/compressed payloads, dynamic code loading from external sources, or mismatched signatures. Flag DEX files loaded at runtime from /tmp or app cache directories; legitimate apps rarely do this.

suggestion.title: Flying Eagle RAT Malware Signature Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Flying Eagle' as malware family. Pipeline failed to generate any IOC-based or signature-based detections. At minimum, known sample hashes/domains should be matched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create YARA/signature rules for Flying Eagle APK samples if hashes or package names are available in threat intel feeds. Cross-reference device event logs against malware repositories (APKCombo, VirusTotal, ANY.RUN). Alert on process execution matching known Flying Eagle process injection patterns or library loading sequences.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Run RAT When Imported Into Node.js'—indicating code execution via install scripts or require hooks during package load. Pipeline missed this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawning from npm/node processes with unexpected parent relationships (e.g., child shell spawning network utilities). Flag install scripts that execute arbitrary binaries or spawn reverse shells. Correlate with npm install timing.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Network from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT payload 'run when imported'—must establish C2. Pipeline missed C2 detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Node.js/npm processes for expected network destinations. Alert on connections to non-package-repo IPs/domains (e.g., outbound to dynamic IPs, non-standard ports, or known C2 infrastructure). Correlate with recent npm install.

suggestion.title: Known Compromised NPM Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'joyfill' packages as compromised. Pipeline should maintain and query IOC feed for package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs, package-lock.json, node_modules directory creation, and package manager output for known-bad package names or versions. Alert on installation from npm registry of packages on compromise feeds.

suggestion.title: RAT Process Behavior from NPM Context
suggestion.rationale: Payload explicitly identified as 'RAT'—classic post-exploitation behavior (process hollowing, credential stealing, file enumeration) should be detectable if running under Node.js parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for credential access APIs (lsass, SAM), file listing on sensitive paths, or process injection from Node.js child processes. RATs typically enumerate users, list directories, and exfil system info.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Detection—Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Two joyfill packages compromised—suggests either typosquatting, namespace confusion, or account takeover. Pipeline should flag package metadata discontinuities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for package version anomalies: sudden maintainer changes, new versions with suspicious code, package size inflation, or new dependencies added. Cross-reference against known registry mirror logs.

suggestion.title: goshs -b flag without colon separator (credential format validation bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is triggered by `-b 'admin:'` or empty-password config. A UC detecting malformed or semicolon/space-separated auth flags (non-standard syntax) could catch alternative bypass syntax not covered by current regex.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect goshs processes where -b flag syntax deviates from standard colon-delimited user:pass (e.g., spaces, multiple colons, escaped quotes). Capture command line for manual review.

suggestion.title: SFTP authentication accepted despite missing password field (auth state anomaly)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'SFTP accepts connections without password.' A UC correlating SFTP logon success with empty-credential config flags on the local process would directly detect exploitation.
log_sources: Sysmon (EventID 3: network connection + EventID 1: process with empty-cred flags
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SFTP session establishment (event logs or network state) with concurrent goshs process running -b flag without password segment. Low false-positive baseline in production environments.

suggestion.title: goshs version check for v2.1.3 (vulnerable release)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Start goshs v2.1.3 with -b ...' — version pinning is a precise hunting vector. Pipeline should extract version numbers from advisory text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect goshs process execution where version string or help output can be extracted (e.g., from process command line, file properties, or parent execution logs). Correlate against known vulnerable versions from CVE database.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation (CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests.' No detection use case was generated despite this being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for unusual request patterns post-compromise: atypical HTTP methods, malformed headers, or requests targeting known patch-bypass paths. Baseline normal admin/API traffic; alert on deviations combined with 401/403 error spikes or symlink-related filesystem logs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and patch bypass. No use case for detecting symlink manipulation was generated. Article states attacker needs 'filesystem level' access, implying auditable symlink creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on symlink creation/modification in FortiOS directories, especially targeting startup, initialization, or script locations. Correlate with prior exploitation indicators. Look for symlink targets pointing outside expected paths or to world-writable locations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686: Fortinet FortiOS Vulnerability Assessment & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with federal patch deadline 2026-08-10. No vulnerability-scanning or asset-inventory use case was generated despite this being standard CISA KEV protocol (template references `<CVE>` substitution for vulnerability scanner matching).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all systems for Fortinet FortiOS instances with CVE-2025-68686 applied. Track patch date and compare against federal deadline 2026-08-10. Correlate non-patched instances with exposed internet-facing status and prior breach indicators to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Post-Compromise HTTP Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation *after* initial compromise via another vulnerability. Requires detection of anomalous HTTP behavior from already-compromised internal FortiOS devices; pipeline missed this multi-stage correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Fortinet instances flagged with prior-compromise indicators, monitor HTTP requests for: non-admin source IPs, unusual request rates, atypical User-Agent strings, or repeated failures followed by 200 responses. Baseline known-good admin activity; alert on divergence.

suggestion.title: FortiOS: Patch Rollback or Bypass Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'bypass[es] the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No detection for patch-integrity or rollback events. Implies audit log review for patch removal or version downgrades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Fortinet system with a prior-patched CVE-2025-68686 that reverts to an older firmware version, or logs indicating patch removal/bypass. Compare firmware version before/after exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' can reach the vulnerability, implying exposed instances are the prerequisite. Template section explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but no UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiOS instances (product field in config or HTTP headers) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate with CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Baseline: instances should be behind VPN/firewall; any with direct exposure are exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Crafted HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker exploits 'via crafted HTTP requests' to a 'symbolic link persistency mechanism.' No UC for HTTP-level exploitation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS management/API endpoints for anomalous patterns: requests targeting path traversal-like structures, symlink-related paths (e.g., containing '../' or symbolic-link operations), or requests from non-administrative source IPs. CVE-2025-68686 exploit traffic should show crafted payloads before persistence is set.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a post-exploitation persistence indicator the pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Fortinet FortiOS systems, detect creation or modification of symbolic links in sensitive directories (cron, startup scripts, logging paths). Flag any symlink pointing to attacker-controlled executables or configuration files. Post-exploitation, symlinks are the mechanism for maintaining access across reboots.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Filesystem-Level Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level,' indicating multi-stage compromise. Pipeline missed detection for filesystem tampering or secondary exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious filesystem changes on Fortinet FortiOS instances: modifications to /usr/bin, /etc, /var/lib directories; unexpected binary execution with elevated privileges; or process spawning from unusual parent processes. These indicate preliminary compromise via secondary vulnerability before CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Information Access in Fortinet FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'—this data exfiltration or access is the ultimate impact but no detection use case was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or unexpected access to Fortinet FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, or logs (e.g., syslog, diagnostic bundles). Correlate with outbound network activity to C2 infrastructure. Flag reads of /usr/local/bin, /etc/passwd-like files, or config exports by non-administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'via crafted HTTP requests' against FortiOS and CISA KEV status means active exploitation. This is the primary attack vector and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Fortinet FortiOS instances for request patterns associated with CVE-2025-68686 exploitation. Alert on requests bypassing known patches or targeting the symbolic-link persistency bypass. Correlate with asset inventory to identify exposed FortiOS endpoints.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Compromised FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'exposure of sensitive information' post-compromise. Article implies configuration, credentials, or policy data may be accessible to attackers after initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual read access to FortiOS configuration files, certificate stores, or credential databases by system processes. Correlate with outbound network connections to external IPs. Flag if preceded by exploitation of other FortiOS CVEs.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic-Link Persistence Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases,' indicating adversary use of symlinks for maintaining access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan FortiOS filesystem for symbolic links created in startup paths, autoload directories, or system binaries. Monitor for process execution originating from symlinked file paths after exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance and Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-08-10. Article highlights patch-lag risk; rapid asset inventory and remediation tracking is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Fortinet FortiOS systems for CVE-2025-68686 patch status. Identify unpatched instances with exposure to untrusted networks. Flag instances past federal due date 2026-08-10 as critical priority and escalate for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies CVE-2025-68686 and directs analysts to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' with this CVE substituted. Pipeline generated no vulnerability-scanning or asset-inventory UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system and FortiOS inventory for installations vulnerable to CVE-2025-68686. Flag unpatched systems and cross-reference against Federal remediation deadline (2026-08-10) to prioritize patching.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Symbolic Link Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' as the persistence technique deployed after initial filesystem-level compromise. Pipeline failed to suggest filesystem-monitoring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For FortiOS systems with confirmed or suspected compromise, monitor filesystem for symbolic link creation/modification in system and config directories. Alert on symlinks with suspicious targets or creation timing correlating with exploitation signals.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation of FortiOS Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states adversaries bypass security patches 'via crafted HTTP requests' after compromising the product. This exploitation technique should be detected as evidence of active attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For confirmed FortiOS compromises, hunt HTTP request logs for malformed or anomalous patterns targeting known vulnerable endpoints: unusual request methods, invalid headers, or payloads inconsistent with legitimate administrator activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Exposure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly titled 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor.' Pipeline missed the data exfiltration/unauthorized access detection corresponding to the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, detect unauthorized reads/exports of FortiOS configuration files, certificates, VPN credentials, routing tables, or policy objects. Correlate with external C2 or data-staging infrastructure.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Crafted HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote unauthenticated attacker' via 'crafted HTTP requests' targeting FortiOS; this is the primary initial access vector and most detectable phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiOS appliances for anomalous request patterns: malformed requests to admin endpoints (/admin, /system), missing User-Agent headers, unusual character encoding in paths, or requests from external IPs that precede authentication failures or file-system events.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation (CISA KEV) and federal patch due date 2026-08-10; asset inventory must be cross-referenced against CVE-2025-68686 vulnerable builds immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all FortiOS instances and correlate against known-vulnerable versions. Alert on any unpatched instances; escalate post-due-date unpatched assets as critical.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'; this post-compromise technique should be detectable through filesystem monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS system directories for symlink creation, especially targeting /bin, /lib, /var/www, or /opt. Alert when symlinks point outside expected FortiOS installation paths or when symlink events correlate with failed patch updates.

suggestion.title: Pre-Compromise Indicator Hunting on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level'; detection must find evidence of that initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for signs of prior compromise on FortiOS: unauthorized files in web paths, suspicious process execution from web context (perl/python/bash), modified system binaries, or anomalous cron jobs. These may indicate staging for the CVE-2025-68686 exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Unauthenticated Sensitive-Data Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor' via unauthenticated access; detection must track unauthorized reads of configs, credentials, or logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS access logs for successful downloads or reads of sensitive files without corresponding authentication events. Flag API calls or file requests that bypass auth handlers or exploit known auth-bypass vectors.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance Tracker
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-10 is explicitly stated; SOC must automate patch verification and post-remediation testing for compliance auditing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate weekly FortiOS patch-status reports. Escalate unpatched instances at T-72h before due date. Post-patch, verify version via direct checks and retest attack surface. Flag any instances unable to remediate by 2026-08-10.

suggestion.title: FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2025-68686 as indicator to 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan vulnerability assessment logs for Fortinet FortiOS instances flagged as CVE-2025-68686. Prioritize systems matching federal patch-due date (2026-08-10) thresholds. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm remediation status and confirm patch lag.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Crafted HTTP Request Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits via 'crafted HTTP requests' to bypass patch; no detection rule covers malformed/anomalous HTTP traffic to FortiOS endpoints post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS management interfaces (typically port 443, 8443) with unusual payload structures, excessive URL encoding, or symlink-traversal patterns. Correlate with prior filesystem access indicators or known-compromised internal IPs.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism' and bypass attempts; no file-system-level monitoring for symlink creation or manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symbolic link creation/modification in FortiOS application directories (/bin, /etc, /lib, /var) and in paths accessible post-exploit (temp, cache, backup directories). Correlate with prior filesystem-level compromise signals.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Service Restart and Patch Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass of 'patch developed for symbolic link persistency'; detection should cover instances where patched versions are re-exploited or service restarts occur in attack context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiOS service restarts (fortid, httpsd, etc.) occurring after HTTP requests matching the crafted-request pattern. Flag restarts within 5 minutes of anomalous file-system activity or unpatched version indicators.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploit Chain Detection (Filesystem Access → FortiOS Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies two-stage attack: 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' before exploiting FortiOS via HTTP. No rule detects this chained pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate filesystem-level compromise indicators (file writes to FortiOS application paths, unpatched CVE detections) within 1 hour of subsequent crafted HTTP requests to FortiOS. Flag accounts or source IPs that trigger both signals.

suggestion.title: Abnormal HTTP Requests to FortiOS Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploit vulnerability 'via crafted HTTP requests' to bypass authentication. Pipeline missed the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS administrative interfaces for unauthenticated or malformed HTTP requests that bypass expected authentication flows. Flag requests with unusual headers, Content-Type manipulations, or path traversal patterns targeting /admin or config endpoints. Baseline normal admin traffic and alert on significant deviations.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Creation and Filesystem-Level Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases.' This is a persistence vector the pipeline completely ignored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of symbolic links in FortiOS directories (/var, /etc, config directories). Alert on symlink targets pointing to sensitive files like credential stores, configuration files, or system binaries. Combine with privilege elevation events to identify post-exploitation persistence.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline failed to map information disclosure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized access to FortiOS configuration files, credential stores, or system files that contain sensitive information. Detect egress patterns of FortiOS config exports or authentication tokens. Flag access to files known to contain API keys, VPN credentials, or policy settings from unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Patch Compliance and Asset Exposure

suggestion.rationale: Attackers perform reconnaissance to locate SmartConsole instances before exploitation. Public PoC availability increases reconnaissance activity. Pipeline generated no discovery-phase detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning targeting SmartConsole standard ports (4434, 4435, 443) or banner-grabbing attempts. Alert on connection attempts from external IP ranges with no legitimate business justification. Track TLS/SSL certificate queries for Check Point SmartConsole hostnames.

suggestion.title: Automated Agent Credential Misuse Across Multiple Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes an OpenAI agent using 'exposed credentials across four services'—clear lateral movement via stolen tokens. Pipeline missed the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single API key or service principal authenticating from unusual geographic regions, multiple cloud platforms, or with anomalous call patterns (rapid permission checks, data enumeration). Correlate authentication logs across AWS, Azure, GCP, and third-party SaaS for tokens originating from a common source.

suggestion.title: Credential Exposure Detection in Source Code Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Hugging Face is a model-sharing platform; 'exposed credentials' likely means secrets committed or leaked in model configs, notebooks, or training scripts. Pipeline ignored the supply-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on hardcoded API keys, auth tokens, or secrets detected in notebook cells, model card YAML, or configuration commits. Flag patterns matching known token formats (OpenAI API keys, Azure tokens, AWS credentials). Monitor for bulk secret scanning or automated repository enumeration.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Command Execution via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: An OpenAI agent using exposed credentials suggests autonomous command execution or tool invocation. Article states agent 'used' credentials across services—implies actions, not just access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for API calls originating from unexpected geographic regions or IP ranges, rapid execution of privileged operations by service principals tied to ML platforms, and tool-use logs from LLM systems showing curl/wget/python subprocess calls to external services.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Data Exfiltration via API Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Four services compromised implies systematic data access post-breach. Pipeline did not model exfiltration queries or batch download patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline API call volume per token/service principal. Alert on: bulk ListBuckets/ListBlobs, repeated 403 Forbidden errors followed by successful auth (permission enumeration), high-volume GET requests to APIs typically accessed for metadata, or exfiltration patterns (request size growth, unusual file extensions downloaded).

suggestion.title: AI/ML Platform Token Misuse Pattern
suggestion.rationale: OpenAI agent + Hugging Face + three other services suggests attacker specifically targeting ML infrastructure. Pipeline failed to map this vertical-specific attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API keys created or rotated outside normal deployment windows, service principals with broad ML/compute permissions being added to teams, and OAuth tokens with scopes tied to model training or inference APIs showing anomalous usage patterns.

suggestion.title: Git Hook Directory Modification by Repository Writers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Repository Writers Plant a Git Hook'—direct evidence of writes to .git/hooks/ as the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or modification events targeting .git/hooks/* directories, especially unexpected writes by users with repository push access. Correlate with repository access logs and user permission levels. Flag writes outside normal deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: Shell Process Execution Triggered by Git Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states hooks 'run shell commands'—detection must capture arbitrary process spawning when git operations (clone, pull, push) trigger hook scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell process spawning (cmd.exe, bash, sh) with parent process git or git-shell, especially with anomalous command-line arguments or network I/O. Track process lineage from git to unprivileged shell invocations on servers running Gitea.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access by Low-Privilege or External Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires repository writer permissions; detection should flag permission escalation or lateral movement to gain write access for planting hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when users not in standard developer/maintainer groups gain push permissions to repositories. Monitor for repository permission changes immediately preceding suspicious commits containing hook installations. Correlate Gitea authentication logs with unexpected write operations.

suggestion.title: Git Configuration Manipulation via Hook Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Planted hooks can also modify git config to persist backdoors or exfiltrate credentials; detection must cover dynamic hook behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of git config commands within hook scripts or processes spawned by git hooks. Flag modifications to .git/config or credential helpers that point to external binaries or URLs. Monitor for hook scripts that execute multi-stage payloads.

suggestion.title: Gitea Repository Clone/Pull on Compromised Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Victims trigger RCE by cloning/pulling from backdoored repositories; detection on endpoints should catch malicious hook execution when developers interact with poisoned repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor developer machines for git clone/pull operations followed immediately by unexpected child process spawning, DNS queries, or outbound connections. Establish baseline for expected shells/scripts spawned per repository; alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gitea API Calls for Permission Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first obtain or abuse writer permissions; Gitea API logs are the earliest detection point for privilege escalation leading to hook injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PUT/PATCH requests to Gitea API endpoints modifying collaborator/organization member permissions, especially if followed by rapid push events or .git/hooks modifications. Correlate with account compromise indicators (password resets, MFA bypass attempts).

suggestion.title: Android APK Installation—Unsigned or Anomalous Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'source code circulates' + RAT family name establish attacker access to tooling; implies widespread deployment attempts. No execution-phase detection created despite this being immediate post-compromise activity for any Android RAT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK installation via non-standard package managers, unsigned APK execution, admin privilege grants to unknown APK installers, or package management invocations outside normal MDM windows. Correlate package names and signatures against Flying Eagle indicators if leaked source contains build artifacts.

suggestion.title: Android RAT—Command & Control Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states traces 'found on 170 servers'—these are likely C2 infrastructure or malware distribution hubs. Remote Access Trojan by definition phones home; no C2 communication detection generated despite immediate post-execution visibility window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP/DNS traffic from Android processes to known Flying Eagle C2 servers identified from 170-server analysis. Flag periodic beaconing patterns, non-standard HTTP User-Agents, or communication with infrastructure hardened against introspection.

suggestion.title: Android RAT—Sensitive Data Exfiltration (Contacts, SMS, Location)
suggestion.rationale: RAT threat model includes data theft; article describes 'traces' of malware on 170 servers (suggesting forensic footprint of activity). No exfiltration detection created despite high-value data targets (SMS, contacts, location, call logs) being primary RAT payloads on mobile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android processes requesting CONTACTS, SMS, CALL_LOG, or FINE_LOCATION permissions, followed by bulk reads from those content providers, then unusual network egress. Flag compression/encryption of sensitive file types preceding external data transfer.

suggestion.title: Android RAT—Boot Persistence via Receiver Registration
suggestion.rationale: Source code leaked means threat actors can harden persistence. Article threat model is sustained compromise; no persistence-phase UC generated despite BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast hijack being standard Android RAT technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on dynamic registration of broadcast receivers targeting BOOT_COMPLETED, PACKAGE_ADDED, or CONNECTIVITY_CHANGE by non-system APKs. Flag services started by Flying Eagle package names with persistent foreground intent or notification listeners.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance—Scanning from Known Flying Eagle C2/Distribution Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: '170 servers'—source infrastructure for malware/source-code distribution. If any are attacker-controlled, they become scanners for new targets. No initial-access-phase reconnaissance UC despite obvious pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning, mass HTTP GET requests, or SSL certificate enumeration originating from IP ranges/ASNs hosting Flying Eagle infrastructure. Alert on reconnaissance traffic patterns (SYN scans, OS fingerprinting) from known server IPs toward internal network ranges.

suggestion.title: npm Package Import Followed by Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT 'when imported into Node.js'—core attack vector is execution triggered at require() time, yet pipeline generated no detection for abnormal process spawning from Node context post-import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js or npm processes spawning unexpected cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash immediately after package import operations. Establish baseline for normal development process trees and alert on deviations (e.g., network tools, encoding utilities post-require).

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Connections Initiated by Node.js Process Post-Package Import
suggestion.rationale: RAT capability implies command-and-control communication; article specifies 'Remote Access Trojan' but pipeline missed network-based detection of abnormal egress from Node.js to external endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound TCP/UDP from node.exe to non-whitelisted IPs/domains, especially to residential ISP ranges, dynamic DNS services, or ports atypical for npm operations. Correlate timing with recent package installation.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise Detection — Malicious npm Package Metadata Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies specific compromised packages by name; pipeline failed to create detection for suspicious package characteristics (version jumps, maintainer changes, registry manipulation) that precede supply-chain RAT deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious npm package registration patterns: new maintainer on long-dormant project, sudden version spike, rapid re-releases, or package takeover via account compromise. Flag packages with download anomalies (flat trend → sudden spike) preceding vulnerability disclosures.

suggestion.title: Node.js Require() Resolving Obfuscated or Dynamic Module Code
suggestion.rationale: Attack is triggered 'when imported'—payload is likely embedded in package source with obfuscation or dynamic resolution to evade static analysis; pipeline did not suggest AST-level or require-hook detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan imported package source for eval(), Function(), indirect require() calls, or base64-encoded payloads. Flag packages with require() resolution to external domains or non-standard module paths. Use Node.js loader hooks to intercept and analyze module initialization.

suggestion.title: Post-Import Credential Access or Data Exfiltration from Application Context
suggestion.rationale: RAT functionality includes credential theft and data exfiltration; article does not detail specifics but pipeline missed detection for access to .env, secrets, or configuration files post-package import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes reading sensitive files (.env, .npmrc, SSH keys, .aws/credentials) immediately post-import, followed by encoding/compression and network transmission. Alert on accessing parent application secrets or database connection strings.

suggestion.title: npm Package Persistence via Script Injection in package.json or .bin/ Directory
suggestion.rationale: For RAT to survive application restarts, payload likely persists via postinstall scripts or .bin/ injection; article title does not exclude persistence, yet pipeline generated zero persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious additions to package.json 'scripts' fields (postinstall, prestart, prepare hooks calling external binaries or network utilities). Monitor node_modules/.bin/ for unexpected executables or symlinks created post-install.

suggestion.title: ClickHouse escapeValue() bypass: trailing backslash-quote injection in query logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'trailing backslash to escape the closing quote' as the attack mechanism. This pattern must be detected in the actual ClickHouse query logs where escapeValue() executes, not inferred from HTTP logs. Article says: 'Attackers who can control parameter values can inject arbitrary SQL by using a trailing backslash to escape the closing quote.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns in ClickHouse query logs where parameter-placeholder values contain backslash-quote sequences (`\'`, `\"`) followed by SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, FROM, information_schema, etc.). Correlate with @hypequery/clickhouse version < 2.0.2 to confirm exploitability.

suggestion.title: SQL parsing error: ClickHouse rejecting malformed escapeValue() output
suggestion.rationale: Failed parameter substitution due to the escapeValue() bug may surface in error logs before SQL execution. Article describes the vulnerability in the escaping function itself—detection of failures at that layer catches exploitation attempts early.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ClickHouse and application error logs for SQL syntax/parse errors containing keywords like 'escape', 'quote', 'parameter binding', or error codes associated with malformed SQL. Baseline acceptable error rates and alert on spikes, especially from endpoints known to accept user parameters.

suggestion.title: ClickHouse information_schema enumeration post-SQLi (discovery phase)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary SQL execution' is possible post-injection. Attackers typically pivot to schema enumeration to identify tables and columns for data exfiltration. Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior, but this is a standard follow-on to SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify queries against ClickHouse information schema tables (information_schema.*, system.databases, system.tables) originating from untrusted application endpoints or users not normally running DDL queries. Compare baseline—flag deviations indicating reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unusual ClickHouse query complexity and result-set size post-SQLi (data exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers use 'arbitrary SQL' to exfiltrate data. Article does not specify payload tactics, but bulk data extraction is the natural objective of gaining code execution. Need hunt for unusual egress patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickHouse queries with exceptionally high result-set cardinality, long execution time (> baseline + 3σ), or complex JOIN/UNION operators from parameter-driven application queries. Cross-check with network baseline for unusual bulk data transfer from the ClickHouse server to external hosts.

suggestion.title: WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite header after DELETE rejection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'with `Overwrite: T` it additionally performs an explicit `RemoveAll` on the destination'—the attacker's exploitation path is attempting DELETE, seeing it blocked, then sending MOVE with Overwrite header to bypass the protection. This specific sequence is the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DELETE request (HTTP 403) on a WebDAV path followed within 2 seconds by a MOVE request on the same source path with 'Overwrite: T' header present in the request. This sequence indicates active exploitation of the CVE-2026-64863 bypass.

suggestion.title: goshs destination file overwrite via WebDAV MOVE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states MOVE 'additionally performs an explicit `RemoveAll` on the destination'—this is an overwrite attack where an attacker moves a file to an existing destination to destroy it. Must detect MOVE operations targeting paths that already exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MOVE HTTP requests to WebDAV paths where the destination file/directory already exists prior to the MOVE, combined with Filesystem events showing the destination being deleted or modified immediately after. This indicates file destruction via MOVE overwrite.

suggestion.title: goshs flag extraction and vulnerability assessment
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerable configuration detection should also enumerate all process flags to confirm --no-delete is genuinely enabled. Article implies --no-delete should prevent deletion, so baseline must confirm the flag is present AND WebDAV mode is enabled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract full command-line from goshs processes and parse/normalize flags to confirm --no-delete is present AND (-w or --webdav) is present AND no other flags that might override behavior. Flag this as vulnerable configuration requiring urgent patching.

suggestion.title: goshs process execution with colon-terminated or empty-field credential syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly demonstrates the vulnerability via '-b admin:' syntax (empty password after colon). Process detection must regex-match this specific anti-pattern to catch incomplete remediation of CVE-2026-40884.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on goshs process execution where -b flag argument matches regex ^([^:]*):$|^:([^:]*)$ (either empty username or empty password), combined with -sftp flag and absence of -fkf mitigation flag.

suggestion.title: SFTP authentication session missing password phase or accepting empty password
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SFTP accepting connections without password validation. SSH/SFTP server logs should show authentication events where password stage is absent or field empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH authentication logs for SFTP subsystem invocations where password field is empty or missing from auth log entries, or SSH packets show successful auth without user-auth service payload.

suggestion.title: External SFTP client sessions to goshs without prior successful authentication handshake
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated connections being accepted. Inbound connections to goshs SFTP port followed immediately by file operations (without standard SSH key exchange / password challenge in logs) indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to SFTP port where SSH protocol state transitions directly from key-exchange to channel-open without user-auth service, or time between connection initiation and file-operation logging is <2 seconds.

suggestion.title: goshs version identification preceding empty-credential SFTP attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attackers enumerate goshs version before exploitation to confirm CVE-2026-62325 presence. Banner-grab or error-message enumeration followed by unauthenticated SFTP access indicates reconnaissance-to-exploit chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SSH banner requests or version queries to SFTP port with subsequent authentication attempts using empty credentials within 60-second window from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Targeting Web Hosting Control Panels
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes attackers weaponizing GitHub Actions runners to target cPanel and WHM—runners executing commands or network connections to control-plane ports (2087/TCP, 2083/TCP) represent direct attack signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub Actions workflows establish outbound connections to cPanel/WHM default ports (2087, 2083, 2086) or when runner processes spawn command shells (PowerShell, bash, cmd) with arguments targeting known web hosting infrastructure ranges or well-known cPanel/WHM HTTP endpoints.

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Actor Creating Malicious Workflow Targeting External Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: To weaponize runners against external targets, attacker must first commit malicious .github/workflows YAML. Article indicates GitHub is the initial foothold; detection should flag abnormal workflow file creation by compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub workflow file commits from accounts with recent compromise signals (unusual geolocation, first-time 3AM push, account takeover indicators). Prioritize workflows with obfuscated shell code, external action invocations from unvetted publishers, or runs that bypass branch protection rules.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Process Executing Lateral Movement Tools to Remote Server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes runners targeting cPanel/WHM, implying SSH/RDP reconnaissance or exploitation. Runners spawning ssh-keyscan, nmap, or RDP client against external IPs constitute direct attack indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub Actions runner execution events with outbound SSH (22, 2222) or RDP (3389) connection attempts within same workflow run. Alert if runner process list includes ssh-keyscan, nmap, or hydra-style credential tools alongside network traffic to private/datacenter IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Bulk Authentication Failures Against cPanel/WHM from GitHub Infrastructure IP Space
suggestion.rationale: Attackers abuse GitHub runner infrastructure (AWS/Azure-hosted) to brute-force or credential-spray cPanel admin accounts. Article identifies cPanel/WHM as targets; detection should correlate failed logins from runner provider ASNs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel/WHM authentication event logs for velocity anomalies: 5+ failed login attempts in 60 seconds from single IP, or failed logins from IPs residing in AWS/Azure/GCP ASNs. Correlate with GitHub Actions runner IP blocks or cloud provider CIDR ranges.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets Accessed During Workflow Targeting External Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attacker-controlled workflows reference stored SSH keys or cPanel credentials from GitHub Secrets to authenticate to target servers. Article implies credential reuse from pipeline to targets.
log_sources: Workflow run logs with secret references
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflow runs that reference SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, CPANEL_PASSWORD, or host-targeting secrets during steps that also execute network commands or spawn shells. Flag if secrets are accessed by workflows in repositories not owning those secrets (cross-repo exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Anomalous cPanel/WHM Administrative Activity from Compromised Runner Identity
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attacker uses stolen credentials from runner to access cPanel admin console and modify hosting configurations. Article implies infrastructure takeover; admin console logins from unusual geolocation/time represent impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel/WHM admin console for logins from IPs NOT in customer's known location history, or from cloud provider geolocation when customer is on-premises. Alert if admin session creates new hosting accounts, modifies DNS, or exports account data immediately after login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Scanner and Patch Compliance Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' + 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-10'. Baseline scanner query for active exploitation is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Fortinet FortiOS instances for CVE-2025-68686 presence. Flag unpatched systems and enforce remediation tracking against federal due date 2026-08-10. Correlate patch lag with unauthorized access attempts.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Patterns Targeting FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass the patch developed... via crafted HTTP requests.' Requires HTTP-level behavioral detection post-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP access logs for request patterns consistent with patch-bypass exploitation: unusual User-Agent strings, malformed headers, encoded URI paths, or requests to sensitive endpoints from unauthenticated sources. Baseline against known CVE-2025-68686 PoC patterns.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistency Filesystem Abuse Post-Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases... attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Requires correlation of initial access with symlink creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirming initial compromise via unknown CVE (monitor for unexpected process execution, config file access), detect creation of new symbolic links in FortiOS system paths (e.g., /bin, /lib, config directories). Alert on symlink targets pointing to attacker-controlled or temporary storage locations.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Staging and Exfiltration After Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'may allow... exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' Pipeline must emit collection/exfil detection post-symlink establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise (after symlink persistence is established), detect access to sensitive FortiOS config files, certificate stores, or credential repositories. Monitor for unusual archive creation (tar, zip), compression, or bulk file reads followed by network transmission or staging in temp directories.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE Exploitation Chain: Initial Access → Filesystem Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline must map the two-stage attack (initial CVE unknown, then CVE-2025-68686 exploit).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected FortiOS service restarts, privilege escalation attempts, or process spawning with subsequent filesystem-level exploitation (symlink creation, config file modifications). Flag time-to-symlink windows <4h, indicating rapid post-initial-access persistence installation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Exploitation via Crafted HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'via crafted HTTP requests' bypass patches on FortiOS to exploit this CVE. Pipeline ignored the article's direct instruction to 'substitute this CVE' into asset-exposure hunt templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS HTTP endpoints for requests attempting to bypass patch verification mechanisms or targeting known vulnerable paths. Alert on crafted payloads with unusual parameter combinations, path traversal sequences, or symlink-related URIs coinciding with known post-compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Sensitive Information Access Following Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability's core impact is 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor.' No detection rule was generated to monitor for unauthorized access to FortiOS config, credentials, or certificates post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate administrative access to sensitive FortiOS data repositories. Alert on anomalous access patterns to system configuration files, certificate stores, or credential vaults—particularly bulk reads or access from non-administrative processes following exploitation attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker bypassing 'the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism'—a post-exploitation persistence vector. No detection mapped to this filesystem-level technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS filesystem for symlink creation in system library paths, patch verification directories, and startup locations. Alert on symlinks created during or immediately after failed patch installation, failed security updates, or known CVE exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Fortinet Compromise: Upstream Vulnerability Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level.' Pipeline failed to map the prerequisite compromise as a distinct kill chain phase requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exploitation attempts against unpatched Fortinet vulnerabilities (accessible from network) with subsequent CVE-2025-68686 exploitation attempts on same asset within 48-72 hour window. Flag multi-stage compromise patterns where upstream CVE breach precedes CVE-2025-68686 exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiOS Patch Status Discrepancy: Scanner vs. Ground Truth
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends 'one quick check across your fleet' despite scanner assertions. Pipeline provided no hunt for patch-status verification despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate vulnerability scanner reported patch status against ground-truth FortiOS version/build via CLI, API, or config inspection. Flag instances reported 'not vulnerable' but running versions in CVE-2025-68686 affected range—indicates scanner signature lag or version detection failure.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Patch-Bypass HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uses 'crafted HTTP requests' to 'bypass the patch' — this is the delivery mechanism and must be detectable via request pattern anomalies or HTTP log inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiOS management/web interfaces (typical ports 80, 443, 8443) for non-standard User-Agent strings, suspicious parameter combinations, or byte sequences known to trigger CVE-2025-68686 bypass logic. Flag requests from external subnets or unusual ASNs to known FortiOS instances.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Symbolic Link Persistence Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article refers to 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases' — once initial compromise achieved via another vuln, attacker establishes persistence via symlinks, which is filesystem-level and auditable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of symbolic links in Fortinet FortiOS directories (esp. config, persistence, startup paths). Correlate symlink creation with failed patch validation or unauthorized configuration changes within same host within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Initial Compromise via Chained Vulnerability (Pre-cursor to CVE-2025-68686)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker would need first to have compromised the product via another vulnerability, at filesystem level' — the attack chain is two-stage, and the first stage must be detected to prevent progression to patch bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exploitation attempts against known Fortinet pre-auth RCE/path-traversal vulns that would establish filesystem-level access (e.g., CLI injection, unauthenticated API abuse). Correlate with subsequent Fortinet process spawning unusual shells or file I/O patterns.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS External Asset Scanning & Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV categorization implies attackers are actively scanning for exposed Fortinet FortiOS appliances; reconnaissance probes should precede exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-velocity, targeted port scans (80, 443, 8443, 10000-10010, 541, 904) originating from external IPs querying hostnames matching Fortinet appliance naming patterns. Correlate scan source IPs against threat intel feeds for known scanning infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from Fortinet FortiOS Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor' — once compromised, attacker retrieves configs, credentials, VPN tables, firewall rules; this outbound or lateral access must be observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file transfer or base64-encoded data transmission from Fortinet FortiOS processes (sslvpnd, ipsengine, fgfmd, etc.). Alert on SSH/SCP outbound from FortiOS to unusual external hosts, or HTTPS POST requests with large payloads to attacker C2 domains post-compromise window.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiOS Configuration Tampering & Backup Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploit phase likely involves configuration dump or credential harvesting from FortiOS database/filesystem. Detection of unauthorized config.sys access or backup operations is critical forensic indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation (tar, zip, openssl, base64) spawned from Fortinet admin/root context within 10 minutes of earlier compromise indicators. Alert on file read operations targeting FortiOS system database files (system.conf, factory.conf, vpn configuration stores).

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-68686 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with CVE-2025-68686 as primary hunting IOC; template referenced in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results against FortiOS asset inventory for CVE-2025-68686. Federal patch due 2026-08-10; prioritise any unpatched instances given active exploitation in CISA KEV.

suggestion.title: Symbolic Link Persistence Detection on FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'symbolic link persistency mechanism observed in some post-exploit cases'—indicates filesystem-level persistence vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS host filesystems for suspicious symlink creation in critical directories (e.g., /bin, /sbin, FortiOS app paths). Focus on symlinks pointing to sensitive config or binary locations written after exploitation dates.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Request Bypass Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'bypass the patch developed for the symbolic link persistency mechanism...via crafted HTTP requests'; indicates HTTP-layer exploitation attempts post-patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiOS administrative interfaces (typically port 443/8443) for anomalous HTTP request patterns: malformed headers, oversized payloads, unusual HTTP methods, or request sequences matching known bypass signatures. Flag unauthenticated requests with suspicious payload structures.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Information Exfiltration from FortiOS
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor'; implies data read/export capability requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiOS log exports, config file reads, or large data transfers from FortiOS to external IPs. Monitor for CLI commands targeting sensitive directories (/var/log, /etc/passwd equivalents). Correlate with successful HTTP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch Re-exploitation Attempts Against FortiOS
