suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Authentication Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—collection phase is the actual impact, not login alone. Zero collection-phase use cases despite this being stated consequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to FMC, detect unusual data access: bulk policy exports, device topology queries, firewall rule downloads, especially if followed by data staging or transfer to external IP space.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles demand vulnerability scanning; pipeline extracted zero scanner-correlation rules despite explicit CVE and product name in article body. Vuln scanning is the primary detection vector for patch-due compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on positive CVE-2026-20316 detection in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. Prioritize any findings on internet-exposed or untrusted-network-adjacent FMC instances. Correlate with authentication logs to prioritize remediation before federal due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Privilege Escalation from Hard-Coded Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states low-privileged account access but consequence is sensitive data—implies either over-permissioned account or post-login escalation. Zero privilege escalation detections despite this logical path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to elevate privileges from low-privileged hard-coded account: API calls to add admin users, modify RBAC roles, access restricted configs. Flag any permission grants or role changes initiated by or affecting known hard-coded credentials.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Firewall Policy Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized FMC access enables firewall policy bypass or logging disablement. Article describes data access but operational impact (T1562) is implicit—pipeline missed defense-evasion phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC policy and rule modifications initiated by low-privileged accounts or hard-coded credentials. Alert on rules permitting traffic to sensitive subnets, disabling logging, or inserting implicit-allow rules. Correlate with authentication spike to identify attacker probing.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' — FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305, 8307) should not be internet-accessible. This is the initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections to known Cisco FMC management ports from untrusted external sources. FMC is a central security appliance; any direct external access represents exploitation of CVE-2026-20316 or similar management interface vulnerabilities.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detect pattern of credential reuse, default account login, or authentication from anomalous sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known default or low-privilege accounts from unexpected source IPs, especially outside business hours or with rapid repeat attempts characteristic of credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Configuration Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: After login, article indicates attackers will 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — FMC holds firewall policies, VPN configs, threat intel. Detect enumeration activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for unusual policy queries, rule exports, device inventory dumps, or configuration reads by recently-authenticated accounts, especially those associated with hard-coded or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Bypass From Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Cisco FMC controls firewall rules and segmentation policies. Compromise of FMC is a pivot point to disable or modify protections; detect lateral movement originating from FMC post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-standard outbound connections from FMC management interface to protected internal subnets (e.g., SSH, RDP, SMB to servers/endpoints FMC does not normally manage directly).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanning Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (active exploitation). Attackers actively probe for Cisco FMC. Detect scanner traffic and version fingerprinting attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco FMC endpoints that match known vulnerability scanning signatures for CVE-2026-20316, including version detection attempts and hard-coded credential/default account probing patterns.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article objective is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — FMC stores network policies, VPN credentials, threat intelligence. Detect bulk export or exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers from FMC to external IPs, bulk policy/configuration exports to compressed formats, or database dumps by non-administrative or recently-compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match—Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly designates CVE-2026-20316 as CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild). Any scanner detection should trigger immediate investigation. Article: 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and 'Federal due-date dates...frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all vulnerability scanner matches for CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC). Cross-reference patch management systems to identify unpatched instances. Escalate any unpatched occurrences as critical given active exploitation and federal due date of 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure—Internet-Facing Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit, indicating exposure to untrusted networks. Article: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets.' FMC management interface should never be internet-facing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC admin interfaces (port 443 or custom mgmt ports) reachable from WAN/internet via network scans or reverse DNS/shodan queries. Correlate with internal CMDB to flag misconfigured exposures. Prioritize remediation of externally-facing instances given active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication with Hard-coded/Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credentials are a default-account variant (T1078.002/T1078.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins by known default/low-privilege account names from unexpected source IPs or outside business hours. Flag successful authentication attempts immediately following failed attempts (possible brute force of hard-coded password).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'allow...remote attacker to...access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detection must cover Collection phase after credential compromise; low-privilege accounts should not normally query security policies or device inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for data access/export operations by low-privilege authenticated accounts. Flag queries to sensitive objects (firewall rules, device configs, credentials, policy sets). Establish baseline of normal low-privilege operations and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exploitation Attempt Detection—Network Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation 'observed in the wild' means attack tooling/patterns exist. Article: CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited.' Network-level detection of known exploit attempts protects before successful auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS signatures or WAF rules for known CVE-2026-20316 exploit patterns against Cisco FMC endpoints. Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests containing hard-coded credential payloads or known exploit proof-of-concepts targeting FMC admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. This is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases; detection must capture successful logins using known default/hard-coded FMC credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC systems using documented default accounts or hard-coded credential patterns. Correlate failed login attempts (credential spray) followed by successful login. Flag logins from untrusted source IPs to FMC management ports (8300-8302, 443).

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Exposure - CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote attacker' + CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Article body references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated zero use cases. Unpatched systems represent immediate risk with 2026-08-01 due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20316 detections. Cross-reference Cisco FMC systems with network exposure logs—flag systems reachable from untrusted networks. Alert on unpatched FMC systems with patch lag relative to 2026-08-01 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access on Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed post-compromise collection detection. Once credential access is achieved, abnormal data retrieval must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API logs for abnormal bulk data exports, high-volume policy/credential object queries, or data transfers from newly-authenticated accounts. Alert on exfiltration of firewall rules, access control policies, or credential storage to external systems.

suggestion.title: FMC Default Account Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password implies attacker may enumerate or brute-force account names. Article does not explicitly describe but is standard attack pattern for credential-based exploitation. Pipeline should have modeled discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication attempts against FMC using default account names (admin, root, cisco variants). Alert on credential spray attacks using known default account lists against FMC management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Within Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker logs in 'using a low-privileged account' then accesses 'sensitive data'—implies privilege escalation within system to reach administrative resources. Pipeline kill chain omitted privilege-escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC role/permission changes tied to newly-authenticated low-privilege accounts. Alert on API calls requiring admin privilege from low-privilege context. Flag session token elevation or unauthorized function access by compromised account.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Downstream Firewall Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC is management plane for Cisco firewall fleet. Compromise of FMC with 'sensitive data' access likely includes firewall configuration/policy data enabling lateral compromise of managed devices. Pipeline did not model lateral movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual FMC-to-firewall management traffic patterns following FMC compromise. Alert on policy pushes from compromised FMC to large firewall fleet subsets. Monitor for unauthorized firewall configuration changes originating from FMC.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can login—implies internet-facing management interface. Pipeline omitted the canonical asset-exposure hunt for internet-reachable FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances reachable on internet-facing networks (default HTTPS port 443, legacy 8305). Flag any CVE-2026-20316 detections. Cross-reference firmware versions against patch status; unpatched instances are immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Login Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes login 'using a low-privileged account'—the core attack is authentication via hard-coded password. Pipeline missed detection for exploitation-in-progress via credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication endpoints for successful logins from non-administrative source IPs, especially following repeated login failures or network scanning. Alert on sessions authenticating with default/low-privileged account credentials where audit trail does not match expected admin activity. Correlate with external scanning data to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detection should cover unauthorized data queries and exports after authentication compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC database queries or bulk exports (configuration backups, rule exports, threat intelligence dumps, firewall logs) initiated by low-privileged or anomalous accounts. Flag non-interactive data access (API calls, bulk downloads) outside change-management windows or by unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Status and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date 2026-08-01 specified in article—remediation hunt must validate patch deployment before exploitation window closes. Pipeline should have generated patch-compliance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 detections. Cross-reference with patch management system to confirm Cisco FMC firmware is updated to patched versions. Identify all unpatched instances and remediation status; escalate any remaining unpatched instances past 2026-08-01 as critical compliance breach.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' per templates. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure UCs despite this being primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC default management ports (443, 8305, 8307) for external access. Alert on successful authentication from internet-facing sources. Cross-reference with asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for confirmed instances.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation: FMC Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'hard-coded password' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' This is the exploitation mechanism—no detection UC generated for actual attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC authentication using low-privileged default accounts from external IPs. Monitor for patterns matching known hard-coded credential attempts. Flag anomalous geographic/ASN origins.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access: FMC Configuration and Policy Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation grants 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC contains firewall policies, network configs, and threat feeds. No UC generated despite explicit data compromise impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk configuration exports, policy backups, and database extractions from FMC. Alert on unusual API calls querying device configs, network objects, or access control rules. Flag file transfers of FMC archives.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Hunt: Vulnerable Cisco FMC Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal deadline 2026-08-01. No UC generated to identify systems running vulnerable versions despite CISA KEV status indicating active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset/vulnerability scanner for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center/Firepower Management Center versions. Alert on vulnerable versions pre-2026-08-01 patch date. Prioritize internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: FMC Service Enumeration and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active reconnaissance and exploitation in wild. Article describes remote exploitation requiring pre-attack discovery. No reconnaissance-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scanning and service enumeration targeting FMC ports (8305, 8307, 443). Monitor for banner grabbing and version detection probes from external sources. Correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Redis Lua Script RCE Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'RCE Exploit' built by researchers; Lua scripting is the primary Redis attack vector for code execution. Pipeline missed detection rule for eval/evalsha commands with suspicious script content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis for EVAL or EVALSHA commands with suspiciously large payloads or script content attempting OS command execution. Look for SCRIPT LOAD followed by EVALSHA patterns typical of staged RCE delivery. Correlate with outbound network connections from Redis process.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Redis Exploitation Attempt (Known CVE-less Behavior)
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'Redis Zero-Days' explicitly; pipeline should detect anomalous Redis protocol use before CVE publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Redis service listening on public-facing port (6379, 6380) with AUTH failures or unauthenticated PING/INFO followed by complex protocol commands that don't match normal client behavior patterns. Establish baseline of legitimate Redis operations first.

suggestion.title: Kimi K3 Agent Execution or Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article headline names 'Kimi K3 Agents' as the exploit actor; should create behavior-based or hash-based detection for this toolset if samples are available post-analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Kimi K3 agent samples are recovered, generate process behavior signatures (parent-child chains, DLL injection, named pipes). Monitor for tool-specific network signatures or C2 callback patterns. Cross-reference against YARA rules from initial research disclosure.

suggestion.title: Post-Redis-Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful RCE ('built RCE exploit'); should detect lateral movement from compromised Redis host to internal network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH, SMB, or RDP connections initiated from Redis process or user context post-compromise. Flag unusual outbound connection attempts to non-standard ports from the affected Redis host. Baseline legitimate Redis admin traffic first.

suggestion.title: Redis Configuration or Persistence Modification
suggestion.rationale: RCE from Redis typically includes persistence measures; article's '"built" RCE' suggests sustained compromise preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CONFIG GET/SET commands in Redis logs, especially SAVE, BGSAVE, APPENDONLY, SLAVEOF/REPLICAOF alterations. Flag file integrity changes to redis.conf or dump.rdb. Alert on new scheduled tasks or cron entries created by Redis process UID.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis INFO or COMMAND Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers discovering Redis zero-day would probe service version, config, and capabilities; pipeline should detect discovery-phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid sequential INFO, COMMAND, CONFIG GET, CLIENT LIST, MODULE LIST, ACL queries from single client IP within short time window. Establish baseline of admin queries and flag anomalies. Alert if reconnaissance is followed by EVAL/RCE commands within minutes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repoint to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core obfuscation technique enabling the compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs for release tag creation/modification events pointing to commits not on default branch. Alert when tag targets change to commits with no parent branch association or when orphaned commits are tagged as releases.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commit in CI/CD Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates that 'commit is no longer associated with any existing branch' and 'commit hash [is] still navigable' — this is a key enabler. Attackers hide malicious code by committing to branches, then deleting the branch, leaving commit reachable only via direct hash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan CI/CD repository for commits reachable by hash but not by any branch traversal. Cross-reference against git reflog and GitHub audit logs to identify branch deletions followed by tag reassignment. Flag orphaned commits in security-critical repos.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Leaked in CI/CD Logs (Plaintext Exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and 'secret ever appearing in the build log' — the attack's primary impact. Attacker code bypassed GitHub's secret encryption by logging secrets directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD logs for patterns matching known secret formats (AWS keys: AKIA*, private key headers, GitHub tokens: ghp_/ghu_, API keys). Correlate against GitHub Actions workflow definitions to identify steps that should not produce secrets. Alert on secret strings appearing in build logs in any repo using external GitHub Actions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access to Trusted CI/CD Plugin Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack precondition: 'attacker with write privileges on the Action repo.' No mention of how access was obtained, but this represents T1199 — compromise of a trusted dependency with wide reuse (23,000 repos).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on push events to GitHub Action repositories (esp. those with >1000 dependents) by accounts not in change-control approval lists. Monitor for PAT/SSH key usage anomalies: new key registration followed by pushes to master/main in high-visibility repos.

suggestion.title: External Network Call from GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Indicates C2 callback or staged payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted external domains. Flag requests to dynamic DNS, paste sites, or CDNs from within Action workflows. Correlate timing of outbound calls with malicious commit deploy timestamps.

suggestion.title: Multiple Release Tag Reassignment in Single Commit
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit' — unusual pattern: single commit receiving multiple version tag assignments suggests malicious tag management rather than legitimate semantic versioning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ≥2 release tags are repointed to a new commit in sequence within a short time window (same push or consecutive hours), especially if the commit is orphaned or authored by an account outside the project's core committer group.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit hard-coded credentials. Pipeline missed the credential-access phase entirely.
log_sources: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated or unusual authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interfaces. Look for rapid authentication attempts, failed logins followed by success, or low-privilege account logins accessing configuration/sensitive data endpoints post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'. No detection logic was generated for credential-based access exploiting this flaw.
log_sources: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known hard-coded account names or from unexpected source IPs/geolocations. Cross-reference successful logins with vulnerability scanner results to correlate unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Collection phase entirely missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track data exfiltration or bulk reads of sensitive configuration, policy, or credential data from Cisco FMC after successful authentication. Monitor for unusual export, backup, or API query patterns following login events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article body explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides template reference. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible from the internet or untrusted networks. Cross-reference with patch status to identify instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 and prioritize by exposure date against federal patch deadline (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Juniper Junos OS Vulnerability Check (CVE-2025-21590)
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions CVE-2025-21590 (Juniper Junos OS Improper Isolation) but body pivots to CVE-2026-20316 (Cisco). Pipeline extracted neither. Title discrepancy indicates possible copy-paste error or multi-CVE merge; both should be tracked separately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check inventory for Juniper Junos OS instances and scan for CVE-2025-21590 exploitation attempts. Note: article title and body reference different vendors/CVEs; confirm which is in scope for your org.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password vulnerability. This is the exploit's root vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login events using known hard-coded or low-privileged default service accounts (e.g., admin, service, fmc-internal). Correlate failed attempts across multiple IPs in short windows. Any successful login from an external IP prior to 2026-08-01 (patch deadline) should be flagged for compromise assessment.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access After FMC Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker goal is to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-authentication data queries or exports warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to FMC, detect bulk exports, policy downloads, or configuration reads of firewall rules, VPN configs, or certificate data. Flag queries to sensitive tables (users, certs, policies) executed by low-privileged or unexpected accounts within minutes of login.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access, implying FMC is directly internet-routable. Identify exposed instances for immediate remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for FMC management interfaces (typically HTTPS 443, admin portal 8305) responding from internet-routable addresses. Cross-correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unintended exposures. Any match should trigger immediate access log review for suspicious login activity.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker initially accesses 'using a low-privileged account.' Expect rapid escalation to full admin within the FMC or lateral movement to managed firewalls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect role elevation requests or permission changes immediately following low-privileged account authentication. Monitor for API calls requesting full administrative credentials or attempts to pivot to managed Cisco firewalls in the environment via the FMC's management plane.

suggestion.title: Firewall Policy Modification via Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC provides centralized access to manage and modify all dependent firewalls. Unauthorized policy changes enable lateral movement and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy deployments or access rule modifications pushed from FMC to managed firewalls during off-hours or from unexpected admin accounts. Compare policy versions pre/post-compromise window (pre-2026-08-01). Any new rules permitting previously-blocked destinations warrant review.

suggestion.title: Anomalous API or Command Access to FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC exposes REST APIs for automation. Hard-coded credentials enable unauthenticated API exploitation for programmatic data extraction and system recon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC REST API calls (typically /api/fmc_config/v1/...) from unexpected clients or with abnormally high request volumes. Flag queries for device inventory, user lists, certificate exports, or policy metadata. Correlate spikes with known exploitation timeframes or IP ranges associated with credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit — implies public-facing FMC instances. No exposure hunt generated despite template recommendation in body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC instances (TCP 8305/8307) reachable from internet, correlate with CMDB/scanner data. Flag pre-patch deployments (firmware release dates before 2026-08-01). Use shodan queries and passive DNS for external FMC hostnames.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded FMC Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling login without valid credentials. No detection for credential misuse or authentication bypass events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC access logs for authentication success from non-standard/foreign sources using service-account patterns. Alert on login bursts from single IP pre-dating known public PoC availability. Correlate successful logins to public exploit timeline.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation grants 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection for data discovery or exfiltration post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk policy downloads, rule exports, or credential store access via FMC APIs/GUI post-authentication. Establish baseline of admin-role data export frequency; flag deviation from low-privilege accounts or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Correlation & Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends vulnerability scanner matching but pipeline generated zero scanner-centric use case for continuous detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CRITICAL: Auto-escalate scanner detections of CVE-2026-20316 on FMC. Correlate with public-IP ownership and age-since-patch. Classify as P1 if internet-exposed + unpatched past 2026-08-01 due date.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Notepad++ Plugin Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery via 'fake Notepad++ plugin'; pipeline missed the initial infection vector requiring detection of non-standard plugin paths, suspicious plugin filenames, or unsigned DLLs being dropped into plugin directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL or executable files dropped into Notepad++ plugin directories (%APPDATA%\Notepad++\plugins or Program Files\Notepad++\plugins). Alert on file creation by non-admin users or unsigned binaries. Correlate with Notepad++ process launch immediately following file write.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Process Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Malware plugins typically execute commands via Notepad++ process; article implies execution but pipeline extracted no behavioral detection. Classic plugin-based malware escalates via child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when notepad.exe or notepad++.exe spawns children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, wscript.exe). Baseline legitimate plugin behavior first. Prioritize unusual argument patterns (hidden windows, encoded commands, network I/O).

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Notepad++ Plugin Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article headline implies plugin-based persistence mechanism; pipeline missed registry modifications that install plugins at startup or elevate privileges via plugin loader.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Notepad++ or HKCU\Software\Notepad++ for new plugin entries. Alert on modifications to plugin search paths or unexpected DLL references. Correlate registry writes with Notepad++ process events.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Invalid-Signature Notepad++ Plugin Execution
suggestion.rationale: Fake plugins are unlikely to carry legitimate Notepad++ signatures; pipeline missed code-signing and validation checks that would catch malicious plugin binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL load events from Notepad++ plugin directories where the source DLL lacks Notepad++ developer signatures or is signed by unknown CAs. Flag mismatched timestamps between DLL creation and last-write time.

suggestion.title: MATCHBOIL.V2 C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware name 'MATCHBOIL.V2' implies C2 communications; pipeline extracted no IOCs for command servers, domains, or IP addresses. Article likely contains or references known C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Notepad++ or its child processes to unusual ports or non-standard protocols. Alert on DNS queries for hardcoded C2 domains associated with MATCHBOIL.V2. Inspect traffic for beaconing patterns (regular intervals, small payloads, binary protocols).

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Plugin Directory Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake plugin delivery requires write access to plugin folders; pipeline missed detection for unexpected file writes or directory enumeration preceding plugin installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, modification, or deletion within Notepad++ plugin directories outside normal deployment windows. Flag cases where an external process (not Notepad++ itself) writes DLLs to plugin paths. Combine with process context to distinguish updates from attacks.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes external actor gaining management access via hard-coded credentials. Behavioral shift from normal FMC admin patterns (typically internal ops) is strong compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authorized FMC administrators by geographic origin, time window, and typical repository access. Alert on logins from external geographies, especially outside business hours, especially by low-privilege service accounts. Combine with network exposure detection to confirm attack chain.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch/Scan Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-01. Vulnerability scanner hits must correlate with exposure and authentication detections for end-to-end coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE-2026-20316 scanner results into correlation dashboard. Prioritize any positive findings that are also flagged by FMC exposure detection or authentication anomaly detections. Track patch deployment status against federal deadline; flag any unpatched instances as critical.

suggestion.title: NodeBB Unauthorized Admin Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaws 'exposing admin access'—detect rapid admin role assignment or privilege elevation following vulnerability disclosure, indicating post-exploitation persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin account creation, admin group membership changes, or role escalations in NodeBB audit logs with no corresponding administrative workflow ticket. Correlate with unusual login IPs, API-based privilege changes, or bulk permission assignments within 24–72 hours post-advisory.

suggestion.title: NodeBB Private Message Bulk Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'private chats' exposure—detect unusual collection patterns consistent with post-compromise data harvesting from message storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NodeBB API endpoints for sequential message/chat retrieval calls (typically /api/messages, /api/chats paths) originating from single session, user, or IP. Alert on aggregation volumes exceeding baseline, especially from newly-created or recently-compromised admin accounts.

suggestion.title: NodeBB Vulnerability Exploitation HTTP Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Title references '8 AI-found flaws'—pre-patch, detect HTTP request patterns, malformed inputs, or known CVE payload signatures targeting NodeBB endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest publicly disclosed NodeBB CVE exploit payloads and detect attempts to trigger known vulnerable code paths—SQL injection, command injection, or parameter-pollution attacks against NodeBB API/web handlers. Flag against unpatched version inventory.

suggestion.title: Unpatched NodeBB Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Critical severity requires rapid patch deployment verification; detect instances running vulnerable versions post-advisory date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software asset inventory for NodeBB version numbers. Cross-reference against advisory release date and patched version thresholds. Alert on instances exceeding patch SLA without patch deployment, indicating continued exposure window.

suggestion.title: NodeBB API Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Admin exposure suggests possible API-layer authentication or authorization bypass; detect API calls succeeding without valid session credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NodeBB API endpoints for requests lacking valid authorization headers (X-CSRF-Token, session cookie, JWT) that return HTTP 200 or administrative data. Detect unauthenticated or expired-token requests succeeding against protected endpoints.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' with specific CVE substitution. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances matching CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize internet-facing or externally exposed FMC instances. CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Suspicious Authentication: Unauthenticated Access to Admin Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in... using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed the credential access and authentication bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful login attempts using default or hard-coded credentials, particularly from external source IPs. Flag any successful authentication events preceded by unauthenticated access attempts to restricted endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Admin Access from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote attacker' exploitation of management interface. Pipeline missed lateral-movement and command-and-control implications once access is achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interfaces (port 443, 8305, etc.) from unexpected external IP ranges. Alert on high-volume login attempts or rapid iteration through credential combinations targeting FMC systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detector
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' with this CVE. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure or vulnerability-scan query despite the article recommending exactly this hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset-management databases for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances with version/build matching CVE-2026-20316 footprint. Cross-reference with network-exposure assessment to identify internet-accessible FMC instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Core attack vector (hardcoded password T1078.001) not mapped to any detection query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305 typical) for authentication attempts using hardcoded defaults or suspicious low-privileged account usage. Flag successful logins from unexpected sources or outside business hours immediately followed by configuration/data access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access—implies FMC exposed to internet. No network-exposure or service-port detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to known Cisco FMC management ports from untrusted external IP space. Correlate with vulnerability scan results to identify exposed FMC instances with matching software versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—describes data-collection phase. No detection logic for post-authentication data exfiltration or bulk access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk policy/configuration exports, credential dumps, or device-telemetry downloads immediately following suspicious low-privileged account logins. Flag any configuration data transmitted to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Authentication Success from Unexpected Source with Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Direct attack scenario; baseline legitimate FMC login sources and alert on external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Successful authentication to Cisco FMC on port 443 from external IP addresses or non-whitelisted source subnets. Correlate FMC login events against baseline admin workstations; alert on low-privilege or default account logins from Internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Exploit of CVE-2026-20316: Hardcoded Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Known-exploited CVE (CISA KEV); explicit Splunk and KQL hunts for credential stuffing or brute-force attempts against hardcoded account names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Repeated failed authentication attempts using known hardcoded Cisco FMC usernames (e.g., admin, cisco, etc.) or successful logins immediately preceded by brute-force patterns. Flag any authentication success from external networks within 24 hours of enumeration activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Lateral Movement via Sensitive Data Access by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After exploitation, threat actor will query firewall policies, export security logs, or enumerate managed endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk exports of firewall rules, security policies, managed device inventory, or threat intelligence feeds by any low-privilege account. Unusual administrative queries or unscheduled report generation from non-admin accounts indicates post-compromise reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Enumeration and Scanning of Public-Facing Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Cisco FMC as 'public-facing.' Precursor to exploitation is service discovery; external scanners will probe for FMC web interface and endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external HTTP scanning of Cisco FMC (inbound to TCP 443 with repeating GET/HEAD requests to default paths like /admin, /login, /api, /.well-known). Alert if scanner fingerprint or ASN matches known threat actor infrastructure or active vulnerability scanning campaigns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC — Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'log in...using a low-privileged account...access sensitive data.' Detection should cover vertical escalation attempts from low-privilege shell to admin privileges on FMC host.
log_sources: Host OS privilege escalation logs (sudo, RunAs)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC system logs and RBAC audit trails for role elevation requests, sudo invocations, or administrative API calls originating from user contexts assigned low-privilege roles. Flag privilege boundary crossing within 1 hour of initial login.

suggestion.title: Remote Hardcoded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—the hardcoded password enables successful remote auth without credential compromise; direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful remote login to Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) using default or low-privileged account names from external IP ranges. Correlate with geographic anomalies and baseline auth patterns. Flag immediate-success login attempts after multiple failed tries (credential spray on known default accounts).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration/Credential Export from Compromised FMC Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-authentication data extraction is the impact; requires monitoring FMC audit logs for unauthorized data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy exports, configuration downloads, credential object viewing, or threat-rule retrieval by low-privileged or default accounts. Alert on bulk configuration backups or API credential-store queries from newly-authenticated low-privilege sessions, especially from external origins.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Public IP Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires remote access to FMC; article implies internet-accessible management interface. Per template guidance, asset-exposure hunt required to identify vulnerable deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances listening on public-routable IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate scanner results to identify patch status vs. CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with external threat intelligence for public FMC service fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration Against FMC Default Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password enables direct auth, but pre-exploitation reconnaissance may include probing default account names; article phrase 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' suggests scanning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid-fire failed authentication attempts against Cisco FMC default/common account names (admin, root, cisco, etc.) from single or distributed external IPs. Flag dictionary attacks or credential-spray patterns targeting FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305). Monitor for failed-then-successful login sequences.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Version Fingerprinting and Banner Grabbing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically perform version enumeration before targeting known-vulnerable versions; discovery precedes exploitation in attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/S requests to Cisco FMC login pages, error responses, or API endpoints that leak version information. Alert on repeated scripted banner-grabbing attempts or User-Agent strings typical of vulnerability scanners targeting FMC. Correlate with known-vulnerable version strings from vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Unusual Outbound Data Transfer from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, exfiltration of sensitive firewall data (policies, rulesets, credential objects) would manifest as outbound connections; article mentions 'sensitive data within impacted systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS, SFTP, or unencrypted data transfers from FMC appliances to non-management IPs, especially from low-privileged authenticated sessions. Monitor for API calls exporting configurations, rules, or credential objects to external destinations. Correlate with prior auth anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Unauthenticated Remote Login Attempts with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'—indicates either default/hard-coded credentials or credential stuffing. Pipeline must detect successful authentication from external sources using low-privileged or well-known Cisco FMC service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305, 8307) from external IP ranges. Flag logins using service accounts or low-privilege defaults. Correlate rapid sequential auth attempts against FMC endpoints with known hard-coded credential patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 exploitable remotely without credentials—requires internet-exposed management interface. Article implies threat actors access from external networks; pipeline must scan for exposed FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory and alert on any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference firewall inbound rules permitting external access to FMC admin ports (443, 8305) against approved remote-work policies. Query external scanning data for exposed FMC endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—implies post-breach data exfiltration. Pipeline must detect anomalous queries/exports to threat databases, topology, or policy configs by low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk exports, API queries for threat definitions, or topology data retrieval by low-privilege accounts immediately post-authentication. Alert on unusual data volumes sent to external IPs from FMC instances within 1 hour of failed/successful unusual login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability and Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-08-01. Pipeline must provide asset-exposure and version-compliance checks for all Cisco FMC instances organization-wide.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and device inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference product versions against published CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable version ranges. Track patch-deployment status for all instances with automated escalation if unpatched beyond 2026-08-01 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Asset Inventory & Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild... patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline must emit baseline asset-exposure hunt to locate unpatched Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) / Firepower Management Center instances. Verify patch status against vendor remediation guidance. Prioritize externally-exposed or management-zone appliances. CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; absence of coverage is high-risk.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to FMC via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability... allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline must detect authentication attempts using known hard-coded or default accounts against FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins using default or hard-coded account names from unexpected sources. Correlate with failed login storms or scanner activity against FMC management ports (443, 8305). Hard-coded password exploitation bypasses normal multi-factor auth controls.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Collection from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation, attacker will query policies, credentials, configuration, and system metadata from the management center.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API and database access logs for unusually broad or high-volume queries targeting sensitive objects: firewall policies, VPN/IPSec credentials, network topology, administrative users, or system backups. Detect bulk exports or sequential read patterns indicative of data harvesting.

suggestion.title: FMC-to-Managed-Firewall Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article implies FMC is high-value compromise target. Once breached via hard-coded password, attacker will pivot to managed firewalls to persist and expand compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect configuration deployments, firmware updates, or administrative commands from FMC to managed devices that originate from anomalous sessions (recent hard-coded credential login, off-hours, unusual source IP, rapid-fire pushes). Baseline normal deployment cadence and scope.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Management Interface Access (Failed Logins + Success Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploitation attempts will generate authentication failure logs followed by success. Pipeline must surface login-anomaly detection distinct from normal admin behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (TCP 443, 8305) for failed login attempts followed by successful login, rapid-fire login attempts, or successful logins from non-standard geographies/source IPs. Correlate with public PoC activity or vulnerability scanner hits.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation within Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data.' Attacker will attempt to escalate from low-privileged hard-coded account to administrative role within FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts or role/permission modifications within FMC initiated by the low-privileged account or shortly after hard-coded credential login. Flag unusual account creation or group membership changes.

suggestion.title: Redis Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'RCE Exploit' built for Redis zero-days. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Redis port activity (6379/6380) combined with command execution payloads. Flag connections from unexpected source IPs followed by shell command injection patterns (e.g., CONFIG SET, EVAL with shell metacharacters).

suggestion.title: Redis Vulnerability Scanning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Title describes researchers discovering 'Redis Zero-Days'—reconnaissance and scanning phase precedes exploitation. Pipeline omitted discovery/reconnaissance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect probing for Redis services via port scans on 6379 or version-enumeration queries (INFO command from reconnaissance tools). Baseline: legitimate Redis admin tools vs. automated scanners via timing/breadth patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Redis Data Access or Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: RCE on Redis typically enables data exfiltration or corruption. Pipeline should surface data-exfiltration and impact use cases for this attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk Redis key enumeration (KEYS *, SCAN) or large data dumps over network. Cross-correlate with process execution of data-transfer tools (curl, wget) or unexpected database exports.

suggestion.title: AI-Driven Vulnerability Research Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article uniquely frames threat as 'Kimi K3 Agents Found [exploits]'—novel angle on automated/AI-assisted vulnerability discovery. Pipeline missed actor/capability modeling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag enrollment or experimentation with AI-powered security tools (e.g., LLM agents, automated exploit generation frameworks) in development or research environments. Track downloads, API calls, or sandbox behaviors associated with these tools.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Moved to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit' and demonstrates re-pointing v35 tag. Core obfuscation tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub release tags being deleted and recreated on different commits within short timespan, especially tags pointing to commits with no parent branch ancestry. Detect tag movement to commits outside mainline history.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit in Trusted Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights orphaned commits as 'key enabling factor' and walkthrough shows commits that exist but aren't reachable from any branch—central to hiding malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits in high-value repos (Actions, libraries) that are tagged/released but unreachable from main/develop branches. Cross-reference commit SHAs in release tags against branch HEAD history.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposed in GitHub Actions Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs'—core impact. GitHub's encryption failed in this context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Actions workflow logs for patterns matching GitHub secret format (e.g., `ghp_`, `ghs_` prefixes) or known cred structures. Alert on decrypted/unmasked secrets in public repos.

suggestion.title: External Payload Fetch from GitHub Action Step
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound connections from GitHub Action runners to non-CDN/non-standard hosts. Flag curl/wget/git clone to external repos during action execution in previously-benign actions.

suggestion.title: Write Access to Popular Shared GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on'—initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new collaborator additions with write/maintain roles on high-dependency Actions repos. Alert on disabled branch protections or suddenly-elevated permissions on key maintainers.

suggestion.title: Commit Author/Timestamp Anomalies in Action Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article shows attacker created malicious commits on orphaned branches then re-tagged them—timestamps and authorship may misalign with normal release cadence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag release tags that point to commits authored by unexpected accounts or with timestamp gaps relative to previous releases. Cross-check commit author vs. repo maintainer roster.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — pipeline missed T1190 initial access and T1110.4 credential attack entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces (typically port 443) for unauthenticated login attempts, successful logins from external/untrusted networks, or rapid authentication attempts against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions. Baseline legitimate admin access and alert on anomalous source IPs, geographies, or credential usage patterns.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — pipeline produced no collection-phase detection despite explicit post-exploitation data access mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data access patterns from low-privileged FMC accounts: configuration exports, policy exports, API queries, or backup downloads executed outside maintenance windows. Monitor for data egress from FMC to untrusted destinations or unusually large/rapid data transfers inconsistent with normal replication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article directs analysts to asset-exposure hunt per templates but pipeline generated zero asset-inventory UCs despite CISA KEV federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances in your environment and cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Flag any FMC instances exposed to internet-accessible networks (port 443 inbound from external), any unpatched instances, and prioritize remediation before federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Remote Management Session Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated remote access to FMC — pipeline missed T1021.1 remote service session detection and anomalous session behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management session logs for anomalous session characteristics: sessions from impossible geographies, sessions with unusual duration patterns, multiple concurrent sessions from same low-privileged account, or sessions executing administrative commands inconsistent with account role.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication from Internet-Routable IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit and gain access—implies FMC is reachable from public internet. Management appliances should never log in from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (typically port 443) for successful SSH or HTTPS login sessions originating from non-internal CIDR ranges. Basline legitimate admin IPs; flag anomalies. Correlate successful logins with subsequent data access or config changes.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Account Exploitation—Failed-to-Success Login Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'low-privileged account' with hard-coded credentials; attackers typically iterate login attempts before success, especially if password is slightly obfuscated or multi-tenanted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed authentication attempts to FMC followed by successful login within 60 seconds from the same source IP. Correlate with known default account naming conventions if available (e.g., 'admin', 'svc_*'). High-fidelity brute-force indicator for this appliance class.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-auth data exfiltration is the attack goal, not just shell access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk exports, configuration downloads, or policy/ruleset queries originating from non-standard admin accounts or IPs within 10 min of successful authentication. Flag any export of device configs, credentials, or network topology.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—many organizations have scanners reporting 'patched' when FMC auto-updates are misconfigured or deferred. Direct version check needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances; cross-reference with known-vulnerable versions (all versions prior to patch release date 2026-08-01). If scanner says 'patched' but version is <patched version, flag as high-risk false negative. Correlate against network exposure data (is FMC internet-facing?).

suggestion.title: FMC Internet Exposure Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Management appliance should be internal-only. Article's 'remote attacker' language + CISA KEV status implies instances are already exposed and being scanned/exploited by threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network telemetry for inbound connections to known FMC management ports (8305/TCP, 443/TCP, 22/TCP) from internet-routable source IPs. Cross-reference against WHOIS; flag any external connection as high-priority remediation target. Supplement with external port scan data (Shodan, Censys) to validate exposure.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration/Policy Changes by Low-Privileged or Anomalous Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker with FMC access may disable logging, add backdoor accounts, modify firewall rules, or exfiltrate managed-device credentials. Low-privileged account performing admin-level changes is a red flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy/rule changes, account creation, or logging disablement in FMC by non-admin accounts or from anomalous IPs. Baseline legitimate config-change cadence; flag out-of-band or after-hours modifications to audit retention or alerting rules.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Notepad++ Plugin File Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is fake plugin delivery; pipeline should detect plugin file creation + Notepad++ process loading it. No UC generated despite clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .dll or .lua files written to Notepad++ plugin directories (typically %APPDATA%\Notepad++\plugins\) followed by Notepad++ process image-loading those files. Correlate with suspicious process spawning or network connections from Notepad++ process.

suggestion.title: MATCHBOIL.V2 Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware name (MATCHBOIL.V2) explicitly mentioned in title; pipeline should have generated signature-based or behavioral detection for known C2 traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from Notepad++ process to known or suspected MATCHBOIL.V2 C2 endpoints. Look for outbound HTTPS/HTTP on non-standard ports or to domains with suspicious registration patterns.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Plugin Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake Notepad++ plugin'; should surface distribution vector (domain, file host, watering hole, etc.) and chain user-download behavior to execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of .zip or .exe files impersonating Notepad++ plugins from non-official sources. Flag parent process (browser) spawning installer or plugin-placement process; correlate download URLs against known malware distribution channels.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Process Anomaly - Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Plugin execution should enable lateral movement/command execution; standard Notepad++ does not spawn child processes. Pipeline missed behavioral detection angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Notepad++.exe spawns child processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, regsvcs, mshta) without user initiating external tool launch. Notepad++ should rarely execute child processes; high-confidence trigger if process parent is Notepad++ and child is known LOLBin.

suggestion.title: UAC-0099 Tooling Indicators - MATCHBOIL.V2 File System Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: UAC-0099 is named threat actor in title; pipeline should enumerate known file paths, registry keys, process names associated with this group's MATCHBOIL.V2 variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of known MATCHBOIL.V2 registry persistence keys (e.g., HKCU\Software\Microsoft\...) or file system artifacts (temp folders, %APPDATA% subdirs) associated with UAC-0099 campaigns. Cross-reference with threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can 'log in' to access 'sensitive data'—exploitation manifests as authentication attempts to FMC web interface. No UC generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC web interface logs for unauthenticated access attempts, successful logins with hard-coded credentials, or session establishment from unexpected source IPs. Alert on POST requests to authentication endpoints followed by successful session tokens without legitimate admin correlation.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Use Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'hard-coded password'—attacker exploits known embedded credentials. No UC addresses detection of this credential material in authentication logs or credential material disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for authentication events using patterns associated with default/hard-coded credentials (credential spray from single source, consistent timing patterns, access outside business hours). Baseline legitimate admin logins; alert on authentication failures followed by success using same credential set.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template reference, yet pipeline generated zero asset discovery or exposure hunts. Foundation requirement for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances in environment. Cross-reference against patch database for CVE-2026-20316 patching status. Flag any FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks or exposed to internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access & Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker gains 'access [to] sensitive data within the impacted systems'—must detect unauthorized queries, exports, or reads of configuration/credential repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC database logs for unusual data exports, policy dumps, or credential queries. Correlate query source accounts against known administrator identities. Alert on bulk data access patterns inconsistent with normal FMC administration workflows.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy & Firewall Rule Tampering Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with management-center access can modify firewall policies to enable lateral movement or persistence. Article's 'sensitive data access' scope does not exclude policy-layer compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy/rule modifications by non-administrative accounts or from unexpected source IPs post-exploitation window. Alert on creation of permissive rules, credential updates, or policy exports by low-privileged users.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Accessibility from Public Networks
suggestion.rationale: Critical management appliance should not be remotely accessible. Article describes 'remote attacker' exploitation—detect when FMC mgmt interface reachable from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Cisco FMC management port (typically HTTPS/443) receives inbound connections from external/untrusted networks. Correlate with authentication attempts to identify exploitation probes. Baseline legitimate access; escalate any new external source IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation of 'affected device'—T1190 depends on detecting public-facing FMC instances. Article phrase: 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' and CISA KEV status confirms internet exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances responding on management ports (443, 8305) from internet-facing IPs. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2026-20316. Alert on first successful connection from unexpected geolocation or non-corporate IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' This is credential-based access exploitation distinct from asset discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins with known hard-coded service accounts. Detect rapid authentication attempts against FMC endpoints. Flag successful remote authentication sessions from non-standard source IPs immediately after discovery.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Collection from FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Attacker uses hard-coded credentials to authenticate, then collects firewall policies, configurations, or intelligence feeds—a collection phase distinct from network-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal data-access patterns in FMC audit logs. Alert on unusual volume of policy exports, configuration downloads, rule database queries, or sensor information requests within minutes of non-standard authentication. Flag bulk API calls exfiltrating monitoring or policy data.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account Privilege Escalation within FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—implies post-auth privilege escalation to perform administrative changes (policy deployment, sensor management, credential modification) is possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for privilege-escalation patterns: low-privileged user accounts attempting to modify high-privilege objects (deploy policies, modify admin accounts, manage sensors). Alert on permission-denied events followed by lateral movement or alternative attack paths.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy/Configuration Exfiltration via Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise with hard-coded access, attacker will export firewall policies and rules for reconnaissance. Article: 'sensitive data within the impacted systems' includes policy rules, sensor configuration, and threat intelligence integrated into FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk policy exports, rule database downloads, or configuration backups from FMC management console to external or suspicious destinations. Monitor for API calls retrieving sensor rules or threat-intel feeds. Correlate timing with non-standard authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Facing Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' threat and is CISA KEV (actively exploited). Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but no UC was generated. Asset inventory and port-scanning correlation is the foundational detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (standard ports: 8305, 8307) accessible from the public internet or untrusted networks. Cross-reference external port-scan data, shodan queries, and internal asset inventory to identify exposed FMC instances vulnerable to T1190 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'use of hard-coded password'—the attack vector is direct credential abuse. Article describes login 'using a low-privileged account' implying known credentials, yet no UC detects authentication anomalies or credential-guessing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts (T1110) from external IPs and successful logins using hard-coded or default account names. Alert on authentication from non-standard source IPs, off-hours access, or credential-stuffing patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20316 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Following Cisco FMC Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' This is the exploitation outcome—detection must track low-privilege account pivoting to high-value data stores post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful FMC authentication from suspicious sources with subsequent access to sensitive repositories (threat intelligence feeds, security policies, system configurations). Flag low-privilege or default accounts querying protected data stores—indicator of post-breach data collection.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute-Force Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploits are often automated and mass-targeted. Article does not mention brute force explicitly, but the attack pattern (T1110) is inherent to credential-guessing campaigns against exposed FMC instances.
