suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces (port 443, 8305) for HTTP 401/403 responses followed by successful login from the same source IP, or direct successful authentication without a preceding login challenge. Baseline expected authentication request patterns and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Login to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'. Pipeline did not generate detection for known-password or default-credential attacks against FMC authentication endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login events to FMC using low-privileged service accounts or default usernames (e.g., admin, service, default_user, or vendor-specific defaults). Correlate with successful session establishment and subsequent data-access queries.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Pipeline generated no detection for unauthorized data collection following credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting successful low-privileged authentication to FMC, monitor for API calls or UI navigation to configuration endpoints (policies, rules, credentials, threat-intel integrations). Alert when accessing sensitive objects (e.g., ACP objects, VPN configs, threat feeds) from atypical session contexts.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation. Pipeline did not generate asset-enumeration or vulnerability-scan detections for exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exposed Cisco FMC instances via port scans targeting 443, 8305, or FMC service banners. Correlate external source IPs with successful probes. Cross-reference against your vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 hits and confirm patch status.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management appliance controlling distributed firewalls; article does not mention scope but compromise of FMC creates high risk for lateral movement to managed devices. Pipeline missed this amplification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting FMC compromise, monitor for policy push, configuration deployment, or SSH/CLI connections initiated from FMC to managed firewall appliances. Alert on unexpected device-configuration changes or new management sessions to appliances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication with Default/Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite clear credential-access attack vector inherent in hard-coded password vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC (typically ports 8305, 8307) where username matches known default or hard-coded accounts, especially if preceded by failed login attempts or originating from external IP ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data confirming CVE-2026-20316 presence.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploiting management center. Pipeline missed the lateral-movement and C2 channel risk from exposed, unpatched FMC instances acting as enterprise pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC administrative ports (8305, 8307, 443 on known FMC IPs) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 scanner hits. Flag any device showing both exposure + unpatched status as high-priority remediation candidate.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Firewall Rule Changes by Suspicious Account
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password grants 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems.' Post-exploitation, attacker could modify security policies or rules—a persistence / defense-evasion technique the pipeline did not surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration or firewall rule modifications originating from default/low-privileged accounts or from IPs outside normal administrative ranges. Establish baseline of legitimate policy changes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attempts Against Cisco FMC Login
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'hard-coded password' vulnerability is often discovered through brute-force or credential-stuffing campaigns. Pipeline omitted T1110 variants despite this being a direct attack vector for active KEV.
log_sources: WAF / reverse proxy logs (if FMC exposed via proxy)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for >5 failed authentication attempts to FMC within 5 minutes, especially with dictionary or known-default usernames. Cross-correlate source IPs and check for patterns consistent with automated credential-stuffing tools.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 or Data Exfiltration from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC manages enterprise firewall policies and has visibility into network traffic. Attacker gaining 'access to sensitive data' could pivot to C2 or data exfil. Pipeline omitted command-and-control, exfiltration, or lateral-movement phases entirely.
log_sources: Network egress logs from FMC host
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound traffic from FMC (updates, NTP, syslog). Flag unexpected outbound connections to unknown IPs/domains, especially over non-standard ports. Monitor for DNS lookups to suspicious TLDs from FMC.

suggestion.title: Unsuccessful FMC Remediation: Patched Status Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles emphasize patch lag. Pipeline generated no UC to verify patch status or detect cases where scanners claim patched but exploitation logs suggest otherwise—a key SOC triage differentiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco FMC instances flagged as vulnerable by scanner (CVE-2026-20316) against patched versions in asset inventory. Alert on cases where device version suggests vulnerability but scanner has not rescanned recently. Federal patch deadline 2026-08-01 is enforcement trigger.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed to Untrusted Networks (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access the device. Asset-exposure hunt explicitly recommended in article to validate non-vulnerable status despite patch lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 against Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) assets. Cross-reference with network segmentation logs to identify FMC instances reachable from untrusted networks or the internet. Flag any asset with inconclusive or positive scan results after federal remediation due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication with Hardcoded/Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability enables login 'using a low-privileged account' with 'hard-coded password'. Successful authentication logs with default credentials are the exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins matching known default account names or hardcoded credential patterns. Alert on any successful auth followed by data access, especially from unexpected source IPs, unusual times, or geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Sensitive Data Access in Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: successful attacker gains 'access [to] sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Activity logs should show data collection post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk exports of firewall policies, access control lists, or configuration data from Cisco FMC within 24 hours of successful authentication using low-privileged accounts. Alert on policy downloads or sensitive file access immediately following login.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Status Verification Post-Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and lists federal due date 2026-08-01. Organizations may report 'not vulnerable' despite unpatched instances in production.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Cisco FMC instances flagged in vulnerability scans (CVE-2026-20316) with patch management records. For any instance showing positive/inconclusive scan results after 2026-08-01 due date, verify patch actually applied and validate FMC version against fixed releases.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed to Internet (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can reach the device, proving internet exposure. Standard asset-exposure hunt required: scan for Cisco FMC banners/SSL certificates on public IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center is observed listening on internet-routable IPs on ports 443, 8305, or 8307. Cross-reference with external scanning services (Shodan, Censys) for FMC banner fingerprints. Flag any HTTPS certificate with FMC indicators from untrusted ASNs.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Login to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes remote attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'. This indicates successful authentication exploit; must detect successful logins from unusual geographies/IPs to FMC management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Cisco FMC management interface from external IP ranges, especially from low-privilege or service accounts. Establish baseline of legitimate FMC administrators by source subnet and geography. Flag first-time logins from previously-unseen locations within 24h.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Burst to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may guess hard-coded credentials via credential-stuffing or brute-force before success. Multiple failed attempts in quick succession is a credential-guessing signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ failed login attempts to Cisco FMC from a single source IP within 10 minutes. Alert immediately if followed by successful authentication. Monitor for patterns targeting known default/service account names (if PoC released).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration Export from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. In FMC context, sensitive data means firewall policies, access rules, audit logs, and device configurations. Post-authentication exports are the collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for configuration backup exports, policy retrieval, or bulk audit log access immediately following authentication from external IPs. Alert on API calls to /api/fmc_config/*/policies or /api/fmc_config/*/devices with unusually large result sets from non-administrative client IDs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Device Inventory Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: After gaining access to the management center, attacker can query downstream firewall inventory to map network topology. FMC device APIs are a logical discovery target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential queries to Cisco FMC device endpoints (/api/fmc_config/*/devices, /api/fmc_config/*/devicegroups) from a single authenticated session. Flag rapid enumeration of device lists, network segments, or security policies within 5 minutes of login—typical of post-breach reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repositioning to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker deleting original version tags and relocating them to malicious orphaned commit: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' This is a direct, observable attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for tag deletion followed by tag creation pointing to commits not reachable from main/default branch. Alert on release tags moved to orphaned commits within short time windows. Correlate git tag operations with commit reachability checks.

suggestion.title: Unexpected External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This is the detection vector that revealed the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections from GitHub Actions runners to external IPs/domains not in whitelist, especially those hosting code or binaries. Correlate workflow execution timing with unexpected egress traffic. Flag unusual DNS queries or HTTP requests during CI/CD pipeline execution.

suggestion.title: Encrypted GitHub Secrets Exposed in Plaintext CI Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the impact vector requiring log monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Action logs and CI/CD pipeline output for patterns matching GitHub secret formats (typically alphanumeric tokens 20-50+ chars). Cross-reference with known secret prefixes. Alert on secrets appearing in logs where they should be masked by GitHub's encryption. Monitor for log export or download attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Write Access and Commit Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes prerequisite: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit.' The attack depends entirely on this access. Detecting unexpected commits from unusual contexts is a preventive measure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to high-visibility GitHub Actions repos from unexpected contexts (unusual committer identity, atypical time-of-day, new SSH keys, API-only pushes). Establish baseline for normal maintainer commit patterns. Flag commits immediately followed by tag operations or branch deletions.

suggestion.title: Rapid GitHub Tag Deletion and Rewrite Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Attack sequence explicitly described: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit.' Rapid deletion-recreation is a detection red flag distinct from normal versioning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub audit log events showing tag_deleted followed by tag_created on same repo within seconds/minutes. Flag when multiple version tags are manipulated in short window. Require approval for tag operations on repos with >1000 dependents.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Dependency Modified Without Normal Release Process
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates attack: 'the attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo' affecting 23,000 dependent repos. Detect when widely-used dependencies are modified outside normal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For GitHub Actions with >1000 stars or >10,000 dependents, alert on code commits not following established release/review process. Monitor for commits appearing in release tags that bypass standard CI/CD gates. Cross-reference Action usage telemetry against version timeline anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit; FMC must be internet-facing or accessible from untrusted networks. Article phrase: 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances on network (typical ports 443, 8305). Flag any exposed to untrusted subnets or internet-routable. Cross-check against patch status for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Attempts with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password.' This is the exploitation vector; detection must capture login attempts using known hard-coded or default credentials. Article phrase: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account names or patterns typical of default credentials. Establish baseline of expected service accounts; flag anomalous logon sources or off-hours access.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After hard-coded credential compromise, attacker will query FMC for security policies, firewall rules, threat intelligence, or network configuration. Article phrase: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for data queries (policy export, rule export, intelligence feed access, configuration dump) initiated by low-privileged accounts or from unexpected administrative contexts. Flag bulk downloads of security-relevant configuration.

suggestion.title: FMC Low-Privilege Account Creation or Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' can be abused; attacker may attempt lateral privilege escalation within FMC to gain admin rights. Article phrase: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC access control logs for attempts to grant elevated permissions to the low-privileged account that made initial successful authentication via hard-coded credential. Flag permission changes by newly authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due date 2026-08-01; patch lag is the primary risk. Detection must confirm patch deployment to all Cisco FMC instances. Article phrase: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Cisco FMC instances; verify version >= patched release for CVE-2026-20316. Any instance on unpatched version is exploitable; prioritize for emergency patching before due date.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement via Compromised Management Access
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a control plane management center; successful compromise enables attacker to modify firewall rules, deploy malware policies, or exfiltrate threat intelligence. Lateral movement risk is severe. Article phrase: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' (systems managed by FMC, not just FMC itself).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for policy deployment, rule modification, or device management commands initiated by the compromised low-privileged account. Establish baseline of expected policy change patterns; flag unusual bulk deployments or changes to perimeter rules.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as detection approach. Pipeline must generate asset discovery for Cisco FMC systems before exploitation attempts can be hunted. Article phrase: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]'. CVE-2026-20316 requires baseline of affected systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management systems and vulnerability scanners for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Enumerate systems running affected versions (pre-patch). Correlate with internet-facing asset registries to identify exposed instances at highest exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Remote Authentication Attempts Against Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts using default/hard-coded credentials against FMC. Article phrase: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (typically HTTPS 443) for login attempts from external/non-corporate IPs using known hard-coded account names ('admin', 'cisco', etc.). Flag both failed and successful authentication events with these credentials, especially from geographic anomalies or VPN exit points.

suggestion.title: Credential Misuse: Hard-coded Account Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials are exploitation prerequisite; pipeline must distinguish legitimate admin access from attacker use of embedded default credentials. Article phrase: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC logins via hard-coded/default account credentials (e.g., internal admin account with factory-default password not changed post-deployment). Correlate with network source IP reputation and compare login timestamp against known patching windows to detect exploitation before patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Compromised Cisco FMC Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Impact phase: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline must detect unauthorized queries, exports, or downloads of firewall policies, network topology, or security configuration after successful hard-coded credential use. Article phrase: 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for policy/configuration exports, API calls for network topology retrieval, or report generation initiated from authenticated sessions using hard-coded accounts. Establish baseline of normal low-privilege account activity; flag bulk data exports or reconnaissance queries inconsistent with baseline.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement via Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC sits at network perimeter with visibility/control of managed firewalls. Compromised FMC can be pivot point. Article implies post-access phases: 'access to sensitive data' suggests attacker persistence or C2 capability through compromised management console. Article phrase: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow...access to sensitive data'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious FMC administrative actions from sessions authenticated via hard-coded credentials: firewall rule modifications, policy disablements, logging configuration changes, or deployment of new security policies to managed devices. Flag changes that reduce visibility or enable lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'—detection required for external login attempts against exposed FMC management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interface from external IP ranges. Correlate successful logins outside administrative subnets with CVE-2026-20316 scanner detections. Flag any access using default or low-privileged credentials.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exploitation for FMC Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'—detect abuse of documented default credentials for remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC auth logs for login attempts using known hardcoded/default account identifiers. Alert on successful logins from untrusted networks or outside maintenance windows. Flag concurrent failed-then-successful patterns consistent with credential brute-force.

suggestion.title: Sensitive FMC Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—after compromise, attacker exports firewall policies, threat intelligence, or management configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk export operations from FMC (configuration backups, policy exports, intelligence feeds). Alert on archive creation followed by exfiltration to external IPs. Monitor for API calls or backup downloads by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Policy Modifications via Compromised Console
suggestion.rationale: FMC is security control plane—compromised instance allows attacker to modify firewall rules, disable threat inspection, or create policy exceptions affecting entire managed network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC configuration changelog for policy disablement, exception creation, or ruleset changes outside change control windows. Alert if modifications originate from low-privileged accounts or outside business hours. Flag any rule disablement for DLP, IPS, or threat prevention.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Policy Deployment from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC enables attacker to push malicious policies to managed firewalls, facilitating network-wide lateral movement and command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious FMC policy deployments with anomalous network activity (new allowed routes, disabled filtering to sensitive subnets). Alert on policies that whitelist unexpected IPs or enable broad access between protected network segments.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposure and Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates remote access exploit—require immediate asset inventory and exposure assessment to identify vulnerable FMC instances reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute authenticated and unauthenticated scans against internet-routable IPs for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) / Firepower Management Center. Match CVE-2026-20316 signatures. Verify all FMC instances are gated behind VPN or restricted to administrative subnets. Alert any management interface reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Inventory and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Prerequisite hunt to identify vulnerable assets before exploitation detection can begin. Must complete before 2026-08-01 deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference with patch management systems to identify running versions prior to the patched release. Flag instances with unknown or overdue patch status relative to federal due date.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—direct signal of exploitation via hard-coded credentials. This is the exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account credentials. Alert on authentications originating from external or non-management IP ranges. Flag velocity spikes indicating brute-force or credential-stuffing attempts against the FMC management interface.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access and Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit allows 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detection must hunt for evidence of data collection and exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for unusual data access patterns: bulk exports of configuration objects, policy rules, certificates, or network intelligence data. Alert on data access by low-privileged or newly-created accounts, or outside normal change windows. Correlate with authentication anomalies to identify post-compromise data staging.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure to External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker' implying network exposure as prerequisite. Detection must confirm whether FMC management interface is reachable from internet, enabling exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (typically 443, 8305, 8307) from unauthorized external IP ranges. Correlate internet-exposed traffic with exploitation signatures, failed authentication attempts, or known CVE-2026-20316 exploit payloads. Review and tighten network ACLs to restrict FMC management access to authorized networks only.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Cisco FMC Data Exfiltration Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sensitive data 'access' for potential theft. Hunt for evidence of data being staged, compressed, or transferred to attacker infrastructure post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from Cisco FMC servers to external or atypical destinations for unusual volume or protocol usage. Look for DNS queries to suspicious domains, SSL/TLS connections to non-vendor IPs, or large data transfers. Correlate with successful hard-coded credential authentications to identify active compromise with data theft.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration and Version Audit for Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article references federal patch due date as compliance obligation. Organizations will be asked about CVE-2026-20316 remediation status by auditors/regulators by deadline—must have systematic version and configuration audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute version enumeration across all Cisco FMC appliances to confirm running software versions. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-20316. Generate compliance report showing patch status (patched/unpatched/unknown) for each instance, sorted by remediation deadline. Escalate any internet-facing unpatched instances to incident response immediately.

suggestion.title: Detect Cisco FMC authentication via hardcoded/default credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hardcoded password is the attack vector; detections must hunt successful logins with known defaults or anomalous low-privilege account usage against FMC management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FMC audit logs and firewall logs for successful authentication attempts using default or hardcoded credentials. Correlate network logs showing HTTPS/SSH to FMC management ports (443) from unexpected sources. Flag rapid-fire login attempts (brute force) and successful logins followed by bulk data export.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability-scanner integration hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article directly cites 'CVE-2026-20316' and notes CISA KEV status means active exploitation. All vulnerability scanners must flag this CVE against Cisco FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all detections of CVE-2026-20316. For each flagged Cisco FMC instance, cross-reference with asset management to confirm exposure status (patched vs. unpatched). Correlate with access logs 30 days pre-detection to identify any successful exploitation before vulnerability scanner alert.

suggestion.title: Monitor Cisco FMC for sensitive data access by low-privilege accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Successful exploitation via hardcoded password grants low-privilege accounts access to FMC configurations, policies, and telemetry. Hunt for anomalous data export or policy/config backup initiated by low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Cisco FMC audit logs for configuration exports, policy backups, or syslog/event bulk retrieval initiated by low-privilege accounts or service accounts. Flag API requests for large data sets from single-session or newly-created accounts. Correlate export events with successful hardcoded-credential logins.

suggestion.title: External asset exposure hunt — Cisco FMC management interface reachability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker' exploiting public-facing vulnerability, implying exposed Cisco FMC management console. Scan perimeter for accessible FMC instances on typical management ports (443, 8443).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Shodan/Censys for Cisco FMC management interfaces with SSL certs matching your organization or industry. Run external port scans for open 443/8443 on known FMC IP ranges. Validate firewall policies restrict FMC access to authorized jump-box / VPN ranges only; flag any instances accessible from internet or untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Threat-intel feed monitoring for CVE-2026-20316 exploitation payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article: CISA KEV status guarantees exploitation in the wild. Monitoring threat-intel feeds, PoC repositories (Exploit-DB, GitHub), and dark-web paste sites for published exploits, credentials, and reverse-shell payloads specific to CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to threat-intel feeds (Shodan, Exploit-DB, GitHub) for new PoC code or public exploits targeting CVE-2026-20316 and Cisco FMC hardcoded credentials. When new PoC appears, correlate with your FMC asset list and access logs to assess if any instance was targeted in the window between PoC release and your patch deployment.

suggestion.title: IDS/IPS and WAF detection for CVE-2026-20316 exploitation signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article: Remote unauthenticated attack implies network-detectable exploitation attempts. Deploy IDS/IPS rules and WAF signatures to catch hardcoded-password authentication-bypass attempts and known CVE-2026-20316 exploit traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable Suricata/Snort rules (or Palo Alto, Fortinet equivalents) specifically for CVE-2026-20316 exploitation. Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to Cisco FMC login endpoints with known hardcoded usernames or bypass payloads. Flag TLS/SSL handshake anomalies and malformed authentication requests to FMC management interface.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Integrity Anomaly – Hash/Content Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Adform Script' was 'poisoned' — direct evidence of script modification. Pipeline missed detection for unexpected changes to third-party JavaScript served from CDNs/tag managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cryptographic hashes or byte-count anomalies in third-party script responses (e.g., Adform, Google Tag Manager). Flag when script size changes unexpectedly, content hash diverges from baseline, or script version tags are incremented without vendor announcement.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution in Page Content
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'swap crypto wallet addresses' on customer sites. Pipeline missed regex-based detection for wallet address variations embedded in JavaScript or DOM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and baseline cryptocurrency wallet addresses (Bitcoin, Ethereum, XMR) from inline scripts and payment pages. Alert on appearance of new or unknown wallet addresses, especially in high-traffic third-party scripts. Cross-reference with known attacker wallets from blockchain analysis.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Connections from Advertising/Analytics Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned Adform script must exfiltrate or communicate; article implies script is executing unauthorized code on thousands of customer sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline known destinations for Adform and similar ad-tech scripts. Flag unexpected DNS queries or TCP connections initiated from script execution context, especially to non-WHOIS-attributed IPs, recently-registered domains, or IP ranges associated with crypto services.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise – Third-Party Tag/Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Adform (third-party script vendor) compromise affecting 'customer sites'. Pipeline failed to map T1195.002 or generate supply-chain integrity rule.
log_sources: Script load events from browser telemetry
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script includes from third-party vendors (e.g., script src= from Adform CDN) that execute code inconsistent with vendor's documented behavior. Correlate across fleet: if 100+ endpoints load the same Adform script variant with unusual DOM-mutation or exfiltration patterns, escalate as supply-chain compromise.

suggestion.title: JavaScript DOM Injection – Payment Form/Wallet Field Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Mechanism described: script 'swaps' wallet addresses, implying DOM mutation or form-field interception. No detection rule generated for JavaScript analyzing/modifying payment or crypto input fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scripts that query or mutate elements containing cryptocurrency addresses, wallet inputs, or payment forms. Alert if non-whitelisted scripts access innerHTML/textContent of wallet-related fields or invoke crypto-library functions (e.g., web3.js).

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Installation from Non-Standard Source
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'fake updates to deliver surveillance malware' as the execution vector. Pipeline produced no detection for update-chain compromise despite this being the primary attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or invalid code-signing certificates on software installers. Detect child processes spawned from installers in %TEMP% or %APPDATA% with network access patterns. Alert on processes launched with names mimicking legitimate OS updaters (svchost.exe, rundll32.exe) from unusual directories.

suggestion.title: Wi-Fi Beaconing and Network Hijacking Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack is 'hijacked hotel wi-fi'—network-level compromise of access point. Pipeline missed initial access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate client devices connecting to Wi-Fi SSIDs shortly before fake-update campaigns. Monitor for Wi-Fi deauthentication floods (KRACK-style attacks). Detect HTTP 302 redirects from legitimate update servers to attacker-controlled domains on hotel networks.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Payload is explicitly 'surveillance malware' with collection capabilities. No detection use case maps to C2 callback patterns from infected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to newly registered or uncommon domains immediately after fake-update execution. Detect recurring beaconing intervals (30s–5min) typical of surveillance implants. Correlate process network access with screen-capture / audio-capture system calls (T1113, T1123).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Update UI Overlay
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates commonly display fake login prompts. Article payload is surveillance-grade malware, likely harvests credentials or session tokens from hotel guest devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-manager API calls from update-installer child processes. Detect password entry into windows spawned by update processes. Alert on clipboard data exfiltration immediately after fake update completes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Update Server Domain Registration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack hinges on tricking users to download from spoofed or typo-squat update domains. Article mentions 'fake updates' but pipeline extracted zero related domains or IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate legitimate software vendor domains with recently registered homoglyphs or typo-squats in hotel network traffic. Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to update domains with valid-looking certificates issued to non-official entities. Monitor whois registration deltas for bulk domain registration (>5 domains in 7 days) sharing update-server naming patterns.

suggestion.title: Process Tree Anomalies from Update Installer
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate updates spawn predictable child processes; surveillance malware spawns screen-grabbers, clipboard monitors, keyloggers. No detection maps installer child-process patterns to known surveillance TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline: legitimate installers (Adobe, Windows, Chrome) spawn <3 children with predictable names. Flag installers spawning >5 unique child processes, especially rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, or svchost.exe with unusual command-line arguments. Correlate to suspicious DLL loading from APPDATA/temp.

suggestion.title: Detect AiTM proxy interception at captive portals
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets travelers via captive portals using Adversary-in-the-Middle techniques; 'CaptiveCrunch' campaign name references this vector directly. Pipeline missed entire attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP traffic interception patterns at public WiFi networks, DNS hijacking at captive portal handlers, or forced HTTPS downgrades. Flag connections to attacker-controlled proxy IPs that intercept auth requests at scale.

suggestion.title: Detect ClickFix malware delivery via phishing/social engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'ClickFix' technique as malware delivery method ('malware delivery and credential theft'). Pipeline failed to capture this social-engineering-based attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix patterns: fake error messages in compromised travel-related webpages driving users to download executables. Flag browser downloads of .exe/.msi from unexpected domains after user clicks on embedded links.

suggestion.title: Detect OAuth/session token theft post-AiTM compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'token theft' as objective; AiTM attacks at captive portals directly expose OAuth tokens and session cookies. Pipeline missed post-compromise credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token exfiltration post-AiTM compromise: AAD sign-in events from attacker-controlled IPs, impossible-travel anomalies (WiFi airport IP → user home IP within seconds), or token use from VPN/proxy infrastructure associated with Midnight Blizzard infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect malware execution from captive portal download chains
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'malware delivery'; article describes multi-stage attack (phishing → download → execution). Pipeline produced no detection logic for malware staging or execution from compromised portal infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of payloads downloaded from captive portal infrastructure or URLs matching travel/hotel domains. Flag living-off-the-land execution (PowerShell, WMIC, rundll32) used to decode/execute second-stage malware, and monitor for parent-child process chains initiated from browser processes with low reputation.

suggestion.title: Detect lateral movement post-malware execution on traveler devices
suggestion.rationale: Midnight Blizzard campaigns historically pivot to corporate networks post-compromise; article targets travelers, implying endpoint compromise before VPN/corporate access. Pipeline missed post-execution pivot detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised traveler devices for inbound connections to corporate VPN, RDP, or SSH ports immediately post-infection. Flag unusual credential use from geolocations consistent with Midnight Blizzard staging infrastructure (Eastern Europe, Russia-affiliated cloud providers).

suggestion.title: Detect ClickFix social engineering posts on compromised travel booking sites
suggestion.rationale: Article references ClickFix as delivery mechanism; ClickFix typically uses fake browser alerts on compromised webpages targeting high-traffic travel sites. Pipeline produced no webpage/content-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor travel booking / airline / hotel domains for injected JavaScript that generates fake system alerts (browser update prompts, malware warnings) with download links. Flag domains serving ClickFix payloads via static analysis (file reputation, certificate age, payload hosting patterns).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated signup followed by SQL-injection attempt in same session
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allowSignUp: true' enabling unauthenticated signup, then 'loggedIn' ACL allows immediate exploitation. This two-step attack pattern (signup + SQLi) within one session is the actual attack flow; pipeline missed it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful /api/auth:signUp (HTTP 200/201) with subsequent request to /api/myInAppChannels:list containing SQL-injection patterns (COPY, UNION, pg_sleep, --) from same source IP within 120 seconds. Alert on combination of signup + immediate SQL payloads.

suggestion.title: COPY TO PROGRAM SQL injection in latestMsgReceiveTimestamp filter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'COPY TO PROGRAM' as the RCE mechanism via the vulnerable filter field. Pipeline UC_9_3 flags generic SQL keywords but misses specific COPY...TO PROGRAM syntax that triggers shell execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search /api/myInAppChannels:list query parameters for 'COPY' adjacent to 'PROGRAM' or 'TO', optionally with shell metacharacters (pipes, semicolons, backticks, $()). If database audit-logging is enabled, flag COPY...TO PROGRAM statements executed by the application service account. This is the immediate RCE staging step.

suggestion.title: Time-based blind SQL injection probing on latestMsgReceiveTimestamp field
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies no escape/parameterization on the $lt filter value. Attackers will probe with time-based techniques (pg_sleep(N)) to confirm blind SQLi before RCE. Pipeline missed detection of probe/reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/myInAppChannels:list requests where latestMsgReceiveTimestamp filter contains pg_sleep(), PG_SLEEP(), or WAITFOR DELAY patterns. Correlate with abnormal HTTP response times (timeouts, delays >5 seconds). Flag repeated probing from same source IP across multiple sleep durations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit FMC, requiring immediate exposure hunt. No use case generated despite canonical asset-exposure template cited in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco FMC instances on internet-facing interfaces. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-20316. Flag any unpatched instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for repeated failed attempts followed by successful login using known default credentials or low-privileged built-in accounts, particularly from external IP space.

suggestion.title: FMC Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detection requires monitoring for data queries/exports by compromised low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries targeting threat policies, network configurations, or managed-device telemetry from low-privileged FMC accounts. Flag data exports initiated post-authentication from external sources.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Firewall Fleet
suggestion.rationale: FMC compromise enables command execution against managed Cisco appliances. Article implies sensitive data access includes managed-device state; requires monitoring for policy/config pushes post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous FMC authentications with subsequent configuration updates, policy pushes, or command execution against downstream managed Cisco Secure Firewall appliances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Patch Compliance Hunt vs. Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-08-01. Standard compliance hunt missing. Patch-lag is 'the silent killer' per article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Cisco FMC appliances remediated or mitigated by 2026-08-01 deadline. Flag any instances running vulnerable code versions post-deadline, especially if internet-facing.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset & Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation—requires external reachability. Pipeline generated no asset-inventory UC despite referencing template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances exposed to untrusted networks on management ports (443 default). Query asset inventory for FMC product matches. Cross-check installed version against Cisco's published CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions. Flag instances unpatched past federal 2026-08-01 deadline.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'hard-coded password...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in with low-privileged account.' No detection generated for credential exploitation attempts or successful usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful remote login from external/untrusted IPs using built-in/low-privileged accounts (common patterns: admin, monitor, default usernames). Alert on repeated failed auth attempts targeting known hard-coded credentials within 5-minute windows. Correlate successful auth with source IPs not in trusted admin ranges.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No UC models data exfiltration or extraction post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After identifying successful hard-coded credential login, correlate with FMC data-access events: policy exports, device-inventory queries, configuration backups, certificate/key extraction. Baseline normal admin query volume and flag anomalous bulk exports or access to sensitive crypto material within 10 minutes of suspicious authentication.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV active-exploitation status demands attack-pattern detection. Article lacks specific signatures but pipeline should model brute-force/bypass attempts against known hard-coded credential endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco FMC (default TCP 443) for high-frequency authentication attempts from single source IP over <10 minute window (brute-force on hard-coded accounts). Flag 401/403 response sequences followed by successful 200 from same IP. Detect common password-spray payloads targeting /admin, /login endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanning & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01). Pipeline must generate inventory-driven compliance hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Tenable/Qualys/Rapid7 for CVE-2026-20316 detections across all assets. Cross-reference Cisco FMC instances in CMDB against patched version baseline (Cisco advisory). Generate daily report of unpatched instances, escalate any unpatched instances present on 2026-08-02 (day after federal deadline) as breach-risk alert.

suggestion.title: Data Quality: Title/Body CVE Mismatch Detection

suggestion.title: Cisco Firewall Management Center — Internet-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability affects 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center' exploitable by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' CISA KEV entry implies active exploitation; pipeline provided no asset-exposure use case despite referencing _TEMPLATES.md asset-exposure pattern in article body.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Brute-Force — Cisco FMC Authentication

This is T1078.001 exploitation, but pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting login attempts with known weak or default credentials against FMC.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Audit — Hard-Coded Account Disabled Status
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation; article identifies low-privileged default account as attack vector. Pipeline provided no configuration-compliance use case to verify hard-coded accounts remain disabled or have been password-changed across the fleet.

Alert if any FMC reverts to default authentication state or re-enables local low-privileged accounts post-patch.

suggestion.title: Successful Cisco FMC Remote Access — Source IP Anomaly

Correlate timing with CISA alert publication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces (typical ports 443, 8305) for authentication attempts from external IP space. suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access Within Cisco FMC Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact includes 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—must detect anomalous data exfiltration or bulk queries of policies/credentials after exploitation foothold.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Network Exposure

Query firewall allow rules for any path from external/untrusted zones to FMC (ports 443, 8305, 8307). Compare against approved secure administrative access baselines and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker gains authenticated access to FMC which manages firewall estate—must detect anomalous use of FMC to pivot into managed firewall infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious FMC commands that alter firewall rules or access managed devices immediately after unexpected remote login to FMC. Flag policy changes or credential exports from FMC initiated by non-standard user accounts or from unusual access patterns.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Compliance: CVE-2026-20316

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Detection via Vulnerability Scanner

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-20316 discovery on any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center asset. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify systems where patch lag exists despite scanner findings.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data exports, policy rule downloads, or bulk configuration queries originating from authenticated but unexpected accounts or IPs immediately following successful FMC login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center inventory against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Alert on confirmed vulnerable instances, especially those exposed to internet per firewall rules.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Detection

suggestion.title: FMC Privilege Escalation via Low-Privileged Account

suggestion.title: Sensitive data access or configuration changes post-FMC authentication

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 patch compliance scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due-date 2026-08-01; asset inventory must scan for vulnerable Cisco FMC versions to identify unpatched devices before exploitation occurs.

suggestion.title: Network isolation of Cisco FMC from untrusted segments
