suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' exposed to 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access, requiring detection of all instances on the network for patch-status validation and exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center or Firepower Management Center instances visible in asset-management, port-scanning (ports 443, 8305, etc.), or vulnerability-scanner results. Cross-reference with patch-management logs to identify CVE-2026-20316 exposure and federal due-date risk (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Detect successful authentications from unexpected network ranges or anomalous login patterns indicating exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC login from public IP ranges, non-corporate networks, or geographic anomalies. Also flag credential-spraying patterns (repeated failed attempts followed by success) and logins to unpatched FMC versions matching CVE-2026-20316 affected builds.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged FMC Account Rapid Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Attack succeeds with 'low-privileged account' but immediately gains 'access to sensitive data'—indicating privilege escalation or horizontal movement within FMC post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track FMC activity following successful login from unexpected source: detect privilege-elevation requests, admin-level API calls, unrestricted configuration file access, or role-membership changes within 5–30 minutes of initial access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration or Threat-Intel Data Export
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall policies, threat-intelligence rules, and network topology—detect bulk exports post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk policy exports, threat-intelligence rule pulls, or network-topology queries from FMC via API or UI following anomalous login. Monitor outbound data transfers from FMC servers to external IPs or cloud storage within 1 hour of successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Persistence via Administrative Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker likely establishes persistence through new accounts or credential manipulation. 'Sensitive data access' suggests dwell-time and continuity of access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new administrator, service, or read-only accounts on FMC following anomalous login from external source. Flag password changes on existing admin accounts without associated change-management tickets within 60 minutes of unexpected access.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Against Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: CVE root cause is explicit: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline should detect the exploitation technique itself—credential-stuffing or brute-force attacks using known/default credentials against exposed management services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated authentication attempts to Cisco FMC (or any exposed management interface) using known-default or low-entropy credentials (e.g., 'admin'/'admin', manufacturer backdoors). Flag credential-stuffing campaigns with >10% success rate against unpatched CVE-2026-20316 targets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—implies FMC reachable from untrusted networks. Core asset-exposure hunt: identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible on public-facing network paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound connection attempts to FMC default management ports (443, 8305) from external/non-administrative IP ranges. Correlate successful connections with hosts returning Cisco FMC TLS certificate or HTTP response headers identifying Firepower/FMC software. Flag any instance not in approved administrative CIDR blocks.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded FMC Account Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling 'low-privileged account' access. Attackers will attempt login with embedded default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface using default/low-privilege account names from external or non-expected administrative IP addresses. Baseline legitimate FMC admin logins; flag deviations in source geography, time-of-day, or login count anomalies.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems'—FMC stores firewall policies, threat intelligence feeds, integration credentials, and VPN configs. Should detect abnormal data download/export activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk queries, backup exports, or API-driven downloads of FMC configuration, policy, or event databases by authenticated sessions from non-administrative IPs. Flag export operations outside maintenance windows, policy imports/exports to untrusted destinations, or credential access from FMC token/config storage.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'. Article template references mandate compliance hunt; pipeline did not generate patch-verification use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute Cisco-native vulnerability assessment or third-party scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) querying for CVE-2026-20316-affected Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center versions. Baseline all FMC instances against patched version manifest; escalate unpatched systems not meeting federal 2026-08-01 compliance deadline to patch management.

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Administrative Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: hard-coded credential compromise allows unauthorized admin interface access. Should hunt for privilege escalation, rule/policy tampering, or credential harvesting once foothold established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for suspicious administrative actions post-compromise: policy modifications, user account creation/deletion, integration credential changes, event log purging, or export of firewall rules/threat data. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or session anomalies to identify lateral-movement or data-theft indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit this, implying network accessibility. No asset-exposure hunt was generated despite template reference in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound network traffic to Cisco FMC default management ports (8305/TCP, 22/TCP) from untrusted networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for unpatched FMC versions (patch due 2026-08-01). Alert on any successful connection where patch status is unknown or confirmed vulnerable.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Success Post-Hardcoded-Credential Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using hard-coded password. No detection rule for authentication attempts to FMC or anomalous login patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC admin interface from non-administrative IP ranges or geographic anomalies. If hard-coded credentials are disclosed, trigger detection on ANY successful login attempt. Baseline legitimate FMC administrator logins and alert on deviations in time-of-day, source IP, or frequency.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within impacted systems' after logging in as low-privileged user. No post-exploitation detection for unauthorized data access was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API calls, config exports, or policy downloads initiated by low-privileged accounts. Alert on bulk data retrieval, policy/credential exports, or access to system configuration files by users without documented administrative need. Correlate with T1190 exploitation attempts in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute-Force Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability is exploitable via brute-force or credential-stuffing if password is weak or publicly disclosed. No attack-pattern detection for repeated failed auth or credential-stuffing activity was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to Cisco FMC from any single source IP. Alert on ≥5 failed attempts within 5 minutes, or ≥20 failed attempts within 1 hour (threshold adjustable per environment). Cross-reference source IP against known credential-stuffing infrastructure and public exploit databases.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker compromises FMC (which manages downstream firewalls/appliances), they can pivot to managed security devices. Article's 'sensitive data' likely includes device credentials. No lateral-movement detection rule was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for administrative connections FROM Cisco FMC management interface TO managed devices (Cisco ASA, Firepower sensors, IOS devices, etc.) using non-standard credentials or outside change-control windows. Alert on policy pushes or configuration changes initiated from FMC shortly after unpatched FMC access is detected.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due-date 2026-08-01. No asset-inventory use case for detecting unpatched FMC instances was generated, despite this being the most basic CISA KEV response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center / Firepower Management Center instances. Flag any instance with version < [patched version] as high-risk. Generate report of systems still outstanding as of 2026-08-01 federal due-date for escalation to asset owners.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit; CISA KEV status implies active wild exploitation. Requires asset discovery of FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances listening on external-facing interfaces or routable from the internet. Correlate with asset inventory and CVE-2026-20316 patch status to prioritize highest-risk instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'hardcoded password vulnerability' enabling login. Detect successful authentications exploiting the hardcoded credential or anomalous authentication patterns against FMC admin accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected external sources, especially targeting default or privileged accounts. Correlate failed login patterns with successful authentication to detect credential-stuffing or hardcoded-credential exploitation.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker goal as 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect unusual data retrieval or export activity following successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC authentication, flag bulk data access, configuration exports, policy downloads, or access to credential/key storage that deviates from baseline administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance & Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-08-01; CISA KEV requirement. Article explicitly references vulnerability scanner use for CVE matching. Standard compliance hunt for actively-exploited vulns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and patch systems for Cisco FMC version/patch levels. Flag instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 or lacking patches prior to the federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Hardcoded Credential Brute-Force or Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded passwords are discoverable via public disclosure, OSINT, or binary analysis. Article implies credential is exploitable by unauthenticated attacker, suggesting it may be guessable or already public.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential login failures against FMC accounts followed by successful authentication from the same source, or unusual patterns consistent with dictionary/brute-force attacks against common default accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-20316' as detection indicator; CISA KEV means actively exploited in the wild. Vulnerability scanner results are the first-line detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for instances of CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. Alert on any unpatched instances, particularly with FMC reachable from untrusted networks. Federal patch deadline was 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—must detect network-level access to management interfaces before credential use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, typically) from external/untrusted sources. Alert on repeated connection attempts, especially followed by authentication failures. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 exploit signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'log in to affected device using a low-privileged account'—implies known/default credentials being used. Authentication logs must show successful logins from external IPs or service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to FMC from external IP ranges or from accounts typically used for system services. Look for authentication patterns consistent with hard-coded/default credential use (rapid success, specific service account, off-hours). Cross-reference with Cisco advisory for actual account names.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-authentication data collection is the attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual database queries, large data exports, or API calls to extract configuration/credential data from FMC immediately after successful authentication. Look for queries on sensitive tables (user credentials, firewall rules, threat intelligence feeds) from non-standard sources.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Plane Configuration Changes by External Actor
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC can pivot to modify security posture; article implies access to 'sensitive data' but also control of management functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC configuration modifications (firewall rules, user accounts, threat defense policies) made from external IPs or during unusual maintenance windows. Baseline legitimate change windows and alert on deviations. Correlate timeline with authentication log anomalies.

suggestion.title: Egress Connections from FMC to Suspicious Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Compromised management appliance often used as pivot; unusual outbound traffic from FMC infrastructure signals potential C2 or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from FMC to non-whitelisted destinations, especially to known malicious IP blocks, dynamic DNS, or high-entropy domains. Baseline expected egress (threat intelligence feeds, licensing, support) and alert on anomalies with high confidence.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' — must detect successful FMC management auth from IPs outside trusted administrative ranges, at odd hours, or from untypical geographies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) for successful authentication events originating from non-whitelisted sources. Hard-coded credential exploitation typically succeeds on first or early attempt; alert on successful login from unexpected network segments or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Default/Low-Privilege Account Logon to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'log in using a low-privileged account' — detection must key on successful authentication with known default/service account names against FMC
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to FMC using accounts with names commonly associated with hard-coded defaults (e.g., 'cisco', 'admin', 'service', 'test'). Establish baseline of legitimate usage of such accounts and flag deviations in source IP, timestamp, or subsequent actions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation grants 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems' — detection must flag extraction of device configs, credentials, firewall policies after successful auth
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for export or retrieval of sensitive configuration objects (network device credentials, firewall rules, access policies) immediately following authentication from untrusted IP. Compare post-auth data-access patterns to baseline administrative workflows.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center on Internet
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active remote exploitation; article describes 'remote attacker' — must discover FMC management interfaces exposed to internet
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC signatures on internet-facing IPs: port 443/8305, SSL certificate fingerprints, HTTP response headers matching FMC version. Correlate against internal asset inventory to identify out-of-policy exposed instances requiring immediate remediation before patch due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article's Indicators of Compromise section explicitly lists 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner outputs for Cisco FMC instances reporting CVE-2026-20316. Alert on unpatched FMC installations, prioritizing those with internet exposure. Correlate with external network asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Login to Cisco FMC with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via hard-coded password vulnerability. This credential_access / exploitation phase was unmapped to any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface from unexpected/external sources. Monitor for low-privilege account logins without preceding authorized access patterns. Alert on access using known default or hard-coded account names.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege Cisco FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication. This collection/impact phase completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for sensitive configuration/policy exports, device data downloads, or API queries executed by low-privilege accounts. Alert on anomalous data access patterns from newly-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: T1190 mapping ('Exploit Public-Facing Application') implies FMC is internet-accessible. External accessibility precedes exploitation but no network reconnaissance UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8308) exposed to internet via external scanning or Shodan. Cross-reference with internal IPAM/asset data. Alert on externally-routable FMC management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Known Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is specifically 'use of hard-coded password'. Once credential details are disclosed, direct exploitation attempts become detectable but pipeline missed this UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Upon vendor disclosure of hard-coded credentials, create detection for login attempts using the known credential pair. Monitor for repeated authentication attempts with published hard-coded username/password combinations.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Center Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'—requires first identifying which instances exist on network; no asset inventory hunting logic provided. CISA KEV requires rapid inventory sweep.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network traffic patterns consistent with FMC web console discovery: successful HTTP/HTTPS connections to typical FMC ports (443, 8305) with banner/header grabs revealing 'Cisco', 'Firepower', 'FMC', or SSL certificate issuer matching Cisco. Baseline against asset inventory to find undocumented instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Account Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'—pipeline extracted zero detection logic for login attempts. Article names no specific account; typical low-privilege defaults on Cisco appliances are 'admin', 'cisco', or appliance-specific (e.g., 'servicewm'). No use case addresses baseline login patterns or credential-spray signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to any FMC instance from source IPs not in approved management CIDR. Flag repeated failed login attempts to same account followed by success within sliding window. Establish baseline of legitimate admin login times/sources; deviations indicate credential reuse or brute-force success.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration and Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no detection logic provided for post-compromise data access or configuration changes. Attacker with FMC access can pivot to managed firewalls, extract ACLs, security policies, or admin credentials stored in FMC database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected API calls or database queries from authenticated FMC sessions (especially low-privilege accounts) requesting policy exports, credential stores, or managed device configs. Monitor for bulk file downloads or API exports of security policies, user accounts, or device configurations immediately after successful FMC login.

suggestion.title: FMC Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access but FMC is a management center—pipeline missed the path to higher privilege or lateral movement to managed firewall instances. Typical follow-on: attacker escalates to admin within FMC or uses it as pivot point to firewall appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to modify user roles within FMC (escalate low-privilege account), or outbound connections from FMC instance to managed firewall appliances with command patterns inconsistent with normal orchestration. Flag any configuration push to firewalls immediately after unauthorized FMC login.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Administrative Actions on Cisco Secure Firewall Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies FMC (management center) but does not detail *what* an attacker would do post-access; pipeline generated zero logic for behavioral anomalies. Typical post-compromise: disabling security policies, adding backdoor accounts, modifying logging, or exfiltrating policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of admin actions (policy adds, rule modifies, logging config changes) per user/role over rolling 7-day window. Alert when low-privilege account or out-of-hours admin account triggers administrative operations exceeding baseline variance. Specifically flag: disabling audit logs, modifying syslog destinations, adding new admin users, policy deletes/disables.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance for FMC Ports and Services
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses remote unauthenticated access but provides no reconnaissance hunt logic. Attackers must discover FMC first—port scanning, service fingerprinting, or SSL certificate inspection on ports typically used by FMC (443, 8305). Pipeline produced zero asset enumeration logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network probes targeting FMC-typical ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external/untrusted sources, especially port scans followed by successful connection attempts. Flag SSL certificate enumeration (TLS SNI probes, JARM fingerprinting) against FMC web interface from IPs not in approved admin range. Baseline internal FMC discovery; external attempts are high-confidence.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and 'currently being exploited' (CISA KEV status). No hunt generated despite explicit 'asset-exposure' template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS access to Cisco FMC management interface (default port 443) from external/untrusted sources without prior authentication. Baseline port 8305 (FMC internal comms) and 8307 (threat defense communication) for unexpected inbound sessions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default/Hardcoded Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling login as 'low-privileged account'. No credential-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from the low-privileged hardcoded account. Correlate with source IP geolocation; exploit attempts will cluster from non-regional networks.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gain 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'. No collection/data exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk reads of FMC configuration, threat definitions, policy objects, or device inventory exports immediately after authentication. Baseline normal policy management queries; flag anomalous volumes or off-hours access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'exposed assets' requiring standard asset-exposure hunt. No exposure-detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run weekly Shodan/Censys queries for 'Cisco FMC' or 'Firepower Management Center' with ports 443, 8305, 8307 open to the internet. Cross-reference asset inventory; any unmanaged instances are immediate remediation targets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due 2026-08-01. Article specifies 'match against your vulnerability scanner'—no scanner-driven hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scans for 'CVE-2026-20316' or 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center' findings. Filter by 'not patched' or 'not remediated'; escalate any findings dated after federal due date 2026-08-01 as compliance violations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Cisco FMC Administrative Actions
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence risk. Attacker with low-privileged account access may escalate or persist via policy/rule changes. No lateral-movement or persistence hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for creation of new user accounts, permission grants, or policy rule modifications by the compromised low-privileged account or from unexpected source IPs. Flag any rule adds that white-list malicious C2 ranges or disable intrusion prevention rules.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded FMC Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated zero UCs for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for successful authentication using default or low-privilege service accounts from non-whitelisted IP addresses. Correlate with rapid-fire failed login attempts preceding success (credential guessing). Alert on any low-privilege account accessing administrative data stores post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat allows 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed the post-exploitation data exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual query patterns and data export operations originating from low-privilege FMC accounts immediately after successful authentication. Flag bulk config downloads, policy exports, or credential-store access by accounts that did not previously perform such actions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation in-the-wild Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active exploitation observed. Pipeline provided no active-exploitation hunting use case despite article title emphasizing 'observed exploited in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network traffic signatures associated with known CVE-2026-20316 exploits. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner logs for unpatched FMC instances matching affected versions. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to FMC management interface from external networks combined with subsequent successful auth within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unusual Authentication Patterns to FMC Management Console
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password means low-privilege account default credentials; article establishes remote unauthenticated access. Pipeline did not generate anomaly-detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for FMC authentication from approved source IPs and times. Alert on spike in failed login attempts followed by sudden success from previously unseen geography. Correlate with system asset exposure (public IP on management interface detected by scanner) to identify high-risk targets.

suggestion.title: Default FMC Service Account Activity Post-Patch Verify
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions low-privileged account abuse; federal due-date is 2026-08-01, creating audit/patching windows where detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FMC auth logs for any successful login to 'admin', 'default', or other low-privilege default accounts. Baseline expected sources (internal automation, vendor support). Alert on new-source logins or geographic anomalies. Cross-reference with patch compliance to identify unpatched systems with active authentication abuse.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repointing to Non-Branch Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' Tag manipulation to point to obfuscated commits is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags are moved to commits unreachable from default branch. Correlate with multiple tags repointed to same commit within 48 hours, indicating deliberate tag hijacking.

suggestion.title: External Network Ingress Tool Transfer from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
log_sources: GitHub Actions runner network egress logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected HTTPS/DNS requests from GitHub Actions runners to non-whitelisted domains during CI/CD execution. Prioritize requests to dynamic DNS, hosting providers, or freshly-registered domains coinciding with action run invocation.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exfiltration in GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Attack goal was 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs'—core exfiltration mechanism. No detection hypothesis addresses exposed credentials in workflow logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for high-entropy strings and credential patterns (AWS keys, API tokens, JWT signatures). Alert when secrets appear in logs without prior opt-in to secret masking, correlate with recent action version updates.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits Assigned to Released Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article explains attacker strategy: 'had the attack commit orphaned from any branches' then repointed existing tags to it. Orphaned + tagged commits are high-signal obfuscation pattern.
log_sources: GitHub GraphQL API commit ancestry queries
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits with tags that lack ancestry path to any active branch. Alert when orphaned commits are tagged shortly after creation or when multiple historic orphaned commits are suddenly tagged.

suggestion.title: Compromise of High-Dependency GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action' and attacker compromised the upstream repo itself—textbook supply chain attack on trusted dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor actions with >1000 dependents for unauthorized commits, version tag changes, or external URL additions in workflow definitions. Require approval before merging to main or tagging release on high-impact action repos.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Write Access Grant to Public GitHub Action Repo
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo' made the compromise possible. Write-access grants to shared infrastructure repos are critical to detect preemptively.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new collaborators or teams added with push/admin permissions to action repositories. Flag user grants from outside the organization or from accounts with no prior contribution history. Require CISO approval for write access to any repo with >500 dependents.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Instance Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit; exposed FMC instances must be inventoried. Pipeline missed asset-exposure hunt entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cisco FMC service fingerprints (ports 443, 8305) on internet-facing assets. Cross-reference CVE-2026-20316 scanner results against asset inventory. Alert on FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: FMC Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'; attacker exploits hardcoded password as primary attack vector. Pipeline missed credential-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed login attempts to FMC from external IPs targeting low-privilege accounts. Flag successful remote logins to FMC from non-corporate IP ranges. Correlate failed-then-successful patterns.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Data Extraction from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'; post-compromise, attacker reads firewall configs, credentials, policies from FMC. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API/database logs for bulk reads of sensitive config objects by low-privilege accounts. Alert on exports, backups, or unusual queries immediately following suspicious login.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance — Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Remediation Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-08-01; pipeline ignored deadline tracking despite note: 'Federal due-dates frequently match timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors/regulators.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patching progress for all Cisco FMC instances against 2026-08-01 federal deadline. Alert on unpatched assets 7 days before due date; escalate to compliance/audit for missed deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable FMC Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry with 'observed exploited in the wild' and federal patch due 2026-08-01. Pipeline must deliver basic vulnerability scanning baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Cisco FMC instances for product identification and version detection. Flag FMC versions released before CVE-2026-20316 patch date. Correlate with exposed management interfaces detected on external-facing IPs or DMZ segments.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'. Pipeline must detect use of embedded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for logins with default or hard-coded service accounts (typically 'admin' with embedded password). Flag successful logins from unexpected source IPs or outside business hours. Correlate multiple failed login attempts followed by success with hard-coded credentials.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit management center. Detection must catch initial access attempts before authentication succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management port (TCP 443) for connection attempts from external networks. Flag instances where unauthenticated TLS sessions attempt to reach FMC API endpoints or web interface. Detect banner-grabbing or service enumeration against FMC.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Data Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Once authenticated via hard-coded password, detect data collection and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC database and API logs for bulk data exports, policy configuration dumps, or credential harvesting from FMC's managed device inventory. Flag unusual database queries by low-privileged accounts accessing firewall rules, VPN credentials, or device configurations.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Instance Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation is only possible if FMC is reachable remotely. Article context implies management interface is public-facing (CISA KEV exploitation). Asset hunting is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute external asset scanning for Cisco FMC management interfaces on internet-facing IPs (default ports 443, 8305). Fingerprint by TLS certificate CN, HTTP headers, or FMC-specific response patterns. Flag any internet-routable FMC instances as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC 'Management Center' manages firewall fleet; compromise grants attacker pivot point to managed security appliances and network configuration abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC communication to managed firewall/IPS/AMP appliances for unauthorized API calls, credential pushes, or policy modifications initiated by the low-privileged account compromised via hard-coded password. Detect unexpected management traffic from FMC to internal security devices.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repositioning to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit' and notes 'the attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' No detection UC generated despite this being a primary obfuscation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags in public repositories are repointed to commits not on any tracked branch, or when tag push events occur from unusual accounts. Correlate Git tag changes with orphaned commit creation or push anomalies that precede them.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exposed in CI/CD Logs via Action Execution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Pipeline missed this credential exfiltration indicator despite article stating secrets appeared unencrypted where logs are public.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching known secret formats (AWS keys, API tokens, PII). Flag runs where encryption/redaction mechanisms fail to mask sensitive output, particularly when tied to dependency updates or version changes.

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Action Version Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Attack leveraged a widely-used open-source Action (23,000 dependent repos). Article does not mention detection of 'which repositories are consuming the compromised Action version' despite this being a critical supply-chain surface. Pipeline generated no tracking mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of pinned Action versions and monitor workflow files for usage of high-impact third-party Actions. Alert on rapid version changes, orphaned version references, or versions lacking corresponding GitHub releases.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from CI/CD Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Pipeline should have generated detection for unexpected egress from CI runners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline network egress from CI/CD jobs by Action, workflow, and organization. Flag external connections not present in baseline or deviating from expected patterns, especially to newly-registered or low-reputation domains.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commit Creation in Release-Critical Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates orphaned commits as primary obfuscation: 'having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' and 'these factors added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack.' No detection generated for orphaned commit abuse in public/critical repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits reachable only via direct hash reference or tag, not via any branch HEAD. Alert if such orphaned commits appear shortly before release tag updates or in repositories with high downstream dependency.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication Brute Force Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via hardcoded password; brute force is the canonical attack path. Pipeline generated zero credential-access detections.
log_sources: firewall management interface SSH/HTTPS access logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management ports (22, 443) for high-velocity failed authentication attempts. Alert on ≥10 failed logins within 5 minutes from single source IP. Correlate with successful authentication immediately following spray window to confirm credential compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Successful Login from Anomalous Source Post-Brute-Force
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device'; successful auth following failed spray is the post-compromise pivot. Pipeline missed initial-access / credential-access correlation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish geographic and IP-range baseline for authorized FMC admin logins. Alert on successful authentication from novel source IP, especially within 30 minutes of failed brute-force attempt. Cross-reference source IP reputation against threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Inventory and Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch deadline (today: 2026-08-01). Article template explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt; pipeline generated zero asset-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Cisco FMC with CVE-2026-20316 present. Cross-reference with network exposure data (internet-reachable, VPN-exposed, DMZ placement). Generate alert for each affected instance not patched by due date (2026-08-01). Correlate scanner data with firewall/proxy access logs to identify which instances have internet-facing management interfaces.

suggestion.title: FMC Authenticated Session Data Access and Export Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could access sensitive data within impacted systems'; post-compromise data collection is implicit but pipeline missed collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FMC admin activity (configuration reads, policy queries, standard reports). Alert on sessions performing unusual queries: bulk exports of security policies, threat intelligence databases, device configuration snapshots, or raw audit logs. Flag exports outside business hours or from non-standard admin accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Policy Modification Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded-credential compromise enables unauthorized admin access; persistence/evasion via configuration change is high-risk follow-on. Article does not describe post-exploitation behavior; pipeline missed impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FMC audit logging records all configuration changes with actor, timestamp, and delta. Baseline authorized admin change patterns and business windows. Alert on firewall rule insertion, IPS/IDS policy modification, logging/audit configuration disablement, or threat intel feed replacement. Correlate with authentication anomalies (successful login post-brute-force).

suggestion.title: Successful authentication to Cisco FMC with hard-coded credential
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. This is the core exploitation path and is fully detectable via authentication logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs (typically syslog or TACACS+) for successful logins using known hard-coded account names (e.g., 'admin', 'fmcadmin') from unexpected source IPs or with abnormal timing. Correlate with failed attempts suggesting brute-force before success.

suggestion.title: Multiple authentication attempts to Cisco FMC (credential enumeration)
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploitation implies attacker must discover or guess the credential. Article phrase 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' suggests brute-force or default-credential scanning precedes successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC (port 443, 8305) from single source IP within short time window, followed by successful login. Threshold: >5 failures then success within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unexpected remote access to Cisco Firewall Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and FMC is typically admin-tier asset. Any remote access from untrusted networks or outside change windows should trigger alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TCP connections to Cisco FMC (port 443/8305) from external or unexpected networks outside maintenance windows. FMC should have highly restricted access profile; any connection outside known admin ranges warrants investigation.

suggestion.title: Data access and potential exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Post-authentication, monitor for abnormal data retrieval, export, or forwarding behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for unusual database queries, policy exports, configuration downloads, or large data transfers out of management network. Baseline normal admin activity; alert on bulk data retrieval within hours of suspicious authentication.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from low-privileged FMC account
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions hard-coded password grants 'low-privileged account' access. Attacker will likely attempt to escalate to admin or root to access full sensitive data. Monitor for privilege escalation attempts post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC login with hard-coded credential, detect failed sudoers attempts, privilege elevation requests, or role-change commands. Cisco FMC runs on Linux; monitor /var/log/auth.log and FMC audit trail for privilege escalation patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner findings on exposed Cisco FMC instances
suggestion.rationale: Standard patch-lag hunt mentioned in article. Asset-exposure detection: any Cisco FMC instance responding on management ports suggests potential target for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner findings (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) identifying CVE-2026-20316 against network exposure data (port 443/8305 accessible from untrusted networks). Flag any unpatched FMC instances as critical; cross-check with asset inventory for deployment date vs. patch due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Authentication Attempt via Hard-coded Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' This is the direct attack vector and must be detectable via authentication logs showing successful login with known default/low-privilege accounts against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful login attempts using low-privileged or default account credentials from internet-facing sources. Correlate with failed attempts preceding success to detect brute-force or credential-stuffing patterns. Baseline normal FMC admin login locations and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Brute-Force Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password' exploitability. Attackers scanning for exposed FMC instances will attempt to authenticate using known default credentials. Detect high-frequency login failures followed by success or persistent failed attempts against FMC.
log_sources: Network IDS logs targeting port 443/8305 (typical FMC ports)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed authentication attempts (5+) within 10 minutes to Cisco FMC followed by a successful login, or sustained failed attempts indicative of credential enumeration. Correlate source IP reputation against public FMC instances.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Cisco FMC Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 affects specific Cisco FMC versions. Vulnerability scanners and asset inventories must identify exposed FMC instances and flag those with vulnerable software versions prior to the federal due date (2026-08-01).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco FMC asset inventory against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20316. Flag all externally accessible FMC instances with version < [patched version]. Correlate with any failed/successful authentication attempts from public internet ranges.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Access from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After successful authentication via hard-coded credential, attackers will exfiltrate FMC data (policies, network topology, credentials, firewall rules). Detect unusual data access or export activity.
log_sources: Network traffic egress (DNS, HTTP, HTTPS to external C2)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for data export, policy retrieval, or credential access by low-privileged accounts post-authentication. Flag mass downloads of configuration files, firewall rules, or device credentials. Correlate with outbound network traffic from FMC to known malicious IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: A compromised FMC instance provides attacker with visibility into managed firewall estate and ability to modify rules/policies. Detect lateral movement commands or reconnaissance activity originating from FMC post-breach.
log_sources: Managed firewall logs (detecting policy changes from FMC)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from FMC to internal subnets targeting non-standard ports (SMB, RDP, SSH). Detect firewall rule modifications originating from the FMC console following suspicious authentication. Monitor DNS requests from FMC for reconnaissance domains.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Network-Accessible Exposure Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' and CISA KEV implies 'observed exploited in the wild.' Confirm FMC is exposed to internet and reachable on management ports (typically 8305 HTTPS). This is a prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform network scans to confirm Cisco FMC is NOT externally accessible on standard management ports (8305, 443 for FMC). If FMC is internet-facing, immediately isolate and patch. Cross-reference firewall rules to confirm management access is restricted to known admin networks only.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Authentication with Known/Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password vulnerability—this is credential access with pre-known credentials, not a random brute force.
log_sources: Firewall/proxy logs capturing HTTPS management-port access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC (typically port 443, 8305) where username matches known hardcoded account names (e.g., 'admin', low-priv defaults) and login source is external/unexpected. Track failed login attempts followed by success with low-privilege accounts—pattern suggests credential-stuffing after discovery.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers gain 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires hunt for post-compromise data collection/exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data-access patterns in FMC audit logs: policy exports, rule/configuration bulk queries, or unusual API calls from low-privilege accounts. Look for file transfers or data staging following successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Facing Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation and MITRE mapping cites T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application)—implies vulnerable FMC instances exposed on internet.
log_sources: Network flow data (external to internal FMC)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate assets running Cisco FMC management on public-facing ports. Cross-reference against patched inventory to identify unpatched instances. Correlate external network flows targeting FMC management ports (443, 8305) with failed/successful logins.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Discovery and Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'use of hard-coded password'—implies attackers may have or derive the embedded credentials and attempt reuse across FMC fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when the same credential combination (low-privilege account + hardcoded or common password) attempts to authenticate across multiple FMC instances within short time window, or when authentication attempts succeed from unexpected geographies/source IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication Success
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — requires baseline of FMC authentication events and alerting on successful logins with known/default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful FMC management interface authentications preceded by failed login cycles (credential stuffing), or from IP addresses/geographies inconsistent with normal administrative access patterns. Correlate authentication source IP reputation against known public proxy services.

suggestion.title: FMC Low-Privilege Account Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — low-privilege accounts should not normally export firewall policies, device configs, or threat intelligence; detect deviation from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API calls or data export requests from low-privilege FMC accounts, especially within minutes of first successful authentication. Flag access to /api/fmc_config endpoints containing policy, device, or intelligence data.

suggestion.title: FMC Public-Facing Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190) — requires detection of scanning and probe attempts targeting exposed FMC web interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FMC management endpoint (port 443, paths /login, /api, /) with exploitation payloads, unusual methods, or credential-testing patterns. Alert on rapid POST /login attempts followed by successful 200 response and immediate API enumeration.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco FMC Inventory Urgency Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV published 2026-07-29; federal patch due date is 2026-08-01 (today). Requires immediate confirmation that no instances running vulnerable versions remain in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco FMC version inventory against CVE-2026-20316 patch advisory. Any FMC instance on versions before the fix release constitutes active compromise risk and requires immediate priority patching or isolation.

suggestion.title: FMC Command & Control over Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Article refers to 'impacted systems' (plural); successful FMC compromise enables lateral movement to firewalls managed by FMC. Detect unauthorized configuration pushes or commands to downstream devices.
log_sources: FMC to firewall SSH/HTTPS session logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for configuration pushes or remote execution commands from FMC to managed firewall devices that occur shortly after suspicious low-privilege account authentication or API abuse in FMC logs.

suggestion.title: FMC Default Credential Brute-Force Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password' implies attacker either knows or will enumerate the credential — typical brute-force signature required before successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 5+ failed authentication attempts against FMC followed by success within 5 minutes from the same source IP. Cross-reference source against known Cisco FMC default credential lists (factory defaults, hardcoded creds released in advisories).

suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Poison Adform Script' — detection should catch unauthorized modifications to third-party ad scripts before deployment to customer sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adform CDN responses and script hashes for unexpected changes. Alert on script version mismatches between expected and delivered payloads. Implement integrity checks on critical third-party JavaScript before injection into DOM.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Anomalies in Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites' — malicious wallet replacement in transaction flows requires detection of address substitution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect regex patterns for cryptocurrency wallet addresses in web traffic and compare against known legitimate addresses. Flag when a page serving crypto transactions suddenly references new or previously unknown wallet addresses.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: 'Poison Adform Script' implies injection or modification of trusted external JavaScript — baseline third-party script content hashes and alert on deviations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain SHA256 hashes of known-good versions of popular ad tech and analytics scripts. Alert when browser requests to script CDNs return content with unexpected hashes, especially if correlated with new DOM modifications.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise Detection via Script Source Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is poisoning 'across customer sites' using a single compromised source — detect when one upstream change impacts multiple downstream organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate script injection or delivery anomalies across multiple customer/tenant boundaries. If one upstream service (Adform) shows modification activity followed by correlated downstream alerts from unrelated customers, escalate as supply chain compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DOM Mutations Targeting Payment/Wallet Fields
suggestion.rationale: Wallet replacement occurs post-render — detection should monitor JavaScript's DOM-manipulation APIs for suspicious modifications to payment or crypto address fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DOM mutation observer events and element replacements targeting input fields with 'wallet', 'address', 'payment', or 'crypto' in their selectors or aria-labels. Alert if third-party script (especially ad-tech) modifies these fields post-page-load.

suggestion.title: Ad-Tech Infrastructure Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Adform is a major ad-serving platform; compromise of the script distribution point requires infrastructure-level detections for unusual authentication or deployment activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adform API keys, CDN credentials, and deployment pipelines for unusual access patterns: off-hours logins, geographic anomalies, permission escalations, or bulk script updates without corresponding ticket trails.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Update Delivery over Unencrypted Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi pushes fake updates to deliver.' Pipeline must detect unsigned or mismatched-signature binaries distributed over public networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable/installer downloads over public Wi-Fi networks. Cross-reference file hashes against legitimate vendor signatures. Flag execution of binaries lacking valid digital certificates. Prioritize .exe/.msi/.dmg/.apk from non-standard update domains or spoofed infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Capability Detection (Screen/Audio/Keystroke)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'surveillance malware' payload. This implies persistent collection via screen capture, audio recording, and keystroke logging—detectable via API/syscall monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes loading screen/audio capture APIs (DirectShow, CoreAudio, AVFoundation) or executing syscalls for input/screen enumeration, especially if spawned from staging locations (Temp, Downloads) or recently installed software. Correlate timing with Wi-Fi connection events.

suggestion.title: Certificate and Update Server Signature Spoofing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Wi-Fi redirects update checks to attacker infrastructure via ARP/DNS spoofing. Detection must validate certificate chain integrity before software installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SSL/TLS connections to known software update domains (Apple, Microsoft, etc.) presenting self-signed, expired, or brand-mismatched certificates. Correlate with public SSID connection logs. Alert on certificate issuer mismatch even if the chain validates successfully.

suggestion.title: Rogue or Hijacked Wireless Access Point Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi.' Detection must identify unauthorized AP spoofing, weak encryption on known SSIDs, or suspicious SSID behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor device associations to hotel/public Wi-Fi from unexpected geographic locations or unusual hours. Alert on missing WPA2/WPA3 encryption on known hotel networks, rapid SSID changes, or multiple access points with identical SSID and conflicting MAC addresses.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon and Surveillance Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware requires persistent command-and-control and egress for exfiltrated data (screenshots, audio, keystrokes). Pipeline failed to surface C2 infrastructure or exfil patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS from devices post-hotel-Wi-Fi access, especially to newly-registered domains or IPs lacking reputation history. Flag frequent small-packet requests (keystroke logs, periodic screenshots) or large sustained outbound transfers typical of surveillance data staging and exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Authenticated editor credential abuse: PATCH to non-standard endpoints post-SSPP
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated editor' required, but UC_5_2-5_3 don't correlate credential context. After successful __proto__ pollution, attacker retains editor context but accesses protected resources. Missing: hunting for SAME credential making unexpected POST/PATCH/DELETE calls to admin endpoints after SSPP attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authenticated Web.http_user logins with subsequent PATCH requests containing __proto__, then flag the same user making GET/POST to admin endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/@apostrophecms/admin/*) shortly after. Indicates credential hijacking or role-based access bypass via prototype pollution.

suggestion.title: Object.prototype mutation: shared-state pollution affecting concurrent requests
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'process-wide authorization bypass'—implying Object.prototype modifications persist across requests. Missing: detection of anomalous response behavior (e.g., multiple unrelated API endpoints returning data out-of-band or shared state leaks). Phrase: 'process-wide authorization bypass' suggests runtime memory compromise, not just single-request tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-SSPP exploitation, look for cross-request anomalies: simultaneous 200 responses from protected endpoints by different users/sessions with shared response patterns, OR rapid-fire API calls with identical response times (suggesting cached/polluted prototype). High specificity but requires baseline of normal concurrent behavior.

suggestion.title: POST-exploitation: mass enumeration of now-accessible protected resources after SSPP
suggestion.rationale: Article states auth bypass leads to 'process-wide authorization bypass' but doesn't detail the post-exploitation data-exfil phase. Once prototype is polluted, attacker gains broad access. Missing: hunt for sudden spike in 200 responses to protected endpoints from single source post-PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After UC_5_4 correlation (PATCH + GET within 30min), measure the rate of subsequent GET requests to endpoints matching `/api/v1/@apostrophecms/*` from same source. Spike in 200-responses (>10x baseline) within 5 minutes of successful SSPP indicates resource enumeration post-privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt: PATCH with $pullAll and array-type payloads targeting __proto__
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies `$pullAll` patch operator is the gadget. Current UC_5_2 looks for __proto__ OR pullAll as string keywords, but doesn't confirm the structural PATCH payload format (JSON body with operator). Missing: more precise signature detection for actual SSPP payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Splunk: detect PATCH requests where POST body contains both `"__proto__"` AND `"$pullAll"` as JSON keys in same object, e.g., `{"__proto__": {...}, "$pullAll": [...]}`. Reduces false positives vs. keyword-only detection. Requires HTTP body inspection.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: vulnerability scanners probing for ApostropheCMS with version-specific payloads
suggestion.rationale: UC_5_5 finds exposed endpoints but not scanning behavior. Article doesn't mention version detection, but publicly disclosed SSPP implies scanner activity. Missing: hunt for reconnaissance patterns (HEAD requests, OPTIONS, or version-probing User-Agents) targeting @apostrophecms endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on User-Agent strings containing known vuln-scanners (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) making requests to `/api/v1/@apostrophecms/*` endpoints, or HEAD/OPTIONS requests to discovery paths. Early-stage indicator of active reconnaissance before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal WiFi Exploitation Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'CaptiveCrunch' directly indicates malware delivery via compromised WiFi captive portals. Article targets 'travelers worldwide'—a mobile/airport/hotel WiFi victim profile. No detection UC was generated despite this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous DHCP/DNS responses or SSL certificate mismatches on public WiFi. Monitor for unexpected captive portal redirects to non-standard ports or domains mimicking legitimate hotel/airport login pages.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Proxy Activity
suggestion.rationale: Schema keywords list 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' as explicit technique. AiTM requires proxy infrastructure, certificate forging, or traffic interception—core IOCs and network signatures that pipeline failed to surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificates issued by unusual CAs or self-signed certs for known legitimate domains (banks, email, travel sites). Monitor for SSL decryption/re-encryption patterns in proxy logs or anomalous certificate chains.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'ClickFix'—a social engineering technique that tricks users into downloading or executing malware through fake error popups. No execution-phase UC was generated despite this being a core delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of suspicious popups/dialogs overlaying browser windows, particularly those mimicking Windows/macOS/Android system errors. Correlate with subsequent unsigned executable downloads or suspicious child process spawns.

suggestion.title: Token Theft and Unauthorized Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'Token theft' as explicit objective. Article describes credential + token-based attacks. Pipeline missed detection logic for stolen session tokens, browser cache theft, or credential manager extraction post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access_token or refresh_token exfiltration via process memory dumps, clipboard access targeting auth caches, or unusual API calls reading %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials or browser profile token stores.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Malware Execution on Travelers
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'malware delivery' as primary objective; no detection use case generated for execution phase despite this being central to the campaign. Expect payload staging, lateral movement within traveler networks, or C2 callbacks.
