suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Authentication Attempts to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in…using a low-privileged account.' This is the attack vector—hard-coded creds allow direct login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated authentication attempts to Cisco FMC (default port 8305, 443) from external/unexpected sources. Flag successful logins from non-whitelisted IPs or during off-hours, especially if preceded by scanning or enumeration.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Usage in Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' If the cred is known or disclosed, attackers will attempt login with the fixed password.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded or default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'root', vendor defaults). Cross-correlate against credential management system to confirm hard-coded vs. provisioned secrets.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker…to access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall policies, rule sets, and network topology—high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual volume or frequency of data exports, policy downloads, or configuration backups from FMC. Alert on egress of firewall rulesets, topology maps, or credential repositories to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sensitive data' access; FMC has visibility and potential control over managed firewalls. Compromised FMC can pivot to firewall estates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for unusual push operations to managed devices (firewall rule changes, policy deployments, software updates) especially if correlated with unauthorized FMC login or unusual administrative sessions.

suggestion.title: Federal Compliance Deadline Tracking for CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01. Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Flag any running versions ≤ patched version as of 2026-08-01. Escalate to compliance team and remediation workflow immediately.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Redirect to Malicious Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit'—direct tag manipulation as a supply-chain attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository push events for unexpected modifications to release tags, especially version tags (v1, v35, etc.) being repointed to different commits. Alert when a tag's commit reference changes after initial creation, particularly if the new commit is orphaned or off main branches.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in High-Value Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies orphaned commits as a 'key enabling factor': 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' provided obfuscation that eluded detection during the initial compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits pushed to supply-chain-critical repositories that are immediately not reachable from any branch or tag. Flag orphaned commits in high-risk repos (DevOps tools, widely-used actions), especially if subsequently tagged or if push logs show tag manipulation.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Appearing in Plaintext in Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Central attack outcome described: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs. This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching encrypted secret formats (AWS key prefixes, OAuth token structures) appearing in plaintext output. Cross-reference with repository secrets to detect when a secret's value is unencrypted in build logs; correlate with recent action version or workflow file changes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Runners
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the detection method that exposed the attack: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from GitHub Actions runners for unexpected external domains/IPs not matching documented action dependencies. Alert on network calls initiated by recently-modified actions or actions using newly-redirected version tags.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized or Anomalous Write Access to Popular GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Foundational enabler described as: 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo that houses this GitHub Action code'—write access to 23,000-repo-dependency is the root cause and should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository access changes for high-impact projects (popular actions, widely-forked libraries, DevOps tools used by 1000+ repos). Alert on unexpected write-permission grants, service-account privilege escalation, or access grants to accounts without prior org activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: GitHub Action Version Tag Digest Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates consumers pin versions by tag: 'uses: tj-actions/changed-files@v35'—23,000 repos reference version tags expected to resolve to specific commits, enabling tag-redirect poisoning of all downstream users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For GitHub Actions workflows, maintain a whitelist of expected commit SHAs per action version tag (e.g., v35 → known SHA). Flag when a pinned action version resolves to an unexpected commit hash in workflow runs, indicating tag manipulation or redirect.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' This is the core exploitation mechanism and must be detected at authentication layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account identifiers or weak credential patterns. Alert on low-privileged account access to management interface followed by queries to sensitive configuration objects. Baseline typical access per role; flag deviations in query scope or export frequency.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access to Exposed FMC Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' — requires detection of FMC management interface exposure and inbound exploitation traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to FMC management ports (TCP/443, TCP/8305) from non-management networks or external IPs. Flag multiple authentication failures (potential exploitation attempts) followed by successful access. Correlate with known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration Data Exfiltration via Low-Privileged FMC Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-authentication data extraction must be detected to identify successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls from low-privileged accounts querying or exporting sensitive FMC objects (firewall policies, threat intelligence feeds, VPN credentials, user/device inventory). Alert on bulk exports or access to restricted configuration fields outside normal baseline for account role.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Presence in Cisco FMC Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly instructs 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Presence detection is foundational; federal patch deadline 2026-08-01 requires high-fidelity asset visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC instances for CVE-2026-20316 using version fingerprinting or vulnerability-specific detection. Alert on all unpatched instances as critical; flag post-deadline unpatched systems. Cross-reference with internet-exposure data (Shodan/Censys queries) for externally-accessible FMC instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Access from Attacker Infrastructure or Anomalous Geography
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential attacks often originate from compromised VPS, Tor exits, or datacenters. Geographic/network anomalies indicate likely exploitation rather than administrative access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate FMC administrative access: source geographies (corporate offices, VPNs, SOC), time-of-day patterns, source ASNs. Alert on logins from VPN exit nodes, Tor, datacenter IP ranges, high-risk countries, or night-time access outside normal patterns. Correlate authentication failures with successful access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Authentication via Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using 'hard-coded password' — authentication is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful remote logins using low-privileged or service accounts, especially from external networks. Baseline normal admin access; alert on off-hours access, geographic anomalies, or velocity patterns consistent with credential spray.

suggestion.title: FMC External Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' under T1190 exploit context — requires discovery/inventory of exposed FMC instances before credential attack can occur. Pipeline missed initial-access reconnaissance layer entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Cisco FMC instances with management interfaces (443, 22) exposed to untrusted networks. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner data; prioritize unpatched instances. Flag any FMC accessible without VPN gateway or firewall restriction.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' as the objective — requires detection of lateral data movement after credential compromise. Zero post-authentication collection detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk configuration retrieval, policy exports, or topology data queries by low-privileged accounts, especially following successful remote authentication. Baseline typical administrative queries; alert on unusual scope or volume within 24 hours of login event.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Detection in FMC Configuration Baselines
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'use of hard-coded password' — implies credentials embedded in configs, backups, or setup scripts. Pipeline failed to suggest config-baseline detection for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC configuration files, disaster-recovery backups, and initial setup logs for embedded credentials or hardcoded account strings. Correlate with version checks against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions. Alert on any instance not patched by 2026-08-01 still in operation.

suggestion.title: Failed-Then-Successful FMC Authentication (Credential Spray Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded credential scenario implies attackers test multiple accounts or timing before successful login. Spray-attack pattern detection essential for this attack class but absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 8+ failed authentication attempts to FMC followed by success from the same source IP within 10-minute window. Separate signal from legitimate lockouts by correlating with user account policies. Flag external IPs especially.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and references 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190). Asset exposure is the foundational hunt for any remote-exploitation KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accepting inbound connections from untrusted networks on management ports (typically 443, 8305, 6526). Cross-reference asset inventory against vulnerability scan results to find exposed/unpatched instances before exploitation occurs.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password' allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Attackers will attempt to leverage these credentials; detection requires monitoring authentication events to FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hardcoded/default account names from external sources or multiple failed auth attempts preceding success. Correlate with network telemetry to confirm source is untrusted.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access on Cisco FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat actors 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after authenticating. Detection must cover data exfiltration or bulk-export of policy/configuration data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or access to sensitive objects (threat intelligence feeds, VPN credentials, firewall rules) on Cisco FMC shortly after unexpected successful authentication. Baseline normal admin activity first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Inventory Check Against CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and CISA KEV implies active exploitation. Inventory-based detection is mandatory for compliance and active-threat response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances and compare version/patch level against the fixed version for CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize instances that are both unpatched and reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Lateral Movement from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC has privileged access across the network to managed firewalls; article threat model implies attacker may pivot after initial compromise to 'sensitive data' across managed infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC initiating connections to managed firewall instances, internal infrastructure, or policy-management targets outside normal change-management windows. Correlate with authentication anomalies on the FMC itself.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'—implying management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks. Article references asset-exposure hunt template but pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for FMC management interface access (ports 443, 8305) from non-whitelisted networks. Correlate with failed authentication attempts suggesting reconnaissance. Baseline legitimate mgmt IPs/users and alert on deviations, especially from external/residential IP space.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Hard-Coded Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'log in using a low-privileged account'—pipeline must detect successful authentication via hard-coded or default credentials mapped to low-privilege FMC roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC auth logs for successful logins from generic/service accounts or with known default credential patterns. Correlate with failed attempts (brute force indicator). Alert if low-privilege auth immediately followed by privilege escalation attempts or sensitive config access.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—this is the actual harm; pipeline must detect exfiltration or bulk reads post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication, hunt for bulk export/read of firewall policies, device configs, monitoring data, or stored credentials. Flag policy/config exports by newly-authenticated users outside normal admin patterns. Correlate exports → lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs: 'CVE-2026-20316—match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline IOC output is empty; must surface this CVE for scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2026-20316 against all vulnerability scan reports. Flag Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances—both current and legacy 'Firepower Management Center' names. Verify patch status; assume scanner false-negatives and manually confirm patch installation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute Force / Hard-coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via 'hard-coded password vulnerability' — direct credential compromise threat requiring login attempt detection and suspicious-credential-pattern matching
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (ports 8305–8307) for high-volume failed/successful authentication attempts. Alert on successful logins from unexpected source networks. Establish baseline of normal administrative access patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Access from Low-Privileged FMC Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'low-privileged account' and can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — data exfiltration via the compromise is a key post-exploitation indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when low-privileged user accounts query firewall rules, threat intel, or policy data from FMC. Correlate successful logins with abnormal data retrieval volume or sensitive object access (e.g., crypto keys, site-to-site VPN configs).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised FMC Management Channel
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a centralized management plane controlling downstream Cisco firewalls across the environment — compromise creates risk for policy injection and fleet-wide reconfiguration. 'Sensitive data' access likely includes control over managed devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-FMC-compromise, hunt for unusual FMC-to-firewall API calls, unexpected policy pushes to devices outside normal change windows, or creation of new admin accounts on managed firewalls. Flag any device reconfiguration immediately following FMC login anomalies.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active wild exploitation; article references 'exploit public-facing application' (T1190) — asset discovery and exposure assessment are foundational to limiting blast radius
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances exposed to untrusted networks (internet, DMZ). Cross-reference against approved management VLAN/jump-host topology. Flag any FMC management interface reachable without documented bastion-host intermediary.

suggestion.title: Adform CDN Script Hash Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Hackers Poison Adform Script'—direct script modification. No detection for script integrity monitoring or hash anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CSP reports and script-src violations. Alert when Adform script hashes (SHA256 of *.adform.net/*.js) diverge from known-good baselines. Cross-reference script variants across customer sites; broad rollout of new hash = potential supply chain compromise. Exclude legitimate Adform updates via vendor advisory.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism is 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites'—direct wallet substitution in rendered pages. No detection for payment-form tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DOM mutation observer payloads or inline script insertion targeting form fields, payment containers, or text nodes matching crypto wallet patterns (0x + 40 hex, 1A-3J alphanumeric, etc.). Alert on script-injected regex substitution of wallet addresses in page source or visible content.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Network Beacon to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned Adform script must exfiltrate wallet swaps or beacon compromised state. Article implies C2 or data exfil; no detections for script-initiated outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Adform script's normal outbound destinations (*.adform.net, analytics partners). Alert on new/rare external FQDN or IP initiated by Adform script context. Correlate with other customer sites; if N sites suddenly beacon to attacker-owned IP post-compromise, escalate.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Transaction from Suspected Compromised Page
suggestion.rationale: End goal is financial theft via substituted wallet addresses. No detection for unusual crypto transactions originating from users on affected sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser proxy logs (user session on site with Adform script) with downstream blockchain transactions in victim's wallet for that timeframe. Alert on transactions to newly-seen recipient addresses immediately post-visit. Whitelist known payment processors; flag direct-to-exchange or direct-to-attacker transfers.

suggestion.title: Unusual Adform Script Load from Non-Standard Path or Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must inject poisoned script or redirect legitimate requests. Article implies script-hosting compromise; no detection for off-path or CDN-bypass loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor script-src CSP violations or X-Content-Type-Options mismatches on Adform imports. Alert when script-src = attacker-controlled domain or non-HTTPS, or when script loads from IP instead of FQDN. Correlate load timing: if poisoned version appears only to subset of users, indicates targeted rollout or cache-poisoning.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Incident: Adform Script Integrity Baseline Divergence
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is Adform platform compromise or MitM on CDN. No kill-chain reconstruction identifies the breach vector; detection should flag supply chain compromise patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Customers should publish SRI (Subresource Integrity) hashes for third-party scripts. Alert when script contents hash to unexpected value despite matching URL. If Adform CDN is compromised, site-served SRI will fail; correlate SRI violations with user-agent, referer, and geo. Check for geofenced poisoning (attacker serves malicious variant only to specific regions).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Following Software Update
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is delivered via 'fake updates'—the update installation should trigger process execution detection logic. Detection of unexpected child processes spawned by updater binaries is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where a known software updater executable spawns child processes with network activity or file write permissions. Fake updates typically install payloads immediately after extraction. Cross-reference process trees against legitimate update behavior for that application.

suggestion.title: HTTPS Outbound Connections to Anomalous Domains Post-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'surveillance malware'—malware must beacon to command-and-control. Detect outbound HTTPS or HTTP connections initiated shortly after update process completion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by or related to update mechanisms that establish outbound connections to unrecognized domains within minutes of execution. Surveillance malware typically performs initial C2 check-in or beaconing. Use known-good domain whitelist for legitimate updaters to reduce FPs.

suggestion.title: Compromised or Spoofed Wi-Fi Network Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi'—network-level detection of spoofed SSIDs or anomalous DHCP/DNS responses from hotel networks offering updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when endpoints receive DHCP or DNS responses from hotel Wi-Fi networks (identifiable by SSID patterns) that offer unexpected software updates or redirect legitimate update traffic. Monitor for man-in-the-middle indicators such as certificate mismatches or DNS sinkholing to known malicious update servers.

suggestion.title: Update Traffic Interception or Certificate Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery mechanism as fake updates—endpoints should validate update certificates. Detect SSL/TLS certificate mismatches or invalid chains for known software vendors over hotel networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS certificate validation failures or unexpected certificate issuers for legitimate software publishers when updates are requested. Compare certificate chains observed in hotel/public networks against known-good chains from corporate environments.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is explicitly 'surveillance malware'—detection should focus on telemetry exfiltration, screen recording, keylogging, or camera access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access patterns consistent with surveillance: reads from screen buffer, keyboard input hooks, repeated file system scanning of documents/photos, or attempts to access camera/microphone APIs. Correlate with network exfiltration to unknown external IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Update Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article's core mechanism is compromised update distribution—this is supply chain compromise. Detect when legitimate update channels serve unexpected binaries or versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor update downloads for hash mismatches against known-good publisher hashes, unexpected file sizes, or version downgrades. Alert on update installations that do not match the published publisher's release notes or signatures.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS SSPP: JSON request-body payload containing __proto__ and $pullAll operators
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability triggered 'via the `$pullAll` patch operator' but queries only inspect URL parameters. Payloads are likely POST/PATCH body JSON: {"$pullAll": {"__proto__": ...}}. Current UC_6_2 misses this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* endpoints where request body JSON contains both `$pullAll` key and `__proto__` string. Correlate with 5xx error responses (exploitation attempts) or 200 success (successful pollution).

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS post-exploitation: authenticated user accessing previously-denied admin endpoints after SSPP window
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'process-wide authorization bypass' indicates Object.prototype pollution modifies global authorization logic. Detection should track 403/401 responses for same user/session followed by 200 responses to admin endpoints within hours, not minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each authenticated user, track 403/401 attempts to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/admin/* endpoints. Correlate with subsequent 200 responses from same user to same endpoint family within 24 hours. Flag as privilege escalation via authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS SSPP gadget chain: NODE_OPTIONS or process.env property access post-pollution
suggestion.rationale: Object.prototype pollution typically chains to RCE via environment variable gadgets (NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_DEBUG, etc.). Article's 'process-wide' phrasing suggests environment-scope compromise. Current detections miss this escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js processes spawned with suspicious NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_DEBUG, or modified process.env (via WMI/ETW) immediately following ApostropheCMS API PATCH activity. Flag command injection payloads in env vars (backticks, $(…), etc.).

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS SSPP: Rapid sequence of 401→200 status codes for same endpoint by same user
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker should immediately test whether pollution worked by re-accessing denied endpoints. Article describes authorization bypass; tracking auth failure→success should be near-real-time indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 10 seconds of authenticated user receiving 401/403 on /api/v1/@apostrophecms/admin/*, track for 200 response from same user to same endpoint. Fast retries after auth failures suggest active exploitation testing.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS SSPP: Constructor property injection patterns in API payloads
suggestion.rationale: Prototype pollution often chains via `constructor.prototype` gadgets. While article focuses on `__proto__`, comprehensive detection should also flag `constructor` property writes to Object.prototype paths in PATCH/POST payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies for JSON patterns matching `{"constructor": {"prototype": {…}}}` or nested constructor chains sent to ApostropheCMS piece-type API endpoints. High specificity; low false-positive rate.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal Exploitation and Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references captive portal attack infrastructure (CaptiveCrunch campaign targeting travelers); pipeline missed entire initial access vector despite prominence in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious DHCP or DNS responses from public WiFi networks that redirect users to captive portal clones. Detect mismatches between advertised portal domain and actual certificate CN. Alert on travel-associated geolocation patterns followed by suspicious network redirects.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering and Fake Browser Prompts
suggestion.rationale: Schema keywords include 'ClickFix' attack vector; pipeline ignored this social engineering tactic despite its role in malware delivery chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual browser child processes spawning from fake system-UI prompts (fake Windows Defender alerts, fake antivirus scareware). Look for script-injected fake popups in public WiFi portal pages. Alert on process creation chains that include browser → cmd/powershell with obfuscation following user interaction with suspicious dialog.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Browser Token Interception via Captive Portal
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention AiTM and token theft; no detection use case for interception of session tokens or credentials on compromised public networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSL/TLS proxy certificates installed on endpoints immediately following public WiFi connection. Detect HTTP traffic on HTTPS endpoints (downgrade attacks). Alert on abnormal authentication token requests from endpoints connected to suspicious captive portals within 10 minutes of connection.

suggestion.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass via Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Title highlights 'credential theft' and schema includes 'token theft'; pipeline missed detection for MFA token interception and account takeover post-credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential compromise indicators (public WiFi geolocation + malware execution) with subsequent successful logins from different geographies within 2–4 hours. Flag access from IPs not associated with victim's typical location. Monitor for token refresh anomalies after captive portal compromise.

suggestion.title: Midnight Blizzard Malware Payload Delivery and Staging
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'CaptiveCrunch' and threat actor Midnight Blizzard referenced in title; pipeline should have generated execution-phase detection for injected malware payloads on compromised networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for executables written to temp directories immediately after captive portal authentication. Detect Windows script engines (cscript, powershell, mshta) spawned with suspicious URLs or encoded payloads. Correlate process creation with known Midnight Blizzard tool signatures or behavior patterns (e.g., token credential process dumping).

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The implant masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is the primary execution and evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SspiCli.dll (SSPI client library) being loaded into AppVShNotify.exe or other processes not typically requiring SSPI authentication. Flag SspiCli.dll loaded from non-standard locations or before legitimate system DLL chains are established. Correlate with RPCRT4.dll delay-load patterns.

suggestion.title: NightLedger backdoor reconnaissance activities
suggestion.rationale: Article documents NightLedger capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' These post-compromise behaviors are detection-rich.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect correlated process enumeration (tasklist, Get-Process, wmic), followed by screenshot capture operations and file enumeration, especially when originating from unusual parents or in rapid succession. NightLedger establishes reconnaissance patterns detectable through process telemetry.

suggestion.title: WebSocket-based command and control tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies ArcBridge and BridgeHead are 'custom WebSocket-based tunnelers for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' Low-signature C2 requiring specific network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket (ws:// or wss://) connections from endpoints not typically initiating such traffic. Flag sustained WebSocket sessions to non-standard or newly observed endpoints. Correlate with backdoor execution indicators and unusual network client behavior.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-themed spear-phishing with credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment/hiring lures impersonating known platforms (LinkedIn, Indeed, etc.) or videoconferencing services. Monitor for redirects to file-sharing services (Mega, Drive, OneDrive) in phishing campaigns. Flag lookalike domain registration patterns targeting aviation/aerospace targets.

suggestion.title: Malware staging from file-sharing services post-phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain: 'malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services' following phishing. This is a critical ingress point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for archive downloads (.zip, .rar, .7z) from file-sharing domains following phishing campaigns. Flag extraction of executables, DLLs, or scripts from recently-downloaded archives. Correlate with parent process (browser) and destination directories indicative of malware staging.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via backdoor-controlled tunnels
suggestion.rationale: Article introduction states Mirage Kitten uses 'custom multi-stage malware to gain persistent access and exfiltrate sensitive data' targeting aerospace/defense sectors. Exfiltration is primary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large outbound data transfers over WebSocket tunnels (ArcBridge/BridgeHead) from compromised systems. Monitor for file reads from sensitive directories (aerospace/defense typical data stores) followed immediately by tunnel traffic. Flag unusual data volumes from endpoints in government/defense sectors.

suggestion.title: Exposed FMC Asset Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access FMC. Article references standard asset-exposure hunt template for this CVE as operational imperative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20316 matches on Cisco FMC instances. Cross-reference exposed FMC assets with border ingress rules to identify internet-reachable instances. Prioritize remediation against federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'log[s] in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. Must hunt authentication exploitation of known weak credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected IPs immediately following connection attempts. Alert on rapid successive login attempts consistent with credential stuffing. Flag low-privilege account logins to FMC web/API from atypical source geographies.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall configs, deployment logs, and managed-device credentials; compromised access triggers data theft hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual report generation, policy exports, or credential-store queries from the compromised low-privilege account. Alert on FMC API calls to CredentialManagement, PolicyExport, or DeviceCredentialSync endpoints from unexpected accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: FMC is the network control plane managing downstream firewalls. Compromise enables pivoting to all managed security appliances; article's 'impacted systems' likely extends beyond FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH, HTTPS, and proprietary FMC-to-device communication deviating from baseline config-management patterns. Alert on manual command execution on managed firewalls initiated from a compromised FMC instance.

suggestion.title: FMC Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation grants 'low-privileged account' access. Hunt privilege escalation as critical next step in attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo invocations, RBAC permission grants, or new admin-account creation initiated by compromised low-privilege account. FMC escalation often involves modifying user policies or AccessControl rules—flag unexpected permission assignments correlated with anomalous login IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Rule/Policy Tampering for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sensitive data' includes firewall policies and managed-device configs. Compromised FMC poses persistent backdoor risk via rule injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall policy changes deviating from change-control process: new rules permitting unexpected traffic flows, new service accounts, SSH-key injections on managed firewalls, or disabled logging. Cross-reference against approved change windows and request owners.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 explicitly named as Known Exploited Vulnerability; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Required minimum: scan for this CVE across asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset management database for instances of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) with CVE-2026-20316 unpatched. Cross-reference against scan date and federal patch due date of 2026-08-01. High priority given CISA KEV active exploitation status.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Firewall Management Center Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit; implies FMC is public-facing. This is fundamental asset-exposure hunt, not surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances reachable from internet on management ports (typically 443, 8305). Cross-reference with corporate network diagram; unexposed instances indicate misconfiguration or perimeter bypass. Screen for any internet access logs to FMC management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication with Hard-coded Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. Zero detection logic in pipeline for credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected source IPs to known low-privilege built-in accounts (e.g. admin, service, default). Flag sequences: failed + successful auth, esp. from geographically impossible locations or off-hours. Correlate against known hard-coded credential lists if available from Cisco advisories.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Cisco FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; no detection for exfiltration or data discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data exports, configuration downloads, or sensitive-data queries (firewall rules, credentials, network topology) within 1 hour post-authentication by low-privilege or anomalous account on FMC. Baseline normal admin activity; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Configuration or Credential Changes
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded account compromise enables lateral persistence; article does not preclude attacker modifying FMC config or accounts. Persistence detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for account creation, privilege elevation, or policy/configuration changes initiated by low-privilege or newly-seen accounts. Alert if admin accounts added or VPN policies modified post-breach window.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force / Credential Stuffing Attempts Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials may be shared across instances; attackers likely probe multiple targets. No defensive detection for attack-in-progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication attempts to FMC from single or low-diversity source IPs within 5-minute window. Especially sensitive: attempts using known hard-coded account names (if disclosed by Cisco). Correlate with honeypot/decoy FMC instances if deployed.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation (T1078.004)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device' via hard-coded password to 'access sensitive data.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core attack vector. Credential-access detection is essential for hard-coded-password vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded account identifiers or from non-trusted source IPs. Baseline normal authentication patterns and alert on atypical access times, source geographies, or bulk data operations following successful low-privileged login.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure & Asset Inventory (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker' accessing 'public-facing application' (CISA KEV semantics). Pipeline must generate asset-exposure hunt per recommended template but produced no use cases. This is critical for initial-access prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for internet-reachable Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (ports 443, 8305 typical) via external asset scans. Cross-reference Shodan/Censys for exposed FMC instances. Alert on any accessible from non-organizational IP ranges and correlate against patch inventory for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Low-Privileged FMC Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker gains 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data within impacted systems.' Pipeline missed collection-phase detection entirely despite clear data-exfiltration risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when low-privileged Cisco FMC user accounts export firewall policies, retrieve threat intelligence feeds, or access configuration backups. Baseline normal data-access patterns for low-priv roles and flag volume or sensitivity anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanning & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate immediate patching. Pipeline should generate standard vulnerability-scanning use case but produced none. Federal due date 2026-08-01 requires tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute authenticated and unauthenticated scans targeting Cisco FMC instances with CVE-2026-20316 check enabled (fingerprint: firmware versions < fixed build). Flag any vulnerable systems and calculate patch lag. Correlate asset inventory against scan results to identify systems missing from tracking.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability enables 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' to bypass login. Pipeline missed authentication-bypass detection use case entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface for HTTP(S) requests that trigger administrative functionality without prior successful authentication. Alert on session tokens issued before login completion or requests bypassing `/login` flows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Authentication Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—requires detection of unusual login patterns to FMC management ports (443, 8305).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline administrative access to FMC management interface by source IP, time-of-day, and account. Alert on spike in failed authentication attempts followed by successful login, or successful logins from IPs outside known admin ranges. Correlation with public-IP exposure (Shodan/Censys) increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Exploitation - Cisco FMC Default Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article core flaw: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'—detection must key on default/hardcoded account names and authentication patterns inconsistent with normal admin behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful logins to known Cisco FMC default account names (e.g., admin, operator) from external or non-approved administrative IP ranges. Cross-reference against threat intel for published Cisco hardcoded credentials. Alert if account has no prior login history or login occurs outside standard maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Sensitive Data Access from FMC Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat accesses 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-auth detection should identify data collection/exfiltration by low-privileged principal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API and database access logs for low-privileged accounts querying security policies, device configurations, credentials, or network topology. Alert on bulk exports, configuration backups, or policy downloads initiated outside change-management window. Correlate with successful authentication from external IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation; direct CVE-based detection required alongside vulnerability scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVE-2026-20316 into vulnerability scanner, correlate positive detections with successful authentication events on same host. Monitor IDS/IPS for public exploits targeting this CVE. Cross-check asset inventory against Shodan for exposed FMC instances; validate patching status.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Reconnaissance and Version Probing
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password exploits are version-specific; article's 'affected device' implies attacker must identify and enumerate FMC instances first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS probing of common FMC paths (/admin, /login, /status) returning 200/302 (successful banner grab). Alert on repeated 404 responses or User-Agent scanning from single source. Monitor for DNS lookups to FMC management hostnames followed by connection attempts within minutes. Flag nmap/Shodan API queries from internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Data Exfiltration - Outbound Transfer Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of access to 'sensitive data'—final-stage detection must identify data leaving the FMC environment after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Cisco FMC server following successful authentication event (within 5-30 min window). Alert on large data transfers (>100MB) to external IPs, especially if compressed/encrypted. Flag unexpected protocols (sftp, ftp, http-put) from FMC for non-backup scenarios. Correlate with query activity in API logs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable FMC Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes Cisco FMC versions are vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 ('Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center contains a use of hard-coded password vulnerability'). Pipeline must correlate inventory against patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances. Cross-reference against vulnerability database for CVE-2026-20316 presence. Flag any FMC instance with version < patched threshold (vendor not specified in article, use Cisco security advisory). Alert if patch adoption lags federal due-date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exposure to Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation, implying FMC management port (typically 443/8305) is internet-facing. Exposure is the attack surface enabling T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound network flows to Cisco FMC management interfaces (standard ports: 443, 8305) from public or untrusted IP ranges. Compare against baseline of expected management source IPs. Alert on anomalies indicating exposure.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. This is T1078.001 abuse—detection must correlate FMC auth logs with known default/built-in accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FMC authentication logs (if available via syslog/API) for login attempts using well-known default or system accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'root', 'fmc'). Spike in failed logins or successful logins from anomalous source IPs signals exploitation attempt. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 known-exploited campaigns if threat-intel provides.

suggestion.title: FMC Data Access Pattern Anomaly Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detection must monitor for abnormal data retrieval post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC data access logs for unusual queries or bulk exports of sensitive configuration or policy data, especially from low-privileged accounts or recently-authenticated sessions. Baseline normal admin behavior; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Detection (Splunk/KQL)
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability exploitation hunt. Article provides CVE and CISA KEV status; pipeline should generate templated searches for firewall/proxy logs monitoring exploitation signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search proxy/firewall logs for HTTP requests to known vulnerable FMC endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api, /login). Correlate with known exploit payloads if public PoC released. Cross-reference source IPs against CISA threat advisories or public CVE databases for exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication via Hard-Coded Default Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker as 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password vulnerability. This is the primary exploit vector; pipeline generated zero detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center audit and authentication logs for successful logins using default/hard-coded credentials (common defaults for this product family). Flag rapid failed-then-successful authentication sequences and any low-privileged account access outside business hours or from non-managed source IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access by Compromised Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' This indicates post-authentication data exfiltration requiring detection against FMC audit trails and access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy object access, threat intelligence feed retrieval, or security policy configuration reads by low-privileged FMC accounts outside normal administrative patterns. Baseline per-user access permissions and escalate when thresholds exceeded or protected objects queried.

suggestion.title: Network-Level Detection of FMC Management Interface Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access to management interface. Network sensors should detect anomalous connection patterns to FMC control plane ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTPS traffic to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) from non-managed external sources. Flag successful authentication (HTTP 200) within 3 connection attempts; correlate with failed HTTP 401/403 responses in preceding requests.

suggestion.title: API Token Generation by Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers holding hard-coded credential access may create persistent API tokens for programmatic data extraction beyond single-session access, enabling 'access to sensitive data' described in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API credential generation (OAuth tokens, API keys) by low-privileged FMC accounts. Track token lifespan, reuse frequency, and associated bulk data queries (policy exports, threat feed downloads). Flag tokens generated during off-hours or by accounts with no API access history.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CISA KEV entry' with 'observed exploited in the wild' and describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access pattern; no use case was generated to detect exploitation attempts despite this being the primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces for HTTP POST requests to authentication endpoints from external sources without prior TLS/certificate validation failures. Correlate with attempts to exploit CVE-2026-20316 via vulnerability scanner signatures or public exploit PoCs targeting FMC version <7.3.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Abuse Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerability as 'use of hard-coded password' allowing 'low-privileged account' access; no detection for credential-based initial access was generated despite this being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known hard-coded account names (e.g., 'admin', 'netadmin') from sources not in internal IP ranges. Correlate multiple failed logins from external sources followed by a successful session within 1 minute.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from FMC Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after hard-coded password exploitation; no collection-phase detection for data exfiltration from FMC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk data exports, policy downloads, or large-volume API queries initiated by low-privileged accounts immediately after authentication success. Flag any database backup operations or configuration exports from non-administrative contexts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date 2026-08-01; pipeline generated standard template reference but no baseline inventory use case for tracking unpatched FMC instances in fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances and cross-reference against vendor security advisory versions. Alert on any FMC version <7.3.x (assumed vulnerable version from CVE pattern) with last patch date older than 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: FMC Public Exposure Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' exploited by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies active external scanning for exposed FMC instances precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on external connection attempts to FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8302) exhibiting scanning patterns: rapid connection cycling, SSL/TLS handshake failures, or banner-grab sequences. Escalate if source IPs are non-whitelisted or geographically anomalous.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability described: 'use of hard-coded password'; attacker logs in as 'low-privileged account.' Hunt for authentication attempts using known default credentials against the FMC management interface from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentications to FMC management console using default/hard-coded usernames (admin, default, etc.) from external or anomalous source IPs. Alert if authentication succeeds after prior failures, or outside normal maintenance windows. Correlate with failed attempts to identify brute-force precursors.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise 'could allow...access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall policies, VPN credentials, threat intelligence, access-control rules—all high-value targets for attackers pivoting into downstream network infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for policy exports, configuration backups, credential inventory queries, or threat-intelligence downloads initiated by accounts outside the normal admin cadence. Alert if exports are staged for transfer (temp files, archives) or transferred to non-production systems.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Admin Activity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker using hard-coded credential would exhibit behavioral anomalies: source IP/timezone incongruent with legitimate IT staff, unusual action sequences, or rapid cross-device changes. Establish baseline of legitimate admin workflows to detect deviation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC admin activity (authorized users, typical source IPs, action frequency, device scope). Alert on: access outside business hours, from geoIP incongruent with admin staff, bulk firewall rule modifications, or config pushes affecting unexpected device subsets.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC is a high-trust pivot point with network access to all managed firewalls. Attacker would execute commands on downstream devices, modify security policies, or exfiltrate device credentials to compromise additional network assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for commands executed against managed devices (config pushes, CLI commands) from compromised/low-privilege accounts. Alert if: unauthorized rulesets are deployed, security features are disabled, backdoor access is created, or device credentials are extracted via FMC management interface for reuse.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active in-the-wild exploitation. Immediate asset hunt required to inventory vulnerable FMC instances not patched, especially internet-facing or high-criticality deployments managing sensitive network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanners for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances flagged with CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference against CMDB for: patch status, external exposure, network segment (DMZ/production), and downstream dependencies. Prioritize immediate isolation or access-control hardening for unpatched instances with public IP or high-trust role.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Authentication Bypass via Hard-coded Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—this is the primary attack vector and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center authentication logs for successful logins from external IP addresses using service or system accounts, especially low-privileged accounts. Flag rapid authentication sequences or logins during off-hours to identify potential exploitation.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker,' confirming the FMC is externally reachable. Default Cisco FMC ports (443, 8305, 8307) must be monitored for unauthorized external access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound network traffic to Cisco FMC management ports from untrusted external networks. Correlate failed authentication attempts with subsequent successful logins to identify exploitation campaigns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration and Policy Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After authentication, the attacker will export firewall policies, network configurations, or intelligence data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for data export operations, policy downloads, API calls for configuration retrieval, or large file transfers initiated by low-privileged FMC accounts, especially to external or suspicious destinations.

suggestion.title: Firewall Policy Modification via Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: An attacker with FMC management access can alter firewall rules, disable logging, or modify access control lists to enable lateral movement or cover tracks. Article implies access to sensitive configuration data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected firewall policy changes, rule modifications, access control list updates, or logging disablement on devices managed by the FMC, particularly during or shortly after the exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Verification for CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and marks this as CISA KEV (active exploitation). Immediate asset inventory validation is required to identify exploitable unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanning tools and device inventory systems for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances running vulnerable versions prior to the patch release. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scan Hit — CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the canonical detection vector for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any asset scan reporting CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS critical, CISA KEV, patch due 2026-08-01). Correlate scan date against patch-management records to identify lag. Even patched systems benefit from one-time inventory confirmation given active exploitation in the wild.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Login to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'. Pipeline did not surface authentication-attempt detection despite this being the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC (ports 443, 8305 default) for successful authentication events from unauthenticated sessions or sessions using hard-coded default credentials. Watch for authentication bypass attempts or login sequences that skip password prompts entirely.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Access to FMC — Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow...access to sensitive data within impacted systems'. No use case for detecting exfiltration of FMC-hosted sensitive configs, policy rules, or device management credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data exports, config downloads, or sensitive-data access (policies, device credentials, firewall rulesets) from FMC sessions tied to hard-coded or anomalous authentication. Baseline normal admin export sizes and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Network Reconnaissance — Exploitation Probe
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation pathway. Pipeline should include hunt for port scanning, service enumeration, or version-discovery probes targeting FMC management interfaces as precursor to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound probes to FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external IPs. Correlate scan patterns (e.g., rapid connection attempts, version-probe User-Agent strings) with post-exploitation FMC access logs to identify attack chains.

suggestion.title: FMC Default / Hard-coded Credential Usage Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CVE hinges on 'hard-coded password' abuse. Pipeline did not generate detection for repeated failed/successful logins using known default credentials or behavioral markers of credential-stuffing against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts from external sources using low-privileged account names (e.g., 'admin', 'default', 'fmc', 'support') with failed password attempts followed by success, or rapid successive logins from same source IP. Cross-reference against known Cisco default credentials if available.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC External Access Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center as vulnerable product and describes remote unauthenticated exploitation. FMC management interfaces are typically Internet-facing. Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for external (non-internal) network connections to known Cisco FMC management interface ports (443, 8305, 8307). Correlate with Cisco FMC service fingerprints and banner-grabbing activity. Flag unusually high connection rates or repeated failed connections from non-administrative source IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly a 'hard-coded password' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' This is T1078 (Valid Accounts) exploitation; no detection for credential-based access post-exploitation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known default or hard-coded account credentials. Alert on successful low-privilege account access from non-administrative source IPs. Baseline normal administrator login patterns and flag deviations in geography, time, or frequency.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Collection/exfiltration phase is core to the threat model but no detection for post-exploitation data access patterns was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful Cisco FMC authentication by a low-privilege account, monitor for bulk policy/config exports, API calls accessing protected data, database queries, or unusual file transfers. Alert on any access patterns exceeding baseline for the compromised account's role.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Inventory and Patch Status Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and CISA KEV status (active exploitation in the wild). Asset-exposure hunt must correlate vulnerability scanner findings with patched vs. vulnerable instances; no use case generated despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances affected by CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with asset inventory for patch status. Prioritize unpatched instances for immediate remediation and increase monitoring intensity until patch is deployed.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Remote Login Attempts with Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded password is the exploit vector. Pipeline generated zero detections for credential-based FMC access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface for authentication attempts with known hard-coded usernames and successful login from non-standard source IPs. Correlate against baseline of legitimate FMC administrator access to detect anomalous remote auth.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Successful authentication is entry point; data exfiltration is the objective. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After anomalous FMC authentication, detect queries against sensitive FMC data stores: firewall rule objects, access control lists, policy configurations, device credentials. Establish baseline for low-privilege account queries and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Asset Inventory and Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal remediation due 2026-08-01. Article: 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)'. Standard asset-exposure hunt template invoked in article but pipeline generated zero inventory/patch queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco FMC instances; cross-reference software versions against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability database. Prioritize internet-facing FMC management interfaces. Track patch deployment timeline vs. federal due date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Unauthorized Firewall Policy Modification
suggestion.rationale: FMC is firewall management plane. Compromised FMC can enable rule modification, credential harvesting, or persistence. Article implies access to sensitive firewall operational data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modifications to firewall policies, ACLs, or rule sets after anomalous FMC authentication. FMC is critical trust boundary — correlate policy changes with network traffic anomalies or lateral-movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Data Exfiltration to External Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data' implies extraction of firewall policies, security configs, or infrastructure blueprints. Pipeline failed to generate exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers from FMC to external or non-organizational IP addresses. Baseline expected FMC outbound traffic (license checks, backup uploads). Alert on unusual volume, timing, or destination correlation with policy/credential exports.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Internet-Facing Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploitation requires network reachability. Article: 'remote attacker' implies FMC is internet-exposed. Pipeline omitted network-exposure hunt despite article's reference to asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC management interface (443/tcp) exposed to public internet using Cisco FMC SSL certificate signatures or Shodan queries. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unexpected external exposure. Alert on first-time internet reachability.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-Coded Credential Login Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'—explicit hard-coded credential abuse. Pipeline produced zero detection use cases for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded service accounts or default credentials. Alert on successful logins from external IPs post-publication. Baseline legitimate admin access patterns and flag deviations (e.g., off-hours, unusual geolocations, high-volume API calls post-auth).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Unauthorized Remote Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access; pipeline missed network-level detection for management interface compromise. FMC listens on non-standard ports (8305, 8307, 443); exploit requires initial connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TCP connections to Cisco FMC management ports from non-whitelisted IPs or unexpected geolocations. Alert on rapid connection probes (port scanning) targeting FMC. Correlate network access logs with failed authentication attempts. Given CISA KEV status, threat is active; prioritize connections from commodity IP space.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2026-20316: Patch Compliance and Remediation SLA
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero compliance-tracking use cases despite KEV-mandated federal remediation deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco FMC deployments. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 positives. Flag unpatched instances and generate compliance alerts 7 days pre-deadline and daily post-deadline. Track patch deployment status to closure.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Configuration and Policy Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker goal is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'; pipeline missed post-compromise collection phase. Once authenticated via hard-coded creds, attacker will exfiltrate policies, device configs, threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit and API logs for bulk data exports, policy/config downloads, device-information queries, or threat-intelligence database access by low-privileged or service accounts. Alert on large data transfers over HTTP/HTTPS post-login. Baseline normal admin activity and flag anomalies in volume, scope, or timing.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Lateral Movement and Persistence via Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—implicit that FMC controls downstream Firewalls/IPS devices. Once compromised, attacker can push malicious configs, backdoors, or firewall rules via FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for configuration deployments to managed Firewall/IPS devices, especially outside change-management windows or by unexpected users. Alert on policy changes that weaken security (e.g., allow-all rules, disabled IPS signatures, port-forwarding redirects). Correlate with unauthorized FMC login sessions.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Attackers Exploit Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Flaw'—no detection use case for web-layer injection payloads targeting the vulnerability vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP/HTTPS requests to VeloCloud Orchestrator API endpoints containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(…), |, &, ;, newlines) in parameter values, particularly in fields accepting configuration or policy inputs. Correlate with 4xx→5xx transitions or error logs indicating command interpretation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawn from VeloCloud Orchestrator Service
suggestion.rationale: Command injection implies remote code execution; 'Attackers Exploit' indicates active abuse but zero detection for T1059 execution indicators on affected host
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) initiated from VeloCloud Orchestrator parent process or service account. Flag unusual child processes, especially those with network connectivity or file modification post-spawn.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Orchestrator
suggestion.rationale: Critical RCE on centralized SD-WAN orchestrator creates pivot point for network-wide compromise; no detection for post-exploitation lateral movement suggested
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound SMB, RDP, SSH, or WinRM connections from VeloCloud Orchestrator host to internal network ranges after successful command injection signatures detected. Correlate with unusual login attempts on target systems.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Authentication Anomaly Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After RCE, actors often establish persistent access paths; no use case for detecting credential abuse or unusual auth patterns post-compromise in title or inferred content
