suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins to VeloCloud Orchestrator UI or API from new source IPs, impossible-travel scenarios, or during off-hours coinciding with exploitation signatures. Alert on creation of new service accounts or API keys post-incident.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised VeloCloud Orchestrator
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN orchestrator has visibility/control over all branch traffic; critical exposure for exfiltration but no detection use case generated for data staging or egress indicators
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers from VeloCloud Orchestrator to external IPs (especially non-CDN, non-Arista IP ranges), unusual DNS queries for attacker infrastructure from Orchestrator context, or encrypted tunnels to unknown destinations during exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline did not surface detection for successful/failed authentication attempts to exposed FMC instances using known hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces for successful authentication events sourced from external/unexpected networks with low-privileged or service-account credentials. Correlate with vulnerability scanner signatures for CVE-2026-20316 on internal network segments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends: 'CVE: CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline did not generate detection use case for asset exposure hunting or patch status verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances detected by vulnerability scanners as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with patch baseline to identify systems missing CVE-2026-20316 patches as of federal deadline 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow... access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed detection for data exfiltration or unauthorized queries after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24–72 hours of FMC hard-coded credential compromise, detect large data transfers, configuration exports, or policy dumps from FMC to external IPs or unusual internal destinations. Alert on bulk download of firewall rules, topology data, or security analytics.

suggestion.title: FMC Exploitation Attempt Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active exploitation: 'CISA KEV only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Pipeline did not model attack surface or web-request anomalies consistent with T1190 exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FMC management endpoints (commonly TCP 443/8300) with suspicious patterns: directory traversal attempts, exploitation payloads in POST/PUT bodies, or use-agent anomalies. Correlate with known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation PoCs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication via Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. This is the primary attack mechanism and must trigger on authentication using service/default accounts from external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC admin interface (ports 443, 22) from external IP ranges using low-privilege service accounts or usernames matching hard-coded credential patterns. Correlate repeated failed attempts followed by success. Trigger on any external authentication to FMC management plane regardless of account privilege level.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Exposure (T1190 - Internet-Facing Management)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation and maps to T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). FMC management interface must be internet-facing for remote exploitation to occur. Hunt for exposed Cisco FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances accepting inbound connections on management ports (443/tcp, 22/tcp, 8305/tcp) from untrusted external IP space. Correlate with version banners or SSL certificates identifying affected FMC versions. Flag any FMC management interface reachable from WAN/internet perimeter.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-compromise, attackers exfiltrate policies, threat intelligence, or network configuration. Monitor for bulk data access by low-privilege accounts immediately after authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large policy exports, rule backups, or bulk queries executed by low-privilege or service accounts within 15 minutes of successful login. Flag outbound network data transfers from FMC to external IP addresses carrying policy or configuration payloads. Monitor API endpoints for bulk policy retrieval by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance and Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch-due date 2026-08-01. Article explicitly names 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center' and 'Firepower Management Center' as affected product. Verification of patched status is mandatory compliance check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC instances for CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability status. Alert on any FMC running vulnerable versions on or after federal patch-due date (2026-08-01). Cross-reference version detection against official Cisco patch bulletins. Generate compliance report on FMC patch lag by asset and business unit.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Security Policy or Rule Modification
suggestion.rationale: Compromised low-privilege FMC account could be used to disable logging, weaken firewall rules, or create backdoor policies to maintain persistence. Article's 'access sensitive data' phrasing implies potential for config manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC policy and firewall rule change logs for modifications initiated by service/low-privilege accounts. Alert on disabling of logging, IDS/IPS, or threat inspection policies. Flag creation of new allow rules or modifications to existing deny rules by non-admin accounts. Establish baseline of authorized policy changes and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline produced zero use cases monitoring FMC authentication. Should detect logins with known hard-coded or default account names from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs for authentication events using hard-coded or default service account names. Alert on successful logins from non-whitelisted source IPs, especially external/internet-facing sources, and correlate with failed attempts indicating attack reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-20316 and mandates federal patch by 2026-08-01; pipeline IOCs are empty. Should trigger on scanner detection of this CVE in FMC inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner finding CVE-2026-20316 in Cisco FMC instances. Prioritize by asset criticality and internet exposure. Cross-reference scanner timestamps with authentication logs to detect potential post-scan exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Against Cisco FMC Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password implies brute-force feasibility; article describes 'remote attacker' accessing exposed interface. Pipeline missed brute-force-specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication attempts against Cisco FMC management port (typically HTTPS/443) from single source IP within 5-minute windows. Escalate if followed by successful login. Baseline for false positives from legitimate admin troubleshooting.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no use case detects post-auth data exfiltration. Should monitor for config exports, policy downloads, or credential access by low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag administrative data operations (policy export, credential query, config download, syslog access) by accounts with limited privileges or from new/unexpected login sessions. Alert if low-privileged authenticated user attempts sensitive reads outside normal job function.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerable Software Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article targets specific product (Secure Firewall Management Center); pipeline contains no version-specific IOCs. Should identify FMC instances running vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances and extract software versions. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vendor advisory to identify vulnerable version ranges. Flag for immediate patching, compensating controls, or isolation. Repeat post-patch to confirm remediation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote attacker'—implies public-facing exposure. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure or external-reachability detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Passive and active intelligence gathering to identify Cisco FMC instances accessible from internet. Correlate external scan results with internal asset inventory to find shadow instances or misconfigured network segmentation. Recommend internal-only management access and VPN-gating for remediation.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—requires detection of failed/successful login attempts with default or hard-coded credentials against Cisco FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for failed login attempts using known default account names or rapid successive login attempts from external IP ranges. Baseline legitimate FMC access by source IP and flag deviations. Alert on successful logins from unexpected geographic regions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Specific CVE identifier provided—requires patch-status tracking and inventory of Cisco FMC installations against vulnerable versions to identify exploitation targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for Cisco FMC instances flagged with CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with asset inventory and patch management data to identify systems still running vulnerable versions post-federal due-date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'remote attacker' access to FMC—scanning for internet-exposed management instances is prerequisite detection for asset exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct network discovery scans for Cisco FMC management console ports (443, 8305, 22) reachable from untrusted networks. Correlate with firewall ingress rules—flag FMC management interfaces exposed to internet without VPN/authentication gateway intermediary.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of large data transfers or unusual administrative access patterns following successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting suspicious FMC authentication, monitor audit logs for configuration exports, rule set downloads, or credential queries. Flag network flow anomalies (large outbound transfers from FMC on unusual ports). Cross-reference with DLP to identify sensitive data signatures (policy configs, threat intel, logs).

suggestion.title: FMC Management Console Access Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Firewall management centers should only be accessed from controlled administrative networks—anomalous remote access patterns indicate exploitation attempts or successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate FMC management console access (IP ranges, user accounts, times). Alert on access from non-whitelisted IP ranges, VPN bypass patterns, or successful logins outside business hours. Prioritize alerts where geographic location contradicts account operator baseline.

suggestion.title: FMC Low-Privilege Account Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Attacker compromises with 'low-privileged account'—requires detection of privilege escalation attempts or lateral movement from compromised FMC account to downstream assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC activity logs for privilege escalation requests, role/permission modifications, or API calls attempting higher-privilege operations. Correlate with network flow data for outbound connections from FMC to managed firewalls or downstream infrastructure using compromised low-privilege session credentials.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit—implying exposed FMC instances are the attack surface. Pipeline missed reconnaissance phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC instances exposed on internet-facing networks (management port 8305/tcp). Query firewall allow-rules, external asset discovery, and network segmentation logs for external connectivity to FMC appliances. Flag any FMC management interface accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Inventory Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline failed to translate this into scanner-based detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all Cisco FMC instances against CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability catalog. Flag instances running unpatched versions (pre-2026-08-01 patch date). Cross-correlate scanner results with asset inventory and federal remediation tracking to prioritize high-risk exposures.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability mechanism: 'hard-coded password' enables 'unauthenticated' access. Pipeline did not map credential-access detection layer for default/known-bad credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded/default low-privileged credentials. Alert on successful authentication with these accounts, particularly from external/anomalous source IPs. Establish baseline of legitimate hard-coded-credential use for maintenance/testing to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'access[es] sensitive data' via compromised low-privileged account. Pipeline did not generate collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of typical low-privileged FMC account data queries and exports. Alert on anomalous policy downloads, configuration exports, or sensitive-data queries (firewall rules, threat logs, encrypted traffic metadata) from accounts lacking history of these activities. Monitor bulk report generation or data API calls.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Brute-Force and Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password attack presupposes attacker performs reconnaissance/enumeration of credentials. Pipeline did not detect exploitation attempts against authentication interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed authentication attempts against FMC management interface with pattern consistent with credential guessing (multiple user/password combinations, systematic enumeration). Correlate failed attempts with successful login using same or related credentials. Alert on authentication failures from external source IPs followed by successful logon.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This tag manipulation is the core obfuscation enabling 23k repos to pull malicious code via normal versioning semantics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs for tag creation, deletion, or reassignment events, especially when tags point to commits outside primary development branches or lacking ref/heads/* ancestry. Alert on tags reassigned to commits accessible only via direct hash navigation (orphaned commits).

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Referenced in GitHub Action Workflow Definitions
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes orphaned commits as a 'key enabling factor' for obfuscation and notes attackers could 'point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo.' Workflows referencing non-existent branches or orphaned SHAs are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse GitHub Action workflow YAML files (.github/workflows/*.yml) to detect 'uses:' statements referencing commit SHAs or tags that resolve to commits without refs/heads/* entries in the default branch ancestry. Flag as potential supply-chain manipulation.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Job Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs,' describing a vulnerability where GitHub's secret encryption was bypassed. This is the primary impact vector affecting dependent repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions run logs for plaintext patterns matching secret formats (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, OAuth credentials). Cross-reference against repository secrets metadata to identify unintended exposure. Alert on secrets appearing in logs from modified workflow steps or during external network operations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Call from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This exfiltration/command-fetch pattern is detectable via runner egress monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner egress for unexpected curl, wget, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest calls to external IPs/domains not whitelisted in CI/CD policy. Correlate with workflow logs and user identity to identify runs that fetch code from unexpected sources, especially correlated with secret exposure events.

suggestion.title: Write Access Granted to High-Dependency GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root enabler: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Unexpected permission escalation to write/admin on critical Actions repositories is detectable via repository access audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository collaborator audit logs for unexpected additions of users or service accounts with write permissions on repositories categorized as Actions, npm packages, or other widely-consumed dependencies. Alert on permission escalation to write/admin on high-impact projects and require approval workflow.

suggestion.title: Direct Commit to Protected Branch Without Pull Request Review
suggestion.rationale: Article scenario involves attacker using write access to commit malicious code. This suggests commits bypassed branch protection rules or lacked pull-request review workflows that would catch anomalous changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect direct commits pushed to protected branches (main, release/*) that circumvent pull request code review workflows. Alert if branch protection settings are modified or disabled immediately prior to suspicious commits, or if commits appear with no associated PR audit trail.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — direct indicator of hard-coded credential exploitation attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded accounts or with unusually high failure-to-success ratios from non-admin network segments. Flag successful logins from external/untrusted source IPs where internal FMC access is not expected.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' + CISA KEV template mandates asset-exposure hunt for publicly-accessible instances before credential exploitation can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external attack surface for Cisco FMC management interfaces (default ports 443, 8305) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output: any device tagged as FMC + publicly routable + unpatched against CVE-2026-20316 is exploitable within SLA window.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states goal is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — attackers will pivot to data collection after authentication succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk data exports, policy downloads, or telemetry queries from FMC API/UI immediately following a successful hard-coded credential login. Anomalous destinations for exported configurations or rule-sets should trigger escalation.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Account Authentication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as using 'low-privileged account' with hard-coded credentials — legitimate access patterns differ sharply from exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for low-privileged hard-coded account usage (frequency, source IPs, time-of-day, actions performed). Alert on deviations: night-time logins, batch login attempts, access from DMZ/external ranges, rapid role-privilege checks, or lateral-movement commands.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance and Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article published 2026-07-29, federal due date 2026-08-01, indicates imminent threat window. Pipeline must correlate CVE scanner results with authentication logs to catch unpatched + exploited systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-match assets tagged CVE-2026-20316=vulnerable in scanner output against FMC authentication logs. Any unpatched Cisco FMC showing successful remote login from non-administrative source constitutes confirmed exploitation. Compare login timing to known exploit PoC availability dates.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability in public-facing application. Must locate and inventory exposed Cisco FMC management consoles before exploitation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management console (TCP 443, path patterns typical of FMC UI) accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate against known datacenter or office CIDR ranges. Flag externally routable FMC instances as critical remediation candidates.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is hard-coded password in FMC. Detection must capture login attempts using known default accounts or patterns associated with credential stuffing/brute-force.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts or successful logins using hard-coded/low-privilege service accounts. Alert on velocity spikes in failed auth to FMC management port. Correlate source IP reputation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Access with Low-Privilege Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detection must flag anomalous low-privilege account activity within FMC post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track FMC admin console actions performed by low-privilege service accounts. Flag commands that query, export, or access sensitive configuration data (firewall policies, credentials, network topology) when issued by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-compromise, attacker will dump firewall policies, network config, credentials. Detect data staging or export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk data queries or exports (policy export, config backup, credential listing). Detect large unencrypted data streams exiting FMC to non-expected IPs. Flag simultaneous read of sensitive objects (firewall rules, user accounts) by single session.

suggestion.title: Authentication Spike and Timeline Correlation to CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: KEV status implies active exploitation. Detect surge in auth attempts to FMC management interface, correlate to CVE-2026-20316 patch deadline (2026-08-01) and known exploit availability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC management port auth request volume. Alert on anomalies exceeding 3σ from baseline, especially from external sources. Prioritize investigations if org not patched by federal due date. Correlate spike timing with public exploit PoC releases.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and Federal due date 2026-08-01. Inventory FMC versions and detect unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 across Cisco FMC instances. Compare patched version against known-vulnerable versions. Escalate any unpatched FMC post-deadline as critical incident.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default/Hardcoded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using hardcoded password vulnerability — no detection for authentication attempts with known default credentials against FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated authentication attempts against Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 443) using common default/hardcoded credentials (admin/admin, admin/password, etc.). Flag successful authentications from unauthenticated or unexpected sources that deviate from baseline administrative patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Unauthenticated Access from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access FMC — detection needed for unauthorized inbound connections to management interfaces from external networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interfaces from external/unexpected IP ranges. Correlate with successful authentication events to confirm exploitation of hardcoded credential vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker goal: 'to access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — detection needed for config export, credential harvesting, or policy data extraction from FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for export/download of firewall configurations, security policies, VPN credentials, or network topology metadata from FMC, especially following authentication via hardcoded accounts or from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Presence & Patch Status Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends asset-exposure template hunt substituting 'CVE-2026-20316' and specifies federal due-date 2026-08-01 — no scanner-driven detection for vulnerability presence or patch compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execute baseline scan to identify all Cisco FMC instances and cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 detection. Verify patch deployment status against federal compliance deadline of 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised FMC to Managed Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Cisco FMC is a management hub; compromise via hardcoded credentials creates pivot point for lateral movement to firewalls under management. Article implies downstream access risk but UCs missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC-to-managed-firewall communication that deviates from established policy-update baselines or originates from compromised FMC credentials. Alert on unauthorized policy or rule deployments to downstream appliances.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Asset Inventory Discovery
suggestion.rationale: No asset-discovery hunt generated despite article recommending 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and requiring patching of all FMC instances by 2026-08-01.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances via service fingerprinting, banner grabbing, certificate inspection, or API endpoint detection. Build baseline inventory for ongoing compliance and exposure monitoring.

suggestion.title: FMC Internet-Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' explicitly recommended and template referenced. Attack requires 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' reach to FMC. This is the first and most critical hunt—identify exposed instances before attackers do.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (default ports 8305/tcp, 443/tcp for HTTPS) responding to internet-facing queries. Cross-reference against internal asset inventory to surface unmanaged or shadow instances. Alert on any FMC reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Exploitation requires successful authentication via hard-coded credentials. Monitor FMC auth logs for repeated login attempts or successful access using known default account names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to FMC admin accounts using weak or default credentials associated with CVE-2026-20316. Flag both failed brute-force patterns (multiple attempts in short time from single source IP) and successful logins from non-standard administrative workstations.

suggestion.title: FMC Data Exfiltration Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Once authenticated via hard-coded account, attacker can exfiltrate policy configurations, network topology, or audit logs. Monitor for bulk data exports or API queries from suspicious sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FMC accounts performing unusual queries or bulk exports of policies, network objects, or audit logs, especially within minutes of a login from an unfamiliar source IP or off-hours access pattern.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Continuous scanning ensures no FMC instances remain unpatched for known-exploited CVE-2026-20316 after compliance deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare all Cisco FMC asset versions against CVE-2026-20316 patch advisory. Alert on any instance still running vulnerable version post-remediation deadline (2026-08-01). Flag as high-priority even if no current exposure detected, as attackers actively scan for unpatched FMC.

suggestion.title: FMC Service Banner Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker,' implying reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Detect attempts to fingerprint FMC banners or version strings via HTTP/HTTPS/SSH, indicating active scanning for vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS banner grab attempts, SSH version probes, or port scans targeting FMC default ports (8305, 443, 22) from external sources. Correlate with active CVE-2026-20316 scanning campaigns in threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—requires exposed management interface. Article explicitly references asset-exposure hunt templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-accessible Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (typical ports 443, 8305). Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner findings. Flag any open-internet FMC access as critical even if patched—patch lag is explicit concern in article.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Login to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' via 'hard-coded password'—this is the exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC authentication to low-privileged default or service accounts, especially from external/untrusted networks or unusual geographies. Baseline normal FMC login behavior and flag anomalies in timing, source IP, account privilege level.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes endpoint: attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—collection phase of exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privileged FMC accounts exporting policies, rules, network configurations, or device inventories. Flag policy-dump commands, backup file creation, or API calls to retrieve sensitive objects within minutes of new account login. Alert on bulk data queries by newly-provisioned sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Status Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires federal remediation by 2026-08-01; article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Validate actual patch status across fleet regardless of scanner assertions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Cisco FMC devices for installed version (show version via SSH/API). Cross-reference against patched versions from Cisco PSA for CVE-2026-20316. Flag any instance < patched baseline as exploitable, even if vulnerability scanner cached result says 'not vulnerable.'

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Low-privileged attacker access may permit config modifications, policy tampering, or backdoor insertion—explicit risk from article's 'access sensitive data' language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for configuration changes by low-privileged accounts or newly authenticated sessions. Alert on user/account creation, SSH key addition, VPN policy insertion, or failover-link tampering during time windows matching external login anomalies.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes poisoning of Adform script. Pipeline should detect unauthorized modifications to ad-tech vendor scripts before deployment to customer sites. Article phrase: 'Hackers Poison Adform Script'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to Adform script files or delivery infrastructure (checksum mismatches, signature validation failures). Alert on unsigned or newly-signed script variants. Track script parameter changes that modify behavioral flow (particularly wallet address substitution patterns).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution in Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: swapping legitimate wallet addresses for attacker-controlled ones. Article phrase: 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites'. This is DOM manipulation and content injection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript execution that modifies wallet address fields or transaction destination values at runtime. Flag scripts that search-and-replace blockchain addresses or inject new wallet identifiers into payment forms. Correlate with outbound crypto transactions to non-whitelisted addresses.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Source Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks depend on bypassin script authenticity checks. Pipeline should surface detection around ad-tech vendor script validation. Article phrase: 'poisoned Adform script to swap...across customer sites' implies compromise of trusted vendor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate script source origin via certificate pinning, SRI (Subresource Integrity) hash mismatches, or CDN route anomalies. Alert when Adform script is served from unexpected IP ranges or with modified Content-Security-Policy headers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Behavior: Outbound Crypto Address Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious script must communicate or store attacker wallet addresses. Detection should catch scripts making unusual DNS queries for crypto exchanges, wallets, or C2 infrastructure. Article implies script knows alternative wallet addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scripts generating DNS queries to cryptocurrency service domains (exchanges, wallet providers, block explorers) from ad-tech context. Flag inline scripts that construct or encode hex-encoded Ethereum/Bitcoin addresses. Detect WebSocket or HTTP exfil to crypto monitoring services.

suggestion.title: Ad-Tech Script Parameter Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned Adform script likely modified via injection into query parameters or script configuration. Detection should catch parameter tampering specific to ad-tech platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual query parameters on Adform script load requests (e.g., extra cryptographic material, obfuscated callback URLs, or base64-encoded wallet lists). Flag requests with syntax errors in ad-tech parameters or unexpected callback hosts.

suggestion.title: Crypto Wallet Address Exfiltration via Ad Network
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is to redirect payments to attacker wallets. Detection should catch collection and transmission of wallet data through ad-network infrastructure. Article: 'Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scripts encoding legitimate wallet addresses (via regex or DOM scraping) and transmitting them to attacker-controlled collection domains. Monitor for unusual egress on port 443 to non-CDN IPs from Adform script context. Flag Base64/hex-encoded strings matching known cryptocurrency address formats.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Wi-Fi Network Spoofing or Hijacking Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes hijacked hotel Wi-Fi as attack vector: 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi Pushes Fake Updates'. Pipeline generated no initial-access detection. Should detect rogue SSID cloning, unauthorized DHCP serving, or DNS hijacking on enterprise/hospitality networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious Wi-Fi access points or network infrastructure changes. Look for duplicate SSIDs from unexpected BSSIDs, DHCP pools redirecting to attacker-controlled gateways, or DNS responses inconsistent with legitimate ISP authoritative servers. Correlate with user device connections to rogue networks.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'Pushes Fake Updates to Deliver Surveillance Malware'. Pipeline generated zero execution detections. Should capture fake update prompts, out-of-band update initiation, unsigned or mismatched signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for update prompts or installers originating from non-standard sources (hotel guest networks, ad-hoc HTTP instead of HTTPS, unsigned binaries). Detect process execution of update-related files downloaded from untrusted network segments. Correlate unsolicited update UX with eventual surveillance malware execution.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware C2 Communications from Hotel Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Surveillance Malware' payload but pipeline generated no C2 or collection detection. Should detect outbound C2 beaconing, encrypted exfiltration, or keylog/camera capture traffic from guests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 beacons or exfiltration patterns from endpoints connected to hotel guest Wi-Fi: unusual outbound HTTPS to low-reputation IPs/domains, beaconing intervals inconsistent with legitimate software, DNS queries for suspicious subdomains, or encrypted payloads to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting or Keystroke Logging via Guest Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Surveillance Malware' but pipeline produced no credential-access or collection hypotheses. Typical hotel Wi-Fi attacks harvest login credentials or capture sensitive input from guests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for keylogger/screen-capture library loading (e.g. user32.dll hooks, directx input interception), unusual input-device drivers, or clipboard access from low-integrity processes. Correlate with process execution from hotel Wi-Fi-delivered installer.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware requires persistence, but pipeline generated no persistence detection. Attackers typically install scheduled tasks, services, or registry runkeys from hotel Wi-Fi compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks, Windows services, or registry HKLM/HKCU Run keys by processes spawned from the fake-update installer. Look for tasks executing from suspicious locations or with unusual intervals. Cross-reference task/service binaries with malware families.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Behavior Post-Wi-Fi Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies widespread guest infection risk but pipeline generated no behavioral anomaly detection. Surveillance malware on hotel guests' devices will exhibit increased CPU, network, or battery drain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify spikes in network egress, sustained CPU/memory by suspicious processes, or unexpected wake-locks on mobile/laptop devices shortly after guest Wi-Fi connection. Correlate with known malware process names or suspicious network destinations.

suggestion.title: PATCH request with JSON body containing $pullAll operator to ApostropheCMS API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'authenticated editor to write arbitrary values to Object.prototype via the $pullAll patch operator.' No UC inspects request body for the actual payload structure (JSON with $pullAll key). This is the definitive attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* where Content-Type is application/json and the request body contains the JSON key '$pullAll' at any nesting level. Correlate with authenticated user session context to identify legitimate vs. malicious editor activity.

suggestion.title: Successful data access to protected ApostropheCMS endpoints post-PATCH without re-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'process-wide authorization bypass.' A successful PATCH pollutes Object.prototype globally; subsequent requests from different users/sessions should still succeed if auth bypass persists. No UC detects cross-session authorization failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cases where a PATCH request from one user is followed by successful GET requests to protected endpoints from a different user/session ID within seconds, without corresponding re-authentication events. This signals auth context pollution.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS API error responses or exceptions containing '__proto__' or 'constructor' strings
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'confirmed gadget' implying the vulnerability has known error signatures or exceptions. Application error logs or HTTP error responses may leak evidence of failed prototype-pollution attempts or gadget invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ApostropheCMS application error logs or HTTP error response bodies for JavaScript prototype keywords (__proto__, constructor, Object.prototype). These may indicate attempted or successful prototype-pollution exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS authenticated user session generating PATCH then immediate administrative API actions from same session
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attacker as 'authenticated editor' but the impact is 'process-wide authorization bypass.' After exploiting, the same editor session may gain elevated capabilities (reading/modifying admin fields, accessing user data). No UC detects privilege escalation within a single session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH requests from an authenticated editor account with subsequent API calls to protected/admin-only endpoints from the same session. Compare called endpoints against the editor's baseline privileges; flag unauthorized cross-privilege calls.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed PATCH requests to ApostropheCMS API from same source within short window (exploitation attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Article states the gadget is 'confirmed,' implying attackers may probe multiple payload variations. Rapid PATCH attempts with varying payloads are unlikely in legitimate use and suggest exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* from the same source IP within 60 seconds where HTTP status indicates errors (4xx, 5xx). This pattern suggests payloads being refined or multiple gadgets being tested.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Session Proxy Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes AiTM as core technique: 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' is listed in schema keywords; common in Midnight Blizzard traveler-targeting campaigns to intercept and relay authentication sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect proxy-based credential interception by identifying authentication requests passing through attacker-controlled infrastructure, unusual token issuance patterns from non-canonical IP geographies, or simultaneous session logins from geographically disparate locations for the same user within subsecond intervals.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Execution via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Schema explicitly tags 'ClickFix' and 'social engineering'; ClickFix is Midnight Blizzard's known technique for driving malware execution through deceptive browser notifications and fake warnings to travelers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users executing files or scripts within minutes of clicking suspicious browser-popup links, especially from hotel/airport networks (GeoIP or SSID correlation). Flag parent processes matching known browser vendors spawning unexpected child processes like cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal Spoofing and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: CaptiveCrunch campaign name and 'credential theft' keyword indicate spoofed captive portals at travel hubs; no use case covers detection of fake login pages or harvested travel-related credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to lookalike travel-provider domains (hotels, airlines, airports) from public WiFi networks, especially with traffic volume or certificate anomalies. Correlate user credentials reuse across non-travel platforms post-event. Monitor for email alerts about suspicious login attempts on travel-linked accounts within 24–48 hours of portal interaction.

suggestion.title: Midnight Blizzard Malware Delivery Campaign Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title and actor keywords ('Midnight Blizzard', 'malware delivery') establish malware as primary payload; pipeline failed to generate detections for malware staging, C2 beaconing, or post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe, .msi, .dll, or script files downloaded from travel-related URLs (airlines, hotel booking sites) or email with headers spoofing travel providers. Correlate with process execution anomalies (parent process mismatch, unsigned binaries, living-off-the-land execution from temp directories).

suggestion.title: Token and Session Cookie Theft Post-AiTM
suggestion.rationale: Schema lists 'token theft', 'credential theft', and keywords imply session hijacking; no use case specifically detects token/cookie exfiltration or downstream token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect stolen tokens by identifying OAuth/session tokens used from non-canonical IPs or user-agents within minutes of credential entry, especially tokens reused across multiple cloud services (Azure, Microsoft 365, AWS) from geographically distant locations in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Geographically Anomalous Travel-Related Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'travelers worldwide'; no use case captures impossible-travel or geographically improbable access to travel-linked accounts or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts to travel-linked accounts (airline loyalty, hotel chains, airport systems) from IPs >2000km distant within <2 hours, or from VPN/proxy IPs correlated with Midnight Blizzard infrastructure. Correlate login geo with user's last-known location.

suggestion.title: NightLedger DLL Hijacking via AppVShNotify.exe Sideloading
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes signature technique: 'NightLedger masquerades as SspiCli.dll and is designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is the core execution mechanism and should have immediate coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for AppVShNotify.exe spawning or loading unsigned SspiCli.dll from non-system paths, especially alongside RPCRT4.dll imports. RPC API calls to methods requiring authentication should precede SspiCli loading. Cross-reference creation timestamps of SspiCli.dll against AppVShNotify.exe execution; mismatches suggest sideloading.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling Activity (BridgeHead/ArcBridge Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes two custom WebSocket tunnelers ('ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling') deployed during post-exploitation. 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) initiated by unexpected processes, particularly from engineering/security-focused endpoints. BridgeHead/ArcBridge show anomalous patterns: inbound tunneling operators controlling victim networks through WebSocket channels. Correlate with NightLedger indicators and aerospace/defense targeting profile.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing with Third-Party File-Sharing Redirects (Recruitment Lures)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector in detail: 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services. These lures included recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms.' This is documented initial access but has no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email clicks leading to lookalike videoconferencing domains followed by redirects to third-party file-sharing services (Mega.nz, file upload sites). Correlate with recruitment-themed subject lines and aerospace/aviation/defense company employee targeting. Flag downloads of .zip/.rar archives from these redirects.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Post-Compromise Reconnaissance (Process Discovery & Screenshot Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies backdoor capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' These post-compromise behaviors are signature indicators for NightLedger activity but lack detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 10-60 seconds of process execution, detect suspicious query patterns: Get-Process calls, tasklist.exe, wmic process listing, or registry enumeration of running services. Correlate with ScreenCapture API calls or GDI+ image buffer operations. NightLedger discovery pattern: enumerate → capture screen → exfil.

suggestion.title: RPCRT4.dll Delay-Loading SspiCli.dll Authentication Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article technical detail: 'AppVShNotify.exe imports RPCRT4.dll, which can delay-load SspiCli.dll when it invokes an RPC API that requires authentication.' This is a forensic and behavioral indicator unique to NightLedger's implementation approach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppVShNotify.exe → RPCRT4.dll → SspiCli.dll load chain where SspiCli is unsigned, resides outside System32, or has mismatched timestamps. Authenticate via code signing certificates; legitimate RPCRT4 SspiCli chains use Microsoft-signed DLLs.

suggestion.title: Masquerading Backdoor File Names (SspiCli.dll Impersonation)
suggestion.rationale: NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll' — a legitimate Windows authentication library — to evade detection. This masquerading technique should trigger when unsigned DLLs use system library names outside proper versioning paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or loading of SspiCli.dll outside C:\Windows\System32 and C:\Windows\SysWOW64 with version info mismatches (missing or false Microsoft signature). Cross-check against NIST/MS libraries; malicious SspiCli often lacks proper version strings or certificate chains.

suggestion.title: FMC Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states FMC vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' — indicating public-facing exposure. Pipeline generated no asset-exposure hunt despite template explicitly referencing _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco FMC devices. Cross-reference exposed management IPs against internal asset inventory; flag FMC instances reachable from untrusted networks or with direct internet routing.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — indicates credential-based access. No credential_access phase detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded account names (often 'admin' or vendor-default accounts). Correlate with failed login attempts prior to success. Flag logins from non-standard timezones or IPs outside known corporate ranges.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account Accessing Sensitive FMC Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data' — indicates privilege escalation or lateral data access after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on low-privileged FMC user accounts querying, exporting, or accessing configuration data, policy definitions, or firewall rule sets that should only be readable by high-privilege roles. Track data exports via API, GUI, or configuration backups.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Access from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability enables remote unauthenticated access to management interface. No detection for unexpected source IPs or geographic anomalies in management plane access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC management access locations (expected admin IP ranges, VPN gateways, secure admin networks). Flag login attempts to FMC management interface from IPs outside baseline or from known public internet ranges; particularly logins followed by API calls or config queries.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Policy Manipulation Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains FMC access via hard-coded password, article implies sensitive data access — potential stepping stone to firewall policy tampering, rule disabling, or traffic redirection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit FMC configuration change logs for modifications to firewall policies, access control rules, logging rules, or threat intelligence feeds made by low-privileged accounts or during windows inconsistent with change management schedules. Alert on mass rule deletions or logging disablement.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from FMC to Protected Firewall Assets
suggestion.rationale: FMC is the management plane for Cisco firewalls; compromise provides vantage for lateral movement to managed perimeter devices. Article does not mention this, but is implicit in 'FMC contains sensitive data'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FMC compromise indicators with subsequent unexpected API calls, SSH sessions, or management-plane logins from the FMC to managed firewall devices outside normal admin activity patterns. Flag new admin account provisioning on managed devices shortly after FMC access.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access possible, indicating network exposure. Pipe scanner output for FMC instances visible to untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances reachable from internet or non-corporate IP ranges. Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 detections and correlate with network-reachability scan data. Flag any FMC instances responding on standard management ports (443, 8305) from public IPs without documented proxy/VPN enforcement.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication: Low-Privilege FMC Logins
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detect authentication using known default/hard-coded FMC credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins by documented low-privileged default accounts (e.g., 'admin', service accounts with known weak passwords). Alert on: first-time logins from untrusted geographies, login anomalies (time-of-day, source IP patterns), and account lockout recovery after failed login bursts. Baseline legitimate administrative access and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Query and Export by Suspicious Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—policies, credentials, topology. Detect queries or bulk exports by compromised low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query FMC audit logs for data-access operations (policy export, rule dump, config download, credential retrieval) by low-privilege accounts. Flag access to sensitive object classes outside normal change-control windows. Correlate with failed-login or suspicious-login events preceding data access to isolate compromised-credential scenario.

suggestion.title: Patch-Claim vs. Vulnerability-Scan Mismatch: CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'; federal due date 2026-08-01. Detect claimed patches that don't match actual vulnerability-scan results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare vulnerability scanner output (CVE-2026-20316 detections) against asset inventory patch dates. Flag any FMC instances claiming patch date ≥ 2026-08-01 but scanner still reports vulnerable version. Cross-validate with firmware/OS patch records from host agents to identify desyncs.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement: FMC-Extracted Credentials Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password grants access to 'sensitive data'—FMC stores embedded credentials (SNMP, API keys, SSH). Detect lateral movement after FMC compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-FMC compromise, attacker exports stored credentials or policy configs. Monitor for FMC initiating connections to infrastructure outside normal baselines (target firewalls, managed switches, threat intel feeds). Alert on SSH/SNMP/API authentication attempts to those targets using credentials or patterns consistent with FMC-embedded values.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Successful Auth from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device.' Pipeline missed detection UC for anomalous FMC authentication patterns by source geography, ASN, or frequency baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC access logs for successful authentications from IPs outside administrative baselines. Alert if preceded by ≥3 failed auth attempts within 60 seconds using low-privileged account names (e.g., 'admin', 'fmc_user').

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline omitted detection for credential-stuffing or repeated-attempt patterns against known default/low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequential failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC using hardcoded or low-privilege account names, followed by successful login. Baseline expected failure rates per source IP; flag >10× normal rate.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication (Cisco FMC)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed collection-phase UC for policy exports, configuration retrieval, or credential dumps from FMC after successful low-privilege authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy exports, configuration backups, or credential queries initiated by low-privileged accounts within 5 minutes of failed-then-successful authentication or from new-to-site source IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies internet-facing FMC instances are prerequisite for active exploitation. Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' requires asset-level validation. Pipeline omitted vulnerability/asset correlation UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and scanning tools for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Cross-reference public IP address data to confirm internet exposure. Correlate with patch-management output to identify systems still running vulnerable versions post-due-date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Network Reconnaissance (Port/Service Scanning)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'currently being exploited in the wild' (CISA KEV). Pipeline missed early-stage UC for attacker reconnaissance: port scanning or HTTP probing against known FMC default ports (443, 8305).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences of failed TCP connections to Cisco FMC default ports (443, 8305) from external IPs, followed by successful HTTP 200/302 responses (successful probing). Baseline external probe rates; flag >2σ deviations per source subnet.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — initial connection attempts to exposed FMC management endpoints must be first detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) from untrusted/external sources. Correlate unauthenticated connection attempts with authentication events to identify exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability leverages 'hard-coded password' to bypass authentication — detection must flag login attempts using known weak/default credentials documented in Cisco advisories or credential stuffing against FMC accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful or repeated failed authentication to FMC using low-privileged or default account names. Alert on authentication from geographically improbable or off-hours sources, especially from internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Within Compromised FMC Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication — collection activity via compromised management interface is critical second-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual policy exports, rule queries, or credential vault access from authenticated but anomalous sessions. Alert on bulk config dumps or API calls targeting security objects outside normal admin patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes urgency ('patch due 2026-08-01') and active exploitation; asset inventory for exposed instances is remediation prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco FMC instances with internet-routable IPs or DNS; cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Identify instances without VPN/WAF access controls.

suggestion.title: FMC Administrative Session Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential abuse typically manifests as access anomalies outside legitimate admin behavior — logins from unexpected geographies, IPs, or outside operational hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate FMC admin access (time windows, source IPs, user agents). Alert on successful authentication outside baseline — especially low-privileged accounts accessing sensitive functions.

suggestion.title: FMC Security Policy or Firewall Rule Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hard-coded credentials, adversaries prioritize extracting security policies and rule sets — article specifies 'sensitive data' is target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for policy/rule export operations targeting multiple rule sets, triggered by non-administrative accounts, or followed by lateral data transfer to external networks. Flag bulk policy API queries.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit via hard-coded password; standard CISA KEV workflow requires asset inventory. Referenced template `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` was never applied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and network telemetry to identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances exposed on internet-facing networks. Correlate against patch status; alert on unpatched FMC with listening ports 443/8305.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'use of hard-coded password' allows login. No UC captures failed/successful auth attempts with default/hard-coded account names against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs and firewall authentication events for login attempts using known hard-coded or default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'root', 'cisco'). Alert on successful authentication from external IP ranges; correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability status.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No UC detects unauthorized reads of FMC configuration, policy, or credential repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data retrieval from FMC after successful low-privileged login: bulk export of firewall rules, threat intelligence policies, or credential stores. Baseline normal admin activity and alert on out-of-hours access or high-volume reads.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model includes gaining access to 'impacted systems'; confirmed compromise would likely result in policy/rule modification to maintain persistence or evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new administrative accounts or modification of existing firewall policies/rules within 48 hours of initial login with low-privileged hard-coded credentials. Flag any changes to logging, alerting, or access controls.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states affected product is 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' with known CVE-2026-20316. Standard asset-exposure hunt: identify vulnerable versions before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20316 findings against Cisco FMC assets. Cross-reference asset inventory for FMC versions pre-patch. Establish baseline of exposed FMC management interfaces (ports 8305/443) accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Remote Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' via hard-coded password. Detection should cover authentication attempts against FMC management interface from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for: (1) failed login attempts from external IPs, (2) successful low-privileged account logins from non-administrative networks, (3) login attempts immediately followed by privilege escalation attempts or configuration queries.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after low-privileged login. Should detect unusual query/export patterns on configuration, policy, or credential repositories post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal administrative queries against FMC sensitive data (policies, device configs, credentials). Flag low-privileged accounts or non-administrative sources querying sensitive policy/credential repositories, especially bulk exports or unusual command sequences.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Default Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'hard-coded password'. Should detect authentication using known/default credentials against FMC management services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication for use of known default account names (admin, root, cisco, etc.) from any source IP. Flag successful logins using default credentials or logins where password hash/attempt matches known weak/default values.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability is only exploitable if FMC management port is accessible remotely. Article implies public-facing exposure by noting 'remote attacker' can exploit.
log_sources: Network asset scanning (Shodan, Censys, internal port scans)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal network for Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 443, 22) accessible from DMZ or external networks. Correlate with vulnerability scanner to identify exposed+vulnerable instances. Flag any FMC management traffic from non-administrative network segments.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'public-facing application' and explicitly calls for asset-exposure hunt template. Phrase 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker' presupposes internet accessibility—exposure detection is the baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305, 8307) receiving inbound connections from internet-sourced IPs. Correlate asset inventory with firewall logs for inbound access to management ports and cross-reference against public scanning data (SHODAN, Censys) to identify externally-discoverable instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'; this implies detection of default/hard-coded usernames or weak credentials in authentication logs distinct from normal admin activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication events for successful remote logins with low-privilege or default account names from external IP sources. Detect rapid authentication attempts (credential spraying) followed by success, or logon events from non-standard geographies/ASNs not matching organizational patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Following Remote Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states impact: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Post-exploitation behavior requires detection of unauthorized data operations by compromised low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Cisco FMC configuration exports, credential dumps, policy retrievals, or audit log access occurring within 30 minutes of successful external authentication. Monitor for bulk API calls to sensitive endpoints (user lists, configuration snapshots, credential APIs) or CLI commands exfiltrating sensitive data from low-privilege sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Unpatched + Exposed Asset Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and emphasizes cross-checking unpatched systems even when scanners report otherwise. Federal due date 2026-08-01 creates hard compliance deadline for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances lacking CVE-2026-20316 patches as of federal due date 2026-08-01. Cross-correlate unpatched status with network exposure (internet-accessible, inbound firewall rules, lack of VPN requirement) and flag as immediate remediation requirement. Alert on scanner false-negatives where patched status conflicts with actual system version.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt – CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV' status means 'observed exploited in the wild' and recommends 'asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL.' Pipeline provided zero use cases despite explicit template guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances exposed to the network (internet-facing or accessible from untrusted segments). Correlate asset inventory against CVE-2026-20316 patches. Flag unpatched instances with priority due to active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Detect Hard-Coded Credential Login to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed credential-access detection entirely. Hard-coded password abuse is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs for successful authentication with low-privilege accounts from unexpected source IPs. Correlate failed + successful login patterns on the same interface. Flag logins from non-administrative network segments or after hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Sensitive Data Access from FMC After Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline did not model exfiltration or post-compromise data collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual data exports or API calls from FMC after successful low-privilege authentication. Monitor for bulk downloads of configuration, policy, or traffic logs. Flag data egress to external networks or cloud storage.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts on Exposed FMC Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies active scanning and exploitation attempts. Pipeline provided no behavioral detection for exploit-in-progress signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to known FMC management endpoints (e.g., /admin, /login) from untrusted sources. Monitor for credential enumeration or brute-force patterns against FMC API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized remote login to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' — direct credential compromise. Core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC administrative interfaces for successful authentication events from unexpected source IPs, especially those geographically anomalous or outside normal administrative access patterns. Alert on any successful login using the hard-coded credential account (if known) or unusual authentication success rates post-patch date.

suggestion.title: FMC sensitive data access via hard-coded account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — exfiltration/data access is the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for data export, configuration download, or policy/rule retrieval events from FMC originating from low-privileged authenticated sessions. Baseline normal data-access patterns and alert on deviation, especially for threat intelligence exports, firewall rule sets, or network topology data.

suggestion.title: Remote service session to exposed FMC management interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies exposed management port. T1021 variant for remote infrastructure access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to FMC management ports (8305/tcp, 443/tcp) from untrusted external IP ranges. Correlate with failed/successful authentication attempts. Alert on any connection attempt before credentials are submitted (connection establishment alone is suspicious for an internal appliance).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scan confirmation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context: patch lag is common; 'worth one quick check across your fleet.' Direct vulnerability signature detection.
