suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for administrative account creation, password resets, or privilege escalation events immediately following detected unauthorized access. Alert on creation of new admin accounts or modification of existing account permissions by low-privileged users. Correlate FMC admin activity with external source IP addresses.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempts on Exposed Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation in the wild; no use case generated despite this being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ingress traffic to Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 8307) for exploitation signatures, proof-of-concept attempts, or authentication flows using known default credentials. Alert on successful logon from untrusted networks immediately post-vulnerability publication.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage Against Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' as attack vector; credential access via known defaults is detection gap despite this being the exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to FMC using well-known default credential pairs or low-privileged built-in accounts from external sources. Correlate with failed authentication velocity patterns indicating brute-force or credential testing attempts.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'remote attacker' access to management interface; discovery of exposed FMC instances on untrusted networks is prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management interfaces exposed to untrusted networks via port scanning (8305, 8307) or HTTP response fingerprinting. Flag instances responding with FMC-specific certificates or HTTP headers that should not be externally reachable.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access and Exfiltration from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacker 'access to sensitive data within impacted systems'; FMC stores encrypted credentials, firewall policies, and network topology requiring data-loss detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised FMC for suspicious bulk exports, configuration dumps, or API calls exfiltrating firewall rules, device inventory, or credential store contents. Detect large outbound flows from FMC post-compromise or unusual data serialization patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker logs in with 'low-privileged account'; escalation path to full FMC control or credential access undetected despite being logical post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FMC systems post-successful low-privileged authentication, monitor for shell escapes, sudo abuse, or API privilege-escalation attempts. Alert on successful transitions from low-priv contexts to admin operations (certificate/credential access, policy modification).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Access via Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credential compromise is a direct attack vector requiring authentication-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 443, 8305) for login attempts using known hard-coded credential pairs. Alert on successful authentications from unexpected source IPs, geolocations, or off-hours access patterns. Correlate authentication logs with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Exposure Assessment

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset-management systems for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances running vulnerable versions. Cross-reference against patched inventories to identify unpatched FMC deployments exposed to CVE-2026-20316 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device.' Pipeline never generated use case for detecting default/hard-coded account access despite this being the exploitation pathway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC management interface using default or hard-coded account credentials. Correlate with failed authentication attempts, source IP geolocation mismatches, and suspicious API calls immediately post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires exposed management UI. Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implying internet-accessible FMC. Pipeline missed asset-discovery and exposure-hunting use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management interfaces exposed on internet-routable IPs by scanning known FMC ports (443, 8305) or correlating with public threat feeds (Shodan banners). Alert on any web requests from non-corporate external IPs to FMC management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive Data via Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after authentication. Pipeline did not generate collection/impact-phase detection for post-exploitation data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for low-privileged or default accounts exporting device configuration, policy rules, or network topology data. Alert on bulk queries to sensitive data repositories correlated with successful hard-coded credential authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Configuration Changes Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Successful FMC compromise enables policy manipulation. Article context ('sensitive data access') suggests potential for firewall-rule tampering. Pipeline missed persistence and impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall policy, access-control rule, or device-management configuration changes executed by default or low-privileged accounts, or changes occurring within 48 hours of vulnerability disclosure date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Authentication with Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' — successful authentication with hard-coded credentials is the primary abuse vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful remote authentications to Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center console from external networks. If vendor publishes hard-coded account names, flag any login attempts using those credentials. Correlate multiple failed attempts followed by success within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 (public-facing exploitation) and federal patch due-date implies active scanning — asset exposure hunt is the canonical first detection layer per article template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 matches, filter for exposed or internet-routable Cisco FMC instances. Cross-check management interface IP addresses against network segmentation policy to identify violations allowing external access to administrative console.

suggestion.title: FMC Admin Console Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation signals active, in-the-wild exploitation — probes and exploitation attempts against exposed FMC instances should be detectable via network telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS traffic to known FMC management ports for exploit signatures. Alert on clusters of 5xx errors or authentication failures concentrated on admin endpoints, request patterns matching known PoC tools, or unusual HTTP methods (POST/PUT) to API paths during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised FMC grants 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — attackers will modify policies or exfiltrate configurations to maintain persistence or move laterally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized configuration pushes from FMC to managed firewalls post-compromise. Flag bulk policy exports, new admin accounts created via FMC API, or changes to threat intelligence feeds. Correlate with failed authentication attempts on the same day.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Collection from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data' — FMC stores firewall policies, network topology, threat intelligence, and audit logs; post-exploitation this becomes an exfiltration target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large or unusual API calls retrieving security policies, network object lists, or audit log exports from FMC. Alert on file transfers from FMC server during off-hours, or API calls by non-provisioned accounts querying bulk configuration or threat data.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force / Password Spray Against FMC Admin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerabilities attract credential enumeration — article implies known/guessable credentials exist enabling unauthenticated remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire authentication attempts against FMC console using common hard-coded account names (admin, root, etc.) or public PoC credentials. Flag source IPs performing 10+ failed attempts followed by success within 1 hour, or 50+ failed attempts across multiple accounts in 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'—core attack behavior. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit authentication anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC (ports 8305, 8307) from non-whitelisted external IPs. Baseline legitimate FMC admin source IPs and alert on anomalies. Correlate low-privileged account logins from external sources with subsequent administrative actions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Collection-phase detection entirely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for policy exports, configuration downloads, or credential access initiated by low-privileged FMC accounts. Flag large data transfers or unusual query patterns from accounts with minimal history of administrative access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Reconnaissance and Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' requiring discovery before exploitation. Pipeline missed pre-exploitation reconnaissance indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or HTTP/HTTPS banner-grab attempts against Cisco FMC management ports (8305, 8307, 8308). Flag version-detection probes, service-fingerprinting, or SSL certificate enumeration preceding authentication attempts from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default and Hard-coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'use of hard-coded password.' Pipeline ignored default-credential and credential-store enumeration techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication attempts using known default Cisco FMC account names (admin, root, cisco, etc.) or common hard-coded credentials. Flag successful logins with default credentials or attempts from credential-injection/spray toolkits (Nuclei, Metasploit Cisco modules).

suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Failure or Unexpected Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'poisoned Adform script'—implying hash/signature deviation from baseline or published integrity manifest. Core detection angle completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to Adform CDN endpoints for script resources; compute or compare published hash/SRI (Subresource Integrity) attributes against observed delivery. Alert on mismatch. Cross-correlate script-load timestamp with known compromise window if published. Detect via CSP violation logs if SRI is enforced client-side.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution in HTTP Response Body
suggestion.rationale: Article core payload: 'swap crypto wallet addresses'—replacement logic must occur in DOM or during script execution. No detection query suggested for this direct impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies from compromised script for known legitimate wallet patterns (Bitcoin/Ethereum address formats). Correlate frequent wallet-pattern mutations within same session or across users hitting same CDN endpoint. Detect via JavaScript runtime hooks (Frida/Burp) or traffic decryption if HTTPS interception available. Flag if attacker wallet address appears in outbound crypto transactions.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Script Behavioral Anomaly: Unexpected Network Calls or DOM Writes
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malicious script modifies wallet addresses; implies behavioral deviation (crypto-oriented network calls, suspicious DOM mutation patterns). Pipeline missed behavioral monitoring layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile baseline behavior of Adform script (typical domains called, DOM selectors touched, event handlers registered). Generate alerts when script deviates (sudden calls to wallet services, mining pools, or uncommon TLDs; regex-based form field patching). Correlate with user reports of missing/diverted payments.

suggestion.title: Adform Domain Certificate or TLS Anomalies During Compromise Window
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often involve infrastructure takeover; certificate reissue, pinning bypass, or MITM interception are possible pivot points. No mention of cert-chain validation or anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for unexpected issuances under Adform's domain or known CDN CNAMEs. Compare deployed certificate chain against historical baseline (issuer, serial, validity window). Alert on sudden re-issuance, new CAs, or short-lived certificates. Correlate with DomainWhois changes or DNS delegation updates.

suggestion.title: Script-Loading Source Validation: Unexpected Adform CDN Endpoint or CNAME
suggestion.rationale: Article implies script came from Adform infrastructure; attackers may have modified DNS, cache-poisoned, or injected via compromised origin. No IOC for malicious endpoint—critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain allowlist of legitimate Adform script-delivery endpoints (CNAME chain, A records, IP ranges). Alert on script loads from unexpected IP, subdomain, or ASN. Cross-check against public CDN reputation lists and WHOIS changes. Correlate DNS queries to Adform infrastructure with timing of malicious payload detection in customer logs.

suggestion.title: Outbound Cryptocurrency Transactions Exceeding Baseline Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article's impact is wallet-address swap leading to attacker enrichment; detection must cover transaction-ledger anomalies or user complaints of misdirected payments tied to web session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users affected by Adform compromise (from web-traffic reconstruction) against external indicators of confirmed stolen crypto—e.g., attacker's public wallet receiving inbound transfers, blockchain tx timestamp aligned with user session time. Alternatively, surface user-reported disputes/chargebacks mentioning unexpected crypto sends after visiting affected e-commerce or payment sites.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Executable Execution from Browser/Update Cache Post-Fake-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fake updates to deliver surveillance malware.' No execution-phase detection generated despite this being the core delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned process creation from temp directories (AppData\Local\Temp, %windir%\Temp) immediately following update-prompt windows or installer terminations. Flag process launches from browser download directories with mismatched file signatures.

suggestion.title: Hotel Guest-Network MITM Detection (SSL Downgrade, Self-Signed Certs)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi.' Network hijacking enables traffic interception; no initial-access or defense-evasion detection rule for this fundamental MITM posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for certificate chain validation failures on software update domains (mismatched CN, self-signed issuer). Flag TLS 1.0/1.1 downgrades on guest networks. Alert on HTTP (cleartext) update traffic from known hotel SSIDs.

suggestion.title: Malware-Delivered Surveillance Capability Activation (Screen/Audio Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'surveillance malware' as impact. Zero detection rule for post-compromise data exfiltration by stealer/surveillance payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned processes calling Windows API sequences for screen capture (BitBlt, GetDC, GDIPlus), audio capture (WASAPI, waveIn*), or keyboard hooks (SetWindowsHookEx). Correlate with unexpected network exfiltration to non-corporate IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DNS Queries / HTTP Requests to Fake Update Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake-update delivery mechanism; no IOC extraction or C2 communication detection. Pipeline should surface malware/update server domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS requests to domains resembling legitimate software vendors (e.g., 'updates-security.com', 'patch-portal.net') from guest-network IPs. Flag HTTP/S requests to non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 9090) for 'update' resources. Cross-reference against known malware delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Update Binary Delivery (T1195.002 - Compromised Software)
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'fake updates.' Compromised Software (T1195.002) is the defining technique; pipeline surfaced no supply-chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on update binaries signed by spoofed or revoked certificates. Flag file-size mismatches between legitimate and downloaded update payloads. Monitor for update processes writing to registry persistence locations or spawning child processes outside normal update workflows.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Traffic Interception on Guest Wi-Fi (ARP Spoofing, DNS Redirect)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi pushes fake updates.' Network hijacking requires MITM primitives; no defense-evasion detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected gateway MAC changes on guest-network clients. Flag gratuitous ARP replies from non-gateway hosts. Monitor for DNS responses from non-authoritative resolvers (rogue DHCP or DNS spoofing). Alert on HTTP redirects to IP addresses for domains normally resolved to different IPs.

suggestion.title: Prototype pollution via malformed JSON patch: PATCH with __proto__ or constructor.prototype in body
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'apos.util.set() traverses dot-notation paths without sanitizing __proto__' and 'via patch operators ($pullAll)'. All current UCs search URL, not body. Requires WAF/proxy body inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PATCH/POST to /@apostrophecms/* with Content-Type: application/json where request body contains __proto__, constructor.prototype, or $pullAll operator. Baseline: should be zero in production.

suggestion.title: Authorization context corruption: POST/PATCH followed by access to publicApiProjection-protected resource
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass...publicApiProjection checks'. Detection should look for subsequent API calls to /user or /global endpoints with unexpected permission levels from same user session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track API calls from authenticated editor sessions. Alert if user with 'editor' role suddenly accesses /api/v1/@apostrophecms/user or /global after a PATCH to core utility endpoint. Cross-reference session tokens.

suggestion.title: Apostrophe CMS /api/v1/@apostrophecms/global access from editor-role session
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates /global endpoint requires elevated privileges that prototype pollution can bypass. Direct access from editor context is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200 responses to GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/global from authenticated sessions with role=editor. Baseline expected: zero or admin-only. Compare against documented RBAC.

suggestion.title: Apostrophe util.set() deprecation warnings or error stack traces in logs
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'apos.util.set() traverses...without sanitizing'. Defensive patches may log warnings when __proto__ is encountered. Error logs from attempted exploitation are forensic indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse application error logs for stack traces or warnings containing 'apos.util.set', '__proto__', or 'Prototype pollution attempt' from Node.js process logs. Correlate with HTTP timestamps.

suggestion.title: Detect ClickFix Social Engineering Attack Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'ClickFix' as part of campaign; this pattern (fake tech-support prompts → script execution) is a documented Midnight Blizzard vector requiring behavioral detection on process spawning from Office/browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of suspicious interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe) from browser processes or Office applications within 30 seconds of user browser navigation to attacker-controlled domain. Correlate with user reports of fake support popups.

suggestion.title: Detect AiTM Token Interception on Public WiFi
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Adversary-in-the-middle' and 'token theft'; travelers on airport/hotel WiFi are high-risk. Detection should flag authentication token exfiltration patterns from unmanaged networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AAD/Exchange sign-ins from public WiFi networks (geolocation + network context) followed by unusual token reuse from different networks within 10 minutes; indicates interception and token replay.

suggestion.title: Monitor Malware Delivery via Travel-Related Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'travelers worldwide'; subject lines/URLs referencing flights, hotels, visas should be prioritized. Article implies social engineering + malware combo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of downloaded file within 2 minutes of user clicking travel-themed email link; specifically watch for suspicious file extensions (.vbs, .ps1, .exe) or renamed system tools launched from Downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass via Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'token theft'; AiTM operators harvest OAuth/MFA tokens to bypass 2FA. Sign-in graphs should flag impossible travel + token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sign-in events where user authenticates with MFA from one geography, then immediately (within 15 min) performs sensitive action (e.mail send, data export) from IP geographically inconsistent with both user and token-grant location.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Harvesting via Fake WiFi Authentication Portals
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks on travelers rely on captive portal spoofing. Article indicates 'credential theft' via network compromise in transit environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 302/307 redirects from legitimate travel-related domains (.airlines.com, .booking.com) to attacker-controlled lookalike domains; correlate with subsequent HTTPS requests to the decoy domain capturing credentials.

suggestion.title: Detect PowerShell-based Malware Installation Post-ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix typically drops PS scripts; Windows keyword in schema. Second-stage malware installation follows social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe spawned with -EncodedCommand, -NoProfile, or -WindowStyle Hidden within 5 minutes of ClickFix-associated process chain; check for registry modifications (RunOnce, Run) or scheduled task creation.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking - SspiCli.dll Targeting AppVShNotify.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents NightLedger masquerading as SspiCli.dll 'designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is a defense-evasion technique that must be detectable before backdoor reaches execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious DLL loaded from non-system paths as SspiCli.dll when imported by AppVShNotify.exe. Monitor for DLL files written to %TEMP% or %APPDATA% matching known system DLL names but lacking proper code signing. Alert on AppVShNotify.exe loading DLLs from search-order exploitable locations.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneler C2 - BridgeHead and ArcBridge
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers (BridgeHead, ArcBridge) explicitly used for 'covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' BridgeHead observed in post-exploitation in Egypt and Pakistan aerospace organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) from non-browser processes, especially from System/SYSTEM user context or uncommon parent processes like rundll32.exe, svchost.exe. Monitor for long-lived WebSocket connections with irregular traffic patterns or connections to recently registered domains.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing with Recruitment and Videoconferencing Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'highly tailored social engineering lures' including 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives on third-party file-sharing services.' This is the documented initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment-themed subjects paired with shortened URLs or redirects to file-sharing services (mega.nz, archive.org, etc). Flag clicks on lookalike domains impersonating known videoconferencing platforms (zoom-login, teams-auth patterns). Correlate with known targeting sectors (aerospace, aviation, defense, telecom in MENA region).

suggestion.title: NightLedger Backdoor - Screenshot Capture and Process Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article details NightLedger capabilities including 'screenshot capture' and 'process discovery' as reconnaissance functions post-exploitation. These are distinct collection-phase activities enabling further targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes with gdiplus.dll and winspool.drv loaded alongside cmd.exe or rundll32.exe execution. Monitor for tasklist.exe, Get-Process (PowerShell), or wmic.exe invoked from unusual parent processes. Correlate with creation of image files in temp directories immediately after process discovery attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Tunneler Deployment After Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'BridgeHead being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization. The deployment followed targeted spear-phishing activity.' This represents the transition from initial access to persistence/C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 24-72 hours of phishing-campaign email clicks detected in MENA-based aerospace/aviation/defense organizations, detect new service installation or scheduled task creation for tunneler processes. Look for rundll32.exe launching with unusual DLL arguments, or svchost.exe spawning child processes that establish WebSocket connections.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Delivery from Third-Party File Sharing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack flow: 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' This is the execution payload delivery mechanism after social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads from known file-sharing services (mega.nz, archive.org, mediafire.com, etc.) with archive extensions (.zip, .rar, .7z) originating from untrusted referrers. Monitor auto-extraction and child-process spawning from archive payloads. Flag if extracted files match known NightLedger/BridgeHead/ArcBridge signatures or masquerade as system DLLs (sSppiCli.dll, etc).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'unauthenticated, remote'—FMC must be internet-facing. Article's own guidance references 'asset-exposure hunt' but no detection was generated. Detect publicly accessible FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances on public IPs or externally resolvable FQDNs. Correlate with asset inventory to surface unmanaged/exposed FMC deployments that lack expected network segmentation or WAF protection.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Brute Force or Known-Password Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability'—attackers will attempt login with known credentials or dictionary attacks. No monitoring for FMC auth attempts despite this being the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC admin login endpoints (default ports 443, 8305) for repeated failed authentication from external IPs, or successful logins using low-privileged accounts from unexpected geolocation. Flag any authentication outside typical admin access baselines.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from Low-Privilege Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems' using compromised low-privilege account. Pipeline missed the collection phase entirely—no detection for unusual data reads, exports, or API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track data export operations, bulk policy downloads, device telemetry extraction, or threat-intelligence feed access from non-admin FMC accounts. Alert on high-volume or time-of-day anomalies in data retrieval patterns that deviate from documented admin workflow baselines.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Remote Login Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated zero detections for remote login attempts against exposed FMC consoles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed and successful SSH or HTTPS login attempts to Cisco FMC management port from external/unexpected sources. Cross-reference against known hard-coded credentials CVE-2026-20316. Elevated urgency for successful logins.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies vulnerability mechanism: 'use of hard-coded password.' Pipeline extracted neither T1078.001 (Default Accounts) nor T1555 (Credentials from Password Stores).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful login events on Cisco FMC using known-low-privileged account names associated with CVE-2026-20316. Flag any queries for system credentials or password stores post-login.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Exploitation Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker objective: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline generated no collection-phase detection despite explicit statement of intent.
log_sources: File/API call logs for security policies, device configs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful low-privileged FMC login, hunt for bulk data exports, API queries to fetch policies/device data, or config file access. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Management Console Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article context emphasizes CISA KEV (actively exploited); article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due-date of 2026-08-01. Pipeline did not generate asset-exposure detection for Cisco FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Cisco FMC management interfaces (port 8305/TCP, port 443/HTTPS on FMC hostnames). Cross-check against organizational asset inventory; flag instances not patched for CVE-2026-20316 with patch-due date warnings.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Matches
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with explicit federal patch deadline 2026-08-01. CVE-2026-20316 is the primary IOC that must be extracted for vulnerability scanning baseline. Article prescribes: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: **CVE:** `CVE-2026-20316`'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 matches against Cisco FMC instances. Cross-reference scan results with asset inventory for exposed or unpatched FMC appliances. Escalate any unpatched matches discovered after federal patch deadline (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts Against FMC Management
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'unauthenticated, remote' but can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—indicating hard-coded or default credential exploitation. Phrase 'low-privileged account' reinforces use of weak, known credentials rather than brute-force.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (HTTPS 443, 8305) for successful logins using known default/hard-coded accounts (admin, root, cisco). Alert on logins from unexpected source IPs, especially if followed by sensitive data access or configuration changes. Track authentication failures followed by success with different credentials (indicating credential grinding).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access and Exfiltration from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores VPN pre-shared keys, firewall policies, threat intelligence feeds, and device credentials—all high-value targets for exfiltration or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for credential export, configuration backup, or credential dump operations initiated by non-admin or low-privileged accounts. Alert on database queries to credential storage or VPN tables. Track egress network traffic from FMC to external IPs for encrypted data transfers or unusual protocol patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from FMC Management Plane to Subordinate Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Cisco FMC is a central management appliance controlling deployed Firepower/ASA instances. Article's reference to 'impacted systems' (plural) implies FMC compromise cascades to managed devices. Attacker can use FMC's trusted management channel to deploy malicious configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management commands to subordinate firewalls, especially ACL modifications, threat prevention disablement, or credential extraction. Alert on configuration deployments initiated by service accounts or unusual administrative users. Cross-correlate FMC compromises with downstream firewall configuration changes.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'remote attacker' exploiting 'public-facing application.' FMC management interfaces exposed to the internet without network segmentation face immediate exploitation risk. Article references asset-exposure hunting as canonical detection methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for internet-routable Cisco FMC management interfaces. Cross-reference with firewall rules to confirm management access restricted to internal/VPN ranges. Search Certificate Transparency and SHODAN for FMC hostnames. Flag any externally-accessible FMC post-discovery.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Tracking Against Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' CISA KEV entries trigger legal remediation obligations. Pipeline should generate compliance hunt linking patch status to federal deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for Cisco FMC vulnerability status against CVE-2026-20316. Establish compliance baseline requiring all FMC instances patched by 2026-08-01. Daily report unpatched instances by business unit. Escalate any Cisco FMC still vulnerable 30 days before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication - Hard-coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded password abuse is the root attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using low-privileged service account credentials (e.g., 'admin', 'fmc_user') from external/unauthenticated sources, especially with repeated failed attempts followed by successful login. Baseline legitimate FMC access sources and alert on anomalous geographic or ASN origins.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation data collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on queries, exports, or access to sensitive FMC data stores (user credentials, managed device configs, encryption keys) originating from low-privileged or service accounts, especially via bulk data operations or SQL queries. Correlate with initial_access timestamps.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation - Cisco FMC Network-Based Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active wild exploitation of hard-coded password vulnerability. Signature-based network detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Cisco FMC login endpoints (standard ports 443, 8305) with known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation patterns: default credential payloads, timing consistency with automated tools, or IDS signatures matching Cisco security advisory. Flag requests from non-whitelisted sources.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance - CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01.' Compliance enforcement and asset discovery attack precursor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances running versions prior to the patch release. Flag unpatched instances immediately; correlate with network access controls to identify externally-reachable FMC instances still vulnerable post-due-date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Management Access from Unexpected Network Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' No legitimate reason for FMC management access outside trusted network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network connections to Cisco FMC management interfaces from IP space outside your organization's trusted sources. Establish baseline of legitimate FMC management endpoints (e.g., SOC admin VLANs). Alert on connections from cloud providers, residential ISPs, or known proxy services.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Export or Sensitive Backup Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Post-access data exfiltration: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' implies configuration/backup extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy/rule exports, configuration backups, or certificate/key material accessed via FMC CLI, API, or UI from non-administrative or low-privileged accounts. Correlate with lateral movement indicators (multiple device policies accessed sequentially). Monitor for out-of-band data transfer attempts (USB export, email, API to external endpoints).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Status Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes CISA KEV = actively exploited. Pipeline should instantiate template at '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' with CVE-2026-20316 as primary IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center systems reporting CVE-2026-20316 as unpatched. CISA KEV implies active exploitation in the wild; patch lag is a critical risk indicator even if scanners miss edge cases.

suggestion.title: FMC Unauthenticated Remote Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account.' Behavioral indicator: detect login attempts to FMC from untrusted sources, especially with default or hardcoded account names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any remote authentication success to Cisco FMC admin interfaces (default ports 443/8305) from external IPs or unexpected geolocations. Hard-coded password exploits succeed on first or few attempts; correlate with unusual post-login behavior.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privilege Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains access 'to access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation hunt: detect low-privileged FMC accounts querying configuration, logs, or policy data they should not access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for data exports, configuration downloads, or log queries initiated by accounts created post-infection or with anomalous login patterns. Low-privileged accounts should not access firewall policies or audit trails.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Accessible Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is cited for KEV entry; FMC management interfaces must never be externally routable. Article implies network-level detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify any Cisco FMC management endpoints (port 443, 8305, 8307) reachable from the public Internet or untrusted network segments. Cross-reference with asset inventory; flag as critical exposure if external routing detected.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Change Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password access to FMC provides persistent foothold; attacker may alter firewall policies, logging, or authentication rules to maintain access and evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC policy changes, authentication rule modifications, or logging disablement performed by low-privilege accounts or outside normal maintenance windows. Correlate with login anomalies from same time window.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access to 'Secure Firewall Management Center' — requires FMC to be internet-exposed on management ports. Article states asset-exposure hunt is canonical detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly routable Cisco FMC management interfaces (typically TCP 443, product signature in SSL cert or HTTP response headers). Correlate with cloud asset inventories and port-scan activity pointing to FMC ports from untrusted ASNs.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'use of hard-coded password' allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' with known low-privileged account. Detection of credential usage is explicit detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known or published hard-coded account names (if disclosed in advisories). Flag successful auth from non-admin sources, especially from external/unexpected IPs.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account Access to FMC Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could...access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account. This is the post-auth collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries, API calls, or file access by low-privileged FMC accounts targeting sensitive configuration data (firewall rules, network topology, credential stores, policy databases) that are typically accessed only by administrators.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication Source to Cisco FMC Management
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV confirms active exploitation. Low-privileged account logins to management interface should originate from expected admin networks; geographic/ASN anomalies indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline geographic origin, ASN, and time-of-day patterns for FMC admin logins. Alert on successful authentication from non-enterprise ASNs, impossible-travel scenarios, or off-hours logins to low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Lag Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and Federal due-date is 2026-08-01. Inventory of unpatched/outdated FMC versions is compliance and risk detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset scanner and CMDB for Cisco FMC product installations with version < [fixed version for CVE-2026-20316]. Cross-reference against patch dates to identify systems >30 days past vendor fix availability.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection in Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-20316 affecting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC); vulnerability scanner matching is the first defense per article's own recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances in vulnerability management platform. Alert if CVE-2026-20316 score is unpatched or patch date is after 2026-08-01 federal due date. Correlate against network device inventory to verify patch status.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Authentication to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'logs in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—implies successful authentication post-exploitation. Monitor for low-privilege FMC user logins, especially from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305) by low-privilege user accounts (service, guest, test accounts). Baseline normal access patterns and flag connections from non-administrative source IPs or after-hours access.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Remote Access to FMC Management Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' accessing FMC; initial access is network-based. Monitor for connections to FMC management interfaces from untrusted or external networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound/inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443/tcp, 8305/tcp) from untrusted networks. Establish baseline of authorized management sources. Alert on connections from external IPs, IoT devices, or non-administrative VLANs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access or Export from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—collection phase. Monitor for data reads, exports, or exfiltration from FMC post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk data queries, report generation, or export operations initiated by low-privilege FMC accounts within 1 hour of first successful authentication. Flag unusual data volume transfers from FMC management console to external systems.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Brute Force or Password Spray Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'use of hard-coded password'; attackers may attempt multiple hard-coded credential combinations. Monitor for authentication attempts using known default/hard-coded FMC credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts to FMC using credential patterns consistent with hard-coded passwords (e.g., 'admin:admin', default service account patterns). Flag 5+ failed attempts within 10 minutes followed by success. Correlate against known Cisco FMC default credentials.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Changes or Policy Modifications by Low-Privilege User
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated, attacker may modify firewall policies or configuration to maintain access or disable logging. Monitor for unauthorized changes from low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall rule changes, logging policy disablement, or authentication settings modifications initiated by low-privilege FMC user accounts. Require approval workflow for configuration changes and flag any changes made outside change windows by unexpected users.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using hardcoded or default credentials, rapid brute-force attempts against low-privileged accounts, or authentication from untrusted source IPs. Escalate immediately given KEV active-exploitation status.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Authentication Configuration Access

Flag any read access to sensitive firewall rules, VPN configurations, or managed device lists within minutes of successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credentials are the core exploitation mechanism and require direct detection in authentication logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC login events for successful authentication with known hard-coded account names. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC data-access logs for bulk policy exports, credential vault access, or unusual configuration downloads immediately following hard-coded credential authentication. suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Accessible Port Exposure

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC External Management Interface Access

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connection attempts to Cisco FMC management interfaces (TCP 443, 8305, 8307) from external/non-trusted network segments. Correlate with authentication attempts; high-risk if preceded by port scanning or HTTP fingerprinting probes.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration & Sensitive Data Exfiltration

Alert on new API tokens issued to low-privileged accounts or anomalous mass-retrieval of firewall rules, device inventory, or security logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Exploitation Signature

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Asset Exposure Hunt

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Unauthorized Access Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Cisco FMC admin interface from unexpected source IPs, during non-business hours, or with geographic impossibility (velocity check). Correlate login events with failed preceding attempts. Baseline legitimate administrator login patterns and flag significant deviations.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Enumeration and Export
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall policies, threat intelligence databases, and network topology—bulk access requires detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk exports of firewall configurations, threat intelligence database queries, or policy enumeration across managed devices. Alert on data access scope inconsistent with administrator's normal responsibilities (e.g., querying firewall rules for unrelated business units).

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC provides control plane access to downstream managed firewalls. Article's 'sensitive data access' implies potential reconnaissance for lateral movement to security infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After suspicious FMC login, monitor for unauthorized policy deployments, firewall configuration changes, or commands sent from FMC to managed devices. Alert on policy modifications diverging from change management tickets or occurring outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Default Credential Usage Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly hard-coded password. Detection must distinguish default account usage from normal administration and flag anomalous login patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for built-in FMC administrative account login frequency, source IPs, and time-of-day patterns. Alert on logins from new geographic locations, repeated failed attempts indicating credential guessing, or login-to-data-access patterns matching exploitation (e.g., login → immediate policy export).

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Attackers Exploit Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator Command Injection Flaw' — no IOC or detection case was generated for exploitation attempts despite 'crit' severity.

Alert on HTTP POST/PUT to /api/* endpoints with suspicious input followed by HTTP 200 or error responses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from VeloCloud Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Command injection implies post-exploit arbitrary command execution; article describes active exploitation but pipeline generated no execution detection. 'Attackers Exploit' indicates successful code execution occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or curl processes spawned by VeloCloud Orchestrator service accounts (vcg, velocloud, root in context of container). Flag PPID chains with Java/web service parents and child processes making external network calls.

suggestion.title: Webshell or Script Upload to VeloCloud Web Directory
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploitation typically leads to persistence via web shell. Article does not indicate opportunistic/wiper behavior, implying attacker persistence intent. Pipeline missed persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VeloCloud root directories and /opt/velocloud paths for creation or modification of .jsp, .php, .py, .sh, or .aspx files with recent timestamps. Cross-correlate with PUT/POST HTTP requests to /api/* or /upload endpoints in the 60 seconds prior to file creation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 or Data Exfiltration from Compromised Orchestrator
suggestion.rationale: Critical infrastructure compromise typically results in C2 callback or lateral movement preparation. Pipeline generated zero C2/exfiltration detection despite active-exploitation scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-standard outbound TCP/UDP connections from VeloCloud Orchestrator to external IPs on high-numbered ports (>10000), or DNS queries to newly-registered/suspicious domains. Flag beaconing patterns (callbacks at regular intervals) and anomalous protocol usage (raw sockets, non-HTTP).

suggestion.title: Credential or Configuration Extraction from VeloCloud Database

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-read or grep operations targeting /etc/velocloud, /opt/velocloud/config, or system keystore paths. Monitor for unusual SQL queries against VeloCloud configuration databases (SQLite, PostgreSQL) selecting password, credential, or certificate columns in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Orchestrator to SD-WAN Edge Nodes

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH, TLS, or proprietary protocol connections from VeloCloud Orchestrator to internal VeloCloud Edge devices with anomalous frequency, timing, or credential patterns. Flag file-transfer operations (scp, rsync) to edge nodes or remote code execution attempts via management APIs.
