suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC Console
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability enables access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC stores firewall policies, network topology, and credential material. No data exfiltration detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or data transfers from FMC console during low-privileged or suspicious sessions. Flag unusual payload sizes, timing (after-hours), or destination IPs inconsistent with legitimate backups or documentation workflows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable FMC Asset Inventory — Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (active exploitation) with Federal patch due 2026-08-01. Recommended hunts section references templates but no concrete asset-exposure use case was generated to find vulnerable unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances running versions affected by CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference patch status against Federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01). Identify FMC management interfaces exposed externally or behind public-facing load balancers (non-RFC1918 IPs or cloud WAF origins).

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attacks Against Hard-coded FMC Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Once hard-coded credential characteristics become public, attackers may attempt variations or distributed testing across multiple FMC instances. No credential-access or brute-force detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed FMC authentication attempts from the same source IP within a short window, especially targeting known low-privileged or service account patterns. Establish baseline of expected login frequency per source and flag deviations indicating probing behavior.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit exposed instances. CISA KEV listing means active scanning and exploitation is occurring. No asset inventory check was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC, formerly Firepower Management Center) instances on network perimeter. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-20316 and compare deployment dates to federal due-date 2026-08-01. Flag any unpatched FMC exposed on standard management ports (443, 8305, 8307).

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows login 'using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. No detection for default or service-account authentication was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC using hard-coded or default service account names (e.g., 'admin', 'service', 'fmc-backup'). Baseline expected login times and locations; flag off-hours or geographic anomalies. Correlate with failed authentication spikes immediately preceding successful logins.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation. No network-level or application-level exploit signature or behavioral pattern was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound network traffic to Cisco FMC ports (443 HTTPS, 8305/8307 management) from external IPs with indicators of exploitation: malformed authentication headers, credential-guessing patterns, or payloads known to trigger hard-coded account bypass. Flag any successful connection followed by immediate administrative queries or configuration changes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Access from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection for data exfiltration or sensitive-data queries post-authentication was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to FMC using hard-coded account, alert on extraction of security policies, firewall rules, or customer traffic logs. Flag bulk data exports, API calls querying sensitive objects (rule sets, decryption keys, logging configurations), or downloads of backup/configuration files immediately following initial access.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Spike Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hard-coded password attack vector but does not specify if initial access requires brute-force enumeration. Pipeline should detect credential-spray or repeated-attempt patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate failed login attempts to Cisco FMC instances across 5-minute windows. Alert on >10 failed attempts from single source IP or >20 unique IPs attempting login within 1-hour window. Correlate failed-attempt clusters with known exploitation CVE-2026-20316 scanner traffic or exploitation frameworks (e.g., Metasploit FMC hard-coded-account modules).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Management Port Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes unauthenticated remote attacker access: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'. Requires network-level discovery of FMC instances on typical HTTPS ports (443, 8305).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SYN/connection attempts to Cisco FMC default management ports from untrusted external networks. High-volume scanning to port 8305 or 443 with Cisco service banners indicates reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation — Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data'. Detection gap: distinguish low-priv account login from subsequent data access indicating credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful login to Cisco FMC followed immediately (< 5 min) by access to configuration, user lists, or sensitive data export by that low-privileged account from external source IP.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Storm on FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exploitation may be preceded by reconnaissance; hard-coded password likely already known to attackers. Mass failed logins indicate active exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on >10 failed FMC authentication attempts within 2 minutes from single external IP, or >50 attempts within 10 minutes across multiple IPs targeting same FMC instance.

suggestion.title: FMC Patch Compliance Scan — CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due-date 2026-08-01 and patch urgency. Asset-exposure hunt required per article template guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center versions < patch version for CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with last observed patch date from Nessus/Qualys; alert if >90 days stale.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC After Low-Priv Login
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states compromise enables 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Detection should focus on what data low-priv account should NOT be accessing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for low-privileged accounts exporting, downloading, or copying firewall rules, access control lists, VPN credentials, or policy configurations. Flag any data transfer to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Lateral Movement via Compromised Low-Priv Account
suggestion.rationale: Article notes access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems' (plural). Low-priv FMC user account may be pivoted to access managed firewalls or adjacent systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privileged FMC account performing device configuration changes, policy updates, or API calls to managed firewalls from external IP address. Flag changes deployed to production devices within minutes of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Brute Force Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in... using a low-privileged account' — indicates known hardcoded passwords are being weaponized (T1110.4, T1552.007). Pipeline missed credential stuffing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for failed then successful login attempts using known hardcoded account names (fmc, admin, etc.) from external networks. Alert on successful FMC authentication from IP addresses not in baseline management-access whitelist, especially if followed within minutes by sensitive-data queries or configuration exports.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' and federal KEV designation indicate vulnerable FMC instances are discovered and targeted externally (T1190, T1200). Asset-exposure hunt required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC management interfaces (TCP 443, 8305) reachable from internet-routable IPs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 presence. Baseline all Cisco FMC instances by IP and location; flag any newly exposed or responding from unexpected networks. Cross-check against patch-management data for systems past federal due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — collection and exfiltration phase is implicit but pipeline generated zero detections. Hardcoded-credential compromise enables ongoing data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-authentication monitoring: detect bulk data exports (policy rules, network topology, device inventory) initiated by hardcoded or low-privileged accounts. Flag anomalous API query patterns: rapid sequential requests to sensitive tables, exports of firewall policies or connected device configs, or SFTP/HTTP pulls of large data sets from FMC to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exploitation Chain Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation presupposes discovery; article's 'public-facing' status means scanners precede breach. Pipeline missed initial reconnaissance phase (T1595, T1592).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scanning activity targeting Cisco FMC ports (443, 8305) from external sources: repeated SYN attempts, HTTP/HTTPS banner grabs, requests for known FMC web paths (login page fingerprints). Correlate source IPs against known vulnerability scanner vendors. Alert on multiple external IPs probing same FMC instance within 24h — indicator of active reconnaissance preceding exploitation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised FMC Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded credential disclosure (T1552.007) enables persistent FMC access; article implies attacker can re-authenticate and pivot. Pipeline missed persistence and lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC authentication sources (admin workstations, orchestration IPs, management subnets). Alert on successful logins from new geographies, out-of-hours, or rapid sequential authentication from different source IPs. Correlate FMC sessions with downstream lateral-movement indicators: API calls from FMC to threat-defense devices, SSH tunnels from FMC to other infrastructure, LDAP queries from FMC to domain controllers.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable System Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch due date 2026-08-01; pipeline must operationalize urgency via continuous inventory alignment. This UC enforces accountability and compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory query: identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner database for CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability presence. Generate escalation for any unpatched instances not yet addressed past 2026-08-01 deadline. Separate alerts for internet-facing FMC vs. internal-only; prioritize exposed instances as immediate containment risk.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and establishes CISA KEV mandate. No asset-exposure UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC, formerly Firepower Management Center) instances matching CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions. Prioritize exposed management interfaces reachable from untrusted networks; federal patch deadline is 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password. No UC for detecting credential-access events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface with default or low-privileged account names. Track failed-attempt clusters preceding successful login; correlate source IP with CVE-2026-20316 scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires network-accessible management interface (unauthenticated, remote). Article does not mention VPN gating, implying direct exposure. No network-based detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, 22) from external/untrusted sources. Correlate with port-scanning or service-banner-grab activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access and Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—implies configuration data, credentials, and firewall policies stored on FMC. No collection or exfiltration UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk data exports, configuration backups, credential dumps, or policy-rule downloads following low-privileged account access. Flag non-standard authentication events accessing sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC to Managed Firewall Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC can orchestrate changes to managed firewalls and access managed-device configs. Article mentions sensitive data access but does not limit scope to FMC local storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration deployments, policy updates, or credential provisioning from FMC to managed devices during or immediately following unauthorized FMC access. Correlate with account/IP anomalies.

suggestion.title: Remote Unauthenticated Access to Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access FMC. No network-layer detection rule generated for FMC management port access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections from untrusted external networks to Cisco FMC management ports (8305, 8306, 443). Correlate with HTTP POST requests to FMC login endpoints and response codes indicating authentication bypass (HTTP 302 redirect to admin dashboard without valid credentials).

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'use of hard-coded password' that enables login. No credential-access detection logic generated for this primary exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful login immediately following connection from external IP using username patterns associated with default/hard-coded accounts (admin, root, fmc_user). Alert on successful authentication without corresponding password-change activity in subsequent 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Accessing Sensitive FMC Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'low-privileged account' but accesses 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—clear privilege escalation or overpermissioned data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag audit log entries showing low-privilege FMC user accounts (verified via role/group membership) performing reads on sensitive objects: firewall policies, access control rules, VPN configurations, or administrative user accounts. Detect role-mismatch queries to /api/fmc_platform endpoints for privileged data.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Collection or Configuration Export from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' without limitation; no detection for data staging/exfiltration of policies, configurations, or asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests to /api/fmc_platform/v1 endpoints requesting large result sets (policy objects, device inventories, rule sets) or requests to backup/export endpoints. Monitor for archive file creation (tar.gz, zip) of FMC configuration directories or database exports outside scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Brute Force Authentication Against FMC Following Failed Attempts
suggestion.rationale: If hard-coded credentials are not immediately known, attackers will probe with common default passwords or leaked credential lists. No brute-force detection for FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed authentication attempts to FMC within 5 minutes from single external IP, followed by successful authentication from same source. Correlate with failed attempts using known default username variants (admin, administrator, root, fmc) to identify credential-guessing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Configuration Modifications by Unauthorized FMC Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with account access may modify firewall policies, disable logging, or create persistence mechanisms. No detection for unexpected administrative changes from low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy modifications, access rule edits, authentication settings changes, or interface reconfigurations performed by low-privilege accounts or accounts accessing FMC outside normal geographic/temporal patterns. Prioritize changes disabling logging, modifying default-deny rules, or creating new administrative accounts.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'poison Adform script'—core attack is unauthorized modification of a third-party ad-serving script deployed across multiple customer sites. Pipeline should detect deviation in file hash, signature verification failure, or unexpected script source origin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to Adform script file hashes, signature verification failures on trusted ad-serving resources, or script sourcing from non-canonical Adform CDN endpoints. Compare hash against known-good repository or vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Address Substitution in Page Content
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites'—detection must key on pattern: legitimate wallet address replaced with attacker-controlled address in HTTP response body or DOM. This is the direct impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze HTTP responses and DOM snapshots for cryptocurrency address anomalies: multiple wallet addresses in a single response, address format mismatches (e.g., checksums invalid), or cluster of similar-looking but distinct addresses within ad injection contexts. Correlate with known-good address baselines per customer.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Script Execution in Ad-Serving Context
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned Adform script executes on victim browsers to perform wallet substitution—requires detection of unexpected JavaScript execution patterns, DOM manipulation, or exfiltration POST requests originating from ad-script sandboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous JavaScript execution timelines: script load followed by rapid DOM writes, POST requests to external domains within milliseconds of ad-script initialization, or suspicious eval() calls from within ad context. Flag if POST payloads contain cryptocurrency wallet patterns or exfiltrated session data.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Compromise—Third-Party Script Source Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Adform is a legitimate third-party service; compromise of its distribution channel or account means poisoned script reaches all customers simultaneously. Detection must track abnormal script sourcing, unsigned updates, or out-of-band CDN changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deviations in third-party ad-script origins: requests to Adform subdomains not in approved CDN list, version mismatches between expected and served script, lack of HTTPS/certificate anomalies, or geographic sourcing shifts. Cross-reference against vendor advisories and integrity manifests.

suggestion.title: Bulk Cryptocurrency Address Enumeration in Network Traffic
suggestion.rationale: If attacker must enumerate or exfiltrate existing wallet addresses before swapping, detection can catch reconnaissance: multiple wallet-format patterns in a single request, batch lookups to blockchain explorers, or high-cardinality address discovery POST requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual cardinality in outbound requests containing cryptocurrency address patterns (regex: ^(0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}|[13][a-km-zA-HJ-NP-Z1-9]{25,34})\b). Correlate with Adform script load events and flag if requests originate from customer endpoints within 30 seconds of script execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Connections from Ad-Injection Context
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned script exfiltrates crypto wallet data or communicates with attacker C2. Detection must isolate network traffic originating from ad-script sandbox and flag C2-like patterns: DNS tunneling, unusual port usage, or countries/ASNs misaligned with ad-serving geography.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate outbound connections from Adform script context by domain and geographic region. Alert on egress to previously unseen domains, non-standard ports, or high-entropy subdomains (DNS-over-HTTPS tunneling). Flag outbound POST requests with size/frequency mismatches to ad-serving baselines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Update Delivery from Non-Vendor Source
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'fake updates' delivered via hijacked Wi-Fi. Pipeline should detect unsigned or attacker-controlled update packages masquerading as legitimate OS/application patches. Article phrase: 'pushes fake updates to deliver surveillance malware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on update processes (WinUpdateAgent, AppInstaller, MSIExec) spawning from non-standard parents or downloading from non-whitelisted CDNs/vendor domains. Flag updates served over HTTP (unencrypted), from private IP ranges, or with mismatched digital signatures.

suggestion.title: Compromised Hotel Wi-Fi SSID Spoofing & MAC Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires hijacking legitimate hotel network infrastructure to distribute payload. Detection must identify spoofed SSIDs and rouge access points mimicking trusted networks. Article: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSID/MAC pair mismatches (same SSID, different MAC across sessions), unexpected BSSIDs in hotel/public Wi-Fi ranges, and clients connecting to networks with known-compromised credentials or infrastructure signatures.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware C2 Beacon & Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malware must communicate outbound to attacker infrastructure and exfiltrate reconnaissance/surveillance data. Pipeline should identify command channels and data staging patterns. Article: 'surveillance malware' implies ongoing collection and transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections to low-reputation IPs from endpoints post-update. Flag traffic patterns consistent with keylogging (small regular transfers) or screen/audio capture (high-volume, continuous streams). Correlate timing with user activity.

suggestion.title: Endpoint Compromise Chain: Hotel Wi-Fi → Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: Guest device compromised at hotel gains access to corporate/home networks via Wi-Fi. Pipeline must track lateral movement from untrusted to trusted network segments. Implicit in attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag endpoints transitioning from hotel/public Wi-Fi to corporate networks within hours of suspicious update receipt. Monitor for SMB reconnaissance, ARP floods, or NetBIOS enumeration from recently-compromised devices.

suggestion.title: Malicious Update Package File Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake update must be staged, downloaded, and executed on disk. Pipeline should extract malware hash, filename patterns, and file paths used by attacker. No IOCs provided suggests parsing failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious files in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or %SystemRoot%\Temp matching update package naming conventions but with anomalous hash, signer, or metadata. Detect child processes spawned from unusual update binary paths.

suggestion.title: DNS Queries for Attacker-Controlled Update Servers
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates must originate from attacker infrastructure. Initial DNS lookups for update domains are first-stage IOCs. Pipeline extraction should include C2/delivery domain indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries for hostnames resembling update services (updates.*, release.*, patch.*) from devices on hotel/public networks, especially with NXDOMAIN or IP resolution to non-vendor ASNs. Flag rapid CNAME chains or subdomain enumeration.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS JSON payload $pullAll with __proto__ path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'apos.util.set() traverses dot-notation paths without sanitizing __proto__' and uses '$pullAll patch operator'. Attack vector lives in HTTP request body as JSON, not URL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* endpoints with JSON bodies containing both '__proto__' (as a key or path component in dot notation) and '$pullAll' operator. Typical payload shape: {"$pullAll": {"__proto__.isAdmin": [false]}} or similar. Alert if source is an authenticated editor account.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation: Object.prototype pollution side-effects (process-wide property access anomalies)
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'process-wide authorization bypass'—successful pollution contaminates Object.prototype globally. Should detect downstream behavioral changes: error messages changing, permission checks returning unexpected values, all requests from same process exhibiting same bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a confirmed __proto__ PATCH exploitation, correlate that response status (e.g., 200) with immediate subsequent application-level errors, permission-check bypasses, or unusual property access patterns in the node.js process. Look for a 'permission denied' error disappearing after PATCH, or auth-required endpoints suddenly returning 200 to multiple users from the same process.

suggestion.title: Authenticated editor account with atypical API call volume and endpoint diversity post-pollution
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must authenticate as editor first (article: 'authenticated editor'), then pollutes Object.prototype to access protected endpoints. Should detect editor accounts that suddenly access endpoints outside their normal role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the API call patterns per editor account (endpoint types, frequency, methods). Alert when a single authenticated editor's session exhibits a spike in requests to global/admin-tier endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/@apostrophecms/user, /api/v1/@apostrophecms/global) following a PATCH to utility endpoints.

suggestion.title: Authentication context lost: successful API requests missing Authorization header or token post-PATCH
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation succeeds because Object.prototype is poisoned process-wide. Subsequent requests may omit Authorization headers or present invalid tokens that are now accepted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/global or other protected endpoints that return 200 but lack Authorization header, contain expired/invalid tokens, or originate from an unauthenticated context (no session cookie). Correlate these with a prior PATCH mutation attempt on the source.

suggestion.title: Constructor.prototype manipulation via PATCH operator ($set or $pullAll on constructor properties)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'constructor.prototype' as an alternative pollution vector. UC_6_2 mentions it but doesn't isolate it. Variant paths like '__proto__' vs 'constructor.prototype' should have distinct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* with JSON payloads containing 'constructor' and 'prototype' in the same path (e.g., 'constructor.prototype.isAdmin'). Treat with same severity as __proto__ variants.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-53609 patch indicator: successful PATCH responses (200, 204) on utility endpoints from editor accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states this requires editor authentication and a PATCH request. High-fidelity signal: PATCH to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* + successful response status + editor-role source = likely exploitation attempt or testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PATCH requests to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* endpoints returning 200 or 204 from editor-authenticated accounts, especially if the PATCH modifies global or core objects. Alert if patch frequency is high (>10 per minute per source) or targets known pollution vectors.

suggestion.title: Captive Portal Exploitation - Suspicious WiFi SSID & Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'CaptiveCrunch' and targets travelers; campaign exploits captive portals on public WiFi. Article keywords include AiTM, suggesting fake portals redirect users to malicious login pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious captive portal redirects by monitoring DNS queries for legitimate WiFi SSIDs resolving to anomalous IPs, or HTTP 302 redirects to non-standard authentication domains during airport/hotel WiFi connections. Flag when Windows devices attempt CAPTIVE_PORTAL_TEST connections that redirect to non-Microsoft URLs.

suggestion.title: AiTM Proxy Detection - Traffic Interception
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)'; campaign uses captive portals to position proxy infrastructure between users and legitimate services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AiTM proxies by identifying proxy certificate mismatches for HTTPS traffic to cloud services (O365, AWS, GCP), unusual proxy.pac downloads from captive portal IPs, or process injection into browser processes. Monitor for mitmproxy, Squid, or Tinyproxy spawned from WiFi auto-connect scripts.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering - Malware Download via Fake Error
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords mention 'ClickFix' social engineering technique; Midnight Blizzard uses fake system error popups on captive portal pages to trick travelers into downloading malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix payloads by monitoring for .exe, .msi, or .scr downloads initiated from captive portal domains with file names mimicking Windows system tools (WindowsUpdate.exe, SystemCheck.exe, SecurityAlert.exe). Correlate with browser process spawning child processes immediately post-download.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Portal Login
suggestion.rationale: Title and keywords explicitly mention 'credential theft'; AiTM-positioned captive portal presents fake login pages for email, cloud storage, and VPN services targeting travelers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential harvesting by correlating: (1) HTTP POST submissions to captive portal domains containing email/password patterns, (2) immediate failed logons to O365/AWS/corporate VPN from the same device IP within 60 seconds, (3) credential manager access via browser memory dumps or LSASS injection post-logon from WiFi.

suggestion.title: Token Theft & Session Hijacking Post-Portal Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'Token theft'; AiTM captures OAuth tokens and session cookies during HTTPS interception through captive portal proxy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect token theft by monitoring for: (1) logons to cloud services (O365, AWS, GCP) from travel WiFi IP with mismatched user-agent or geolocation vs. normal patterns, (2) token refresh anomalies (unusual token age, device ID changes, impossible travel), (3) cloud app access (email export, admin actions) immediately post-portal exposure without MFA acceptance.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution Post-ClickFix on Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Windows systems; 'malware delivery' keyword and execution context suggest malware persistence and C2 beaconing from infected machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect post-ClickFix malware by monitoring for: (1) process launches from %TEMP%, %AppData% with names mimicking Windows updates, (2) registry run-key modifications (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run), (3) scheduled task creation by explorer.exe or svchost.exe child processes, (4) DLL injection into system processes 60–300 seconds after suspicious .exe download.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication with Hard-Coded or Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'—direct exploitation of embedded credentials. Detection must monitor FMC authentication logs for known default/hard-coded account names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts using hard-coded service account names from external/unauthenticated sources. Baseline legitimate admin IPs; alert on anomalous geolocations or failed-then-successful patterns indicating credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Remote, Unauthenticated Connection to FMC Management Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack is 'unauthenticated, remote'—defenders should detect connection attempts to FMC management services (typically TCP 443, 8305) from external networks, especially from internet-routable IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to FMC management ports from external/untrusted networks. Flag where successful authentication follows, particularly if source IP has no historical access pattern or resides outside organization's trusted admin ranges.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access or Bulk Configuration Export from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—once authenticated, detect bulk data reads, policy/rule exports, or queries targeting security configurations stored in FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API calls post-authentication for bulk exports of policies, threat rules, credential objects, or managed device inventories. Alert on large data transfers or archive creation (e.g., tar, zip) containing security policies post-compromise.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection and Patch Gap Analysis
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates federal patch compliance by 2026-08-01. Defenders must identify unpatched FMC instances before exploitation. Article describes active wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for FMC appliances running vulnerable firmware versions (< patched build). Cross-reference with patch management and asset inventory; prioritize internet-facing instances. Track patch lag from publication date (2026-07-29) to remediation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Low-Privileged to Admin Role Within FMC

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Security Devices

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Access — Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' establishes FMC is publicly accessible on management ports. Standard asset-exposure hunting baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to Cisco FMC Using Default / Low-Privileged Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability' and 'log in using a low-privileged account' indicates credential-based compromise vector. FMC audit logs should capture authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan and Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article lists federal patch-due date of 2026-08-01 and identifies CVE as active CISA KEV. Compliance scanning should enumerate all Cisco FMC instances and flag vulnerability status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20316 matches in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. Prioritize findings on internet-exposed instances. Escalate any vulnerable instance past 2026-08-01 as regulatory non-compliance.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access Within Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-login. FMC audit logs should surface unusual data reads, policy exports, or sensitive-object access outside baseline patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for anomalous reads of firewall policies, rules, access control lists, or threat-intel configuration by low-privileged accounts or from unusual source IPs. Alert on bulk exports or off-hours access to sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Persistence via FMC Admin Account Creation or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise via hardcoded password, attacker may escalate or create backdoor accounts to maintain access. FMC configuration audit logs should flag unauthorized admin account modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new admin accounts in FMC outside change-management windows. Flag privilege escalations of low-privileged users. Monitor for disabling/tampering with audit logging or syslog forwarding.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access affected device — requires baseline inventory of FMC systems exposed to untrusted networks. No exposure hunt generated.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Brute-Force / Known-Bad Logins
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability... allow[s] an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' — no detection use case for authentication attempts using default/hardcoded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for repeated login attempts using known default/hardcoded account names (admin, root, etc.). Flag successful logins from non-administrative source IPs or geographic anomalies. Baseline expected admin login patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unexpected Administrative Access & Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data' — pipeline did not surface detection for lateral escalation or abuse of low-privileged accounts to exfiltrate data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation within FMC after initial compromise — monitor for low-privilege accounts executing high-privilege operations, config exports, or accessing restricted data repositories. Look for sudoers or role-elevation events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — no data exfiltration detection use case defined. Should monitor for bulk exports, API calls for policy/credential extraction, or unusual data transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers from Cisco FMC (policy exports, configuration backups, device lists). Flag API calls to /api/fmc_config endpoints with unusual volume or scope. Detect compression/archiving of config files before transfer.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration & Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article implies access to 'sensitive data' and administrative functions — no detection for unauthorized config changes, firewall rule modifications, or policy disablement that could enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized changes to FMC policies, firewall rules, or logging settings. Monitor for rules that disable alerts, whitelist attacker IPs, or weaken access controls. Correlate with non-standard login context.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Management Interface Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Foundational detection for KEV with remote exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco FMC management interfaces (typically TCP 443, 8305) exposed to untrusted networks. Cross-correlate internal asset inventory against external port scan data. Any internet-facing FMC is critical priority for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Authentication: Hard-coded Default Account Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hard-coded password vulnerability...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using implicit default credentials. Exploit pattern must be detectable via credential attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful login to Cisco FMC from external IP ranges using default/low-privileged account names. Alert on failed+successful authentication sequences (credential stuffing). Baseline: FMC logins should originate only from designated admin networks.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detection must capture data staging and bulk export post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post successful FMC login, detect bulk configuration/policy exports, log downloads, or credential dumps. Detect FMC initiating outbound connections to external IPs carrying sensitive payloads. Volume anomalies: FMC should not export data externally under normal operations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Affected Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly states CVE-2026-20316 with federal patch due 2026-08-01. Vulnerability scanner is authoritative method for detecting exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tools for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) matching affected versions for CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference results with network exposure data. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Track remediation against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Behavioral: Management Interface Access from Atypical Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password allows 'low-privileged account' access; behavioral baseline violation after credential compromise surfaces exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for FMC management interface access: permitted source networks, permitted accounts, permitted hours. Alert on: login outside business hours, login from non-admin subnets, concurrent sessions from disparate IPs, rapid configuration changes post-login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC (ports 8305, 8309) using known low-privileged or default account credentials from external/untrusted source IP ranges. Baseline normal administrative access and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after initial compromise. Must detect lateral movement or data theft following hard-coded password authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormal queries or exports of sensitive objects (firewall rules, VPN credentials, threat intelligence feeds) from newly authenticated low-privileged FMC accounts. Monitor for mass data retrieval anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Coverage
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation implies active exploitation in the wild. Primary detection mechanism is vulnerability scanner alerting on unpatched FMC instances by CVE identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any CVE-2026-20316 detections in vulnerability scan results for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. Correlate with network exposure scanning (HTTPS ports 8305, 8307, 8309) and prioritize by asset criticality.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface External Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—FMC management interface must be externally reachable. Network detection catches exposed management ports before credential exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound traffic to Cisco FMC standard management ports (TCP 8305, 8309) from untrusted external networks. Alert on first-contact to these ports from new source IPs; baseline internal administrative access.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Attack Pattern - FMC Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability implies attacker knows or guesses valid low-privileged account names. Detect enumeration or brute-force attempts targeting FMC user accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated failed login attempts to FMC using common default/low-privileged account names (e.g., 'serviceaccount', 'readonly', 'audit'). Track velocity of failed attempts from single or small IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Successful authentication to Cisco FMC from unexpected sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated no detection for successful auth events post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected IP ranges, geographies, or source types. Hard-coded credential exploitation typically manifests as auth attempts from non-approved management subnets or external IPs, followed by rapid queries to sensitive configuration stores.

suggestion.title: Brute-force attempts against Cisco FMC management interface
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential vulnerabilities are often attacked via credential stuffing or brute-force discovery of accounts; article describes remote, unauthenticated access pattern suggesting repeated attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of failed authentication attempts against FMC ports (typically 443/8305 for management) followed by successful access. Threshold: >5 failed attempts per source IP within 5 minutes, then successful auth.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized data access within Cisco FMC post-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems' after gaining low-privileged account access; pipeline suggested no monitoring for data exfiltration or unusual queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to FMC, monitor for unusual data queries or exports: access to security policies, threat intelligence feeds, device configurations, or credential stores not typical for low-privileged users.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 scanner detection and asset inventory correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active scanning and exploitation; pipeline must surface asset-exposure queries correlating scanner results against network telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset flagged as CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable in scanners. Cross-correlate with network telemetry for inbound connection attempts to those assets on FMC ports, regardless of patch status (patch lag is common).

suggestion.title: FMC management interface access from non-US geographies (federal context)
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV with federal compliance context and 2026-08-01 patch deadline; federal networks should restrict FMC access geographically. No geo-fence detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FMC management console access from IP addresses geolocalizing outside expected regions (US for federal systems). Prioritize overnight or off-hours access from foreign IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from compromised FMC to protected networks
suggestion.rationale: FMC typically manages downstream firewalls and security infrastructure; post-exploitation lateral movement is the likely attack objective. Article does not address downstream impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for command issuance to managed firewalls (policy pushes, rule modifications, device reboots) initiated from newly-authenticated low-privilege accounts or from non-administrative console IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access exposed FMC. Source explicitly references asset-exposure hunt template. Detection of FMC instances (port 8305, SSL cert fingerprinting) is the first hunt layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound HTTPS traffic to port 8305 or SSH (port 22) destined for Cisco FMC hosts. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center' assets. Correlate with asset inventory to identify undocumented or internet-exposed FMC instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling login with 'low-privileged account'. Successful authentication using embedded credentials is the compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful SSH or HTTPS API authentication to FMC (port 8305, SSH port 22) where the source IP is external/non-corporate or the login occurs outside normal business hours. Monitor /var/log/auth.log and FMC audit logs for successful logins immediately preceded by multiple failed attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise FMC Configuration & Policy Querying
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'. After credential compromise, attacker will enumerate policies, network objects, and stored credentials from FMC API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API logs for high-volume queries to policy endpoints (e.g., /api/fmc/v1/*/policy/*) or credential/object retrieval endpoints within 5 minutes of a successful authentication event from a suspicious source. Flag any API query returning > 100 policies or configuration objects.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FMC Vulnerability Confirmation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Nessus/Qualys/Tenable for CVE-2026-20316 findings. Cross-reference with FMC version inventory (retrieved via SNMP or API interrogation). Alert if any FMC version is below patched baseline (vendor will release patch before due date). Include patch-release date and deadline in alert.

suggestion.title: FMC Internet Exposure Risk Assessment

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search firewall logs for inbound connections to FMC management ports (8305, 22) originating from public IPv4 space or unknown external networks. Query cloud-security tools (GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud) for 'public IP exposure' alerts on Cisco security appliances. Confirm all FMC deployments are internal/VPN-only per network architecture.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed Instance Detection (CVE-2026-20316)

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'use of hard-coded password' as the attack vector. Attackers authenticate using known default accounts to gain initial access.

suggestion.title: Privileged Data Access via Low-Privileged Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'access sensitive data' via 'low-privileged account'—post-auth data exfiltration or privilege escalation within FMC. Detect unusual data exports or configuration reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy/rule/config exports, bulk data reads, or configuration backups initiated from newly-compromised low-privilege sessions or external-origin FMC API calls. Flag batch file operations on sensitive FMC directories (credential stores, certificate folders).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Credential/Certificate Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management plane asset; stolen admin credentials or PKI material enables lateral movement to managed firewalls and devices. Detect file/memory access targeting credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for read/copy operations on FMC SSH key stores, API token files, managed-device credentials, or PEM/PKI files. Alert on compression or staging of credential files or config.xml access by low-privilege or external-origin sessions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised FMC Management Plane
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC enables commands to downstream firewalls/devices. Detect anomalous API calls or managed-device configuration changes issued from post-compromise session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC API calls or device management commands (policy push, rule adds, device reboot) from external-origin sessions, low-privilege accounts, or outside change-management windows. Cross-reference device access logs on firewalls to detect spread.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Session Anomaly - External IP Access to Sensitive Functions
suggestion.rationale: Baseline FMC access is typically internal/VPN; external authentication plus sensitive data/policy access is anomalous. Detect deviation from expected access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline FMC access by source IP/country/time-of-day. Alert on successful authentication from external/foreign IPs, especially combined with subsequent policy queries, data exports, or API access. Priority: IPs geolocated to high-risk regions or marked as known scanner/eCrime infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Inventory and Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all network devices and security appliances for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center / Firepower Management Center product instances. suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Login Attempts to FMC

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful login attempts using low-privileged hard-coded accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'support', vendor-documented default usernames). Alert on any successful authentication to FMC management interface from external/unexpected IP ranges or out-of-business-hours access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from FMC

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC logs for unusual data queries, bulk configuration exports, or policy downloads initiated by low-privileged accounts. Alert on any data dump, report generation, or sensitive setting access by accounts that should not have those permissions.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Network Exposure Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing IP ranges for open Cisco FMC management ports (8305, 8307, or 443/SSH if exposed). Cross-reference against approved external access list. Any open FMC management port from the internet is a critical finding and immediate remediation trigger.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Verification

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) from external networks or anomalous source IPs using low-privileged built-in accounts during non-business hours. Hard-coded credential exploitation is typically external-origin and rapid.

suggestion.title: FMC Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker gains 'low-privileged account' then 'access sensitive data'—implies privilege escalation within FMC post-initial-access. No detection suggested.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Data Export

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect policy export, configuration backup, or mass rule download initiated by non-admin or recently-compromised accounts. Cisco FMC logs these as export operations—flag unusual timing, large payloads, or anomalous account source.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Inventory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally-reachable Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (TCP 443, Cisco FMC web interface signatures). Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-20316. Any unpatched, internet-routable FMC is immediately exploitable.

suggestion.title: FMC Account Enumeration

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire failed authentication attempts or repeated API calls to Cisco FMC user/role enumeration endpoints originating from single compromised account. Enumeration queries typically spike within minutes of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Attempts Against Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts against known default/hard-coded FMC accounts are the primary exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for failed login attempts against low-privileged or system-default account names within short time windows. suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—this implies FMC management interface (typically TCP 8305, 443) is internet-routable. Detection must identify exposed asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC management ports (8305, 443) reachable from external networks. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 affected versions. Alert on any FMC asset accessible without VPN/firewall segmentation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Administrative Configuration Changes Post-Login

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC configuration change audit logs for administrative actions (user creation, rule modification, policy changes) initiated from non-standard admin accounts or following authentication events from external IPs. Baseline normal change windows.

suggestion.title: Successful FMC Logins from Anomalous Network Sources

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate FMC admin login sources (corporate IPs, VPN gateways). Flag successful authentications from external/untrusted IPs, particularly to low-privileged accounts. Correlate with failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Scan Findings
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV due-date context ('Federal patch due: 2026-08-01') indicates urgency; pipeline should trigger vulnerability scanner correlation for affected Cisco FMC versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 positives. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify unpatched Cisco FMC instances. Alert on any findings older than vendor patch release date or federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-FMC Compromise

Track access to network segmentation rules, managed device lists, or data-plane traffic inspection logs. Alert on FMC accessing internal systems outside normal SNMP/syslog polling patterns.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Web API Command Injection Attempt
