suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Unexpected Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploits result in OS command execution; pipeline provided no detection for abnormal process spawning from web application contexts or system services running commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is a web service (tomcat.exe, java.exe, nginx.exe, httpd) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh. VeloCloud Orchestrator should not legitimately execute OS shells from web contexts.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of appliances typically enables backdoor installation or direct C2 communication; no detection use cases for anomalous outbound connections from Orchestrator appliances to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from VeloCloud Orchestrator appliance to non-whitelisted external IP addresses or domains on non-standard ports. Correlate with command execution indicators. Baseline known legitimate destinations and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Credential Harvesting or Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Command injection enabling system-level access typically leads to credential theft or backdoor installation; article topic implies post-exploitation activity, but no detection for file access to credential stores or registry modifications was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file access to VeloCloud credential or configuration files (e.g., in /opt/vcg or Windows AppData equivalents), unusual registry modifications, or scheduled task/cron job creation from web service processes initiated via command injection.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection likely requires moving from web service privilege to system/root; pipeline provided no detection for privilege escalation patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or token impersonation where a lower-privileged web service process (vcg, tomcat user) spawns or injects into processes running as SYSTEM, root, or vcg admin accounts. Flag use of exploit techniques like DLL injection or process hollowing.

suggestion.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator Configuration Changes from Suspicious Source
suggestion.rationale: Command-injected attacker will likely modify appliance configuration to maintain access or redirect traffic; no use cases for detecting unauthorized configuration or network policy changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VeloCloud Orchestrator configuration files and databases for modifications triggered by process execution from web contexts or non-admin user accounts. Flag changes to edge device policies, routing rules, or authentication configurations made outside normal change management windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' This is the core attack path; pipeline generated no detection for credential abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded or default credentials. Flag unexpected low-privileged account access from untrusted networks. Correlate with unpatched CVE-2026-20316 instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'remote attacker' and 'public-facing application,' implying external scanning for vulnerable FMC instances. Pipeline omitted discovery-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify external hosts probing known Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, etc.) or performing service-identification scans. Correlate with known-vulnerable versions to flag exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline failed to surface collection-phase detection for policy, credential, or configuration theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk exports of security policies, credential-repository downloads, or large file transfers from FMC by authenticated low-privileged or unexpected accounts. Track configuration backups requested immediately after successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exploitation Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation. Article provides no exploit-specific signatures, but pipeline should have offered behavioral indicators for successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of failed authentication attempts followed by successful low-privileged login and immediate sensitive-data access. Flag malformed HTTP requests or known exploit-framework payloads targeting FMC management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Status Inventory and Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch deadline (2026-08-01) and CISA mandate. Pipeline omitted asset-inventory detection to track FMC deployment and patch gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, CMDB, and network inventory for all Cisco FMC instances, their versions, and patch status for CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize unpatched or version-unknown instances for immediate remediation before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default Account Brute-Force Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password exploitability often involves default credentials. Article does not rule out brute-force as a complementary attack path; pipeline missed this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC using known default account names (admin, operator, etc.) or from non-administrative source networks. Correlate with exploit-framework C2 or scanner signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-20316 in Vulnerability Scans and Patch Reports
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Active exploitation confirmed; must surface in all asset scans immediately regardless of scanner patch-status claims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert whenever CVE-2026-20316 appears in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances across vulnerability reports. CISA KEV status mandates empirical confirmation of patch application; scanner silence is not clearance.

suggestion.title: Monitor Unauthenticated or Low-Privilege Login to FMC Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Direct statement of attack vector; pipeline must detect this authentication anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful FMC logins preceded by no authentication initiation, or rapid failed-then-successful login cycles indicating credential stuffing with hardcoded account. Baseline normal admin authentication patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Sensitive Data Access and Export from FMC Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Kill-chain gap: once attacker authenticates, they must exfiltrate or manipulate. Monitor data egress post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious FMC login with abnormal data transfers (configuration exports, policy downloads, bulk API queries). Establish baseline data-access volume per admin user; alert on >3σ deviations.

suggestion.title: Monitor Unauthorized FMC Configuration and Firewall Rule Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation data access; attacker holding FMC access may persist by modifying managed firewall policies to enable lateral movement or disable logging. No explicit mention, but intrinsic to FMC compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any configuration change to Cisco FMC or its managed firewall devices within 24 hours post-suspicious authentication. Cross-reference account performing change with baseline admin profiles.

suggestion.title: Correlate FMC Compromise with Downstream Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC grants attacker network architecture visibility and firewall-bypass intelligence. Article: 'access sensitive data' could enable operational planning for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish correlation: if FMC compromise indicators fire (suspicious auth + data access), elevate alerting on managed firewall/router logs for new outbound connections, port scans, or DNS queries to rare/external domains.

suggestion.title: Surface Hardcoded Credential Usage in Cisco FMC Instances
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'use of hard-coded password.' If Cisco publishes specific credential format or username for CVE-2026-20316, pipeline must flag any matching authentication attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain rule feed for Cisco security advisories; on CVE-2026-20316 advisory release, extract hardcoded credential patterns (username/account format) and immediately deploy detection rule to flag any login attempt using that pattern across all FMC instances.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt'. Attacker must reach exposed FMC instance (ports 8305, 8307); no detection logic generated for this prerequisite access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances listening on external-facing interfaces or non-management network segments. Flag exposed web UI (port 8305) and API (8307) services. Correlate with vuln-scan results for CVE-2026-20316 presence.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Hardcoded Password Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in…using a low-privileged account'. Hardcoded password represents credential-stuffing / default-account attack vector. No auth-abuse detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts from external IPs followed by successful low-privilege account access. Baseline legitimate administrative access; alert on authentication patterns deviating from known admin network ranges or time-of-day.

suggestion.title: Collection: Post-Authentication Data Access Within Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication. No detection for suspicious data queries, policy exports, or config downloads after credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC authentication, detect bulk policy queries, security-policy exports, network-object enumeration, or sensitive configuration downloads. Flag unusual database access patterns from low-privilege accounts or from non-administrative source IPs within minutes of successful auth.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Assessment: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Match and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV context ('currently being exploited'), federal patch-due date (2026-08-01), and recommends asset-exposure hunt with CVE substitution. No vulnerability-matching detection generated despite explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 presence in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center assets. Flag all unpatched instances. Cross-reference scan dates against federal due-date (2026-08-01) to identify patch-lag compliance risks. Prioritize remediation for internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Network Discovery: Port Scanning for Cisco FMC Service Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires attacker to discover exposed FMC instance. Article establishes remote access vector; reconnaissance must precede exploitation. No network-scanning or service-discovery detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect systematic port scanning of Cisco FMC service ports (8305 HTTP, 8307 REST API, 22 SSH) from external sources. Flag sequential probes across IP ranges, especially patterns indicating automated vuln scanning. Correlate reconnaissance activity with subsequent authentication attempts against discovered FMC services.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' — implies exposed management interface. Must hunt for FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally accessible Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center ports (443, 8305) via Shodan, port scanners, or vulnerability scanners. Correlate with your network topology to identify FMC instances exposed to the Internet or untrusted networks. Any asset tagged 'Cisco FMC' or running FMC software should be restricted to management-only subnets.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'use of hard-coded password'—pipeline must detect when these known credentials are used. Article explicitly states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for successful authentication events using known hard-coded account names (e.g., 'admin', 'operator', or vendor-documented defaults). Flag any successful login from non-standard IP ranges. Cross-reference with baseline 'expected' FMC administrators to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Authentication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' gaining access—detect brute-force, password-spray, or unusual access patterns against FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high velocity failed authentication attempts (>5 failed logins within 5 minutes) against FMC ports 443/8305. Track successful logins from unexpected geographic locations, non-admin VLANs, or external IP ranges. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 scanner signals to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Patterns in FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detect abnormal data query/export activity post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for unusual report generation, configuration exports, or data queries initiated by low-privileged accounts. Flag bulk downloads of security events, policy configurations, or threat logs that deviate from baseline admin behavior. Alert on outbound data transfer from FMC to external hosts.

suggestion.title: FMC Privilege Escalation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies initial access is via 'low-privileged account'—attacker will likely attempt escalation to admin. Detect post-exploitation privilege escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to modify user roles, create new administrative accounts, or elevate privileges within FMC from non-admin sessions. Monitor for execution of high-privilege functions (policy deployment, system configuration changes) initiated by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Network Service Discovery and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must first discover and enumerate exposed FMC instances before exploitation. Article implies reconnaissance phase prior to credential exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration probes targeting FMC management ports (443, 8305, 22) from external sources. Flag host discovery patterns or multiple failed connection attempts to known FMC IP ranges. Correlate with Shodan/vulnerability scanner queries for 'Cisco Secure Firewall' or 'Firepower Management Center.'

suggestion.title: GitHub release tag reassignment to orphaned commits
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit'—this tag-to-orphan reassignment is the attack's obfuscation mechanism and a high-fidelity supply chain attack signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect release tags (semantic version patterns like v\d+\.\d+\.\d+) being moved to commits not on main/master branches, especially commits with zero parent references (orphaned) or unusual timestamps relative to tag creation date. Alert on tag deletion followed by recreation within short window.

suggestion.title: Plaintext secrets exposed in GitHub Actions logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the actual exfiltration mechanism and detection should key on secret format patterns leaked to unencrypted stdout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching secret format (AWS key patterns, GitHub PAT prefixes, API key structures, private keys, tokens). Correlate presence of plaintext secret in run logs with GitHub secret environment variable presence for that repository.

suggestion.title: Outbound network calls from GitHub Actions to external C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External domain fetch from Actions workflow is the payload delivery mechanism.
log_sources: VPC Flow Logs for Actions runners
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions workflow runs to external domains not in allow-list. Flag domains contacted by changed-files or other dependency-tracking actions that deviate from expected GitHub/git-hosting infrastructure. Correlate with run timing and action version changes.

suggestion.title: Write privilege granted to transitive supply-chain repository
suggestion.rationale: Article foundation: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Detection should target privileged access to high-dependency OSS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new write-level access grants to repositories with high dependent-repo count (e.g., >1,000 external consumers detected via GitHub dependency graph). Monitor for unusual collaborator additions to popular Actions repositories. Correlate with subsequent commit activity from new collaborator within days.

suggestion.title: Multiple release version tags pointing to same non-release commit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker moving v35 and 'several existing release tags' to the orphaned malicious commit, creating a many-to-one tag-to-commit mapping that violates semantic versioning expectations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple distinct semantic version tags (v1.0.0, v1.5.0, v2.0.0) all pointing to the same commit SHA. This violates release tag semantics; normal operation has one commit per version. Also flag version tags pointing to commits younger than tag creation timestamp (time-travel artifact).

suggestion.title: GitHub workflow action reference validation mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explains developers assume tag immutability: 'If we're told to use v35 of a particular release, we reference that tag and assume that's what we'll be getting' but tags are mutable pointers, enabling bait-and-switch. Detection should catch when referenced tag commit deviates from expected release artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During workflow-run events, compare the action version reference (e.g., @v35) against the actual commit SHA executed. If the SHA differs from historical baseline for that tag, or if the action name + tag combo has not been seen in organization before, raise detection. Alert if tag points to commit authored by non-maintainer accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Remote Authentication via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'. Core exploitation surface is authentication abuse via known/default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) for authentication attempts from external/untrusted sources. Alert on successful logins using low-privileged or default account patterns, especially preceded by multiple failed attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Once authenticated via hard-coded credentials, attacker harvests firewall configurations, policies, and device inventories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC login, detect bulk exports or large data reads of firewall policies, device configurations, credential storage, or administrative settings. Flag low-privileged or unusual accounts accessing sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Post-Compromise Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC directly controls downstream Cisco firewall infrastructure. Attacker can alter rules, policies, or device registrations for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized changes to firewall policies, device management rules, or administrative account creation within FMC following anomalous authentication events.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article presupposes FMC is network-reachable by remote attackers. Prevent/detect direct internet exposure of Cisco FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous validation: Cisco FMC instances must NOT be directly reachable from untrusted internet ranges. Perform external scans (port 443, 8305) and alert on any successful inbound connections from public IP blocks to FMC.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Compromised FMC to Managed Firewall Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC compromise enables pivot to managed Cisco firewalls. Article's 'sensitive data' surface includes downstream device state and policy, implying active lateral movement capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC-to-managed-device traffic (SSH/HTTPS) for anomalies: bulk device queries, unexpected policy deployments, unauthorized credential access, or exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' No detection for authentication abuse with default creds against FMC ports (typically 8305/TCP, 443/TCP).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed → successful authentication sequences on Cisco FMC management interfaces. Monitor for authentication events using hardcoded account names (if disclosed by vendor) or brute-force patterns against TCP 8305. Correlate with source IP reputation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure — CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies public-facing asset. Template reference suggests asset-exposure hunt; no SPL/KQL generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network discovery (shodan, censys) and internal asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances with public ingress. Match against vulnerability scanner confirming CVE-2026-20316 presence and verify patch status.

suggestion.title: Post-FMC Compromise — Sensitive Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Hard-coded password compromises FMC's full configuration database. No detection for unusual config queries or bulk exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC (and underlying PostgreSQL) audit logs for bulk SELECT queries on credential tables, policy tables, or device inventory. Alert on API calls exporting firewall rulesets, VPN configs, or device status outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege FMC Account Lateral Movement to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article: hard-coded password grants access to low-privilege account with 'access to sensitive data.' FMC typically orchestrates downstream firewalls; no detection for lateral movement via FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/HTTPS connections from FMC host (post-compromise) to managed firewall appliances using service accounts or unusual privilege levels. Alert on config pushes or policy changes issued by low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC API Authentication via Default Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article implies API/SSH access via hard-coded password. FMC exposes REST API on port 8305; no detection for /api/auth or token-generation endpoints with default auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query web access logs for POST to /api/fmc_platform/v1/auth/generatetoken or /api/*/login with 401 → 200 transitions. Correlate repeated 401s from same source with successful login (200) within 60 seconds, indicating brute-force then compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—requires detection of authentication attempts using default/hard-coded credentials, particularly failed attempts preceding successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC admin interface for failed login attempts using known default account names (admin, cisco, etc.), especially failed-then-successful patterns from the same source IP within short timeframe, or successful logins from unexpected external networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Public Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires network-accessible FMC; article implicitly references T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' as the entry vector for remote unauthenticated attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305, 8307) from external/untrusted IP space. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to identify reconnaissance or brute-force activity against exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Sensitive Data Collection on FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—collection phase activity following credential compromise must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual access patterns to Cisco FMC policy databases, credential vaults, threat intelligence repositories, or device configuration files following successful authentication events, especially from newly-authenticated or low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Successful Authentication from Anomalous Source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote attacker' successful login; any authentication from outside expected administrative networks indicates potential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Cisco FMC administrative console logins from IP ranges outside documented trusted administrative infrastructure, residential/proxy IP space, or unfamiliar geographic locations inconsistent with deployment baseline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Detection — Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' CVE-2026-20316 is the primary observable indicator. Pipeline should generate use case for scanner alerts flagging this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings (Qualys, Tenable, Nessus, OpenVAS) reporting CVE-2026-20316 against Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference scanner output with asset inventory to identify exposed FMC appliances.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploits 'public-facing application' (T1190). Implies FMC should not be internet-accessible. Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances (default management ports 443, 8305) responding to internet-routed traffic. Monitor for inbound SYN/HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FMC from untrusted networks. Cross-reference firewall policies and network exposure scans against CMDB.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: hard-coded password vulnerability enables 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' login. Credential brute-force or known-credential exploitation would precede successful access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts from external IPs. Alert on authentication spikes or attempts targeting known hard-coded account names (admin, root, etc.) from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Successful Remote Access to Cisco FMC from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'log in to an affected device' — successful authentication from internet-routable source IP. First indicator of compromise post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to FMC management interface (SSH, HTTPS) from external or untrusted networks, especially if preceded by failed attempts or from IPs with no historical access pattern.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to FMC Sensitive Data and Configurations
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect data access anomalies post-authentication from low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for low-privileged user accounts exporting, viewing, or querying firewall policies, threat rules, or system configurations. Flag unusual API calls, policy downloads, or configuration dumps from newly-compromised sessions.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage in Cisco FMC Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' as direct attack vector. If credential is publicly disclosed, detect its use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If hard-coded credential is disclosed, create detection for HTTP Basic Auth headers or SSH login attempts using that specific username/password combination from external sources. Monitor for programmatic API access patterns inconsistent with legitimate admin workflows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Direct IOC for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface for successful authentication events using default or hard-coded account credentials (common defaults: admin/admin, cisco/cisco). Correlate with source IP reputation and geographic anomalies. Alert on successful remote login followed by immediate sensitive data queries.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthenticated Management Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' explicitly indicates bypass of auth layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco FMC management endpoints (port 443, /admin, /api/fmc) that yield successful responses without prior authentication handshake or token exchange. Flag attempts to access /api/fmc or dashboard endpoints without valid session cookies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Describes post-compromise data collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-scale data queries, policy exports, or configuration dumps from FMC via low-privileged accounts. Alert on API calls to /api/fmc/config, /api/fmc/policy endpoints that export firewall rules, access controls, or credentials. Pair with volumetric egress checks on FMC source IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active exploitation. Article describes credential stuffing / default credential attack against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect and alert on any Cisco FMC listening on internet-facing ports (443) receiving login attempts. Specifically, trigger on 3+ failed auth events from single IP in 5-minute window, followed by successful login using default credentials or within 5 minutes of prior failures. Cross-reference source IPs against known exploit scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Low-Privilege Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'using a low-privileged account to access sensitive data' — unusual privilege levels for sensitive operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for low-privilege user accounts performing high-privilege operations (policy changes, credential access, config export, security policy modification). Establish baseline of low-privilege user activities and alert on deviation. Flag data access requests from accounts that historically only perform read-only queries.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Ad Script Content Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'poison Adform script'—attackers injected malicious code into shared ad-platform JavaScript. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline content hashes for Adform ad-delivery scripts from legitimate sources. Alert when HTTP responses from Adform CDN/delivery domains return script payloads with hash mismatches, unexpected size changes, or novel substrings (cryptocurrency addresses, eval/exec patterns, external callback domains not in baseline).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Replacement in Ad Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'swap crypto wallet addresses'—article describes substitution of legitimate payment wallets with attacker-controlled addresses. No detection hypothesis was synthesized for this payload-level tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP response bodies from known ad-serving domains. Apply regex patterns to identify cryptocurrency addresses (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Monero). Alert on: sudden introduction of wallet addresses absent from historical baseline, multiple distinct addresses from single domain in short timeframe, or addresses matching known attacker-controlled wallets from external feeds.

suggestion.title: Cross-Customer Script Divergence—Supply Chain Poisoning Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Attack affected 'multiple customer sites', indicating attacker compromised centralized distribution point (Adform). No detection logic exists for identifying divergent script payloads delivered simultaneously to different customers from same source URL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate script content hashes downloaded by different customer endpoints from Adform's delivery domain. Alert when content hashes diverge within a narrow time window (e.g., <1 hour), suggesting targeted poisoning or segmented malicious payload deployment. Monitor subresource integrity (SRI) hash validation failures if SRI headers are present.

suggestion.title: Adform Platform Account Compromise or Unauthorized API Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gained capability to inject malicious scripts at source—likely via account compromise, API token theft, or direct platform vulnerability. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized administrative activity on ad-platform accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adform platform account logins for anomalous IP geolocation, off-hours access, or impossible travel. Alert on unusual API calls modifying script configurations, payload sources, or ad-click URL targets. Cross-reference with external threat intelligence on compromised Adform credentials or leaked API tokens.

suggestion.title: Rogue WiFi Access Point / SSID Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes 'hotel wi-fi hijacked'—the attack vector is network-layer impersonation. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for rogue APs matching known SSID patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple active SSIDs matching hotel/corporate brand names from single MAC OUI, or for WiFi clients connecting to SSIDs at unusual signal strength variance. Detect rapid SSID changes or absence of legitimate network management traffic (DHCP, DNS pointing to registered ISP ranges).

suggestion.title: HTTP/HTTPS Interception Delivering Malicious Update Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake updates' pushed via hijacked WiFi—this is MitM injection of software update traffic. Pipeline omitted detection for update streams sourced from non-canonical servers or unsigned executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of executables from non-standard update sources (not vendor CDN IPs, not HTTPS pinned certs). Flag software update processes spawned by browser or network services. Monitor for unsigned or invalid-signature binaries masquerading as OS/app updates.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'surveillance malware'—implies screen capture, audio recording, or webcam hijacking followed by C2 communication. Pipeline did not model collection + command-and-control phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes opening audio/video device handles (snd_pcm_open, webcam device nodes) or reading screen framebuffers. Correlate with unusual egress traffic to private IP ranges or non-standard ports. Flag beaconing patterns to C2 infrastructure not associated with legitimate cloud services.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Invalid-Signed Software Update Installation
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates imply stripped or forged digital signatures. Pipeline should have flagged update processes that bypass signature verification or install from environments without certificate pinning validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installer/update processes that do not validate publisher certificates or that execute with ERRORLEVEL bypass flags. Detect installation of executables with zero or unknown digital signatures in update directories. Correlate update checks routed through proxy/WiFi gateway.

suggestion.title: WiFi Traffic Interception / DNS Hijacking for Malware Distribution
