suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' but pipeline generated no detection for data collection or exfiltration following unauthorized authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate data-access patterns in Cisco FMC (policy queries, config exports, analytics). Alert on unusual query volume, sensitive schema access, or bulk data retrieval following failed authentication attempts or from non-standard sources.

suggestion.title: Authentication Brute-Force to Cisco FMC (CVE-2026-20316 Wave)
suggestion.rationale: During active exploitation of public CVE, expect high-volume credential-guessing attempts. Article mentions 'unauthenticated' attacker implying auth bypass/bruteforce phase. No failed-login detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained failed-authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305). Alert if failure rate exceeds baseline or originates from known-hostile IPs. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 patch verification.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' but pipeline did not generate scan-based detection use case. CISA KEV entries require active scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run active scans for CVE-2026-20316 on all Cisco FMC instances. Flag vulnerable systems for immediate patching. Track remediation status against federal compliance deadline 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center CVE-2026-20316 Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'public-facing application' vulnerability allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using hardcoded credentials. Canonical asset-exposure hunt is mandated by article template and is the first line of defense for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network connections to TCP ports associated with Cisco FMC management interfaces (typically 443, 8305) from unexpected sources or geolocations. Correlate against known Cisco FMC IP ranges or hostname patterns. Prioritize scanning activity from non-corporate subnets targeting these interfaces.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Against Cisco FMC with Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'use of hard-coded password' enabling low-privileged account access. Failed login attempts using known hardcoded credentials (if documented by Cisco) should trigger high-confidence alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for repeated failed login attempts using known hardcoded default account names. Flag successful authentications from unexpected geographic locations or IPs not in IT management CIDR blocks. Correlate failed attempts followed by successful login within short timeframe (credential brute-forcing indicator).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Detection via Banner Grabbing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) formerly known as Firepower Management Center'—version enumeration is standard reconnaissance for exploiting known-vulnerable versions. CVE-2026-20316 affects specific versions; detection should include pre-exploitation scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scanning activity (SYN scans, version probes) against typical FMC management ports. Flag TLS certificate requests or HTTP banners retrieved from suspected FMC instances that reveal product/version. Correlate multiple scanning attempts from same source across short time window (active reconnaissance).

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-08-01 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Vulnerability scanners may report false negatives; active compliance checks post-deadline are critical for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) for Cisco FMC instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference against patch management database for applied patches. Flag instances past federal due date (2026-08-01) that remain unpatched as critical risk. Validate scanner findings with direct unauthenticated access tests if policy permits.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection in VeloCloud Orchestrator Requests
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Command Injection Flaw' being exploited. Pipeline missed HTTP-layer detection for injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, command separators) targeting VeloCloud endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to VeloCloud Orchestrator endpoints (typically :443/api/*, :8443/config/*) for command injection indicators: unencoded pipe (|), semicolon (;), ampersand (&), backticks, $() syntax, or URL-encoded equivalents (%3b, %26). Alert on requests containing both metacharacters and dynamic parameter values.

suggestion.title: Detect Code Execution via VeloCloud Service Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms 'Attackers Exploit' the vulnerability, implying remote code execution. No detection for post-injection process spawning, which is the execution phase after successful command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when VeloCloud Orchestrator service process or its service account spawns unexpected child processes, particularly shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or script interpreters. Flag abnormal working directories (temp, /var/tmp) or unusual parent-child process chains.

suggestion.title: Detect VeloCloud Privilege Escalation Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Command injection exploitation typically leads to privilege escalation or persistence. Pipeline provided no detection for account privilege changes or sudo usage following exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP injection-attempt detection with subsequent sudo invocations, privilege group additions, or account elevation events on VeloCloud hosts within 5-minute window. Flag first-time privilege escalation from service account context.

suggestion.title: Detect Outbound Command & Control from Compromised VeloCloud
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection enables attacker to spawn reverse shells or establish persistence. No command-and-control detection was generated despite exploitation scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from VeloCloud Orchestrator host to non-whitelisted external IPs immediately post-exploitation. Flag non-standard ports (reverse shell ports 4444, 5555, 8888, 9999), encrypted protocols from unexpected contexts, and DNS tunneling patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential/Config File Access from Injected Commands
suggestion.rationale: Post-injection code execution commonly targets credential stores or config files for lateral movement. Pipeline missed collection-phase detections for VeloCloud credential or configuration file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access/reads of VeloCloud credential stores, API key files, or configuration (/etc/velocloud, ~/.velocloud, registry paths) by non-whitelisted processes. Flag unusual file-read sequences suggesting credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator as vulnerable component but pipeline extracted zero IOCs (empty dict). No vulnerable version ranges, affected endpoints, or CVE identifier was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate WAF/IDS signatures for the specific VeloCloud command-injection vulnerability based on vendor CVE advisory. Block requests matching payload patterns (parameter names, encoding, endpoint paths) known to trigger the flaw across all customer VeloCloud instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—implies FMC is exposed to untrusted networks. Need discovery of externally-reachable FMC instances on ports 8305/8306 or via reverse-proxy signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network telemetry for inbound connections to known Cisco FMC management ports from public IP ranges. Correlate successful TCP handshakes with SSL/TLS certificates issued to FMC FQDN. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS GET requests to /admin, /login, or other FMC web paths from external sources.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Hard-coded FMC Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—this is credential-access using a known default password.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known hard-coded account names (e.g., admin, root, or Cisco's documented default accounts). Baseline legitimate FMC management logins; flag logins from unexpected ASNs/geolocations or outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow...access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—successful compromise allows data collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for anomalous data exports, policy downloads, or configuration backups by low-privileged accounts post-authentication. Flag bulk reads of firewall rules, nat tables, or VPN configurations after fresh login from external IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active exploitation in the wild. Vulnerability scanner output is a direct IOC correlation point; alert on any detection of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center running unpatched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Cisco FMC assets identified in your Nessus/Qualys/Tenable scans against CVE-2026-20316 signatures. Alert if any FMC instance is tagged as vulnerable; cross-reference with network exposure data. Escalate if exposed FMC instances have not been patched by federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV articles carry federal compliance dates. Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—compliance deadline is a detection trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all Cisco FMC instances in your environment and version-check against patched build numbers for CVE-2026-20316. Generate compliance report 7 days before due date; escalate any unpatched instances to incident response. Post-deadline, any unpatched FMC should be isolated or access-restricted.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Change Audit for Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access; subsequent lateral movement or privilege escalation to admin role would indicate post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for low-privileged account elevation to admin or superuser role, especially immediately after a fresh successful login. Flag any account creation, group membership changes, or policy modifications initiated by accounts using default or historically-compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposed to Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies FMC must be internet-facing. Asset exposure is the prerequisite attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances with inbound network access from untrusted or internet-facing networks. Correlate listener discovery (port 443, 8305, or FMC admin ports) with internet-routable IP ranges and vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation on FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—explicit hard-coded credential abuse vector. Detection must track weak credential login patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins with default or low-privilege service accounts, especially from unexpected source IPs or geolocations. Hard-coded credential attacks often precede rapid data collection; correlate successful auth with subsequent bulk configuration downloads or ACL exports.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Access in FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After credential compromise, attacker queries firewall policies, logs, or network rules. Detect bulk collection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual read operations on FMC object types (firewall rules, access control lists, traffic logs) by low-privilege accounts or new accounts. Flag large-scale exports, multi-day query scans, or extraction of sensitive network topology data.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Confirmation in Scanner Data
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates correlation: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20316. Direct IOC matching for active inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 matches on Cisco FMC assets. Correlate with patch management and asset inventory to identify systems still vulnerable past federal due date (2026-08-01). Flag any unpatched FMC with network exposure.

suggestion.title: Compliance Gap: Unpatched CVE-2026-20316 Past Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01.' Hardened compliance detection against a fixed remediation deadline tied to federal mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily check: identify any Cisco FMC instance still vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 on or after 2026-08-01. Cross-check patched status against network scan to ensure no bypass or incomplete remediation. Alert compliance and security teams on breach of federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — detection must cover successful auth to FMC with known hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication events for login attempts using known hard-coded usernames (e.g., 'admin', 'root') from external IPs. Flag successful authentications pre-dating last known patch date. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner hits to prioritize affected assets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — detection gap for anomalous FMC data reads/exports after credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data collection patterns in FMC: policy exports, rule dumps, certificate/key access, or bulk configuration downloads by low-privileged accounts or new logins. Baseline normal admin activity and alert on anomalies, especially config/policy exports to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public-Facing Instance Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article defines exploitation vector as 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' — presupposes FMC exposed to internet; canonical asset exposure hunt required per template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external threat intelligence feeds and internal asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances listening on 443 (or mgmt ports 8305–8307) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against patch status and apply 2026-08-01 federal due date as urgency priority.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management appliance controlling firewall policy fleet — successful breach enables lateral movement. Article scope is asset access, but detection should cover FMC-to-monitored-devices communication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC outbound API/SSH/CLI connections to managed firewalls for unusual payloads, new target devices, or off-hours activity. Detect policy pushes to multiple devices in short windows after new FMC login events, especially from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation implies external access. No UC for exposed asset detection despite template guidance on asset-exposure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible on internet-facing IPs. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output confirming CVE-2026-20316 presence; prioritize by patch deadline (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling login with 'low-privileged account' — no UC for detecting credential-based access or authentication anomalies against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC management logins from unexpected geographies, after-hours activity, or default/low-privilege account patterns. Establish baseline of legitimate login activity; escalate anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Compromise Data Access & Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — no UC for detecting policy export, configuration staging, or data exfiltration following breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or large-scale database queries immediately after suspicious authentication. Flag outbound file transfers and HTTPS data flows from FMC infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access the device; implies management interface is reachable. Must hunt for exposed FMC instances on public-facing or untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound traffic to Cisco FMC management ports (443/tcp, 8305/tcp, or documented FMC ports) from external/non-trusted ASNs. Correlate with successful TLS handshakes or HTTP 200 responses to FMC login paths.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'hard-coded password' as the core vulnerability. Detection must trigger on successful authentication using the low-privileged account from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins to the documented hard-coded account from unexpected IP ranges or at unusual times. Establish baseline for legitimate access and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after successful authentication. Detection should track unusual data queries or API calls from the low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API queries and data access patterns from the low-privileged account for bulk exports, policy retrieval, or topology discovery queries that are inconsistent with expected activity.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Bursts on FMC Management
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will probe FMC instances to confirm the hard-coded credentials work. Multiple failed login attempts followed by success is a signature of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >5 failed authentication attempts to FMC admin interface within 5 minutes from a single source IP, especially if followed by a successful login.

suggestion.title: FMC Version Enumeration & Patch Gap Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article requires federal agencies to patch by 2026-08-01. Identify all FMC instances and verify applied patches to confirm remediation completeness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC management interfaces for version strings or build numbers. Flag any instance not running patched version post-2026-08-01. Cross-check against CMDB for remediation tickets.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article notes low-privileged access can 'access sensitive data.' If FMC contains credentials or topology info, post-compromise lateral movement is likely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal outbound connections initiated from the FMC management server to internal hosts (particularly infrastructure targets like domain controllers, databases, or internal PKI) within 30 minutes of successful hard-coded credential login.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' Core attack vector enabling downstream infection of 23,000 repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags in high-dependency GitHub repos are reassigned to commits orphaned from main/release branches, or when tags point to commits authored by anomalous accounts with commit times outside normal patterns.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposed in Plaintext GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs. This could lead to a devastating breach.' Must detect secret value exposure in CI/CD logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions job logs for unencrypted secret values matching known patterns (GitHub token prefixes, API key formats). Correlate with unexpected code changes in action files that might be logging normally-protected variables.

suggestion.title: External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections during GitHub Actions runs to non-whitelisted external hosts. Flag data exfiltration patterns (large uploads, encoded data transfers) or downloads of executable payloads from unfamiliar domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Commits to High-Dependency Open-Source Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit' to a repository relied upon by 23,000 other projects. Indicates either credential compromise or insider threat in supply-chain critical asset.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For repositories with >1000 dependents, alert on commits from previously-unseen or dormant accounts, commits during anomalous hours, or rapid succession of commits followed by branch/tag deletions. Correlate with password reset events or MFA bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Git Commits in Supply-Chain Critical Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies orphaned commits as 'one of the key enabling factors in exploiting the changes-files GitHub Action workflow' and demonstrates: commits that exist but are unreachable from any branch—enabling hidden malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits pushed and immediately orphaned via branch deletion (reachable only via direct hash). In high-dependency repos, flag any orphaned commit created within 24 hours of branch deletions, especially if authored by privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Open-Source Dependency Repository Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Compromised upstream dependency now serving malicious code to thousands of dependent repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cascading failures or anomalies in dependent repositories' CI/CD pipelines following version pin updates or tag changes in upstream dependency repos. Correlate secret exposure incidents across multiple repos with common dependency updates.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in... using a low-privileged account' via hard-coded password. Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting this active exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected source IPs or failed-then-successful login sequences consistent with credential stuffing or exploitation of hard-coded accounts. Correlate with unpatched FMC inventory (pre-patch deadline 2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV implies 'currently being exploited' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline did not generate asset-inventory or vulnerability-scan correlation use case despite explicit vendor/product/CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner findings for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) against internal asset inventory. Prioritize internet-facing or DMZ-deployed instances. Verify patch status against 2026-08-01 federal deadline; flag any systems still running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Suspicious Admin/Low-Privilege Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'low-privileged account... to access sensitive data within impacted systems'. Pipeline missed use case for detecting privilege escalation or sensitive-data access post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication events using low-privileged or default FMC accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'readonly' variants) accessing sensitive configuration data, policy objects, or managed firewall telemetry. Correlate with known-bad source IPs or off-hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—direct evidence of hard-coded credential-based initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC authentication events using known hard-coded service credentials or against default admin/readonly accounts. Baseline normal FMC logins; alert on successful authentications from unexpected source IPs or times, especially followed by data queries within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Management Interface Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'remote attacker' exploiting a public-facing vulnerability—T1190 is the canonical MITRE mapping for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external/untrusted networks. Alert on mass-scan patterns, exploitation payloads in HTTP bodies, or successful access followed by lateral queries to managed firewall endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Inventory & Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch deadline 2026-08-01 (1 day from publication 2026-07-29) requires immediate asset-exposure hunt per regulatory baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate vulnerability scanner results with asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances. Flag all unpatched versions; prioritize internet-facing or DMZ-resident instances. Cross-check patch management records for deployment lag >7 days.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration/Policy Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-exploitation data collection must be hunted to detect breach scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk exports of firewall rules, threat feeds, authentication credentials, or device configurations from FMC within 2 hours of unauthorized login. Monitor for egress transfers of .xml, .json config files or database dumps to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Compromised FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: FMC is the management plane for enterprise firewall fleets; a compromised FMC can push malicious policies across all managed devices—critical blast-radius escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual policy-push commands from FMC to managed firewalls correlating with unauthorized authentication events. Alert on bulk configuration deployments outside maintenance windows or from unusual FMC sessions.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Hard-Coded Password Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password in FMC disables normal credential validation controls—a defense-evasion tactic masking attacker presence from log-based alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication successes that bypass MFA, occur outside login retry policies, or use deprecated authentication paths. Monitor for MFA bypass attempts or changes to FMC authentication configuration post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes this affects 'public-facing application' exploitation; SOC must first enumerate all exposed FMC instances to prioritize response. 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template explicitly recommended in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally routable Cisco FMC management interfaces (TCP 443, port 8305) in edge firewalls and internet-facing network perimeter logs. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 presence. Flag any FMC instance reachable from untrusted networks without VPN/bastion requirement.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Login Success
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'; requires detection of successful authentication via hard-coded default credentials to FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interface authentication logs showing repeated login attempts followed by success with known low-privileged default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'cisco', vendor-documented defaults). Correlate source IPs against known attacker infrastructure or unusual geographic origins.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Configuration Export or Dump
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; post-exploitation hunting required to detect what data was accessed, exported, or logged access to restricted FMC configuration objects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs and database access patterns for low-privileged authenticated sessions accessing policy rules, network objects, sensitive credentials storage, threat intelligence feeds, or exporting device configurations. Flag bulk data read operations or configuration export API calls initiated by low-privileged or newly-created sessions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Privilege Escalation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access but article does not exclude subsequent privilege escalation attempts to gain admin/root on FMC or underlying OS. CVE history for FMC shows privilege escalation is common post-compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for CLI commands, API calls, or console access attempts that request elevated privileges from low-privileged FMC user sessions. Monitor for sudoers rule additions, file permission modifications on FMC application directories, or attempts to modify system accounts post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Hardcoded Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — this is the core attack pattern. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for remote login attempts to Cisco FMC (port 443 typically) from external networks followed by authentication success, particularly with account names or patterns consistent with hardcoded defaults. Look for successful remote shell or API access immediately after authentication. Correlate failed attempts (rate-based) prior to success.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — this collection phase was entirely omitted from kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-successful-authentication to FMC, monitor for bulk data queries (policy configs, audit logs, network topology) or large file transfers from FMC database. Baseline normal admin queries and alert on deviation (unusual tables accessed, unusual export formats, high-volume extraction).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Deployment Status Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and template notes patch lag is 'the silent killer' — vulnerability assessment/patch hunt is completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch management systems for Cisco FMC instances (product name match: 'Secure Firewall Management Center' or 'FMC') and cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Flag any instances still vulnerable after federal due date. Correlate with network exposure (reachable from untrusted zones).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Brute Force / Dictionary Attack
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password vulnerability implies known/guessable credentials. Article does not name the account but defenders should hunt for pattern-based or timing-based auth attempts consistent with exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for high-frequency login attempts (success or failure) within short time windows from single source IPs, especially remote/untrusted IPs. Hardcoded credentials often have consistent usernames — watch for repeated attempts with same username but varying passwords or single-attempt success without prior reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration or Policy Tampering Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'low-privileged account access' — attacker may alter firewall policies or rules once inside FMC to maintain persistence or enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal policy/configuration change frequency and actors (expected admins). Alert on out-of-hours changes, changes by unexpected accounts (especially low-privileged), or bulk rule modifications that deviate from established change patterns. Cross-reference change timestamps with suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Internet-Accessible Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit—implying FMC must be exposed. Article template instructs to run 'standard asset-exposure hunt,' yet pipeline generated zero UCs for this foundational control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cisco FMC instances accessible from the internet via port scanning (8300, 8305, 443) or vulnerability-scanner results. Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unpatched, unaccounted-for, or legacy FMC deployments exposed to WAN without VPN.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Attempts to Cisco FMC Management
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in... using a low-privileged account.' Detection must capture both failed brute-force and successful auth using hard-coded/default credentials from unexpected source IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for failed authentication bursts against FMC (ports 8300, 8305, 443) from external IPs, or successful logins from non-standard source IPs/geolocations. Alert on rapid repeated auth attempts consistent with brute-force spray targeting default credentials.

suggestion.title: Data Access and Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: '[attacker can] access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No UC generated for post-exploitation data collection (policy/config exports, credential stores, syslog datasets, database dumps).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk configuration exports, policy backups, or database extracts initiated from FMC management UI, especially within minutes of suspicious authentication. Detect large data transfers from FMC servers to external IPs or cloud storage. Flag pg_dump or archive tool execution under FMC service context.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Policy and Logging Changes in Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, low-privileged FMC access could be used to disable logging, modify firewall rules, or persist access. Article does not explicitly exclude defense-evasion tactics post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for unauthorized policy changes, rule deletion, or audit log disablement. Alert on new user accounts, role promotions, or credential changes in FMC occurring post-exploit or outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Integrity Deviation from Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers poison Adform script' — requires detection of cryptographic hash mismatches or behavioral deviations in Adform CDN deliveries against known-good baselines, correlated with customer-reported wallet theft incidents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track SHA256 hashes of Adform scripts (adform.net domain) from customer CDN caches and compare against vendor attestation. Flag mismatches within 48–72 hours of crypto theft reports. Correlate with unexpected process spawning or network callbacks from browser memory.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Substitution in DOM/Requests
suggestion.rationale: Core attack objective explicitly described as 'swap crypto wallet addresses.' Requires comparison of wallet addresses visible in browser DOM vs. those in outbound API calls to exchanges or smart contracts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect discrepancies between wallet addresses rendered in webpage source and those submitted in HTTP POST/API calls to crypto exchanges. Flag when a single browser session sends cryptocurrency to two distinct wallet addresses in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack — Unauthorized CDN Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned script must have been deployed to Adform infrastructure. Look for 'unauthorized modifications' to Adform CDN, indicating credential compromise, API key theft, or insider access to delivery infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Adform CDN administrative access for off-hours logins, geographic anomalies, or service account abuse. Flag rapid script version deployments outside normal change windows. Correlate with API key issuance or credential resets.

suggestion.title: Attacker Infrastructure Communication from Poisoned Ad Script
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned script must exfiltrate wallet data or receive C2 commands. Phrase 'customer sites' implies thousands of endpoints executing attacker payload, requiring infrastructure-level beaconing or data exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS queries from customer endpoints to rare or newly-registered domains, triggered immediately after Adform ad script loads. Flag anomalous API calls to cryptocurrency exchange endpoints from ad domain IP space.

suggestion.title: Attacker-Controlled Cryptocurrency Wallet Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Victims' funds redirected to attacker wallet(s). These wallet addresses are the primary IOC and should be mined from the poisoned script payload and monitored on-chain for consolidation and cash-out patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract wallet addresses from captured malicious script samples. Monitor blockchain for inbound transactions from victim wallets, rapid fund consolidation, or deposits to known mixing services. Correlate wallet funding with customer theft reports to establish attribution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Fake Update Delivery Over Compromised Network
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake updates' as delivery vector; no UC detected this supply-chain-adjacent mechanism. Phrase: 'Pushes Fake Updates to Deliver Surveillance Malware'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or self-signed certificate updates delivered over hotel/guest networks. Flag OS update requests to non-standard domains or IPs. Correlate update delivery timing with surveillance malware execution.

suggestion.title: Post-Update Surveillance Malware Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malware establishes persistence after fake update execution; no UC for post-install stability checks. Phrase: 'surveillance malware' installed via updates
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry/startup folder modifications immediately following unexpected update execution. Flag screen/audio capture libraries loading post-update. Monitor for C2 beaconing in 10-30 minutes post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Capability Activation (Screen/Audio Capture)
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'surveillance malware' payload but no UC for detecting exfiltration of screen/audio. Core attack capability not instrumented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on screen capture APIs (BitBlt, GetPixel) or audio capture (WASAPI, GetAudioInputStream) invoked by new/unsigned processes. Correlate with outbound network traffic to likely C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Network Compromise Detection: Rogue Hotel Wi-Fi Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi' as entry point; no detection for network-level compromise or MITM indicators. Phrase: 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For travelers: detect certificate pinning violations on OS update channels. Flag DNS responses for legitimate update servers resolving to non-CDN IPs. Monitor for unexpected gateway IP changes when joining known hotel SSIDs.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Self-Signed Binary Execution Post-Network Access
suggestion.rationale: Fake update delivery implies executable injection; no UC flags untrusted code execution after guest network access. Missing entire execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with missing or invalid code signatures in 0-60 min window after joining guest/hotel networks. Flag binaries with mismatched publisher names in certificate vs. filename.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Surveillance Malware
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware implies active command-and-control; no UC for detecting outbound C2 traffic patterns typical of camera/screen exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for regular outbound connections to rare ASNs/geolocations from endpoints that executed unsigned code post-network-compromise. Screen capture/audio data beacons typically exceed 1 MB per interval; alert on bulk transfers post-update.

suggestion.title: Apostrophe Editor Account PATCH Anomaly on Piece APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authenticated editor' can exploit this. Detection missing for which editor accounts are performing PATCH operations against /api/v1/@apostrophecms/* endpoints, especially outside normal editing hours or from unexpected IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal PATCH patterns per editor account and time-of-day. Alert on editors performing PATCH to piece-type APIs during off-hours, from new IPs, or with unusual frequency. Cross-reference against Web server audit logs to identify editor identity.

suggestion.title: Post-SSPP Authorization Model Degradation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'process-wide authorization bypass' as the outcome. After Object.prototype pollution, auth checks should fail silently or default to permissive. Missing detection for auth errors, missing auth headers, or permission checks that should block but don't.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application error logs for auth-related exceptions that correlate with SSPP PATCH attempts. Look for sudden spike in 403→200 transitions post-exploit (where 403 Forbidden becomes 200 OK for the same endpoint/user combo).

suggestion.title: Protected Endpoint Access by Non-Admin Accounts Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article implies /user/* and /global/* endpoints are normally restricted. After auth bypass, non-admin accounts will access these endpoints and succeed (200). Detection missing for lateral privilege escalation via pollution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of which user accounts can access /api/v1/@apostrophecms/user/* and /global/* with 200 status. Alert on new accounts hitting these endpoints post-SSPP PATCH, especially with Read/List operations that would normally be admin-only.

suggestion.title: Object.prototype Gadget Chain Invocation Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'confirmed gadget' in the truncated body, implying malicious side-effects from prototype pollution (e.g., unauthorized database writes, file creation, code execution). Missing detection for what the gadget actually does post-pollution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected database modifications, file I/O, or subprocess spawning from Node.js process immediately after SSPP PATCH (within seconds). Gadget chains typically trigger observable side-effects—look for anomalous rows inserted, configs modified, or binaries written.

suggestion.title: Repeated Prototype Pollution Payload Attempts (Failed + Succeeded)
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention whether the vulnerability is patched in later versions. Attackers will probe with multiple payload variations. Missing detection for reconnaissance/persistence via repeated __proto__ mutations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Count __proto__, $pullAll, constructor.prototype, and similar proto-pollution keywords in PATCH/POST request bodies per source IP and account. Alert if same source attempts >3 variations within 10 minutes, indicating active probing/exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ApostropheCMS Version Exposure & CVE-2026-53609 Risk Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article severity rated CRIT and assigned specific CVE. Missing detection that identifies ApostropheCMS instances, retrieves version, and alerts if version is ≤ patched version for CVE-2026-53609.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for X-Powered-By, Server header, or /api/version endpoints that expose ApostropheCMS version. Correlate against known vulnerable version range. Alert on vulnerable instances detected, or if version changes (possible post-compromise evasion).

suggestion.title: CaptiveCrunch AiTM Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'travelers worldwide' via AiTM (Adversary-in-the-Middle) attacks on captive portal spoofing. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite keyword 'Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM)' in metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect traffic to HTTP-only login pages from known wireless SSID spoofing patterns or near airport/hotel networks. Flag credential submissions over unencrypted channels from mobile or temporary profiles. Alert on successful logins followed immediately by token exfiltration to C2.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'ClickFix' social engineering attacks but pipeline extracted zero techniques or use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with ClickFix-style payloads (fake Windows defender alerts, browser security warnings) targeting travelers. Match phishing URLs to known malware delivery domains. Flag Process creation events from browser or email client showing unusual child processes typical of ClickFix malware.

suggestion.title: Midnight Blizzard Token Theft Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'Token theft' as core attack mechanism, yet no detection use case generated for anomalous token usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful AiTM credential compromise with rapid downstream token refresh or OAuth token requests. Detect stolen tokens replayed from geographically impossible locations within minutes of compromise. Flag abnormal APIs accessed by newly-acquired tokens (mail export, device list enumeration, etc.).

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery to Travelers via Compromised Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'malware delivery' to travelers; no IOCs or detection use cases extracted for malware payload identification or detonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious executable downloads over airport/hotel WiFi to travelers' devices. Match file hashes against CaptiveCrunch malware signatures. Alert on process execution from temp directories or Downloads following credential submission to spoofed portals.

suggestion.title: CaptiveCrunch C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware-based campaigns require C2 communication; pipeline produced no IOCs (domains, IPs, URLs) despite article being published by Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound traffic from deployed malware to Midnight Blizzard C2 infrastructure. Block known C2 domains/IPs. Alert on characteristic beacon patterns (timing, size, TLS fingerprint) matching CaptiveCrunch malware families.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Traveler Credentials and Device Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft implies exfiltration; no use case for detecting suspicious bulk email/device data exports post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk export of messages, contacts, or device enrollment metadata by newly-compromised accounts. Flag rapid API calls (GetMailboxStatistics, GetUserPhoto, ListDevices) from C2 tokens. Alert on unusual volume of data packaged for exfiltration (zip, tar, rar) in temp directories.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes NightLedger masquerading as SspiCli.dll for DLL search-order hijacking against AppVShNotify.exe. Core evasion technique requiring detection hook on anomalous DLL load sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppVShNotify.exe or similar legitimate executables loading unexpected DLL paths, especially SspiCli.dll from non-system directories. Alert on unsigned DLLs masquerading as Windows system libraries with mismatched file metadata or located in user-writable paths.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing with Recruitment Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers used 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms.' Need email/URL detection layer for hiring-themed phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment or hiring keywords impersonating known HR platforms (LinkedIn, Indeed, etc.) or spoofed company careers portals. Flag redirects to third-party file-sharing services (archive.org, mediafire, etc.) from recruitment-themed phishing links.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Videoconferencing Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives.' Domain similarity and redirect-chain detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains with high string similarity to popular videoconferencing platforms (Zoom, Teams, Webex). Flag redirects from such domains to file-sharing services or executable hosting. Alert on typosquatting patterns (transposition, homoglyphs).

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling – ArcBridge/BridgeHead Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two custom WebSocket tunnelers for covert C2. Behavioral pattern for encrypted tunnel detection via protocol and flow characteristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent WebSocket connections (protocol upgrade to ws:// or wss://) from internal hosts to external IPs, particularly with no corresponding HTTP traffic. Flag WebSocket sessions with unusual duration, byte imbalance, or originating from recently-executed suspicious processes.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Process Discovery Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states NightLedger performs 'process discovery' as part of reconnaissance. Detection of discovery tool execution in lateral-movement timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of process-discovery commands (tasklist, Get-Process, ps, wmic process list) within 5–30 minutes of suspicious DLL load, file-sharing download, or unusual network connection. Raise severity if executed from temp directories or by unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Screenshot Capture by Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: NightLedger malware includes explicit screenshot capability. Monitor for unauthorized screen capture requests from backdoor processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes (especially DLLs, rundll32 execution) invoking screen capture APIs or launching screenshot utilities (mspaint, snippingtool) without user interaction or UAC prompt. Correlate with file write operations to temp directories.

suggestion.title: FMC: Credential Stuffing / Brute-Force Against Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password. Pipeline missed detection use case for repeated failed auth attempts followed by successful login, the canonical credential-stuffing attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated authentication failures to FMC management interface (SSH/HTTPS, typically port 443/8443) from a single source IP, especially from external/public IPs. Establish baseline of normal failed-auth rates per IP; spike >5 failed attempts in 5-min window preceding successful login indicates credential stuffing with known hardcoded password.

suggestion.title: FMC: Successful Remote Authentication from External IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' gaining access. Successful FMC management login from public internet (not internal management subnet) is anomalous and signals exploitation; pipeline generated no detection for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful SSH or HTTPS authentication to FMC management interface originating from external/internet-routable IP addresses. Baseline against known management IPs (SOC, vendor support). Alert on any successful login from unexpected external source; requires immediate verification (may indicate exploitation with hardcoded credentials).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
suggestion.rationale: Article describes remote exploitation of FMC. Pipeline must identify all internet-accessible FMC instances to scope exposure. Article states vulnerability 'could allow unauthenticated, remote attacker' — baseline prerequisite is knowing where FMC is exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct external port scans for FMC management ports (default 443, 8443, 8305) and fingerprint Cisco FMC banner responses. Cross-reference with asset management to identify FMC instances not intended to be internet-routable. Verify patch status against CVE-2026-20316 (federal remediation deadline 2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC: Sensitive Data Access or Export Following Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Pipeline missed detection for post-compromise data queries or bulk exports (e.g., firewall rules, ACLs, credentials) initiated by authenticated user after suspicious login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for queries/exports of sensitive data (firewall policies, device inventory, credentials, ACLs) following authentication from external IP or during off-hours. Correlate successful unusual auth + data access within same session. Low-privilege user exporting policy data is high-risk signal; establish baseline of typical admin queries per role.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific CVE (CVE-2026-20316) known to be actively exploited (CISA KEV status). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; should recommend IDS/WAF signature deployment for exploitation attempts targeting this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy published signatures for CVE-2026-20316 exploitation (likely HTTP-based attacks targeting known FMC endpoints). Alert on any IDS/WAF hit for this CVE against FMC-adjacent IP ranges. Monitor both successful and failed exploit attempts; volume spike may indicate targeted attack campaign.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration: Hardcoded Credential Exposure in Backups or Exports
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is hardcoded password in FMC software. If backups, config exports, or documentation containing this credential are accessible to internal users or exposed, it multiplies attack surface. Pipeline missed insider/post-breach detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement secrets-scanning against FMC configuration backups, exported configs, and internal documentation/wikis. Flag any appearance of known hardcoded credentials (from vendor advisory or PoC). Alert on bulk download or copying of FMC backup files to removable media or external locations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20316 explicitly named as attack vector in article title and body; pipeline generated zero use cases to detect this via scanner or network telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2026-20316 against Cisco FMC. Monitor for network traffic targeting known FMC ports with exploitation patterns. Cross-reference alerts with asset inventory to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hard-coded password enabling unauthenticated remote login; no detection use case generated for this credential-abuse vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known hard-coded account names post-disclosure. Alert on successful logins from unexpected source IPs or followed by privilege-bounded activity. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 scanner hits.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within impacted systems'; no detection for unusual data queries or exports post-authentication by low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC logs for low-privileged user accounts exporting policies, pulling config data, or querying sensitive repositories. Alert on bulk data staging or API calls anomalous to account baseline post-authentication spike.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status (actively exploited); canonical asset-exposure template referenced but no use case populated to identify exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances with internet-facing routes or firewall rules permitting untrusted ingress. Check DNS for FMC A-records in public zones. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Low-Privileged Account FMC Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation uses low-privileged account; pipeline missed detection of admin-level operations by accounts scoped to limited permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for low-privileged FMC user activity. Alert on policy modifications, admin function access, or inter-device management traffic originating from compromised low-privilege session.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'. This is the core attack path and requires authentication log detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using known hard-coded credentials. CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation. Correlate login success with administrative action or data access to flag compromise.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' as vulnerable product. Vulnerability scanners must be hunted for exposed, unpatched FMC instances reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner results for Nessus/Qualys hits on CVE-2026-20316. Intersect with network reachability data (internet-facing, non-DMZ FMC). Flag any unpatched or unremediated instances past federal due-date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Post-authentication data theft requires detection of bulk reads, exports, or configuration downloads via the hard-coded account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for data-export operations, config file reads, or policy downloads following authentication via hard-coded credentials. Detect bulk transfers, archive creation, or unusual query patterns on FMC's threat-intelligence or security-policy repositories.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials require network access to FMC management interface (port 443 typical). Article: 'remote attacker' implies reconnaissance precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port 443 scans and probes targeting FMC IP ranges. Correlate with SSL handshake failures, HTTP 401 responses, or certificate-grab attempts. Flag reconnaissance patterns that precede or cluster near exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Managed Firewall Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management hub for Cisco firewall infrastructure ('Firepower Management Center manages...'). Compromise may pivot to managed devices. Detect policy pushes or credential forwarding to firewalls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous FMC-to-managed-device communications (policy deployments, command execution). Detect credential forwarding or administrator impersonation on downstream firewalls triggered by FMC session.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Security Data from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Threat closes with 'access sensitive data' — implies exfiltration or operational use of FMC's intelligence (threat feeds, firewall rulesets, VPN configs). Unusual egress or data staging must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate FMC data exports (frequency, volume, destination). Alert on off-hours bulk transfers, compression/archiving of configs or threat intelligence, or unusual egress to non-corporate external IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-20316 in Vulnerability Scanner Results
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and recommends patch verification across fleet. Pipeline missed UC for vulnerability scanner detection despite article explicitly referencing asset-exposure hunt pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability management logs for CVE-2026-20316 detections. Flag any Cisco FMC instances reporting vulnerable status; prioritize external-facing assets. Include systems showing as patched to detect patch bypass techniques.

suggestion.title: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Instances Exposed to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploitation, requiring network-reachable target. Pipeline omitted asset-exposure UC which article explicitly recommends as canonical hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network metadata for Cisco FMC instances (typical ports 443, 8305) accessible from untrusted ASNs. Correlate with shodan/censys scans. Flag any management interfaces without IP allowlisting or exposed via VPN concentrators.

suggestion.title: Detect Brute Force or Dictionary Attack Against Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article states hard-coded password enables 'unauthenticated remote attacker' access. Pipeline missed UC for authentication-anomaly detection during exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for elevated failed-login rate from single external IP, followed by successful low-privileged account access from same source. Baseline admin-access patterns; flag geographic/ASN/time-of-day anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Successful Unauthorized Access to Cisco FMC with Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation results in attacker logging in via 'low-privileged account' using hard-coded password. Pipeline omitted UC for successful-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Cisco FMC authentication from external/unexpected networks using low-privilege service accounts, particularly off-hours or without corresponding admin-credential use. Cross-reference with known-exploited-CVE datasets.

suggestion.title: Monitor Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation enables attacker to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline omitted UC for post-compromise data-access and exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk data-access or export events (firewall policies, threat intelligence, configuration dumps) from low-privilege authenticated sessions. Correlate with network egress to external addresses. Alert on unusual data aggregation patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Cisco FMC as Pivot Point for Firewall Policy Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'sensitive data within impacted systems'; FMC management access enables policy modification for lateral movement. Pipeline missed UC for post-compromise lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for policy/rule changes (permit-all rules, object modifications, group creation) initiated by low-privilege or service accounts. Correlate with network allow-list expansion and unexpected inbound rule permits.

suggestion.title: FMC Asset Inventory & Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) contains hard-coded credential vulnerability; inventory of exposed FMC instances and version detection is foundational for CISA KEV compliance hunts. 'Unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' requires asset visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FMC instances on internet-routable IPs via port 443/8305 banners, version probes, or admin-path discovery. Cross-correlate against Cisco EoL/vulnerable version lists. Prioritize systems running versions prior to patches released by 2026-08-01 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device.' Article implies hard-coded account names exist; authentication logs should detect login attempts with known hard-coded credentials or suspicious account patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC admin/appliance logs for successful authentication using known hard-coded account names (e.g., admin, root, default service accounts). Flag successful logins from external IP ranges with no prior authorization. Correlate with failed attempts suggesting credential stuffing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise allows 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation phase requires detection of unauthorized data queries, policy/rule exports, configuration dumps, or sensitive asset queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication followed by bulk queries of firewall policies, VPN configurations, threat intel rules, or asset inventory within FMC. Flag data exports (backup/config downloads) initiated immediately after login by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Low-Privileged FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' is initially compromised; detect attempts to escalate to admin or system-level access within FMC console or underlying appliance OS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege-escalation syscalls or privilege-group additions following initial low-privileged FMC login. Alert on sudo/runas attempts from low-privileged user context within FMC management appliance. Flag role/permission modifications within FMC admin console shortly after unauthorized login.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance & Vulnerable FMC Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch deadline 2026-08-01 drives compliance reporting. Pipeline should generate time-boxed inventory hunt for FMC versions and patch status vs. known-exploited vulnerability timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all FMC instances and extract version, patch level, and deployment date. Flag systems running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 and deployed without patches by 2026-08-01. Report as CISA KEV compliance gap.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — this is exploitation of hard-coded credentials (T1078.001), yet no detection use case generated. Must hunt for successful FMC login with known low-privileged hard-coded account names or success following brute-force failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Cisco FMC logins using known hard-coded account names, especially preceded by failed login attempts from external IP addresses. Hard-coded credentials represent a static attack surface; detect multiple failures followed by sudden success or success from unexpected geographic regions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require asset inventory and scanning hunts. Article provides CVE ID and affected product (Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center); pipeline should alert on scanner findings matching this CVE, prioritizing internet-exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger high-priority alerts when Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center versions matching CVE-2026-20316 scope are detected by vulnerability scanners. Escalate severity if asset is publicly routable (public IP, no corporate proxy) or has external-facing management interface.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article's threat model assumes FMC is 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' accessible—implying public-facing or easily reachable infrastructure. Pipeline missed network-based asset exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances reachable from the public internet by network fingerprinting (TCP 443, SSL cert patterns) or asset scans. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to identify unpatched or unaccounted FMC deployments. Disable external access or enforce VPN/proxy for management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC API and Configuration Data Exfiltration
