suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-privileged account export/read of firewall policies, interface configs, or backup downloads. Baseline baseline legitimate admins and alert on anomalies or after-hours activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active wild exploitation of exposed FMC instances. Article provides no exposure hunt; federal patch due is 2026-08-01.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Cisco FMC instances; verify not internet-routable on HTTPS (443) or FMC port (8305). Cross-correlate scanner CVE-2026-20316 detections with asset registry. Escalate any unpatched FMC post federal due date.

suggestion.title: External Reconnaissance of FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is remote-exploitable on exposed management plane. No pre-exploitation reconnaissance UC generated (port scanning, banner grabbing).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scans targeting 443, 8305 from external IPs. Alert on TLS/HTTP banner-grabbing attempts against FMC ports. Baseline expected management-access sources and flag new IPs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Release Tag Reassignment to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'Create a branch...Then, delete the remote branch. You can still navigate to that commit...Thus, the attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo.' Obfuscation technique hiding malicious code in plain sight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when release/version tags in public GitHub Actions are modified to point to different commit SHAs than their git history indicates, especially when new target commit is orphaned (unreachable from main/branches). Alert on tag deletion + recreation sequences within hours. Cross-reference against Actions with 1000+ external dependents.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation and Branch Deletion Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack obfuscation: 'Create a branch...Then, delete the remote branch. You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch...This is what an orphaned branch looks like. It is one of the key enabling factors in exploiting the changes-files GitHub Action workflow.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of: branch creation → commit push → branch deletion within short window (hours). Flag in production/release branches and Actions repos. Correlate with tag creation/modification on same commit SHA to surface version hijacking.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in GitHub Actions Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Attack goal and impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs...an attacker with write privileges...made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext.' Article emphasizes GitHub normally encrypts secrets so they 'never appear in the build log.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching secret formats (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, database passwords, API keys). Alert when plaintext secrets appear in logs of Actions that should encrypt them, especially in repos using tj-actions/changed-files or related code-manipulation Actions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Egress from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Detection vector that revealed attack: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' Malicious action was downloading secondary payload from external source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from GitHub Actions CI/CD runners to non-whitelisted/newly-registered domains, especially unsigned or low-reputation endpoints. Correlate with commits that introduce curl/wget/download commands in workflow YAML. High-risk if originating from Actions with widespread dependents.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Collaborator Grant to High-Impact GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Enabling factor: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Unknown how access was obtained, but new write permissions to repos with 10000+ dependents is supply-chain critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new user grants (collaborator/admin) to GitHub Actions repositories with 10,000+ dependent repos. Escalate if new user has no prior commits, repositories, or originating IP/geo is anomalous. Cross-reference against GitHub security advisories and monitor for immediate Activity anomalies post-grant.

suggestion.title: Clustered GitHub Repository Mutation Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Attacker performed coordinated obfuscation: committed malicious code, manipulated release tags, created orphaned commits, triggered exfiltration. Each action logs separately. 'The other key enabling factor was moving release tags around the repository' combined with commit → branch delete → tag reassign pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of repo mutations within 2-hour window: branch creation + deletion + tag modification + force push on same repo. Higher risk if affecting Actions repos or release branches. Correlate with write access grants and outbound network activity from CI/CD. Flag if mutations include commit messages referencing version/release/tag keywords.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-20316' as the explicit indicator; pipeline returned empty IOCs. Any vulnerability scanner, Nessus feed, or patch-management system querying this CVE should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Nessus, OpenVAS, or Qualys process launches or network queries that include 'CVE-2026-20316' or 'Cisco FMC' vulnerability checks. Baseline these queries per environment to identify sweeps outside normal patch windows.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded credential access to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allowing 'low-privileged account' login; this is T1078 credential usage, not just T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC (port 443, Management Center interface) preceded by zero or one failed attempt, especially from external networks or using low-privileged service accounts. Hard-coded passwords produce consistent login timings and user-agents.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC internet exposure inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'; FMC should never be internet-facing. Asset-exposure hunt referenced but no inventory rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/WAF logs and DNS records for inbound connections to Cisco FMC (typically TCP 443, 8305) from external subnets. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify management interfaces reachable from internet; escalate any hit as critical before attacker reconnaissance succeeds.

suggestion.title: Sensitive data exfiltration from Cisco FMC post-authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise allows access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'; impact is data access, not just shell access. Detection should monitor for bulk exports or API queries for config/policy/telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for bulk policy exports, configuration downloads, or repeated API calls to /api/fmc_config endpoints from authenticated low-privilege accounts. Baseline normal admin activity; flag anomalies like exports during off-hours or from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Default/hard-coded Cisco FMC credentials in memory or config
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability hinges on hard-coded password embedded in product; red-team or forensic reviews should search for this in memory dumps, config files, or firmware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search memory and disk for known Cisco FMC hard-coded account strings or password patterns in cleartext. Monitor for extraction of FMC config files (fmc.conf, etc.) to external storage. Flag any tool run that attempts credential dumping from Cisco processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' yet pipeline generated zero UCs. Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access exposed systems—requires asset discovery and exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Cisco FMC management interface connection attempts from untrusted networks (typical ports 443, 8305). Cross-correlate with CVE-2026-20316 scanner detections to identify vulnerable assets before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Default Credential Exploitation Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password vulnerability allowing unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—successful authentication via hard-coded credentials is the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Cisco FMC management console authentications from external networks using known hard-coded account names, or temporal clustering of failed/successful auth attempts indicating credential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access in Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker objective: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-compromise data collection is the terminal phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC logs for policy exports, configuration backups, or security rule database queries initiated by newly-authenticated accounts or from atypical network origins following exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—hard-coded password is the attack vector. Pipeline missed T1078.001 entirely and produced no credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC management interface using known default or hard-coded account names (e.g., admin, cisco, default). Correlate source IPs against expected administrative ranges; flag logins from external/untrusted networks. If brute-force telemetry available, alert on rapid sequential auth attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Remote Unauthenticated Access to Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—T1190 exploitation of public-facing application. Pipeline acknowledged T1190 but provided zero network-layer detections for exposure hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for TCP connections to Cisco FMC management interface (default 443) from external/untrusted IP space. Correlate with HTTP 200/302 responses indicating successful handshake. Use Shodan/similar to identify externally-exposed FMC instances; flag those instances in patch-compliance scanner.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Low-Privileged Account Access to Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems'—collection-phase activity post-credential compromise. Pipeline generated no data-exfiltration or data-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit/access logs for queries against policy databases, threat intelligence stores, or credential/VPN config repositories initiated by low-privileged service accounts. Baseline typical access patterns for legitimate operations; alert on bulk reads or access to sensitive object classes (credentials, threat feeds).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—requires detection of authentication success via hard-coded credential. Pipeline generated zero auth-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using low-privileged service accounts from untrusted source IPs or geographies. Establish baseline of legitimate admin access and alert on deviations, especially from internet-routable networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Export Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of configuration/credential exfiltration following compromise. Pipeline omitted collection-phase detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authenticated sessions to Cisco FMC that query, export, or download firewall policy configurations, access control lists, or stored credentials. Alert on bulk API calls to retrieve sensitive objects, especially within 1-4 hours of suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies FMC is internet-facing or accessible without VPN. Pipeline did not generate asset-exposure or network-reconnaissance detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces (TCP 8305, 443) exposed on public-facing segments. Correlate CVE-2026-20316 patch inventory against network telemetry showing external HTTPS connections to FMC ports. Alert on repeated connection attempts across multiple source IPs.

suggestion.title: Brute Force Against Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Account
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password is a known value; attackers can enumerate the account name and systematically attempt login. Article does not rule out reconnaissance/brute-force prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for >5 failed login attempts to the same account within 10 minutes, especially from a single source or distributed sources (indicating coordinated brute force). Flag patterns matching known FMC service-account naming conventions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Authentication Using Hardcoded Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—this is T1078 (Valid Accounts), not just generic exploitation. Core attack step completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC from non-admin source IPs using the documented hardcoded low-privilege account. Hunt for failed-then-successful authentication sequences from external or unusual ASNs to FMC management interfaces within hours of patch miss.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data or Credential Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—implies collection of firewall policies, VPN credentials, and pre-shared keys stored in FMC config. This data access step missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk policy downloads, credential backup exports, or VPN configuration retrieval from FMC via REST API or CLI shortly after anomalous login. Look for temp files containing encrypted secrets or plaintext pre-shared keys.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC as Lateral Movement Pivot to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC is a control plane—attacker gains config write access to all managed firewalls. Article's 'sensitive data' includes keys needed for VPN/tunnel compromise into protected networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious FMC login (T1078) + config export with subsequent unauthorized policy pushes to managed devices. Look for new ACL rules, VPN tunnels, or route additions appearing seconds after FMC compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires network access to FMC management ports (443, 8305). Article: 'remote attacker'—implies exposure. Pipeline correctly referenced asset-exposure template but generated no concrete hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Cisco FMC instances; flag any accessible from internet-routable IPs on management ports. Cross-reference BGP leak/internet IP scanning data (Shadowserver, Censys) for unexpected FMC exposure in your IP ranges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active in-the-wild exploitation. Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—scanner-based detection of unpatched instances is immediate, tangible hunt. Pipeline omitted this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for any FMC with version pre-fix release. Authenticate to all known FMC instances and retrieve 'show version' output; flag those not on patched train. Daily alert if any unpatched instance remains after 2026-08-01 deadline.

suggestion.title: Adform Script Hash Anomaly – Supply Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers poison Adform script' — Adform is a widely-embedded third-party ad network. Detection must identify when cached/served Adform scripts deviate from known-good signatures. Phrase: 'poison Adform script to swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA256 hashes of Adform script payloads against vendor-published checksums. Alert if production Adform script on CDN or in customer logs differs from baseline. Correlate across multiple customer sites to detect blast radius.

suggestion.title: JavaScript-Based Payment Form Hijacking – DOM Mutation for Wallet Address Substitution
suggestion.rationale: The core attack is 'swap crypto wallet addresses' via injected script. This requires real-time DOM manipulation targeting input fields or JavaScript variables holding payment destinations. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript patterns that replace/override wallet address variables or input field values. Look for regex-based string substitution of common cryptocurrency address formats (0x..., bitcoin addresses, etc.) or API calls that POST wallet identifiers to unexpected endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Inline Script Injection in Third-Party Ad Frames
suggestion.rationale: To inject wallet-swapping logic into Adform's script execution context, attackers must inject new inline <script> tags or modify existing script code. Phrase: 'poison Adform script.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inline <script> tags within ad network iframes (Adform domain) that were not pre-approved or that execute wallet-related function calls. Compare Content-Security-Policy headers and detect CSP bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Crypto Addresses and User Payment Metadata via Malicious Ad Script
suggestion.rationale: Poisoned scripts likely exfiltrate original wallet addresses or private key metadata before substitution. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses' implies capture of victim data before replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected HTTPS POST requests originating from Adform script context to domains outside the ad network's approved C2 or data collection allowlist. Flag requests containing cryptocurrency address strings or key-like hex/base58 patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Blast-Radius Correlation – Adform Customer Site Inventory
suggestion.rationale: The attack affected 'customer sites' (plural, wide blast radius). Detection must correlate Adform script compromise across all organization domains to measure attack scope. Phrase: 'across customer sites.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build CMDB inventory of all internal + customer-facing sites that embed Adform scripts (grep for adform.net, adform.js patterns in HTML). Cross-check against list of sites known to have displayed poisoned script. Calculate blast radius and mean-time-to-detection for each affected site.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Replacement Pattern – Regex Substitution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Wallet-address swapping is a deterministic string replacement attack. Detection can pattern-match against known attacker wallet addresses or identify substitution logic in minified/obfuscated Adform script. Phrase: 'swap crypto wallet addresses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deobfuscate Adform script and search for regex patterns or hardcoded wallet addresses. Compare against known attacker-controlled wallets (via blockchain forensics or threat feeds). Alert on match to any customer site serving that script version.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery via Network Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi pushes fake updates.' Pipeline missed the supply-chain-like delivery mechanism where attacker-controlled network serves counterfeit update packages to connected clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for update process execution (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, svchost.exe, updater.exe) spawned from unusual parent processes or initiated over non-standard update server IPs. Flag update binaries with mismatched signatures or unexpected code-signing timestamps.

suggestion.title: Man-in-the-Middle Attack via Wi-Fi Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'hijacked hotel Wi-Fi'—this is network compromise and traffic interception. Pipeline did not reconstruct this critical initial access vector or suggest detection for ARP spoofing, DNS poisoning, or rogue AP beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal Wi-Fi AP announcements (same SSID, different BSSID/MAC), traffic to unexpected gateways, or ARP spoofing patterns. Correlate client DNS requests to attacker-controlled resolvers or certificate validation failures during update checks to known-good update domains.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Execution and Collection from Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Payload described as 'surveillance malware' but pipeline generated no detection logic for post-execution behavior—screen capture, keylogging, camera/microphone access, or data staging for exfiltration typical of surveillance payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unsigned or anomalous child processes spawned by the injected update binary accessing sensitive APIs (BitBlt, GetDIBits for screenshots; SetWindowsHookEx for keylogging; IAudioCaptureClient for mic access). Monitor for new kernel drivers or DLL injection into explorer.exe, svchost.exe, or dwm.exe.

suggestion.title: Masquerading Update Process from Suspicious Network Origin
suggestion.rationale: Article implies fake updates are indistinguishable to users ('fake updates')—this is masquerading. Pipeline should flag update processes executed with forged digital signatures, mismatched publisher metadata, or served from non-official update CDNs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate digital signatures on all update executables at runtime. Flag processes claiming to be system updates but originating from non-standard paths, launched by network-connected processes, or with code-signing certificates issued by unexpected CAs or with invalid timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Certificate or TLS Traffic During Update Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Man-in-the-middle Wi-Fi hijacking would require SSL/TLS interception or HTTP fallback. Pipeline did not suggest detection for certificate pinning bypass, self-signed update-channel certs, or downgrade attacks from HTTPS to HTTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS connections to update domains with untrusted or self-signed certificates, HTTP-to-HTTPS downgrades in update checks, or repeated certificate validation failures followed by retry on alternative protocols. Correlate with client connecting to non-standard Wi-Fi SSID within 5 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Surveillance Malware
suggestion.rationale: Surveillance malware must exfiltrate data; pipeline generated no detection for C2 callbacks, beaconing patterns, or data exfiltration. No mention of monitoring for encoded/obfuscated command channels typical of hotel-targeted spyware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing patterns from devices post-update: regular outbound connections to uncommon ports (non-80/443), DNS queries for suspicious domains, or data transfer volume spikes to unexpected ASNs. Flag TLS connections to IP ranges hosting known C2 infrastructure or hosting provider bulletproof hosters.

suggestion.title: Failed then successful authorization on same protected endpoint from same source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'leads to process-wide authorization bypass.' Attacker likely probes protected endpoint (fails 401/403), then after SSPP exploit succeeds, retries same endpoint (gets 200). This two-stage pattern is the smoking gun.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate same source/endpoint pair with HTTP 401/403 followed by HTTP 200 within 2–5 minutes. Verify user field changes from authenticated to unauthenticated between attempts. High confidence if endpoint is known-protected (e.g., /api/v1/@apostrophecms/admin-*).

suggestion.title: Multiple PATCH attempts to same piece-type endpoint with $pullAll variations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '$pullAll patch operator' as exploit vector. Attacker likely iterates on payload syntax ($pullAll with different __proto__ paths, constructor chains) until one succeeds. Rapid-fire PATCHes indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources issuing >3 PATCH requests to same ApostropheCMS piece-type API within 60 seconds, with request bodies containing `$pullAll` and `__proto__`. Threshold accounts for legitimate batch operations but catches automated exploitation tooling.

suggestion.title: Prototype pollution side-effect: unexpected property access in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as writing 'arbitrary values to Object.prototype.' This causes unusual permission/property errors in Node.js runtime. Look for error logs indicating prototype chain corruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Node.js/ApostropheCMS application error logs for patterns like 'Cannot set property [__proto__/constructor/prototype]', unexpected permission denials on built-in objects, or 'Object.prototype is not [expected type]'. These indicate successful SSPP mutation.

suggestion.title: Data read-access to protected resources immediately after PATCH to piece-type API
suggestion.rationale: The exploit chain: (1) PATCH with __proto__ pollution → (2) authorization bypass → (3) attacker can now read/write protected data. Detect GET/POST to /api/v1/@apostrophecms/[user|global|admin]/* from unauthenticated source within 1–2 minutes of PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH to ApostropheCMS API with subsequent GET requests to protected endpoints (user, global, admin) from same source as unauthenticated. Measure data volume to detect bulk exfiltration.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500 errors during PATCH attempts before subsequent auth bypass success
suggestion.rationale: Malformed __proto__ payloads may cause server errors (500) before attacker crafts correct syntax. Sequence of 500 → success suggests iterative exploitation and final breakthrough.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sources that issue PATCH to ApostropheCMS APIs with HTTP 500 responses, followed within 5 minutes by successful (200) GET requests to protected endpoints as unauthenticated user. 500→200 pattern + endpoint type change = exploitation + bypass.

suggestion.title: Authenticated user PATCH followed by different source performing unauthenticated access
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may use stolen credentials to exploit (PATCH from one IP), then access from different IP to avoid detection. Prototype pollution is process-wide, so exploit and abuse can be from different sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH from authenticated user (e.g., editor account) to ApostropheCMS piece-type API, followed by HTTP 200 on protected endpoints from a different source with unauthenticated user field, within 10 minutes. Suggests attacker stole editor credentials, exploited, then accessed from separate C2.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Targeting AppVShNotify.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' This is a core attack mechanism with high specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppVShNotify.exe loading SspiCli.dll from unexpected paths (non-system), especially following process creation from spear-phishing artifacts or post-compromise activities. RPCRT4.dll delay-loading behavior is a secondary indicator.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneler Command & Control - ArcBridge / BridgeHead
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies two custom WebSocket-based tunneling tools deployed by Mirage Kitten for 'covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling.' Clear C2 channel distinct from typical HTTP proxies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for non-browser processes initiating WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) to anomalous endpoints, particularly post-exploitation. Correlate with tunneling tool artifacts and network persistence patterns.

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Spear-Phishing with Lookalike Videoconferencing Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' Specific social-engineering lure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment or hiring platform branding, shortened URLs redirecting to file-sharing domains (Google Drive, OneDrive, Mega), and archives with mismatched file extensions. Correlate with phishing-lure infrastructure pattern of lookalike videoconferencing sites.

suggestion.title: Process Discovery and Screenshot Capture by NightLedger
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists NightLedger capabilities: 'process discovery, and screenshot capture.' These are telltale reconnaissance activities for lateral movement and data exfiltration planning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process enumeration APIs (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, EnumProcesses) and screenshot capture libraries (GDI+, DirectX) execution within seconds of DLL hijacking or post-exploitation indicators. Correlate with file writes to suspicious temp locations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Tunneler Deployment in Aerospace/Aviation Organizations
suggestion.rationale: Article states BridgeHead 'being deployed during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.' Indicates secondary-stage deployment pattern after successful initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In aerospace/aviation networks, correlate BridgeHead deployment (WebSocket tunneler executables, configuration files) with prior spear-phishing delivery and DLL hijacking events within 24-72 hours. Monitor for tunneler binaries staged in temp directories or admin shares.

suggestion.title: RPCRT4.dll Delay-Loading SspiCli.dll for Execution Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article explains technical mechanism: 'AppVShNotify.exe...imports RPCRT4.dll, which can delay-load SspiCli.dll when it invokes an RPC API.' This indirect loading pattern evades static-analysis detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AppVShNotify.exe → RPCRT4.dll → SspiCli.dll load chains where SspiCli.dll originates from non-system paths. Pair with behavioral analysis of RPC API calls that trigger delay-load to distinguish legitimate from malicious chains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable FMC Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center as the affected product; federal patch due 2026-08-01 makes this immediately actionable for asset inventory validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Cisco FMC instance with version ≤ patched version in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-reference against network segmentation rules to identify public-facing instances at highest risk.

suggestion.title: FMC Successful Authentication from Unexpected Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account'—auth success from non-standard sources (external IPs, off-hours) should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (typically port 443) for successful logins with low-privileged accounts from external networks or after hours. Hard-coded credentials create consistent auth patterns; anomalies in source geography/timing are high-confidence signals.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Export or Query Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' once authenticated—monitor for data collection activity from FMC console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC auth, watch for bulk exports, scheduled reports, or API queries for firewall rules, policy configurations, or logged traffic data. Hard-coded credential exploitation often precedes mass data pulls within minutes of access.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Account Credential Reuse Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credentials in FMC create repeatable auth signatures—same username/password from multiple sources or repeated failed attempts before success suggest automated exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed then successful FMC logins using identical credentials from different source IPs within short time windows. Hard-coded password exploitation often includes scanner or script retries before successful access.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Changes by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hard-coded low-privileged account, attacker may modify firewall rules, disable logging, or create backdoor accounts—untypical for low-priv role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag config modifications (rules, access lists, authentication settings) performed by low-privileged FMC accounts, especially new account creation or privilege elevation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' — implies FMC is reachable from internet. Pipeline missed asset-exposure detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances accessible from untrusted networks. Query for open TCP ports 443/8305/8307, TLS certificate issuer matching Cisco, or HTTP responses containing 'Firepower' or 'Secure Firewall' banner strings. Correlate with CVE-2026-20316 patch status from vulnerability scanner.

suggestion.title: Authentication Attempts Using Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'hard-coded password' enables login without valid credentials. Pipeline failed to surface credential-use detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC login endpoints for authentication attempts using hardcoded or default account names (if disclosed). Flag successful logins from anonymous/untrusted networks or IP ranges outside known administrative CIDR blocks. Correlate with failed attempts to detect brute-force patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Low-Privilege FMC Accounts
