suggestion.title: Failed and Successful FMC Authentication Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploits often present as multiple failed attempts followed by success—detection must identify this pattern indicative of credential-guessing or known-secret exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous login-attempt patterns: >5 failed attempts to FMC within 5 minutes followed by successful authentication (same or different account) from the same source IP. Track per-source-IP to identify systematic exploitation attempts, and correlate with external scanning to confirm CVE-2026-20316 targeting.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-coded Credential Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'—core attack vector requires detection of successful authentication using the compromised low-privileged built-in account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using low-privileged default accounts from untrusted or internet sources. Alert on any successful auth to internet-exposed FMC from unexpected geographic origins. Baseline expected administrative access to filter noise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Internet Asset Exposure for Active Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implying internet reachability. Article template explicitly mentions 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as required for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances and flag those with internet-routable IPs or exposed management ports (443 typical). Cross-reference against external scanning data. Alert on newly discovered FMC instances appearing in public-facing asset inventories.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-exploitation phase must detect unauthorized data collection via the low-privileged account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for unusual data access patterns by low-privileged accounts, especially to firewall policies, threat intelligence feeds, or system configs. Alert on deviation from baseline access for that account role. Correlate with initial access alerts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due-date 2026-08-01. Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'—scanner-based detection essential even for systems claiming patches are applied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-20316 across Cisco FMC fleet. Cross-validate scanner results against patch records to catch false negatives. Flag all vulnerable instances; prioritize internet-exposed systems. Track remediation against federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Status Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal patch due 2026-08-01 and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Standard asset-exposure hunt per _TEMPLATES for CVE-2026-20316.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset DB for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances; cross-reference with patch management system. Flag any instance running unpatched version. Escalate to leadership for federal compliance tracking (due 2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication from Unexpected Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Any successful authentication to FMC is suspicious; baseline expected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to Cisco FMC from IPs not in corporate whitelist, geographic anomalies, or known malicious sources. Hard-coded credential exploitation typically originates from public scanning infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article core issue: 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Monitor for attempts to use known hard-coded or default Cisco FMC credentials extracted from CVE details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts using Cisco FMC system or default accounts. If CVE details expose specific credential pairs, alert on login attempts with those usernames. Correlate repeated failed attempts with successful bypass.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Account Data Export from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account. Monitor data queries and exports by non-administrative users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data export, API calls, or policy queries initiated by low-privileged FMC accounts. Baseline normal export volume and frequency; flag spikes or exports of security policies, firewall rules, threat intelligence, or configuration data.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Scan & Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies accessible management port (443 or 8305). Monitor for scanning and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume connection attempts to Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305) from unexpected sources. Correlate scanning activity with subsequent authentication events. Flag any source IP that scans then successfully authenticates.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Account Persistence via FMC
suggestion.rationale: After hard-coded credential access, attacker may create new accounts or modify group membership for persistence and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for user account creation, group assignment changes, or privilege modifications performed by low-privileged accounts or shortly after suspicious authentication events. Flag any administrative action from a non-admin context.

suggestion.title: FMC Unauthenticated Remote Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can exploit the management interface. This is explicit initial access; Cisco FMC access logs record source IP, timestamp, and success/failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface ports (443/tcp, 8305/tcp) for successful remote login from non-sanctioned source networks. Baseline and alert on successful access from unexpected geolocations, non-business-hours logins, or access from residential/datacenter IP ranges. Correlate source IP against network asset inventory to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Default Account Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions hard-coded password vulnerability enabling access via 'low-privileged account.' This is credential-reuse at scale once attacker obtains the credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any login attempt using the hard-coded credential (once identified via vulnerability research) from source IPs outside corporate networks. Additionally, baseline legitimate low-privilege account usage patterns in FMC; detect anomalous logins (time-of-day, geolocation, volume) on these accounts, which may indicate credential compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC contains security policies, threat intelligence, network topology. Exfiltration should be detected post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create baseline of policy/config access patterns by role and time-of-day. Alert on bulk exports or downloads of threat rules, network policies, or asset lists by low-privilege accounts, from unusual source IPs, or outside business hours. Monitor for unusually large data transfers from FMC to external or cloud endpoints.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Instance Identification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires public-facing exposure ('public-facing application'). This is reconnaissance/pre-exploitation. Recommend immediate inventory of all FMC instances and network exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and firewall rule databases for Cisco FMC instances with inbound WAN/internet access to management ports. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Alert on any FMC instance identified as both exposed and unpatched, prioritize for emergency patching.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status mandates proactive hunt. Query all vulnerability scanners for Cisco FMC instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 via version identification or banner grab.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cisco FMC instances (via SSH, SNMP, or HTTP banner grabbing on ports 443/8305) for version numbers matching CVE-2026-20316 vulnerable range. Cross-reference with patch deployment records. Alert on instances vulnerable + exposed to untrusted networks + unpatched as of patch due date (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' via 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—the exploit path is the hard-coded credential itself, not just network access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs (typically ports 443, 8305) for successful authentication using default/low-privilege account names (e.g., 'admin', 'readonly') from external IP ranges during unusual hours. Baseline normal FMC login patterns by region/admin and alert on anomalous access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—no detection logic provided for data collection phase, which is the impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk export/backup operations on FMC (configuration downloads, policy rule exports, device inventory dumps). Alert on unusual volume or destination IP for data transfers from FMC to external networks, especially outbound to non-corporate CIDR blocks.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'remote' access to 'affected device'—reconnaissance of FMC version/status is a prerequisite. Pipeline missed version enumeration technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to FMC management interface (e.g., /admin, /api/version, /.well-known endpoints) that probe for version info, product identification, or login pages from non-whitelisted IPs. Flag high-velocity probe patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management console; article does not state scope but compromise could enable attacker to push malicious policies or commands to connected firewalls. Missing entire post-compromise lateral movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC-to-managed-firewall communication for unusual policy pushes, configuration changes, or command execution originating from compromise window. Baseline normal policy update cadence and alert on deviations correlated with unauthorized FMC access.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' as entry point—implies attacker must escalate to admin or sensitive data roles. No detection for in-console privilege escalation attempts or lateral escalation within FMC role hierarchy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for privilege escalation attempts (role changes, group assignments, permission grants) initiated from low-privilege accounts, especially during the exploitation window (post-2026-07-29). Alert on successful role promotions to admin within minutes of initial login.

suggestion.title: FMC Default/Hard-Coded Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article imples existence of hard-coded credentials; no detection for attacker discovery of which account names are active or exploitable on target FMC instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on brute-force or dictionary attacks against FMC login endpoints (>5 failed logins in 60 sec, attempt patterns matching known default usernames). Correlate with vulnerability scanning or exploitation tool traffic signatures.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Manipulation on Widely-Depended Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core attack vector enabling the compromise to 23,000 downstream repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories with 100+ external dependencies for tag creation/modification events where the tag moves to a commit not on the main branch or moves backwards in history. Trigger alert if tag modified by account with no recent commit history in that repository.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secrets Exposed in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states the attack 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and details how secrets 'appear in the build log' despite GitHub's encryption. This is the direct impact method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for regex patterns matching common secret formats (AWS_KEY patterns, JWT tokens, API keys, GitHub PATs, etc.). Cross-reference against declared GitHub secrets to identify unexpected plaintext leakage. Alert on matches in public repositories.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Egress Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External C2 or payload fetch is a key IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner network egress for unexpected HTTPS/HTTP calls to non-GitHub domains. Flag calls to dynamic DNS, short-lived domains, or IP ranges known for C2. Baseline expected domains per organization and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits in High-Value Git Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explains orphaned commits as a key obfuscation technique: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext' via 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches.' Orphaned commits are rare in normal development.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically run `git fsck --full` or query GitHub API for unreachable commits in repositories with high external dependence. Alert on new orphaned commits created by accounts that do not regularly work in main/develop branches. Cross-reference with tag manipulation events.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Access Granted to Supply-Chain Critical Projects
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on' as the prerequisite for the entire attack. Unusual write permission grant is the initial pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new write/admin access grants to repositories with 1000+ external dependencies or high GitHub Stars. Implement peer-review requirement for permission changes on critical projects. Flag grants to inactive or recently-created accounts.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Pointing to Non-Main-Branch Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates that tags can point to orphaned/arbitrary commits: 'GitHub tags are just convenient strings pointing to a particular commit.' Abnormal tag targets bypass branch protection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each release tag in a repository, verify the tagged commit exists on main or a tracked release branch. Alert if a tag moves to a commit with no branch ancestry or if the tag's target commit changes (tag repoint). Use `git log <tag> --not main` to detect off-branch tags.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Authentication — Hard-coded Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' No detection UC for suspicious FMC login patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected sources or rapid authentication attempts. Correlation of failed+successful login pairs within short windows may indicate hard-coded credential exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Exposure — Asset Enumeration and Port Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed' FMC systems are targets; article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' No detection for identifying or monitoring FMC asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanners against network asset inventory for Cisco FMC instances running unpatched builds. Flag externally-routable FMC instances (port 443, admin GUI). Compare against baseline to detect new exposures post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access — Suspicious Collection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' No detection for abnormal data access, export, or exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit/API logs for unusual data queries, policy exports, rule extractions, or sensor configuration downloads from low-privileged accounts. Flag rapid sequential reads of firewall rules, sensor configs, or threat intelligence.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement — FMC as Pivot Point
suggestion.rationale: Article implies FMC compromise grants 'access to sensitive data.' Compromised management console is often used for lateral movement into managed sensors/firewalls. No lateral-movement detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FMC-initiated connection attempts or commands to managed sensors/firewalls that deviate from administrative baseline. Flag unusual sensor queries, rule pushes, or policy changes originating from FMC after a compromise window.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Authentication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device' — detection must monitor authentication to FMC, especially from unexpected origins or with known hard-coded account identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center login events for successful authentications from untrusted IP ranges, multiple failed attempts preceding success (credential spray), or logins using known hard-coded account names. Baseline legitimate administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — detection must capture FMC configuration exports, policy downloads, or database queries by compromised low-privileged accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk exports, configuration backups, or policy file downloads initiated by low-privileged accounts or system service accounts. Flag unusual API queries against FMC databases or config dumps to external destinations.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration or Policy Tampering
suggestion.rationale: A compromised management center (via hard-coded creds) becomes a pivot point to alter firewall rules — article does not restrict impact to read-only access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline authorized FMC configuration change actors and flag unauthorized policy deployments or rule modifications. Alert on disabling security controls, adding allow rules for restricted ports, or modifying access control lists from unexpected accounts.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploited only if FMC management interface is reachable remotely; article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' Asset discovery must identify exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center deployments. Cross-check for internet accessibility on TCP 443/8305 using external port scanners or VPN-less access logs. Flag FMC instances without network segmentation or IP whitelisting.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage in Authentication Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism explicitly 'use of hard-coded password' — detection should surface authentication attempts using known Cisco Secure Firewall hard-coded account names or patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication attempts for known Cisco Secure Firewall hard-coded account identifiers (e.g., default admin or service accounts documented in CVE details). Correlate with threat intelligence feeds for exploitation signatures and known attacker IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FMC REST API Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: FMC exposes management API; 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' scenario is consistent with credential-based or default-credential API abuse on management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC API endpoints (e.g., /api/fmc_config/v1) for successful requests from unexpected source IPs, automated scanning patterns, or API tokens tied to low-privilege service accounts. Flag token reuse across multiple source IPs within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Login via Hardcoded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can log in 'using a low-privileged account' remotely and unauthenticated. Pipeline missed the initial-access foothold: authentication attempts with or without the hardcoded credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC admin/management-interface logins from unexpected external networks. Baseline normal access IPs and flag logins from new sources, especially if preceded by multiple failed auth attempts or at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline should surface credential-access detections: payload fingerprints, known-credential stuffing patterns, or authentication-bypass signatures specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20316 exploit patterns (malformed auth headers, bypass payloads in parameters). Flag repeated auth failures immediately followed by success from same source IP. Alert on credential-reuse patterns or automated scanning tools targeting /admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation collection phase: audit logs, config export, rule enumeration, or credential-store access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a successful FMC login, detect anomalous data-access patterns: export of firewall policies, access to stored credentials, bulk rule/config downloads, or database queries from accounts that don't routinely perform those actions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Affected Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)' as the vulnerable product. Pipeline must identify all FMC instances in the environment and cross-reference patch status against the published vulnerability range.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database and vuln scanner for Cisco FMC instances. Flag any unpatched, internet-routable, or externally-exposed FMC instances. Compare version numbers to CVE-2026-20316 advisory. Prioritize remediation by network exposure (external-facing > DMZ > internal).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Web Interface Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: CVE is mapped to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application.' Pipeline should detect web-layer exploitation: malformed requests, path traversal, payload injection, or known Cisco FMC exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC web server logs for exploitation signatures: unusually long URIs, SQL-injection patterns in parameters, repeated 40x responses followed by 200, or requests with known Cisco exploit payloads. Alert on probing activity targeting common FMC endpoints (/admin, /api, /login).

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can reach the service—network exposure is the attack surface. 'Public-facing application' per T1190 mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances responding on standard ports (443, 8305, 8307) from untrusted networks. Correlate with scanner fingerprinting (FMC version in HTTP headers, SSL certificates containing 'Cisco Secure Firewall'). Identify assets in DMZ or external-facing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Login Attempts to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allows attacker to 'log in'. Article explicitly names this as the exploitation method, not code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login events with known hard-coded vendor defaults. Detect both failed brute-force patterns (T1110.004) and successful logins (T1078.001) from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with FMC access within 1 hour of first login attempt.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise 'could allow...access to sensitive data'—attacker goal is data extraction, not just system access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful FMC login, hunt for bulk export of device configurations, policy documents, firewall rules, or threat intelligence datasets. Look for large outbound file transfers or API queries returning >1MB of policy/inventory data. Detect tools like curl/wget targeting FMC endpoints post-auth.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Policy Rule Modifications Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: With FMC access, attacker can disable defensive rules or create backdoors. 'Access to sensitive data' includes operational control per implied impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for firewall policy changes, rule additions/deletions, or device policy re-assignments immediately following suspicious FMC login events. Look for ruleset deletions that disable threat detection, or creation of new allow-rules for suspicious IPs. Correlate timestamp of config change with attacker login event.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' via hardcoded password; this is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management authentication logs for attempts using known default credentials or hardcoded account names (admin, cisco, etc.). Alert on successful login following repeated failed attempts, or login from untrusted network segments. Correlate authentication source IP with threat intelligence for known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' to reach management interface; implies FMC exposed on untrusted/internet-facing network segment rather than properly segmented management VLAN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management ports (typically 443/TCP for HTTPS, 8305/TCP) accessible from public internet or untrusted networks. Scan externally-facing IP ranges for FMC management interface banners. Alert on network flows from external ASNs or geographies outside expected administrative footprint to FMC management ports.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access and Exfiltration from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-authentication; monitor for data extraction patterns inconsistent with normal FMC administration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for unusual query patterns, bulk data exports, or configuration downloads. Flag sessions that extract policies, access control lists, threat data, or user databases. Correlate authentication logs with data-access events to identify suspicious sessions where low-privileged accounts query sensitive data repositories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Match and Exposure Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article template explicitly directs scanning for 'CVE: CVE-2026-20316' as the primary IOC; vulnerability scanner findings are foundational indicators of actively-exploitable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable, Rapid7, etc.) for CVE-2026-20316 findings on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Prioritize findings matching vulnerable product versions per Cisco advisories. Escalate to emergency remediation workflow given CISA KEV federal due date of 2026-08-01; assume active exploitation in-the-wild.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-facing Cisco FMC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability in 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' context with exposed FMC as attack surface; template itself references _TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure but no asset-hunting use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Cisco FMC instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm patches deployed by federal due-date (2026-08-01). Monitor external IP ranges and public DNS records for Cisco FMC management ports (8305/TCP, 443/TCP) reachable from internet. Use network telemetry to detect inbound connection attempts to FMC from non-corporate IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Hard-coded Password Authentication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hard-coded password vulnerability' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' to 'log in'; credential compromise is the attack primitive but no auth-focused detection use case was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins matching known hard-coded credential patterns (default usernames, vendor-documented weak passwords). Flag successful logins by low-privilege service accounts from unexpected geographic regions or at anomalous times. Correlate rapid-fire failed authentication attempts followed by successful low-privilege logon as indicator of hard-coded credential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Data Access: Sensitive Configuration and Audit Log Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow...access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'; post-exploitation data access patterns not captured in any use case despite being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk export operations, API queries, or database reads targeting sensitive FMC data (firewall policies, device configurations, audit logs, security events) by low-privilege or newly-authenticated accounts. Monitor for automated or scripted data access patterns (high-volume downloads in short time windows). Flag administrative data pulls from accounts lacking historical access to those repositories.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Status Validation: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due-date of 2026-08-01 (3 days); scanner-based compliance and remediation-tracking use case necessary but absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query continuous vulnerability scans for CVE-2026-20316 status across all Cisco FMC deployments. Cross-reference scanner findings with patch-management records to confirm remediation completion. Alert on instances still marked vulnerable as of federal due-date (2026-08-01). Track time-to-patch and flag instances exceeding SLA for regulatory audit trail.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Low-privilege Account Access to Administrative Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains 'low-privileged account' access; lateral escalation or privilege escalation from low-priv to sensitive functions not mapped to MITRE or detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for privilege escalation attempts by accounts designated as low-privilege (readonly, viewer, analyst roles). Detect attempts to access administrative API endpoints, modify policy rules, or export full audit logs by accounts lacking authorization. Flag role-assignment changes or permission grants to compromised low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Script Modifications or Injection via Adform CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that 'hackers poison Adform script' — direct evidence of malicious script injection into a trusted ad-delivery supply chain. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for script-source anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network requests to Adform CDN and detect deviations in script hash, content-length, or response headers. Flag if legitimate advertisement domains begin loading unexpected JavaScript payloads from Adform URLs or if Adform URLs are modified in <script> tags on customer pages.

suggestion.title: Detect Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Replacement in Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'swap crypto wallet addresses across customer sites.' No use case exists to catch this form of DOM manipulation or content injection targeting payment addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of cryptocurrency wallet addresses on monitored e-commerce or payment sites. Alert when JavaScript executes document.replace(), innerHTML manipulation, or regex substitution patterns that target hexadecimal addresses matching common cryptocurrency formats (Bitcoin, Ethereum). Correlate wallet address changes with Adform script injection timeline.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply-Chain Script Sources Diverging from Legitimate Publisher Registrations
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploits trust in Adform as legitimate vendor. Pipeline provided no kill-chain entry for supply-chain compromise. Article phrase 'Adform script' implies origin-trust violation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish known-good Adform CDN IPs, ASNs, and certificate subjects. Flag script-serving endpoints that resolve to unexpected geographic regions, autonomous systems, or TLS certificates not issued to Adform or its parent company. Cross-reference with certificate transparency logs for domain registration anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Simultaneous Malicious Script Activity Across Multiple Customer Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'across customer sites' (plural, widespread impact). Pipeline omitted lateral/multi-site correlation detection. A single compromised script affects all downstream subscribers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate script-injection or wallet-replacement detections across all monitored Adform-subscriber domains within a 1-hour window. High-count aggregation (>5 unique customer domains with same malicious pattern in 60 minutes) suggests supply-chain compromise rather than isolated intrusion. Escalate as critical.

suggestion.title: Detect Attacker-Controlled Cryptocurrency Wallet Addresses in Ad-Tech Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is crypto theft via address replacement. Article establishes specific IOC class (malicious wallet addresses) that should be extracted and correlated with web-injection events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of known attacker-controlled cryptocurrency wallet addresses from threat intelligence. Detect when any registered Adform customer site references these addresses in payment forms, checkout flows, or donation prompts. Trigger alert on first reference and escalate if address persists after 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Detect Script Execution Performing String Replacement on Page Content
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism is runtime string substitution of wallet addresses. Article implies regex or string-replace operations in malicious script payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hook JavaScript String.prototype.replace() and RegExp execution on pages known to handle cryptocurrency payments or addresses. Alert on patterns matching wallet-address regex (Bitcoin: ^[13][a-km-zA-HJ-NP-Z1-9]{25,34}$, Ethereum: ^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$) being replaced with unrecognized values or loaded from unsigned scripts.

suggestion.title: Fake Update Prompt from Compromised Network
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi Pushes Fake Updates.' Pipeline must detect browser-injected or network-intercepted update dialogs prompting users to install malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual update installation attempts initiated from Wi-Fi network traffic patterns. Flag if update domain resolves to non-canonical WHOIS registrant or IP geolocation mismatches vendor headquarters. Correlate with lateral process creation (msiexec, installer spawning unexpected child processes).

suggestion.title: MITM Attack via Compromised Hotel Wi-Fi Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Wi-Fi hijacking as attack vector. Must detect ARP spoofing, DNS hijacking, or certificate interception patterns typical of MITM on public Wi-Fi.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on certificate authority mismatches or expired certs served by Wi-Fi gateway IP. Detect DNS responses from gateway IP (vs. ISP resolver) for known CDN or update domains. Flag simultaneous connections to multiple victims from same gateway MAC/IP within short time window.

suggestion.title: Surveillance Malware Post-Installation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is 'surveillance malware.' Must detect screen capture, audio recording, or credential theft post-execution (T1113, T1123, T1056 behaviors).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to screen/audio APIs (BitBlt, GetDC, waveIn*, AUDCLNT_*). Detect unexpected C2 beaconing from newly installed executable (correlation: installation time + network initiation within minutes). Flag data exfiltration patterns (high bytes out, off-hours, to non-US IP).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Executable Installation from Update Process
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain includes fake update delivery leading to malware install. Detect when update processes spawn or download executables outside vendor-signed paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when update-related process (msiexec, wuauclt, installer variants) creates unsigned executables or DLLs in temp/roaming directories. Flag if update binary's parent process is browser or networking service (svchost, lsass anomaly). Correlate download timestamp with installation timestamp for anomalous delays.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSL/TLS Certificate Usage on Public Wi-Fi
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Wi-Fi implies MITM capability; must detect self-signed or mismatched certificates presented to common update/app domains on hotel networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for self-signed or third-party CA certificates served by non-authoritative IPs for software update domains (Microsoft, Apple, Adobe, etc.). Flag CN/SAN mismatches on HTTPS connections. Correlate certificate anomalies with DNS responses from gateway IP.

suggestion.title: DLL Search-Order Hijacking via SspiCli.dll Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: Article states NightLedger 'masquerades as SspiCli.dll and appears to be designed for DLL search-order hijacking, targeting a legitimate AppVShNotify.exe binary.' Core defense-evasion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SspiCli.dll loads from non-System32 directories or triggered by AppVShNotify.exe. Detect SspiCli.dll file writes to temporary, user-writable, or staging directories. Flag unexpected delay-load patterns from RPCRT4.dll that route through suspicious DLL sources.

suggestion.title: Recruitment and Videoconferencing Phishing Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'recruitment-themed content impersonating trusted brands and hiring platforms, as well as lookalike videoconferencing pages that redirected victims to malicious archives hosted on third-party file-sharing services.' Primary initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with HR/recruitment subject lines from external senders linking to or attaching archive files (RAR, ZIP). Alert on clicks redirecting from recruitment/job-portal domains to file-sharing services (archive.org, mediafire, etc.). Flag lookalike videoconferencing domains (zoom-xxx, teams-xxx variants) redirecting to non-corporate infrastructure.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Backdoor Reconnaissance Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies backdoor capabilities: 'reconnaissance, command execution, file operations, process discovery, and screenshot capture.' Behavioral sequence indicates active post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution chains: tasklist/Get-Process → dir/Get-ChildItem → screenshot APIs (BitBlt, GDI+). Alert on unexpected parent-child relationships where AppVShNotify.exe spawns cmd.exe or PowerShell with enumeration commands. Flag reconnaissance patterns in aerospace/aviation sectors targeted per article.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Tunneling Tool Deployment (ArcBridge/BridgeHead)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'two custom WebSocket-based tunnelers, ArcBridge and BridgeHead, for covert network access and operator-controlled tunneling' deployed 'during post-exploitation activities in victim environments in Egypt and at a Pakistan-based aerospace and aviation organization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound WebSocket (WS/WSS) connections on non-standard ports from system binaries or DLLs. Detect persistent WebSocket tunneling patterns indicative of operator-controlled C2. Alert on WebSocket traffic from Egypt- or Pakistan-based aerospace/aviation infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Tunneling Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article documents BridgeHead deployment 'during post-exploitation activities' following spear-phishing compromise. Indicates transition from access to persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry Run key modifications or startup folder modifications associated with ArcBridge/BridgeHead components. Detect file system writes of tunneling binaries to directories like AppData or ProgramData post-intrusion. Monitor for scheduled task creation or service installation by compromised processes.

suggestion.title: Mirage Kitten Malware Signatures and Attribution Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article names three malware families (NightLedger, ArcBridge, BridgeHead) uniquely developed by Mirage Kitten with specific code and behavioral signatures. Requires signature-based and heuristic detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file-hash and behavioral signatures for NightLedger DLL (masquerade pattern, DLL search-order hijacking). Detect ArcBridge/BridgeHead process execution or module loading. Alert on known code patterns, mutex names, registry markers unique to Mirage Kitten malware in aerospace, defense, telecom, and aviation organizations.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication with Known Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded password is an exploitable backdoor account — need detection for login attempts using known weak/backdoor credentials or abnormal authentication success rates on low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins to known low-privilege backdoor accounts or patterns of rapid authentication attempts from external networks. Baseline legitimate FMC admin access and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unusual FMC Management Interface Access from External/Non-Approved Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote attacker...access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC is a management interface; detect access from unexpected IP ranges, geolocations, or non-management VLANs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FMC web/management interface access (port 443, SSH 22) from IP ranges outside known trusted admin networks or with ASN/geolocation mismatches. Correlate with baseline admin access times.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction / Unusual Queries from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Once attacker gains access via hard-coded credential, they will enumerate and exfiltrate configuration, policy, and audit data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit/query logs for bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or unusual API calls to sensitive endpoints (users, device configs, threat intelligence) from low-privilege or newly-seen accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Compliance and Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01' and 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Asset inventory and scanner must confirm patch status; unpatched FMC instances are high-priority breach risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for instances of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center with version < patched baseline for CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference with firewall rule allows (port 443, SSH) and external reachability tests.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-Coded Credential Exposure in Logs or Configurations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline/SIEM may ingest FMC debug logs, error messages, or configuration dumps where the hard-coded credential leaks; need detection for secrets in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan FMC debug/error output and exported configurations for common hard-coded credential patterns (password=, secret=, key=, admin credentials in plaintext). Flag any exposure in logs or unencrypted backups.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Cisco FMC on Internet-Facing Network
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' establishes prerequisite network exposure of management plane. Vulnerability requires internet reachability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances with TCP 443, 8305, or 22 exposed on external-facing interfaces. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20316 patch status. High-risk if exposed and unpatched.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Abuse — Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article core exploit: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Detection must capture successful auth via known default/hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using default/hard-coded account names (admin, root, default service accounts). Flag successful auth from unexpected external IPs, especially if preceded by failed login probes in prior 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Access from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article objective post-exploitation: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect database queries, policy exports, or config retrieval after successful unauthorized auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful low-privileged FMC account authentication with unusual bulk data operations: firewall policy exports, network topology queries, session log retrieval, or configuration backups inconsistent with that account's baseline activity.

suggestion.title: Failed Auth Spike Followed by Successful Low-Privilege Login — Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Typical exploitation workflow: attacker probes for vulnerability before exploiting. Signature: 3+ failed auths in short window → successful low-priv account login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ failed authentication attempts from single source IP within 5-minute window followed by successful login to low-privileged service account within 10 minutes. Alert especially if source IP is external or not in approved admin whitelist.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Fingerprinting via Banner Grab
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must enumerate vulnerable FMC versions before exploitation. Article references product by name; HTTP/SSH banners leak version identifying exploitable builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connection attempts to FMC interfaces (TCP 443, 22, 8305) for banner-grab patterns: HEAD requests, OPTIONS requests, incomplete SSL handshakes, or SSH version queries. Correlate banner-grabs with subsequent failed auth attempts or exploitation signatures within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-20316 as the vulnerability. Pipeline should generate baseline detection rule matching scanner findings against this CVE ID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset running Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316 in vulnerability scanner output. Cross-correlate with patch status to distinguish known-unpatched from remediated assets.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implying network accessibility. Article template recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline must generate asset discovery rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco FMC instances accessible from untrusted networks (external, DMZ, guest). Flag any FMC management console listening on standard ports (443, 8305) reachable from non-administrative subnets.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'hard-coded password vulnerability'—attacker uses known static credentials. Pipeline should generate rule for authentication probe/success patterns matching this exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins from unexpected source IPs using default or low-privileged accounts within 24 hours of CVE disclosure or suspected exploit campaigns. Correlate with vulnerability scanner confirmation of unpatched FMC.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via unauthenticated, low-privileged account. Pipeline should detect data-access patterns post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within FMC audit logs, identify unusual data queries, report generation, or policy export activity occurring immediately after successful authentication from external sources or unexpected geographies. Flag bulk access to sensitive security policies or network configuration data.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version and Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states federal patch due date 2026-08-01 (now overdue as of 2026-08-03). Pipeline should generate compliance-driven hunt to verify patched state across inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management system for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Extract software version and cross-reference against CISA KEV published patch cutoff date (2026-08-01). Alert on any version older than patched release with a compliance SLA based on CISA directive.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access to FMC — requires asset-inventory hunt for internet-exposed instances. Pipeline identified T1190 but generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances (port 8305, SSL subject CN patterns, Cisco FMC banner probing) accessible from public internet or DMZ. Correlate with organizational asset inventory to flag unmanaged or rogue instances.

suggestion.title: FMC CVE-2026-20316 Credential Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hardcoded password vulnerability...log in to affected device using a low-privileged account.' Detect anomalous low-priv FMC logins from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for low-privileged account logins from non-approved IP ranges, off-hours, or from IPs not in baseline admin-access whitelist. Correlate with failed login attempts preceding successful logins (exploitation pattern).

suggestion.title: FMC Post-Compromise Data Access Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detect unauthorized config/backup export or data queries post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for bulk configuration exports, backup file creation/download, policy export commands, or large network transfers initiated from low-privileged authenticated sessions. Baseline normal admin data-export patterns and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Evasion & False-Negative Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article context: CISA KEV entries exploit patch-lag and scanner false-negatives. Verify vulnerability scanner reports match actual FMC patch status on systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scanner results against Cisco FMC version inventory and patch-management logs. Flag systems where scanner reports 'not vulnerable' but version is known-affected (common with hardcoded-credential vulns due to scanner limitations).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Brute-Force Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password vulnerability implies attackers will attempt known default/hardcoded credentials. Detect rapid-fire auth attempts with common default FMC credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for high-frequency failed login attempts using known-hardcoded credential patterns (cisco/cisco, admin/admin) or dictionary passwords targeting FMC service accounts within 5-min windows from single or distributed sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) contains a use of hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline must detect vulnerable FMC instances via scanner. Referenced TEMPLATES.md shows this is the baseline hunt for any KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances where CVE-2026-20316 is reported as unpatched or present. Cross-reference against Cisco advisories to identify vulnerable version ranges. Alert on any FMC asset exposed to the internet or DMZ given the 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' threat vector and federal due date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Low-Privilege Account Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline must detect unexpected or hard-coded credential usage against FMC login endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for logins using known hard-coded or default service accounts. Flag successful authentications preceded by multiple failed attempts, originating from external IPs, or outside business hours. Correlate failed attempts across multiple FMC instances suggesting credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Configuration Data Access Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' FMC contains encryption keys, firewall policies, and rules. Pipeline should detect anomalous bulk reads or exports of restricted config.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC configuration export operations, bulk policy reads, or encryption key access initiated by low-privilege accounts or non-admin users. Flag unusual volumes of config requests or reads to sensitive objects (threat defense policies, SSL keys, threat intelligence feeds) within 1 hour of suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: FMC Network Exposure via Internet Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article implies FMC is exploited remotely by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker.' Pipeline must identify Internet-facing FMC instances at risk. Article references 'canonical' asset-exposure hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network firewalls for inbound traffic to Cisco FMC default ports (8305/tcp, 8307/tcp) from external networks. Cross-reference FMC inventory against external IP asset databases. Flag any FMC instance reachable from the Internet before federal remediation due date.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within impacted systems'—implies FMC access can pivot to downstream firewall rules, managed devices, threat intel. Pipeline should detect anomalous changes to managed security appliances or policy distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect policy push events, configuration updates, or rule changes on managed firewalls/IPS devices initiated by low-privilege FMC accounts or during windows of suspicious FMC authentication. Correlate timing of FMC compromise indicators with downstream device changes to detect lateral movement via policy distribution.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Pre-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'patch lag is the silent killer. Federal due-date 2026-08-01.' Pipeline should generate compliance hunt distinct from vulnerability scanner—confirming patches actually applied, not just flagging unpatched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cisco FMC fleet against patch management records and version inventories. Confirm CVE-2026-20316 patches are installed (version 7.0.x or later per Cisco advisory) on all instances. Alert on any FMC that remains unpatched 30 days before federal deadline (2026-07-02) to allow remediation window.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Remote Access Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device'—requires detection of external network access to FMC management interfaces (typically ports 443, 8305). Pipeline missed initial-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections from untrusted ASNs or external IPs to known Cisco FMC management ports. Alert on any inbound connections to TCP 443 or 8305 where destination is a known FMC server, especially if source is non-corporate IP space.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—CVE-2026-20316 exploits a hardcoded low-privilege credential. Pipeline did not generate credential-based detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FMC user authentication patterns. Alert on successful login using known hardcoded or undocumented low-privileged accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'service' accounts with default/weak passwords). Correlate with network exposure—external login + hardcoded account = likely exploit attempt.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access from FMC Low-Privilege Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—once authenticated, detect suspicious activities from the hardcoded low-privilege account (policy retrieval, config export, data dump).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for sensitive operations executed by the low-privilege hardcoded account: configuration exports, policy retrievals, object dumps, or user/license queries. Alert on any bulk download or export activity from this account, especially if preceded by external authentication.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—pipeline must surface asset-inventory hunts to verify patching status before deadline. No compliance/asset UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances in your infrastructure against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Flag any unpatched FMC appliances (especially internet-facing). Verify patch deployment logs show successful remediation before 2026-08-01 deadline.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Enumeration Against FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded-credential exploits often preceded by reconnaissance/enumeration. Article implies automated or rapid exploitation attempts. Pipeline should detect failed-login patterns against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 5+ failed authentication attempts against FMC management interface within 10 minutes from a single source IP, especially if that IP is external/untrusted. Correlate with successful authentication using hardcoded account to confirm exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Cisco FMC Instances (Unpatched CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`' — this instruction was ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances exposed to untrusted networks without patches for CVE-2026-20316. Query vulnerability scanners for FMC product version ≤ patched baseline, correlate with network exposure scans (shodan, censys, or internal asset inventory).

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential — FMC Authentication with Default Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' — this is the core attack mechanism, yet no detection for abnormal authentication patterns or known-bad credentials was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful login using low-privileged or default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'root', or vendor-default IDs) from remote, untrusted networks. Correlate with failed authentication attempts (brute-force signature) in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Post-Auth Sensitive Data Access — FMC Configuration/Policy Export
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' — the post-compromise data exfiltration step was not captured in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful authentication to FMC, monitor for high-volume exports of firewall policies, configurations, or network topology data. Flag data downloads to external IPs or unusual export formats (bulk CSV, XML dumps) within minutes of successful auth from anomalous source.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Authentication Source — FMC Admin Access from Unexpected Geography
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention geo-fencing but CISA KEV articles are actively exploited; detection should cover authentication from untrusted regions correlating with observed threat actor campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC administrative access by source IP/geolocation and organization hours. Alert on successful FMC login from IP not in baseline (especially foreign VPNs, compromised infrastructure, or residential ASNs) within CISA KEV active-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attempt Surge — FMC Authentication Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploitation is often preceded or accompanied by scanning; article does not mention brute-force but it is a common attack pattern for 'unauthenticated, remote' access to credential-protected systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spike in failed authentication attempts against FMC admin interfaces (exceeding 5-10 per minute from single source). Correlate with source IP reputation and time-of-day analysis; high-velocity failed attempts may indicate automated credential-spraying.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 exploitation attempt detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes the vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV status).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation patterns (version detection probes, authentication bypass attempts) against Cisco FMC administrative interfaces. Alert on successful authentication immediately following suspicious request patterns.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded credential usage against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentication to Cisco FMC using known low-privileged default or hard-coded account names from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with failed authentication attempts using high-entropy or brute-forced passwords.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized sensitive data access post-authentication anomaly on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after gaining initial access via hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for access to sensitive FMC data (policies, credentials, configurations) within 10 minutes of authentication by low-privileged accounts or from IPs with no prior admin history. Escalate if accessed data is exported or forwarded.

suggestion.title: Cisco Firewall Management Center version enumeration and reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific affected product and CVE; attackers must enumerate FMC version/deployment before exploitation. 'public-facing' nature enables remote reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to common FMC discovery endpoints (version info pages, /admin paths, HTTP headers), banner grabbing attempts, or probes for Cisco-specific HTTP response signatures. Alert if followed by exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against Cisco FMC administrative access
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password vulnerability implies attackers may attempt multiple credential guesses. 'unauthenticated remote attacker' gaining access implies no pre-authentication is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >5 failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC administrative accounts within 5 minutes from a single source IP, especially if followed by a successful login or if source IP geolocates to unusual region.

suggestion.title: Detection of exposed Cisco Firewall Management Center management interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article implies public-facing exposure ('exploit public-facing application'); standard asset-exposure hunt should confirm whether FMC admin interface is accessible from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate that Cisco FMC administrative ports (typically 8305, HTTPS) are NOT externally routable. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 on any internet-exposed Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account'—indicates exploitation via credential compromise requiring detection of authentication attempts with default/hard-coded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication attempts to Cisco FMC using known hard-coded or default low-privilege accounts. Flag failed-then-successful authentication sequences from external IP space within 10-minute window, followed by data-access activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Public Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' combined with T1190 mapping indicates FMC management interface reachable from internet, enabling initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management ports (443/tcp, 8305/tcp) accepting inbound connections from untrusted external IP ranges. Alert on pattern correlation: external SYN-ACK + authentication attempt within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from FMC Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of information discovery/exfiltration following successful authentication to compromised FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk configuration exports, credential queries, VPN tunnel enumeration, or network topology downloads occurring within 5 minutes of low-privilege account login from external source. Flag export-to-external-IP patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Policy Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: FMC access grants attacker firewall rule visibility and modification capability; sensitive data access pattern suggests configuration reconnaissance at minimum, potential for rule tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect policy rule creation, modification, or deletion within 15 minutes following compromised FMC authentication. Flag especially rules affecting inbound internet traffic, disabled rules, or new high-permit-rate policies.

suggestion.title: Post-FMC-Compromise Internal Reconnaissance and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC provides internal topology visibility; article's 'sensitive data' access implies discovery of downstream targets for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After FMC compromise, monitor for new east-west network flows from FMC to internal workstations, servers, or credential repositories it does not normally contact. Correlate with DNS lookups for internal hostnames from FMC.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20316 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as a required detection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) installations matched against CVE-2026-20316. Flag any instance with CVSS critical or unpatched status. Expected FP: scanner false positives if product name is fuzzy-matched; tune on vendor=Cisco AND product regex 'FMC|Firepower.*Management'.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' and directs to 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' for asset-exposure hunts. FMC must be assessed for public routable access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for publicly routable IPs hosting Cisco FMC management interfaces.
