suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Backup/Export Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers with FMC access will attempt to exfiltrate configuration, policies, and threat feeds. Article implies 'sensitive data' access but pipeline generated no UC for detecting suspicious backup or config export operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration backup operations, bulk rule exports, threat-feed downloads, or API calls to FMC backup endpoints initiated by low-privilege accounts or from suspicious source IPs. Flag if backup files are transferred to external recipients or cloud storage.

suggestion.title: FMC Credential Change Anomalies

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for new local account creation, password resets, or privilege escalation of existing accounts, especially during windows of known hard-coded credential exploitation. Correlate timing with unusual login events and data access patterns.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Account Authentication & Default Credential Abuse

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Sensitive Data Enumeration & Exfiltration

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FMC to Managed Security Devices

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor connections from FMC to managed firewall devices outside normal change-control windows. Detect mass policy deployments or credential changes originating from FMC to firewalls. Alert on device-to-device lateral movement post-FMC compromise.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article's core premise: vulnerability is in CISA KEV because it is actively exploited. Must detect vulnerable FMC versions. Phrase: 'Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) contains a use of hard-coded password vulnerability.'

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Ingress Access to FMC Management Console

Alert on successful authentication from IPs lacking prior legitimate-admin history. suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Patterns on FMC

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded account names (e.g., admin, fmcadmin, support, common vendor defaults). Alert on failed login attempts using hard-coded accounts (attacker reconnaissance).

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Low-Privileged FMC Access

suggestion.title: Exploitation Signature Detection for CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV confirms active exploitation campaigns. Cisco will publish detection signatures, IDS rules, or exploitation patterns. Pipeline must operationalize once vendor signatures available. Phrase: 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.'

Monitor for malformed TLS handshakes, anomalous HTTP headers, or specific payload sequences targeting FMC auth endpoints. Alert on exploitation attempts even against patched systems (indicates reconnaissance/scanning). Track attacker IP reputation.

suggestion.title: FMC Instance Discovery and Version Probing Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first locate and fingerprint FMC instances before exploitation. Reconnaissance probes for version/build are early-stage indicators of targeted reconnaissance. Implicit in 'exploitation in the wild' — attackers scanning for vulnerable targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management ports for version-discovery requests (HTTP OPTIONS, /api/fmc/version endpoints, HTTPS banner grabs, login-page fingerprinting). Flag external source probing for FMC presence. Correlate version-probing hits with subsequent exploitation attempts within 48-96 hours to identify attack chains.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Release Tag Commit Reassignment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies tag manipulation as core attack: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the primary obfuscation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags (v30+) in high-dependency repositories are moved to different commit SHAs, especially to commits not on main branch or authored by unexpected accounts. Correlate tag changes with new commit creation and lack of associated branch references.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Detection in Repository Context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes orphaned commits—commits reachable via tags but detached from all branches—as 'one of the key enabling factors' for the attack. 'You can still navigate to that commit, even though it is no longer associated with any existing branch.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan critical repositories for commits accessible via tags or refs but not reachable from any active branch head. Flag orphaned commits created outside established release workflows or by non-standard release accounts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Activity from GitHub Actions Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity'—this is how the attack was discovered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected HTTP/HTTPS requests initiated from GitHub Actions workflows, especially to domains outside approved supplier lists. Alert when external network calls appear in recently modified workflow files or in newly-added action versions.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Secret Exposure in GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack objective and impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Threat model explicitly: 'This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for unmasked secrets matching AWS key, token, or API credential patterns. Alert when plaintext secrets appear in workflows executed immediately after repository modifications, especially on public repositories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via High-Dependency Action Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attack impact quantified: 'About 23,000 GitHub repos use this Action' and affected repos compromised transitively. Attack enabled by 'malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on'—textbook T1195.003.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to action versions used across organization, particularly non-standard version tags. Alert when high-dependency actions (1000+ downstream users) receive unexpected commits or tag reassignments outside normal release cadence.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Account Login Attempts

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match

suggestion.title: FMC Management Port Exposure Detection

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Authentication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful login with hard-coded credential, hunt for data access patterns anomalous to low-privileged accounts: bulk policy exports, rule configuration downloads, threat intelligence feeds accessed, or user/host inventory enumeration.

suggestion.title: FMC Account Enumeration Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article references hard-coded 'low-privileged account' implying attackers must first discover or test account names. No detection for account discovery/enumeration against FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or sequential login attempts against common/documented hard-coded account names on FMC (e.g. admin, service, default accounts published in advisories). Flag failed attempts followed by success within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: FMC to Protected Network Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management control-plane; compromise enables lateral movement into protected networks managed by the appliance. Article implies 'sensitive data' includes managed device inventory and configurations, facilitating pivot attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal FMC-to-managed-device traffic (policy pushes, health checks). Alert on anomalous outbound connections from compromised FMC to managed security devices (firewalls, IPS, switches) outside expected management patterns or using non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts on FMC

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center authentication logs for login attempts using known hard-coded credentials, especially from external or unexpected networks. Flag successful logins with low-privileged accounts that bypass normal credential validation.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Exposure from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' access—the management interface must be internet-exposed; detecting exposure is initial access prevention
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces (typically ports 443, 8305) reachable from external IP ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-20316 to identify exposure windows and patch lag indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access or Exfiltration from FMC

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual query volume, policy exports, configuration changes, or intelligence data access within FMC following successful authentication with low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Low-Privileged FMC Account

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track privilege escalation or lateral movement attempts initiated from low-privileged FMC accounts. Flag configuration changes, policy modifications, or admin account creation that would normally require elevated authorization.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Bypass Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tools for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center running unpatched versions. Cross-reference with firewall rules and external IP scanners to identify instances accessible from internet or untrusted networks.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes remote exploitation of 'public-facing' management center—attackers likely scan for exposed FMC instances before attempting authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or probes targeting FMC standard ports (443, 8305, 8307, 8308) from external IPs. Alert on any successful connection attempts to management ports from untrusted networks, especially those followed by HTTP POST/API calls.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attacks Against FMC Low-Privilege Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' is compromised—attackers enumerate or brute-force valid usernames on FMC console.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Authentication on Cisco FMC

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Externally Exposed
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1190 context and article premise require 'public-facing application' — should detect FMC management access reachable from internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Cisco FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8307) accessible from untrusted external networks. Cross-reference firewall allow rules and asset inventory to identify exposure gaps.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance Gap—CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due date 2026-08-01 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—should hunt for unpatched FMC instances before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner and asset database for Cisco FMC versions pre-dating CVE-2026-20316 patch release. Prioritize systems with external management exposure and alert on patch non-compliance relative to federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: iOS Malware Deployment via Leaked Exploit Kit — GHOSTBLADE
suggestion.rationale: Article states Chinese actor 'uses leaked DarkSword Kit to Deploy GHOSTBLADE on iOS'—core attack flow completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search iOS device events for GHOSTBLADE process spawning, file writes, or unsigned code execution. Correlate against known malware signatures and DarkSword kit code patterns. Flag any iOS app installation preceded by exploit-kit staging artifacts.

suggestion.title: Leaked DarkSword Kit Component Transfer or Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'leaked DarkSword Kit' as the delivery mechanism; pipeline extracted zero artifacts or signatures tied to the kit itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network transfers or file downloads matching known DarkSword kit signatures, code-signing certificates, or builder components. Alert on infrastructure serving leaked kit binaries or staging servers.

suggestion.title: Chinese APT Malware Campaign Targeting iOS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes activity to unnamed 'Chinese Threat Actor'; pipeline failed to identify the actor or correlate campaign indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 domains, IP ranges, or SSL certificates associated with Chinese APT groups known to deploy GHOSTBLADE. Flag iOS devices establishing outbound connections to these infrastructure assets or using known malware communication protocols.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Persistence or Privilege Escalation on iOS
suggestion.rationale: Deployment of GHOSTBLADE on iOS implies post-install capability establishment; pipeline did not map persistence or privilege-escalation techniques to any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GHOSTBLADE app behavior post-installation for unusual permissions, background activity, daemon spawning, or kernel vulnerability exploitation attempts. Correlate against jailbreak signatures or iOS sandbox bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: Passkey authentication without User Verified flag
suggestion.rationale: Article states core vulnerability: 'relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor.' Detection should flag auth events where UV=false when passkey MFA is claimed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on passkey authentication assertions where User Verified flag is absent or false, or where signature verification reports UV=0 in the attestation object. Passkey claims MFA compliance but cryptographic proof of user presence is missing.

suggestion.title: Bulk passkey device registration from atypical locations
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface involves exploiting passkey implementation; attackers likely register multiple authenticators. Article mentions 'novel attack surface' suggesting account compromise workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ passkey registrations on an account within 24h, especially from geographically distant or impossible-travel locations, or from non-corporate IP ranges. Attacker establishing persistent access post-credential-bypass.

suggestion.title: Passkey authentication with malformed or missing attestation
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit: validation gaps in passkey implementation. Should monitor for cryptographic failures or truncated attestation structures that indicate attacker tooling or improper client-side validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on passkey challenge-response pairs where attestation object is truncated, signature fails verification, or client claims successful UV when challenge hash does not match server state. Indicates interception or replay attack.

suggestion.title: Passkey authentication from high-risk browser extensions or malware contexts
suggestion.rationale: Passwordless attack surface includes malware/extension interference with passkey flows. Article title signals 'novel attack surface'; delivery vectors likely include malicious tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate passkey authentication success with concurrent execution of unsigned browser extensions, process creation by extension processes, or keylogger-like module loading. Malware may intercept passkey UI or fake authentication prompts.

suggestion.title: Impossible-travel passkey authentication sequences
suggestion.rationale: Passkey compromise would enable remote access; geolocation anomalies indicate account takeover. Article's attack premise is unauthorized authentication via validation bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag passkey authentications from 2+ geographically distant locations within impossible travel time (e.g., 100+ km in <1 hour). Suggests attacker using stolen or compromised passkey material.

suggestion.title: Passkey recovery or re-registration abuse post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once passkey validation is bypassed, attacker may perform account recovery, password reset, or passkey re-enrollment to maintain persistence. Article mentions MFA downgrade as endgame.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account recovery flows (security key re-registration, email/SMS reset) initiated shortly after successful passkey authentication anomalies. Attacker consolidating control post-bypass.

suggestion.title: N-central Server Exploitation and Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Headline: 'Attackers Take Over N-central Servers'—establishes active exploitation; pipeline generated no initial-access detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central web interface for exploit patterns (SQL injection, command injection, path traversal) in HTTP request logs. Alert on unusual HTTP response codes (500→200 transitions) suggesting successful code execution, or scriptblock logging showing PowerShell spawned from IIS/N-central process.

suggestion.title: Attacker Persistence After Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Headline: 'Attackers Take Over'—implies sustained access requiring persistence mechanisms; pipeline missed this kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new local user accounts on N-central servers, installation of scheduled tasks with suspicious binaries, modification of IIS application pools, or deployment of web shells in wwwroot directories. Establish baseline of legitimate service accounts and trigger on deviations.

suggestion.title: Re-Compromise Detection Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Headline: 'Initial Fix Proves Incomplete'—indicates attackers regained access after patch attempt, suggesting backup persistence or exploitable vulnerability in the patch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish FIM baselines of N-central application binaries and config files pre-patch. Post-patch, alert on unexpected file modifications in protected directories or process execution spawning unusual child processes. Monitor for attempts to disable or uninstall endpoint protection.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Compromised N-central
suggestion.rationale: Successful sustained server compromise requires C2 channel; title indicates 'take over' (implying active control); pipeline generated zero C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries to newly registered or suspicious domains from N-central server IP. Detect beaconing patterns (regular outbound connections at fixed intervals) or unusual port combinations (DNS on 443, HTTP on high ports). Cross-reference against abuse feeds and OSINT databases.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Downstream Customers
suggestion.rationale: N-able operates an MSP platform; compromised N-central likely used for pivot into customer environments; pipeline missed this impact chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from N-central servers to unexpected IP ranges outside normal RMM behavior. Detect PowerShell remoting or WMI process creation targeting external systems. Alert on credential usage patterns consistent with attacker enumeration of customer networks.

suggestion.title: Model Load Triggers Unexpected Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states arbitrary code execution via model repositories; pipeline missed the primary attack vector. Article phrase: 'Flaws Could Let Model Repositories Execute Arbitrary Code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process is Python interpreter with active diffusers/huggingface_hub library imports; spawns child process with suspicious CLI (cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash, curl, wget). Correlate with huggingface.co TLS/DNS activity within 30 seconds of parent spawn.

suggestion.title: Diffusers Package Fetched from Non-Official PyPI Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise vectors require detection of dependency resolution anomalies. Pipeline generated no IOC or use case for this. Article premise: compromised/flawed repository distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: pip/Python package manager resolves diffusers, transformers, or torch dependencies to non-canonical registry (not pypi.org, not official mirror). Inspect pip install command-line, HTTP Host headers, and DNS queries for registry access.

suggestion.title: Pickle Deserialization of Downloaded Model Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Hugging Face model serialization (especially .pkl-based) is a known arbitrary-code-execution vector via unsafe deserialization. Article does not specify but title emphasizes execution risk. Pipeline missed this common attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Python process opens .pkl or .bin file from cache directory (~/.cache/huggingface) in read mode, then spawns subprocess or calls os.system/subprocess.run shortly after. Monitor for file I/O patterns consistent with pickle.load() followed by code execution.

suggestion.title: Hugging Face Repository Access Followed by Shell Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Behavioral correlation of model download with execution. No use case generated despite this being the core kill-chain link described in the headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: TLS traffic to huggingface.co (SNI analysis) within 10 seconds precedes spawning of /bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, or pwsh from Python parent process. Exclude whitelisted CI/training workloads.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Diffusers Version Loaded from Local Cache
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverage requires presence of unpatched diffusers library. Pipeline did not flag version-specific IOCs or cache-integrity checks. Article title: 'Diffusers Flaws.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Python application imports diffusers from site-packages or user cache with version string < patched release (determine from CVE timeline). Correlate import with subsequent process spawning or network I/O from same process.

suggestion.title: Model Config Tampering (config.json Signature Mismatch)
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may inject malicious config or hook scripts into model artifacts. Pipeline generated no integrity-check use case. Article premise: model repositories themselves host flaws, implying artifact manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File writes to ~/.cache/huggingface/models/*/config.json or tokenizer.json with timestamps deviating from official release window. Compare file hash against published model card or block unsigned modifications.

suggestion.title: Artifactory Zero-Day Exploitation via API
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Artifactory Zero-Day' was exploited. No detection rule for Artifactory API abuse was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifactory API for exploit payloads matching known zero-day patterns, unusual HTTP methods on /api/ endpoints, and responses indicating code execution. Correlate with failed authentication followed by successful system access.

suggestion.title: Model Repository Mass Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exfiltration of OpenAI models from Artifactory. No detection for bulk repository access or data staging was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >50 MB downloads from model repositories in <1 hour, especially from service accounts or unusual geo-locations. Flag compressed archives or bulk .bin/.pth/.safetensors downloads targeting multiple model versions.

suggestion.title: Service Account Compromise Post-Artifactory
suggestion.rationale: Article references compromise before Hugging Face breach—implies lateral movement. No detection for post-exploitation service account abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service accounts tied to Artifactory making unexpected API calls to external cloud services (HuggingFace APIs, GitHub, cloud storage). Baseline normal service account activity per account and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Artifactory Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation typically includes reconnaissance. Article does not describe credential discovery tactics but they are a prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifactory for password reset activity, token generation, and credential listing commands (AQL queries for secrets). Alert on multiple failed auth attempts followed by valid access using extracted credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deployment to Production Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of model repositories typically precedes deployment of poisoned models. Pipeline missed detection for artifact deployment anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag deployments of model artifacts from non-standard Artifactory accounts, outside change-control windows, or to production environments without approval tickets. Correlate with file hash changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco FMC Administrative Access via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—the core exploit path. Maps directly to T1078 (Valid Accounts) + T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (HTTPS port 443 typical) for successful or repeated failed logins from external/untrusted IPs. Flag authentication attempts using known hard-coded account names. Correlate with FMC version inventory to identify vulnerable deployments.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow...access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Detection must focus on unusual configuration/policy exports and data queries from authenticated FMC sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-scale policy/configuration exports, user database queries, or threat data retrieval in rapid succession from a single FMC session. Flag any data transfers from FMC to external IPs. Monitor API calls to sensitive endpoints (user accounts, device configs) in abnormal patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means actively exploited in the wild. Article: 'observed exploited in the wild.' Network-level signatures required immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy signatures for CVE-2026-20316 payloads targeting FMC management endpoints. Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests from external sources to FMC default ports/paths. Flag attempts to bypass authentication or inject hard-coded credentials into request parameters.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attacks Against FMC Hard-coded Account
suggestion.rationale: Known hard-coded password creates a predictable attack surface. Defenders must monitor for credential-guessing attempts against the identified account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed authentication attempts to FMC targeting vendor-default or common hard-coded usernames. Alert on >5 failed logins within 5 minutes from a single source IP. Correlate with successful login events to detect potential compromise.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Cisco FMC Version Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer'—automated asset inventory discovery is essential. Federal patch due date 2026-08-01 requires urgent remediation timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query internal asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Compare versions against Cisco's published patched release list for CVE-2026-20316. Flag any instance running vulnerable version as critical priority for patching before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposed to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access affected device. Implies FMC is reachable from untrusted networks. T1190 requires public-facing exposure; baseline asset-exposure hunt is the first gate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (TCP/443, HTTPS, known banners) visible on public-routable IP space. Confirm port 443 open + Cisco FMC service banner or certificate CN. False positives: intentional cloud-hosted FMC SaaS instances managed by Cisco.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts Against Cisco FMC Default Account
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password implies attacker tries known default credentials. Article: 'low-privileged account'. Brute-force attempts on default service accounts are detectable in FMC logs and auth systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed authentication attempts within 1 minute against FMC admin interface, originating from single IP, using known default account names (e.g., admin, cisco, fmcadmin). Investigate if source IP is outside normal admin ranges.

suggestion.title: Successful Authentication Using Hard-coded / Service Account Credentials on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'. If attacker obtains hard-coded password (via prior disclosure or leak), successful login with that credential is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful login to Cisco FMC using known service/default account names (cisco_service, fmc_api, admin@localhost, etc.) from unusual geographic region, off-hours, or first time in baseline. Establish baseline of which service accounts should ever authenticate interactively vs. API-only.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Cisco FMC via Sensitive API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'. FMC stores security policies, access control lists, firewall rules. Detection of data export/download from FMC API or database after authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on calls to FMC API endpoints that export bulk security objects (policies, ACLs, threat intelligence feeds) or database queries dumping configuration tables, especially from recently-authenticated low-privilege accounts. Threshold: >100 MB of config data requested in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Admin or Service Account Creation on Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence: attacker logs in with hard-coded credential, creates new admin account to maintain access. Article implies attacker 'access sensitive data', next step is securing backdoor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new admin or API service accounts on Cisco FMC, especially if created by low-privilege account or from unusual source. Correlate with prior authentication spike using default credentials. Flag if new account name matches common persistence patterns (e.g., svc_*, backup_*, mgmt_*).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Network Management Traffic to Suspicious Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker compromises FMC (central management), they can redirect or exfiltrate data via FMC's own C2 channels. Detection of FMC reaching unexpected external IPs after compromise event.
log_sources: DNS query logs from FMC host
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Cisco FMC host (after confirming it's compromised via prior UCs). Alert on FMC reaching non-Cisco infrastructure, non-whitelisted domains, or IPs flagged as C2/malware hosting. Expected traffic: Cisco license servers, Cisco cloud threat feed updates, managed firewall clusters.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Default Credential Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Must detect successful authentication using hard-coded/default credentials against Cisco FMC administrative interfaces from non-corporate IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Cisco FMC admin console using known default account names or from external/suspicious IP ranges. Correlate failed login attempts preceding successful authentication. Flag logins followed by configuration export or database query activity.

suggestion.title: Exposed Cisco FMC Internet Accessibility Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' can access; implies public exposure. Asset-exposure hunt required to enumerate vulnerable instances on internet-routable networks per CISA KEV guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CVE-2026-20316 against network/asset scanners; hunt for Cisco FMC listening on ports 443/8305 in external-facing VLAN segments. Cross-reference SHODAN, Censys, or SSL certificate logs for FMC admin interface exposure. Alert on any external successful connection.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Access from Compromised Cisco FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-compromise data collection must be detected once default credentials are used to authenticate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for unusual database exports, policy backups, or configuration downloads initiated by default/low-privilege accounts post-login. Detect large data transfers or uncommon query patterns. Correlate with egress traffic spikes to non-managed IPs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Configuration Changes Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains write access via 'low-privileged account to access sensitive data.' Detect malicious policy/configuration modifications affecting firewall rules and logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track administrative configuration changes in Cisco FMC, especially policy modifications, access control rule changes, and logging setting adjustments by default/compromised accounts. Flag changes that disable security controls or audit logging.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry mandates remediation by 2026-08-01; detection must identify unpatched Cisco FMC instances across fleet to prioritize remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners, CMDB, and Cisco FMC telemetry to identify all instances running vulnerable versions. Cross-reference with network segmentation data to flag externally-exposed vulnerable instances for immediate isolation/patching.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly instructs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for this CVE and references asset-exposure hunt templates. This is the foundational detection for remediation workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and network inventory databases for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances. Identify unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Cross-reference against patch compliance records to surface exposed assets requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability...allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in'. Detection must focus on authentication to FMC management interface using known hard-coded low-privileged account identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface (default ports 443, 8305) authentication logs for successful login attempts using hard-coded low-privileged account names originating from external/untrusted networks. Correlate successful auth with vulnerability scanner data confirming unpatched CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface External Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) and CISA KEV definition requires active wild exploitation—implies FMC is internet-exposed. Detection should identify externally-reachable management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to FMC default management ports (443, 8305, 10443) from external/untrusted IP ranges. Correlate with network recon signatures (port scans, banner grabs targeting Cisco FMC). Alert on successful connection establishment from unexpected geography or ASN.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Post-Auth Sensitive Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states hard-coded password grants access to 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'. Need post-compromise detection for unusual configuration or policy data queries after successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for authenticated sessions querying sensitive objects: firewall policies, access control rules, VPN configurations, user accounts. Baseline normal administrative queries and alert on high-volume or atypical data access patterns following successful authentication from external sources.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance for Cisco FMC Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite to exploitation: attacker must discover FMC instances. Article implies CISA KEV campaigns are scanning for affected public-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network probes targeting Cisco FMC characteristic ports and fingerprint patterns (Cisco-specific SSL certificates, HTTP response headers). Flag successful banner grabs or service enumeration followed by authentication attempts within minutes. Correlate with external shodan/censys queries for 'Cisco FMC' or default ports in recent scans.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Login to Cisco FMC via Hard-coded Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—this is the primary attack vector and must-detect pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC (TCP 8305, 8302) from external/non-trusted networks using low-privilege or default accounts. Correlate with multiple failed auth attempts from the same source within a 5-minute window (hard-coded cred validation → exploit chain).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Exposed to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application); FMC must be reachable from untrusted networks. CISA KEV entry implies active internet-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to Cisco FMC standard ports (TCP 8305 HTTPS, 8302 Health Monitor, 443) from public-routable IP space. Flag any FMC instance accepting management traffic from internet-facing subnets as critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—post-compromise, attacker exfiltrates firewall configs, threat policies, access logs, and device backups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk configuration exports, threat policy backups, or access log downloads initiated by low-privilege accounts. Alert on .zip/.tar file transfers to external IPs or non-standard SFTP destinations.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force or Reconnaissance of Hard-coded Credential Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Attackers probe for hard-coded credential validity before/after network scanning. Multiple failed logins followed by success indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ failed authentication attempts to FMC within 5 minutes from a single source IP, followed by successful login with a low-privilege account. This pattern is high-fidelity for hard-coded cred exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Firewall Rule or Access Control Modification via Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, attacker modifies access control lists, NAT rules, or threat policies to persist, exfiltrate data, or enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on changes to ACLs, NAT policies, threat rules, or user accounts made by low-privilege FMC accounts. Cross-reference with login anomalies (external IPs, off-hours access) and compare against change-control baselines.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Scanner Detection for Cisco FMC Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV template prescribes asset-exposure scanning; CVE-2026-20316 is the scanner-checkable IOC that instantiates this pattern for this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner to detect FMC instances affected by CVE-2026-20316. Flag any 'vulnerable' or 'unpatched' status and cross-reference network exposure logs to identify internet-facing instances as immediate remediation priority (federal deadline: 2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Scan — CVE-2026-20316
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'use of hard-coded password vulnerability' in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center; CISA KEV implies active exploitation. Asset-exposure hunt is critical first step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instance with CVSS score >7.0 for CVE-2026-20316. High confidence indicator of exploitability and federal remediation deadline (2026-08-01) enforcement.

suggestion.title: Anomalous FMC Remote Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account' — need to surface successful auth after failed attempts or from unexpected network context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful login to FMC low-privileged account (e.g., admin-ui user) after ≥3 failed attempts from same source IP, or successful login from anomalous geo/AS following failed auth sequences.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access or Configuration Export
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — attacker post-compromise will exfiltrate firewall rules, VPN credentials, or policy configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy export, configuration backup retrieval, or large file transfers from authenticated FMC sessions immediately following successful login anomalies. Combine with failed-auth spike in 10-minute window prior.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy or Access Control Rule Modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise lateral movement or persistence: attacker modifies firewall rules to allowlist malicious traffic or disable security controls. Article implies full 'access to sensitive data' — modification rights likely follow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of firewall access control lists, network objects, or VPN policies during or immediately after anomalous authentication events. Flag rule changes that broaden inbound or outbound access.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' implies internet-exposed management port. Pre-exploitation reconnaissance via port scanning or service enumeration is necessary before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning or service probing of typical FMC management ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external IPs. Flag repeated connection attempts to closed or filtered ports followed by successful connection on standard HTTPS port.

suggestion.title: FMC Default or Hard-coded Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'hard-coded password' allows low-privileged default account access. Pipeline should hunt for evidence of default credential use patterns in authentication logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Surface any successful login using documented Cisco FMC default account names (e.g., 'admin', 'service' accounts). Flag logins where password field contains predictable patterns or matches public PoC exploit code.

suggestion.title: Malformed DHCPv6 Option Injection to OpenWrt Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Article states there exists a 'flaw' in DHCPv6 handling on OpenWrt. 'Unauthenticated Attackers' phrase indicates network-level exploitation vector with no credential barrier—suggests packet-injection attack on DHCPv6 daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound DHCPv6 packets (UDP 547/546) for oversized option fields, malformed TLVs, or RFC 3315 constraint violations. Correlate with dnsmasq/odhcpd process anomalies, crashes, or error log spikes on OpenWrt systems.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Child Process from DHCPv6 Service
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states attackers can 'Run Code as Root'—must detect privilege escalation. DHCPv6 daemons run as non-root by default; spawning root processes is post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes with uid=0 are spawned by DHCPv6 daemons (dnsmasq, odhcpd, udhcpc). Correlate with preceding DHCPv6 traffic spikes. Baseline: these daemons should never spawn root children under normal operation.

suggestion.title: Shell or Command Execution Spawned by DHCP Service
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Run Code as Root'—detection must cover shell spawning at root privilege. This is the direct impact of the DHCPv6 vulnerability exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sh/bash/ash execution by or parented to DHCP processes with uid=0. Include patterns for reverse shells, command substitution via /dev/tcp, or eval() of network-supplied input. Correlate timing with suspicious DHCPv6 requests.

suggestion.title: OpenWrt Daemon Crash Cascade from Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts typically trigger memory safety violations before successful code execution. 'Flaw' in protocol handling suggests buffer overflow or similar memory-based vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire daemon restarts (dnsmasq/odhcpd: 3+ restarts in 120 seconds) with associated segfault or abort() log messages. Correlate with malformed DHCPv6 traffic or anomalous option sizes preceding each crash.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cron or Config Modification Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Root code execution enables persistence establishment. Though title does not detail post-compromise steps, detection should cover typical OpenWrt persistence mechanisms (crontab, startup scripts, config injection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/crontabs, /etc/init.d, /etc/config/*, /root/.ssh for unexpected modifications correlated with root process spawning. Flag new user/account creation or sudo rule injection in /etc/sudoers.

suggestion.title: External DHCPv6 Solicitation from Untrusted Network Segment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Unauthenticated Attackers'—attack surface is any network segment where DHCPv6 is exposed. Baseline expected DHCPv6 clients and flag external probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DHCPv6 SOLICIT/REQUEST from external/WAN-side sources or non-LAN IP ranges. OpenWrt routers should only receive DHCPv6 client requests from expected internal subnets. Alert on source IPs from public ranges attempting DHCPv6 interaction.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Unauthorized Remote Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—need detection for successful login from unexpected sources using the hardcoded account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful remote logins from untrusted IP ranges using low-privileged default accounts. Correlate with failed login attempts in preceding window to detect brute-force vectors. Alert on any authentication outside known management subnets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Hardcoded Password Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms CISA KEV status (actively exploited in wild)—need direct exploit detection signature for the hardcoded password authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FMC management interface for authentication bypass attempts, submission of default/hardcoded credentials, or exploitation patterns targeting password validation logic. Flag requests containing known hardcoded account strings or unusual auth parameter structures.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access via Compromised Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems'—once authenticated via hardcoded password, attacker can query firewall configurations, credentials, network intelligence, and threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual API queries or data exports from low-privileged sessions targeting sensitive FMC objects (firewall rules, VPN credentials, network topology, policy configurations). Alert on bulk exports, sequential access to multiple protected objects, or data transfer to external destinations from the compromised account.

suggestion.title: FMC Policy Modification via Exploited Account
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of Firewall Management Center grants attacker ability to modify security policies, disable rules, or alter firewall configurations at scale—article does not restrict this capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for policy changes, rule modifications, or administrative configuration changes initiated from low-privileged sessions. Alert on disable of security policies, whitelisting of suspicious IPs, changes to access control rules, or policy deployment anomalies.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Authentication to Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed the core attack vector—authentication using known hardcoded credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for successful authentication using default/service accounts from unexpected source IPs, especially from internet-routable addresses. Baseline legitimate FMC admin access and alert on deviations in account usage, source geography, or session patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access Following FMC Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-authentication data collection is a distinct detection opportunity pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track authenticated sessions to FMC for bulk queries on sensitive assets: firewall rules, VPN configurations, network topology, threat intelligence feeds, or user credentials. Flag multi-asset queries or exports from low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—requires the FMC management interface to be accessible externally. Pipeline should detect exposed FMC on ports 443 or 8305.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-routable Cisco FMC management endpoints via banner enumeration (FMC version strings on typical management ports). Flag inbound network traffic to FMC management IPs from untrusted ASNs or cloud IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Access Without MFA
suggestion.rationale: Hardcoded password exploitation implies successful authentication without multi-factor enforcement. Pipeline should detect MFA bypass or MFA-absent logins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins to default/service accounts where multi-factor authentication was not enforced or not completed. Correlate with failed MFA attempts immediately prior.

suggestion.title: Configuration Changes Post-FMC Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via hardcoded credentials, attacker may modify firewall rules for persistence or create backdoor access. Article implies sensitive data 'access'—may involve rule modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for policy or ACL modifications originating from low-privilege accounts, unusual source IPs, or off-hours. Flag rule changes that weaken restrictions or create broad allow policies inconsistent with change control baseline.

suggestion.title: FMC Remote Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' to FMC device—core attack vector requiring detection on management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Firewall Management Center administrative interfaces for unauthenticated or low-privileged authentication attempts from internet-facing addresses. Alert on successful logins using hardcoded account names or payload patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20316 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credential Account Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article's vulnerability core: 'use of hard-coded password' enabling login as 'low-privileged account'—need detection for default/embedded credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to Cisco Firewall Management Center using hardcoded or default account credentials. Pattern-match on known FMC default account names, failed attempts followed by successful low-privilege login, and replay of same credential across disconnected sessions.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies post-compromise impact: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—need detection for unauthorized retrieval of firewall policies, credentials, and configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Firewall Management Center for unusual access to sensitive repositories (firewall rules, device credentials, policy configurations) by low-privileged accounts. Alert on bulk exports, API queries for credential objects, or data staging after initial compromise.

suggestion.title: FMC Management Interface Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190)—need asset discovery detection for internet-routable FMC administrative interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances with administrative management ports (443, 8305, 22) exposed to untrusted or public networks. Correlate with patch-status and known CVE-2026-20316 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco Firewall Management Center Public Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states FMC is exposed and unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit. 'Public-facing' in T1190 mapping and federal agencies must remediate by 2026-08-01 imply active scanning. Pipeline failed to generate canonical asset-exposure hunt mentioned in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound probes to Cisco FMC typical ports (443, 8305, 8307) from external or unusual internal sources. Correlate with vulnerability scanner activity or port scans. Baseline known management subnets and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Login via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'hard-coded password vulnerability...allow unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline missed credential-access detection entirely despite explicit authentication vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts and successful sessions from external IPs or anomalous geographies. Alert on successful logins followed by low-privileged account enumeration or configuration access. Baseline legitimate management access.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' after login. Post-compromise collection phase completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk data exports, policy retrievals, or sensitive object queries (managed device configs, threat intelligence, user credentials) from FMC after new or anomalous authentication sessions. Alert on configurations or intelligence data leaving FMC to unexpected destinations.

suggestion.title: FMC Lateral Movement to Managed Devices
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of management center historically precedes compromise of managed devices. Article implies access to 'impacted systems' (plural) but pipeline missed lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FMC compromise indicators with anomalous commands or policy pushes to managed Firewall/IDS devices. Monitor for unauthorized device firmware updates, config changes, or credential resets issued from the management center.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Cisco FMC Public Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker' which requires FMC to be network-accessible from untrusted sources. This is the necessary entry condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful TCP connections to Cisco FMC ports (443 HTTPS, 8305 admin interface) from external/untrusted IP ranges. Alert on FMC login pages accessible from internet-routable sources. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability scan results to identify exploitable instances.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'hard-coded password'—attacker must either know the credential or brute-force it. Authentication logs must be monitored for default/weak credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC login attempts for known hard-coded or default usernames (admin, fmcadmin, etc.). Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts followed by successful login from external source IPs, or on successful logins using weak/default credentials from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized FMC Admin Access from External Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful access by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—external login to FMC admin interface is inherently anomalous and exploitative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful FMC login from IP addresses outside your organization's trusted administrative IP ranges. Correlate with geographic impossibilities, non-business-hours access, or deviations from baseline administrator login patterns.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Extraction from Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Attacker goal is 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—FMC repositories contain firewall policies, security configurations, credentials, and network topology. Post-authentication data queries indicate adversary moving to collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API queries or database reads targeting FMC policy repositories, device configurations, and security group definitions. Flag large sequential API calls to sensitive endpoints within compressed time windows, especially within minutes of newly-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Policy Deployment via Compromised Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: FMC is a management platform that controls downstream firewalls. Exploitation enables lateral movement and defense evasion by pushing policies to disable security controls across the managed infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC audit logs for policy pushes originating from non-standard admin accounts or following external authentication. Flag policy changes that disable security modules, modify firewall rules to whitelist unusual traffic, or add new administrative accounts to managed firewalls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry indicates active exploitation in the wild. Federal patch due date is 2026-08-01. Presence in vulnerability scans is critical indicator of exploitable exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily/weekly scans of all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances must test for CVE-2026-20316. Alert on any positive result. Cross-reference with patch records and inventory to confirm true positives and identify unpatched/unknown instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20316 Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt'; FMC is internet-facing management appliance—primary detection vector is discovering vulnerable instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management systems for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 patch status. Prioritize internet-exposed instances with patch lag relative to 2026-08-01 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication Anomaly - Hard-Coded Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker using 'hard-coded password' via 'unauthenticated, remote' access to 'log in to an affected device'—detect authentication attempts with known hard-coded low-privilege account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for login attempts with hard-coded low-privilege account. Flag any successful login from public/unexpected IP ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for same host to confirm exploitation window.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems'—detect bulk data export or unusual configuration retrieval patterns following successful authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within FMC audit logs, flag bulk policy downloads, device configuration exports, credential lookups, or inventory queries executed shortly after successful authentication. Correlate timing with known exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FMC Instances Post-Deadline Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date '2026-08-01'; any unpatched FMC post-deadline represents non-compliance and active exploitation risk given CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alert for any Cisco FMC instance without CVE-2026-20316 patch applied after 2026-08-01. Include remediation owner, current exposure duration, and CISA KEV exploitation-in-wild evidence in escalation.

suggestion.title: NightLedger Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Nimbus Manticore Deploys NightLedger'—malware execution is the primary attack vector. Pipeline produced zero detection use case despite this being the core IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NightLedger process instantiation, module loading, and file-system artifacts. Monitor parent-process chains typical of malware distribution (Office macros, script execution, MSI install). Establish YARA signatures and file-hash IOCs. Flag registry/scheduled-task creation during malware execution.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article states systems are turned into 'covert relays'—this functionality must persist across reboots. Pipeline missed persistence detection despite this being definitive to the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthorized registry autostart modifications (HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce), new service creation, and scheduled-task installation. Flag unsigned executables in startup directories. Detect DLL search-order hijacking and service-binary replacement.

suggestion.title: Covert Relay Outbound Traffic Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Systems functioning as 'covert relays' exhibit distinctive network patterns. Article describes relay infrastructure for attacker C2 without specifying domains/IPs, but relay forwarding is detectable via network behavior analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound connections on non-standard ports from previously dormant systems. Detect reverse-proxy patterns (inbound-then-outbound traffic pairs). Alert on traffic-volume spikes and anomalies inconsistent with baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Relay Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Covert relay systems imply multi-stage attacks where compromised hosts stage further compromises. Article mentions 'victim systems' (plural), indicating networked compromise. Pipeline ignored lateral-movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network-access patterns: relay-compromised systems initiating connections to new targets. Monitor C$ admin-share access, WMI/RPC execution, and lateral-movement tooling staged through relay systems. Flag process-creation chains converging on relay infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Nimbus Manticore Attribution Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names threat actor 'Nimbus Manticore'. Pipeline produced zero actor-attribution detections or behavioral baseline despite actor name being the first signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish Nimbus Manticore TTP baseline: known C2 infrastructure, malware delivery methods, and exploitation patterns. Alert on re-use of actor-specific techniques even with new malware variants. Cross-reference actor IOCs against email, DNS, and endpoint logs.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery Mechanism Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires initial compromise to deploy NightLedger. Pipeline should detect delivery vectors (phishing, watering-hole, supply-chain) that precede malware execution and relay installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious email attachments or links, unauthorized software installation, and exploitation of known vulnerabilities. Flag if malware delivery correlates with software patching windows or trusted software updaters. Detect post-delivery persistence installation.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Patch Compliance / Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center and federal patch due-date (2026-08-01). Pipeline must surface asset inventory hunts for affected product versions to catch unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and asset databases for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances matching the CVE-2026-20316 affected version range. Alert on hosts with FMC deployed but no recent patch activity or version mismatch against published fixes.

suggestion.title: Hard-Coded Credential Authentication Attempts to FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in using a low-privileged account.' This is a valid-account exploitation pathway not yet modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC management interface logs and proxy/WAF logs for repeated failed or successful login attempts using known default/low-privileged account names (e.g., 'admin', 'fmc'). Correlate with network-originating IPs outside normal management ranges.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Sensitive Data Access from Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article describes goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Exploitation success metrics must include data enumeration/exfiltration after authentication, not just login detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all data queries and exports from Cisco FMC API or GUI post-authentication. Alert on anomalous volume of policy rules, firewall configurations, or forensic data exported in short time window, especially from atypical user accounts or IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure of Cisco FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies the FMC management port is internet-reachable or VPN-accessible. Exposure hunts are canonical CISA KEV response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network telemetry for inbound traffic on standard Cisco FMC ports (e.g., 443, 8305) from untrusted networks. Cross-check against firewall rules and asset inventory to identify FMC instances with non-standard or overly permissive ingress ACLs.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Brute-Force or Credential Stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password attacks often manifest as horizontal brute-force attempts across multiple accounts. Article describes 'low-privileged account' as entry point; repeated login attempts under stress should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed login attempts to Cisco FMC within 5 minutes, or ≥3 successful logins using the same low-privileged account from different source IPs in <1 hour. Baseline normal admin activity first to tune FP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Signature (IDS/IPS)
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation (CISA KEV) justifies development of network-level signatures. Payload or request patterns specific to this vulnerability's exploitation chain should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy/update IDS/IPS/WAF rules to match CVE-2026-20316 exploitation signatures (e.g., requests to FMC APIs with hard-coded credential payloads, or management endpoint probes). Cross-reference with Snort/Suricata communities for SID mapping.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20316 Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker is 'unauthenticated, remote' and requires 'affected device' accessible from network. Exploitation requires exposed management interface. Federal due date 2026-08-01 demands immediate asset discovery and patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20316 affected versions. Prioritize instances with accessible management interfaces (ports 443/8305) by federal patch due date. Use CVSS context + CISA KEV 'actively exploited' to justify emergency patching.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Authentication Attempts via Hard-coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' This is direct articulation of attack method—hard-coded credential exploitation. Pipeline generated zero detection for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to Cisco FMC REST API or CLI from external IPs using service/low-privileged accounts. Monitor for repeated failed login attempts from single source followed by success (credential-spraying pattern). Correlate against known Cisco FMC default/hard-coded credential identifiers published in vendor advisories.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Sensitive Data Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Post-exploitation includes bulk export of firewall policies, credentials, user data, and network topology. Pipeline did not generate detection for data-access/collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for bulk data exports (firewall policies, ACLs, VPN credentials, user configurations) initiated by low-privileged accounts or unexpected contexts. Alert on API calls to enumeration endpoints (GET /api/config/firewall_policies, /api/fwm/managed_devices) with large result sets. Correlate with external data exfiltration (large file transfer, DNS/HTTP tunneling, HTTPS POST with anomalous payload).

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Post-Compromise Firewall Policy Modification
suggestion.rationale: Upon unauthorized access via hard-coded credentials, attacker typically modifies firewall rules to enable persistence or network egress for C2. Article describes 'low-privileged account'—suggests privilege escalation or direct rule-modification capability within FMC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall policy creations/modifications (rules added, updated, or deleted) from low-privileged service accounts, unexpected admin accounts, or IPs linked to initial compromise. Detect rules permitting outbound traffic to known C2 domains, disabling logging/monitoring, or allowing lateral movement. Correlate with suspicious authentication events.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance (Policy/Network Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gains 'access sensitive data'—includes network topology, firewall policies, and user details stored in FMC. Post-compromise reconnaissance patterns include enumeration of policies and network objects to plan bypass/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC API for repeated or bulk queries to network-object endpoints (/api/config/networkobjects, /api/config/firewall_policies, /api/identity/users). Alert on unusual enumeration patterns from low-privileged accounts, particularly rapid sequential API calls that suggest automated reconnaissance. Compare against baseline administrative query patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC: Hard-coded Credential Scanning and Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: CVE centers on hard-coded password vulnerability. Attackers will actively scan and exploit this using known credential sets. Standard brute-force detection may miss credential-spraying attacks using published hard-coded values.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts using known hard-coded account/password combinations documented in Cisco CVE-2026-20316 advisory. Alert on distributed authentication attempts (multiple source IPs within short window targeting same FMC instance). Flag any successful authentication using non-standard service accounts or credentials that should remain unexposed externally.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags CISA KEV status (active exploitation). Pipeline extracted no IOC. Vulnerability scanner results are the canonical first-line detection for known-vulnerable Cisco FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a vulnerability scanner identifies Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize hits on systems exposed to untrusted networks or internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Success
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in...using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline missed T1078 (Valid Accounts) and T1110 (Brute Force) entirely. Hard-coded passwords are credentials reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful login to Cisco FMC low-privilege default or service accounts (e.g., admin, pnadmin) from external/untrusted sources, especially when MFA logs show 2FA was bypassed or not enforced.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access from Compromised FMC Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies post-auth impact: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' This is the collection phase—policy exports, credential access, config dumps from low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on policy configuration exports, security group exports, credential manager access, or diagnostic bundle generation initiated by low-privilege FMC accounts or from newly authenticated sessions without prior administrative behavior.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Cisco FMC Management Interface Discovery
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1190 presumes public-facing application. Pipeline did not propose network reconnaissance hunts for exposed FMC instances (port 443, 8305 banner grabs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cisco FMC management interfaces exposed to internet: query network data for IPs responding on port 443 or 8305 with Cisco FMC SSL certificate/banner; cross-check Shodan/Censys for FMC instances; validate asset inventory alignment.

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Status Inventory Audit
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date is 2026-08-01 (2 days past). Pipeline provided no inventory-based IOC or version-check guidance. Asset inventory is the operational prerequisite for CISA KEV remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management system for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Extract version numbers and cross-reference Cisco advisory for CVE-2026-20316 affected versions. Flag unpatched instances, especially those with external/untrusted network access.

suggestion.title: Failed-to-Successful FMC Login Sequence (Hard-coded Credential Brute-Force Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password attacks often show multiple failed attempts before success, distinct from typical dictionary brute-force. Article's 'unauthenticated...remote attacker' implies reconnaissance or credential enumeration preceding auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 2–5 failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC default/low-privilege accounts from a single external IP, followed by a successful login within 5 minutes, with no intervening password reset or MFA challenge in logs.

suggestion.title: Detect release tag reassignment in GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes persistence mechanism: 'attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 'attacker could point people to the malicious commit simply by updating the changed-files GitHub Action code's repo.' Tag manipulation is the direct propagation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor high-dependency GitHub repositories for release tag modifications, especially tags moving to different commits or newly-orphaned commits. Alert on bulk tag operations or tags reassigned without corresponding source-code audit trail.

suggestion.title: Detect plaintext secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies core impact: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Attack succeeds because malicious workflow code bypasses GitHub's encryption scheme: 'without the secret ever appearing in the build log' is the normal state that was violated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GitHub Actions logs to expect zero secret leakage per GitHub's encryption design. Scan logs for AWS key patterns, GitHub tokens, API credentials, and private key headers. Flag any plaintext occurrences and correlate with recent workflow changes.

suggestion.title: Detect orphaned commits in high-value GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article names orphaned commits as 'key enabling factor' and provides detailed mechanics: commits remain navigable on GitHub even after branch deletion. Combined with tag manipulation: 'attack commit orphaned from any branches' was intentional obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query repositories with high external dependencies for commits without branch references but assigned release tags. Orphaned commit creation correlating with tag updates is high-risk. Monitor commit graph for floating commits in sensitive repos.
