suggestion.title: Detect external network calls initiated from GitHub Actions workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals detection method: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External calls are the observable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network activity from GitHub Actions runners for undocumented external destinations. Baseline legitimate dependency pulls and flag novel external hosts. Correlate with recent workflow or action version changes.

suggestion.title: Detect write-access escalation on supply-chain GitHub repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article names write access as root cause: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo' and 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Write access is the prerequisite that enabled all subsequent steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new contributor access or permission elevation to repositories with high external dependents (1000+ stars or used by 1000+ downstream repos). Flag unexpected write-access grants and lack of corresponding change control tickets.

suggestion.title: Detect tag-pinned dependency resolution to unexpected commits
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector: workflows using 'tj-actions/changed-files@v35' suddenly pull malicious code because v35 tag was moved. Article shows: 'uses: tj-actions/changed-files@v35' — tag reassignment affected all 23,000 dependent repos silently.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For consumers of GitHub Actions, monitor source-pinned dependencies and detect when resolved commits diverge from historical baselines. Flag when a semantic-version tag now resolves to a commit newer than the previous resolution or to an orphaned commit.

suggestion.title: QR Code Embedded in PDF Phishing Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'QR code-embedded PDFs to bypass traditional email gateways' and 'auto-generated, victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct to adversary-controlled M365 credential harvesting pages'. Explicit initial-access vector in >50% of engagements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PDF attachments with embedded or encoded QR codes, especially in messages from external or newly compromised domains. Correlate QR resolution to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Monitor for M365 credential harvesting pages referenced in PDF metadata or decoded QR output.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing M365 Defense Evasion: Suspicious Inbox Rules and SharePoint Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article directly describes: 'creating email inbox rules for defense evasion, leveraging SharePoint to host malicious documents, and sending additional internal and external phishing emails'. These are observed post-compromise behaviors from UAT-11764.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation by newly compromised accounts within hours of phishing success, especially rules deleting, hiding, or forwarding emails. Monitor for unusual SharePoint file uploads from low-risk-score accounts. Correlate phishing detection to subsequent mail-rule or SharePoint events.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Flow Phishing (ARToken PhaaS Platform)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ARToken exposing '80+ API endpoints for device code phishing' and 'bypassing MFA through the OAuth device authorization flow'. Direct bypass of MFA without stealing passwords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authorization flows from unusual geos or IPs, especially multiple rapid-fire flows from same account. Monitor for device confirmation fatigue (repeated approvals over short interval). Flag device code flows immediately preceding token-based lateral movement or suspicious cloud activity.

suggestion.title: Trojanized MeshAgent Backdoor Installed as SYSTEM Auto-Start Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Sinobi operators 'use a trojanized MeshAgent binary as their primary C2 mechanism' installed as 'SYSTEM-level auto-start service, communicating over encrypted WebSocket (WSS) to an attacker-controlled server' enabling 'undetected access for approximately three days'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MeshAgent binary installation with SYSTEM privileges or registry auto-start entries where not pre-authorized. Monitor for WSS outbound connections from MeshAgent to unapproved C2 infrastructure. Hunt for MeshAgent running under SYSTEM context without corresponding legitimate MeshCentral deployment records.

suggestion.title: Zoho Assist Unattended Remote Access Deployment (Warlock/Storm-2603)
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Warlock ransomware operators deploying an installer for the RMM tool Zoho Assist Unattended Agent, which is designed to allow administrative remote control of an endpoint without a user logged in'. Enables covert persistent access without user session requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Zoho Assist Unattended Agent installation outside approved MDM deployment channels. Monitor registry for Zoho Assist persistence mechanisms. Alert on unattended remote connections when no user is logged in or during high-risk hours.

suggestion.title: Service Account Credential Theft from NTDS.dit, Lateral Movement via RDP/WinRM to Ransomware Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes chain: 'obtained from the domain credential store, ntds.dit. The actor moved laterally through the network using RDP and WinRM, leveraging a service account with a weak, easily cracked password' followed by 'deployed the ransomware across the entire domain using a malicious Group Policy Object (GPO) logon script'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on NTDS.dit access outside domain controller operations or admin tools. Monitor RDP/WinRM connections from service accounts to multiple endpoints. Detect GPO modification adding malicious logon scripts. Correlate service account elevation to subsequent rapid encryption across domain.

suggestion.title: FMC Vulnerability Scanner Detection (CVE-2026-20316)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites CVE-2026-20316 and directs to 'asset-exposure hunt' using vulnerability scanners as the primary detection method. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for any unpatched or end-of-life Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances flagged for CVE-2026-20316. High-risk finding if detected post-2026-08-01 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication via Hard-Coded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Hard-coded credential exploitation is the core attack vector—baseline authentication logs must detect anomalous logins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful remote authentication to FMC management interface (port 443 typical) from external IPs or IPs outside normal administrative ranges, especially if followed by privilege escalation or sensitive data queries.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access by Low-Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account post-login. Detection must cover lateral data movement after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC activity logs for queries or exports of configuration data, firewall rules, or policy objects initiated from low-privileged admin accounts; correlate with recent failed/successful logins to detect post-compromise data collection.

suggestion.title: Unpatched FMC Fleet Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal due date 2026-08-01. Inventory of unpatched instances must be a standing hunt, not reactive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline query of all FMC instances in fleet; extract version/patch level and flag any instance running a version known to be vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316; compare against published patch guidance.

suggestion.title: FMC Network Access from Non-Administrative IPs
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential attacks are typically remote and come from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Network segmentation violations to FMC should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of administrative networks that should access FMC management interface. Alert on connection attempts from external IP space, residential ISPs, cloud providers, or VPN endpoints outside approved remote-access ranges.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Public Internet Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'currently being exploited in the wild' by 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies external accessibility. Recommended template asset-exposure hunt (referenced in article) was not generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances on public internet by certificate issuer fingerprint (Cisco/FMC), port 443/8305 banner, HTTP response headers. Alert on Shodan/Censys hits for FMC outside authorized public ranges.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against FMC Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in' using 'hard-coded password'—attack vector is known-credential guessing, not zero-day exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts to FMC from external IPs followed by successful login. Flag logins to default/documented hard-coded usernames (e.g., 'admin', Cisco default creds) from non-corporate IP ranges. Baseline normal login patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege FMC Account Access to Sensitive Policy/Rule Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' via 'low-privileged account'—implies lateral movement within FMC to exfiltrate rules, policies, threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls/exports of security policies, firewall rules, threat feeds, or account directories by low-privilege accounts. Alert on bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or account enumeration queries initiated by compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Vulnerability Assessment and Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article references CVE-2026-20316 by identifier only; no version ranges specified. Fingerprinting to identify affected FMC versions is required for triage and scope assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for HTTP requests probing FMC version endpoints (/api/fmc_platform/v1/info, admin/version). Extract version from response headers, HTTP body, or TLS certificate metadata. Cross-reference against Cisco advisory for affected versions.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Scheduled Backup or Database Export by Suspicious Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers access 'sensitive data within the impacted systems'—FMC database exports and backups are high-value collection targets for threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FMC backup/export initiation by low-privilege accounts or from unusual times/locations. Correlate with recent authentication events to low-privilege accounts. Flag exports to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Federal Compliance Remediation SLA Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-08-01'—CISA KEV compliance is a mandatory SLA. Lack of patching is auditable and carries regulatory risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Cisco FMC instances scanned after 2026-08-01 federal due-date showing CVE-2026-20316 as unpatched. Flag unpatched instances 14+ days past due-date for escalation to compliance/incident response.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential: Cisco FMC Default Account Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account' + 'hard-coded password vulnerability.' Pipeline zero UCs on default credential detection against FMC management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful logins to Cisco FMC management interfaces (ports 8305, 443) using default/low-privileged account names from non-corporate source IPs. Correlate with scripted authentication patterns (rapid successive requests, static credentials) and CVE-2026-20316 inventory flagged devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Public Exposure: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' exploiting exposed appliance. Zero UC for detecting routable Cisco FMC instances on internet-facing interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC appliances reachable from untrusted networks via network segmentation logs or public IP scans. Alert on inbound connection attempts to FMC management ports from non-whitelisted external IP ranges. Cross-reference with unpatched asset inventory for CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration: Cisco FMC Sensitive Config Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline zero UCs for detecting policy/config export, data queries, or API abuse post-credential-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC audit logs for bulk policy rule exports, configuration downloads, threat-feed retrievals, or backup-file generation within 30min of successful authentication via low-privileged account. Flag lateral querying of managed Firewall device configs. Correlate with external data transfer events.

suggestion.title: Authentication Enumeration: Cisco FMC Brute-Force / Account Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded credential exploitation vector implies scanning/enumeration of valid accounts on FMC before exploitation. Zero UCs for detecting authentication reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >10 failed authentication attempts to Cisco FMC management interface from single IP within 10min window. Flag dictionary/credential-spray patterns (rotating usernames, static password). Alert on scanning for common FMC default accounts (admin, root, etc.).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise: FMC Role/Permission Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'low-privileged account' used to breach system. Pipeline zero UCs for detecting subsequent escalation from low-priv session to admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for administrative privilege grants, role changes, or permission expansions applied to FMC user accounts immediately following successful authentication with low-privileged credentials. Alert on admin account creation, policy-modification grants, or audit-log access elevation from suspicious sessions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Cisco FMC → Managed Firewall Devices
suggestion.rationale: FMC is management plane for Cisco Secure Firewall estate. Article implies sensitive data access. Pipeline zero UCs for detecting pivot from compromised FMC to managed perimeter devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/HTTPS connections from compromised FMC toward managed Secure Firewall devices using FMC service accounts. Monitor for policy deployment, firmware upgrade pushes, or configuration synchronization commands to multiple firewall devices in rapid sequence post-breach.

suggestion.title: LockBit Ransomware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Case 01 – Leaked LockBit builder' and tags include 'Ransomware' as primary threat. Pipeline failed to generate detection for known ransomware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known LockBit signatures, file extension mass-renaming patterns, ransom note creation, and registry modifications associated with encryption activity. Correlate with network exfiltration to identify double-extortion scenarios targeting educational data.

suggestion.title: AnyDesk Deployment via Malicious Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Case 02 – DragonForce deployed via AnyDesk'—explicit use of remote access tool for malware distribution. Pipeline missed detection opportunity for remote-access-mediated execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AnyDesk installation and execution, particularly when initiated from unusual processes (e.g., software deployment tools, email clients). Alert on DragonForce or associated process names executing post-AnyDesk startup. Monitor for network connections to AnyDesk relay servers followed by suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: Python Keylogger Execution by Insider
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Case 03 – Python keylogger used by an insider'. Pipeline did not surface insider threat detection combining legitimate user context with malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter execution with keylogger imports (pynput, keyboard, pyautogui) or execution of known keylogger scripts. Escalate alerts when executed by accounts with no historical development/IT activity. Correlate with clipboard access, input system APIs, and data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Software Deployment in Educational Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states machines are 'used by multiple people without accountability', exposing institutions to unauthorized software install. Pipeline missed detection for post-compromise software staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor shared educational workstations for unsigned or suspicious executable creation, particularly in temp directories or system paths. Flag software installation events on machines with elevated user turnover. Correlate with subsequent malware execution or remote access activity.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Credential Abuse via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'attackers can attempt phishing attacks and impersonate the victims in SIM swapping attacks'—threats enabled by PII data exposure. Pipeline failed to model post-exfiltration attack chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of phishing traffic targeting student/staff PII domains post-incident. Correlate external phishing campaigns with known exfiltrated PII sets (CPF numbers, phone, addresses). Flag SIM-swap attempts linked to compromised identity data from educational breaches.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance by Insider Threat Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights insider threat risk due to diverse user groups and minimal accountability; pipeline must detect reconnaissance by legitimate accounts before lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration commands (net group, whoami, ipconfig) or directory queries executed by educational staff with no IT role. Monitor for unusual network scanning (ping sweeps, port scans) from workstations, particularly those shared across users. Escalate when paired with credential harvesting tools.

suggestion.title: iOS App Installation from Untrusted Source / Sideloading Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates GHOSTBLADE deployment on iOS; no iOS-specific initial-access detection was generated. Typical iOS malware distribution bypasses App Store vetting via phishing, MDM profiles, or sideloading—none captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for iOS app installation outside official App Store channels, MDM profile delivery to managed devices, suspicious Xcode installation flows (DarkSword typically used by actors to repurpose legitimate dev tools for malware). Alert on apps requesting excessive permissions (location, contacts, photos).

suggestion.title: DarkSword Toolkit Execution Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'leaked DarkSword kit' but pipeline generated no toolkit-specific detections. DarkSword is a known iOS exploitation framework; its usage should trigger C2 communication and process-spawning signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DarkSword typically invokes specific system binaries and establishes non-standard network channels. Look for spawning of `xcode-select`, `swift`, unusual use of `curl` or network APIs with hardcoded C2 domains, and execution of dynamically-loaded iOS frameworks post-installation.

suggestion.title: GHOSTBLADE Malware Indicators of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Named malware family in article title but zero hash, certificate, or behavioral indicators extracted. Minimum expectation: file hashes, code signing certificates, bundle identifiers, or known C2 sinkhole domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution or installation of apps with bundle IDs or code-signing certs associated with GHOSTBLADE variants. Flag processes spawned by recently-installed third-party apps that attempt to hook system APIs or disable security features.

suggestion.title: Chinese APT Mobile Campaign Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies threat actor as Chinese but no actor name, infrastructure (IPs, domains, ASNs), or historical campaign patterns are captured. Pipeline should surface known APT infrastructure reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network traffic from compromised iOS devices to known Chinese APT C2 infrastructure (previous campaigns, OSINT data, VirusTotal passive DNS). Flag connections to bulletproof-hosting providers, Chinese ISPs flagged for APT activity, or domains registered via known compromised registrar accounts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via iOS Backgrounding / Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes persistent malware on iOS; no detection for data collection (contacts, credentials, messages, location) or exfiltration patterns were suggested. This is typical for iOS spyware campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for iOS processes requesting repeated access to sensitive APIs (Contacts, Photos, Keychain, Location) especially when backgrounded. Flag unusual DNS queries to exfiltration infrastructure immediately after permission grants or during off-hours. Baseline expected data volumes per app.

suggestion.title: Persistence via iOS Launch Daemons or App Whitelisting Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Malware on iOS requires persistence mechanism but none identified. Article implies sustained compromise; should detect iOS-specific persistence (LaunchDaemons, iCloud Keychain abuse, or app-update hijacking).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: iOS malware often persists via MDM profiles, app-update interception, or Siri shortcuts abuse. Monitor for unusual modifications to system plists in `/Library/Preferences/`, installation of unsigned daemons, or Siri shortcut automation that re-launches suspicious apps after reboot.

suggestion.title: Passkey Authentication Without User Verified Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article description states: 'relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor.' This is the core attack surface. Detection must flag passkey assertions where UV flag is absent or false during MFA-required flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebAuthn/passkey authentication events for missing or false User Verified flags on accounts configured for MFA. Correlate with successful access to sensitive resources. Establish baseline of per-user passkey assertion patterns to detect anomalous unverified submissions.

suggestion.title: MFA Policy Bypass: Single Factor Accepted as Multi-Factor
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'reducing MFA to a single factor' indicates the attack downgrades authentication strength. Should alert when MFA policy exists but authentication completes with only passkey (one factor).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication events where MFA policy is enforced but only one factor (passkey) is recorded. Compare configured MFA requirements against actual factors used. Flag accounts where passkey alone satisfies MFA policy when second factor should be mandatory.

suggestion.title: Passkey Reuse Across Devices from Anomalous Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article context 'attack surface in passwordless authentication' combined with unvalidated passkey acceptance creates risk of extracted/cloned passkey replay. Multiple uses of same passkey from different geolocations signals compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on same passkey used for authentication from multiple distinct geolocations or unrelated devices within 24 hours. Correlate with unverified passkey assertions to identify exploitation of validation gaps. High-risk if access precedes sensitive operations (data export, privilege elevation).

suggestion.title: Suspicious RCE Against N-central Management Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attackers Take Over N-central Servers' + 'Initial Fix Proves Incomplete' — indicates successful exploitation and code execution on management infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central service processes for unexpected child spawning, PowerShell invocation, or system utility execution (cmd.exe, whoami, net.exe). Correlate inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to N-central endpoints from untrusted sources with process execution timing.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise on Management Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'take over N-central servers' implies lateral privilege escalation from initial RCE foothold to administrative access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track token impersonation events, UAC bypass attempts, and kernel-mode execution on N-central servers. Monitor for SeDebugPrivilege escalation, suspicious use of icacls/cacls, or indirect process calls from system services.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation on Compromised Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over...after initial fix proves incomplete' — re-compromise capability signals persistent backdoor or account-based persistence planted during initial compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor scheduled task creation, registry Run key modifications, WMI event subscription setup, and service installation on N-central servers. Track unauthorized local or domain account creation coinciding with reported compromise window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Management Plane to Managed Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article implies broad N-central deployment; compromise of central management server creates pivot point to customer-managed systems and agent networks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP/SSH connections originating from N-central infrastructure to managed customer endpoints outside maintenance windows. Monitor for unexpected agent deployment, script execution, or configuration push to managed systems.

suggestion.title: Discovery of Account and System Inventory Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over' — post-exploitation reconnaissance on N-central's account structures and managed customer inventory is standard attacker behavior on management platforms
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for enumeration commands (net accounts, Get-AdUser, ldapsearch, arp, ipconfig) run from N-central service contexts. Monitor LDAP/Active Directory queries over non-standard ports and unusual DNS discovery of customer domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Beaconing from Management Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers take over' implies persistent attacker access mechanism; management plane compromise likely includes C2 callback or ongoing remote access for re-exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted outbound connections from N-central servers to rare/new external IPs or domains on non-standard ports. Correlate SSL certificate usage, detect periodic beaconing via network flow analysis, and identify anomalous DNS resolution patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends substituting the CVE into scanner queries ('Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: **CVE:** `CVE-2026-20316`'). Pipeline produced no scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any vulnerability scan result matching CVE-2026-20316 on Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center devices. Prioritize internet-facing or management-zone instances. Asset is actively exploited per CISA KEV.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'standard asset-exposure hunt' as the canonical approach. No network reconnaissance or asset-inventory use case was generated to identify exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) exposed on internet-facing IPs. Flag FMC login pages or HTTPS banners on ports 443, 8305, or custom management ports. Cross-correlate with known-good FMC management subnets.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Hard-coded Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability is 'hard-coded password' enabling 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Pipeline missed credential-based authentication detection entirely, despite this being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for successful logins using default or low-privileged built-in accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'root', 'fmc_default'). Flag first-time successful authentications from unexpected geolocations or IPs. Correlate with failed auth attempts preceding success (credential stuffing pattern).

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication Access to Sensitive FMC Data
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' via low-privileged account. No post-compromise data-access detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After flagging successful hard-coded credential login, monitor for abnormal data queries, policy exports, configuration downloads, or sensitive report generation from FMC. Flag bulk exports of firewall rules, access-control policies, or threat intelligence feeds by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Initial Session Establishment via Hard-coded Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated remote access using hard-coded credentials. Pipeline missed detection of first-time session creation from attacker-controlled IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new FMC management sessions using low-privileged default accounts originating from non-corporate IPs, especially those geolocated to known adversary regions or Tor exit nodes. Alert on simultaneous sessions from the same low-privileged account across multiple source IPs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post Hard-coded Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker gains access via 'low-privileged account'; missing detection for lateral movement or privilege escalation to administrative roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC role/permission changes immediately following login via hard-coded low-privileged accounts. Flag attempts to grant admin privileges, create new admin accounts, or modify access-control lists by low-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—pipeline missed detection for credential-based access to FMC despite being core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC authentication logs for low-privilege account access outside expected maintenance windows, or successful authentications followed immediately by policy/rule queries. Establish baseline of legitimate admin-account usage and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' vulnerability allowing 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—pipeline should detect network exposure of Cisco FMC management interface via vulnerability scanner and external asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) instances listening on internet-routable IPs, especially on management port (TCP 443). Cross-reference with patch inventory: flag any system not patched by federal due-date 2026-08-01.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Policy Export and Rule Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker gains 'access to sensitive data within the impacted systems' post-login—pipeline missed detection for subsequent reconnaissance and data exfiltration of firewall policies after credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After FMC authentication compromise, flag bulk policy rule exports, configuration backups, or queries to sensitive network zones (DMZ, data-center subnets). Monitor for unauthorized rule export or policy sharing to external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FMC Default Service Account Usage Baseline Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'hard-coded password' vulnerability—pipeline should establish that hardcoded service accounts should NEVER authenticate and flag any such attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify known hardcoded/default service account names for Cisco FMC (e.g., admin, service accounts). Flag any authentication attempt using these accounts as anomalous; establish alert for any geographic or time-of-day deviation from zero baseline.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Console Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated...attacker to log in'—pipeline should detect successful logins to FMC web console from untrusted source IPs or with atypical characteristics (TLS fingerprint, user-agent, speed).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC HTTPS access logs (port 443) for successful authentication from unexpected source IP ranges, unusual HTTP user-agents, or rapid-fire login attempts. Correlate with failed credential discovery scans.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Facing Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—FMC must be exposed to internet for exploitation to occur. No asset-exposure detection despite the article's own template reference to asset-exposure hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for any Cisco FMC instances (default port 443, version-specific banners) accessible from public internet. suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access Post-Compromise

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk configuration exports, policy downloads, or API calls to sensitive endpoints (users, credentials, firewall rules) occurring after successful authentication from anomalous source IP. Flag any outbound data transfer from FMC shortly after hard-coded credential login.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Cisco FMC Vulnerability Scanner Detection

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Attempts

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Management Interface Unauthorized Access

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Sensitive Data Access and Exfiltration

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Service Port Exposure Detection

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt — Cisco FMC Internet Reachability

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC for policy downloads, configuration exports, sensor/device list queries, or audit log retrieval initiated by low-privileged user accounts. Flag unusual access patterns correlating with externally-sourced authentication or newly-detected CVE-2026-20316 vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Brute Force Against Cisco FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—establishes hard-coded credential attack vector requiring detection of repeated auth attempts with known default FMC usernames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed login attempts to Cisco FMC management interface (ports 443, 8305) using known default usernames ('admin', 'maintenance', 'firesight') from external/unexpected IPs. Post-successful-auth, flag sessions originating outside trusted admin ranges.

suggestion.title: Successful FMC Authentication from External/Unexpected Source
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'—implies successful remote login is the exploitation artifact; requires detection of valid auth sessions to FMC from non-whitelisted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center from IP addresses not in trusted admin/management network. Correlate with password policy changes, API token generation, or ruleset modifications post-auth.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Access via Compromised FMC Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of database queries, config exports, or telemetry collection initiated from a low-privileged FMC account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect database reads or bulk config/policy exports performed by low-privileged Firepower accounts. Flag unusual query patterns to tables containing flow data, device inventory, or credentials. Baseline expected access per role and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FMC to Internal Network Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC (management appliance with broad network visibility) is a high-value pivot point; article implies 'access sensitive data' could include lateral movement to monitored systems post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FMC typically has broad outbound network access for telemetry. Detect unexpected outbound connections from FMC to internal assets outside its normal management scope (e.g., bulk connections to databases, file servers, or application tiers not in baseline).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Exploitation Attempt Signature
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly documents this CVE as actively exploited. Article describes hard-coded password in specific product version; detection requires vulnerability-signature match against exposed FMC instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match inbound traffic to Cisco FMC ports (443, 8305) for exploitation payload signatures or known hard-coded password vectors. Cross-reference asset inventory to identify unpatched FMC versions (pre-patch due 2026-08-01) and alert if internet-routable.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Cisco FMC on Public Internet
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attacker' and 'public-facing application' (T1190 context). FMC should not be internet-routable; detection requires port-scanning/banner-grabbing activity against 443/8305.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port-scan patterns probing Cisco FMC default ports (443, 8305) from untrusted IPs. Flag positive banner responses identifying Cisco FMC/Firepower on internet-facing assets. Correlate with vulnerability data to identify unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Repointing to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details attacker 'deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and 're-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is the core obfuscation mechanism enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags (especially semantic version tags like v\d+.\d+.\d+) are moved to commits not reachable from main/default branch, or moved multiple times within a short window. Cross-reference with concurrent commit creation to detect tag-swap patterns.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposure in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs' and 'This could lead to a devastating breach on a public repo where the Action logs are also public.' Secrets exposure is the impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions workflow logs for patterns matching AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, API_KEY, and other credential patterns. Alert on non-masked secrets appearing in public logs or secrets output to stderr/stdout without redaction markers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Network Calls from GitHub Actions Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This is the detection signal that surfaced the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound DNS queries or HTTPS connections from GitHub Actions runners to infrastructure not whitelisted for the Action. Flag egress to non-GitHub-owned IPs during build steps, especially from Actions using elevated permissions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Write Access Changes on Popular GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker required 'write privileges on the Action repo' and compromised 23,000 dependent repositories. Access-level changes on trusted repos are prerequisite to supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when new collaborators with write access are added to repositories tagged as GitHub Actions (>1000 dependents, public Actions marketplace listings). Flag temporary access grants or GitHub Apps gaining Action execution permissions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow File Modifications in Dependent Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised Action version injecting malicious behavior into 23,000 repos' workflows. Detection should surface downstream manifestation: repositories using the Action then exhibit modified workflow files or unexpected step execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Actions that reference tj-actions/changed-files@v35 (or other vulnerable tags) with unexpected workflow step additions, new environment variables, or extra script execution steps added by the Action. Flag when Action execution diverges from its documented behavior in the GitHub Marketplace.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commits in CI/CD Repository with Active Release Tags
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes orphaned commits 'added a bit of obfuscation to hide the attack' and describes how attacker created orphaned commits then tagged them. Detection of this pattern flags suspicious repository states.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan git repositories for commits reachable via release/version tags but not reachable from any branch head. Flag as anomalous when such orphaned commits have recent timestamps and are tagged with release semantics (v\d+, or pinned SHAs in .github/workflows).

suggestion.title: JFrog Artifactory Zero-Day Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'JFrog Artifactory Zero-Day'—pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain phases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Artifactory REST API endpoints for exploit patterns (malformed requests, path traversal attempts, unauthenticated access to internal endpoints). Flag unusual artifact metadata modifications or downloads immediately post-CVE publication.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Model Poisoning via Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'OpenAI Models Exploited' and 'Hugging Face Breach'—pipeline missed model integrity attack vectors
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate artifact repository write events (model uploads, version changes) with downstream consumer pull events. Alert on model weights that diverge from published checksums or appear in unexpected build contexts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised ML Training Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Breach cascaded from Artifactory to OpenAI—pipeline failed to map cross-system propagation phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ML training job submissions for embedded payload injection or unusual model URLs. Track SSH/RDP access from training infrastructure to external or sensitive systems during model download/initialization.

suggestion.title: Exposed API Credentials in Artifact Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Artifactory zero-day likely leaked embedded API tokens or credentials; pipeline did not flag credential-access phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan artifact repository logs and versioned build configs for embedded OpenAI API keys, HuggingFace tokens, or service credentials. Correlate with external token validation services (e.g., Truffle Hog) for real-time credential detection.

suggestion.title: Malicious Artifact Propagation to Downstream Consumers
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates OpenAI consumed poisoned models—pipeline missed collection/impact for end-user detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on organizations pulling or building with artifacts from compromised JFrog namespace during attack window. Cross-reference artifact versions with CVE disclosure timeline; flag any dependency pull post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Model Weights Exfiltration via Training Job Output
suggestion.rationale: Poisoning attack may include silent exfiltration of training data or competitor models—not detected by pipeline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ML training/inference jobs for unusual outbound connections to non-whitelisted storage, object stores, or C2 domains. Flag process execution of model serialization/upload tools outside normal deployment windows.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' Pipeline generated zero detections for this core attack vector. Detection must cover successful login attempts to FMC using default or hard-coded account names from unexpected source IPs or at unusual times.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC management interface (port 8305/8307 HTTPS) for successful authentication events using known default account names (admin, root, support). Establish baseline for legitimate FMC admin logins by IP/time and alert on anomalies. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to confirm FMC instances that have not patched CVE-2026-20316.

suggestion.title: FMC Port Enumeration and Exploitation Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'public-facing application' (T1190) implying network reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Pipeline missed initial reconnaissance phase. Detection should identify port scans or service discovery attempts against known FMC ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connection attempts to FMC management ports (8305, 8307, 443 on FMC hosts) from external IP ranges. Cluster multiple failed connection attempts from single source within short time window. Correlate with known FMC vulnerability exploit traffic signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from FMC Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' Pipeline generated no detection for data collection or exfiltration phase. FMC contains firewall policies, rules, and security configurations—high-value theft targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC for bulk data queries or configuration exports post-authentication. Track large HTTP/HTTPS transfers from FMC servers to external IP ranges. Alert on FMC users performing unusual data queries (e.g., pulling all firewall rules, policy exports, credential lists) especially outside business hours or from new session IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Vulnerability Scanner Findings
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry explicitly requiring federal patch compliance by 2026-08-01. Pipeline should generate use case correlating vulnerability scanner results (Qualys, Nessus, Tenable) against FMC instances in environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner results and flag any FMC instances reporting CVE-2026-20316 as unfixed. Cross-reference with patch management system to identify remediation gaps. Prioritize by exposure: FMC instances accessible from internet-routable networks over internal-only instances. Track compliance with federal patch deadline (2026-08-01).

suggestion.title: FMC Remote Access Session Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Hard-coded password enables unauthenticated login but may trigger unusual session behavior. Article phrase 'remote attacker' suggests attacker originates from external network. Detection should flag geographically impossible logins, multiple concurrent sessions, or API calls to sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate FMC admin session patterns (source IP, login time, session duration, API calls). Alert on: logins from new IP ranges, multiple concurrent login attempts using same account, logins followed immediately by configuration queries, or API calls from default account during off-hours.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output should flag this as CISA KEV (actively exploited, federal due-date 2026-08-01). Generate audit-ready compliance query to identify all Cisco FMC instances and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances. Cross-reference patch management logs for CVE-2026-20316 patches applied before federal due-date. Flag unpatched instances for escalation. Track time-to-remediation vs. federal deadline to support compliance reporting.

suggestion.title: FMC Asset Exposure Hunt — Public Internet Visibility
suggestion.rationale: Article states hard-coded vulnerability affects ability to 'log in to an affected device' remotely unauthenticated. Prerequisite detection: enumerate FMC instances with public IP exposure or DNS resolution. Cited: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' implies network-reachable instances are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory or network sensors for FMC instances (Cisco ports 443, 8305, 8307) with inbound internet routes or public DNS resolution. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify unpatched instances. Alert if FMC is reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: FMC Authentication — Hard-Coded Credential Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hard-coded password vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in.' Detection must hunt for login attempts using known hard-coded credential patterns (if disclosed) or brute-force attempts followed by success. Cited phrase establishes credential access attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs (typically syslog or internal audit trail) for failed login attempts followed by success using specific low-privileged default accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'cisco' if disclosed). Flag sequences of 5+ failed attempts then success within 5 minutes as brute-force-then-compromise pattern.

suggestion.title: FMC Sensitive Data Access — Post-Compromise Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker goal: 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems.' After credential compromise, threat actor will query or export sensitive data (firewall rules, device inventory, threat intelligence feeds, credentials stored in FMC). This establishes data collection/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC data-access patterns: query frequency, data volume exported, export destinations (local, remote, email). Alert on anomalies: unusual query patterns targeting credentials or firewall rules, large export jobs from new low-privileged accounts, exports to external IPs, failed exports followed by retry loops.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration Drift — Post-Compromise Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised FMC instances may be used to alter firewall policies, create persistent backdoors, or add attacker-controlled rules. Article phrase 'access sensitive data' does not preclude attackers also modifying system state. Configuration changes are both persistence mechanism and detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture FMC configuration snapshots on a known schedule (daily). Compare snapshots for unauthorized additions: new admin accounts, new firewall rules, modified access controls, altered logging settings. Alert if changes occur outside change-control windows or from unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: FMC Admin Access Anomaly — Lateral Reconnaissance or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: After gaining low-privileged access via hard-coded password, attacker may attempt privilege escalation or enumerate FMC objects (firewall rules, protected networks, connected devices). This establishes discovery and possible escalation phase not explicitly mentioned but implied by 'sensitive data access' objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FMC administrative action frequency (rule queries, device inventory access, user management queries) per source IP and account. Alert on deviations: accounts normally silent suddenly executing queries, queries from unusual geolocations or ASNs, API token generation from low-privileged context, password change attempts for high-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: FMC Patching Status Validation — Patch Lag Risk Quantification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'currently being exploited' (CISA KEV) with federal due date 2026-08-01. Patch lag is the primary risk. Operationally, teams must validate patching across their FMC fleet at fixed intervals (weekly or post-remediation window).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch inventory for all FMC instances. Compare reported version against fixed version (typically published in Cisco advisory). Generate list of unpatched instances with age-of-vulnerability in days. Alert or escalate if any FMC remains unpatched 7+ days after advisory publish date or 3+ days before federal due date.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Internet-Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated zero UCs. FMC management ports (8305, 443) exposed to untrusted networks are the direct exploitation vector for T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC instances accepting inbound connections on management ports (8305, 443, 22) from non-corporate IP ranges. Cross-reference asset inventory against network telemetry for undocumented FMC systems. Monitor for FMC-specific TLS certificate patterns and HTTP service banners indicating vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: FMC Hard-coded Credential Authentication Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account.' This credential_access phase is the exploitation mechanism and was not mapped to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC authentication logs for successful logins from external IP addresses using low-privileged or default service accounts. Alert on repeated failed authentication attempts from single IP (brute-force pattern). Establish baseline for legitimate remote FMC administrator sessions and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FMC Configuration and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: attacker gains 'access sensitive data within impacted systems.' Successful authentication leads to extraction of firewall policies, ACLs, and stored credentials. Pipeline missed collection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound data transfers from FMC instances (>5MB in <5 minutes). Monitor FMC audit logs for bulk policy exports, configuration backups, or database access by authenticated low-privilege accounts. Alert on suspicious API calls to sensitive FMC endpoints and credential stores.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Patch Status Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate federal remediation by published due date (2026-08-01 for this CVE). Pipeline must generate enforcement UC tied to patch management and scanner correlation for remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20316 against patch management records and software inventory. Identify FMC instances with missing or pending patches. Escalate any instances remaining unpatched past federal due date (2026-08-01). Correlate scanner-detected versions against known vulnerable FMC release versions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to FMC Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker' accessing FMC. Core attack vector requiring network monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Cisco FMC management interface (default port 443) from untrusted sources followed by successful authentication without prior login credentials exchanged. Flag early TCP/TLS completion patterns that bypass normal credential submission.

suggestion.title: Hard-coded Credential Usage Against FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hard-coded password vulnerability' allows remote login with low-privileged account. Requires detection of known weak credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to FMC using documented hard-coded account names (requires threat-intel on Cisco FMC default/backdoor credentials). Alert on successful logins from unexpected geographies, off-hours, or IP ranges inconsistent with legitimate admin pools.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Collection from FMC Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers can 'access sensitive data within the impacted systems' — requires detection of unauthorized data export/query activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FMC access logs for policy exports, configuration bulk downloads, or firewall rule queries originating from newly-provisioned or low-privilege accounts. Correlate timing with preceding unauthenticated access or credential anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20316 Asset Inventory and Vulnerability Scan Matches
suggestion.rationale: Standard CISA KEV hunt pattern: asset exposure detection substituting CVE-2026-20316 as required by template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and CMDB for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20316. Prioritize FMC nodes with internet-routable management interfaces or exposed on untrusted network segments.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Low-Privilege Account Activity in FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploit grants access 'using a low-privileged account.' Attackers constrained to low-privilege context exhibit distinct behavioral patterns distinguishing them from legitimate admin use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FMC management console login by low-privilege service accounts during unusual hours or from new IP ranges. Flag subsequent failed escalation attempts, unusual menu navigation, or policy-query patterns inconsistent with service-account baselines.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Hardcoded Credential Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated, remote attacker to log in to an affected device using a low-privileged account'—core vulnerability vector and pipeline generated zero detection for hardcoded-credential exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco FMC login events using known hardcoded/default service-account names or patterns. Alert on successful remote authentication from non-enterprise IP ranges. Correlate with concurrent version-enumeration probes to detect staged exploitation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Cisco FMC Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires network-accessible FMC instance; article states 'remote attacker' implying external reachability. Pipeline should detect internet-facing FMC instances pre-compromise. Core phrase: 'unauthenticated, remote attacker'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco FMC management consoles (ports 443, 8305) exposed to untrusted networks via port scanning and DNS reconnaissance. Cross-reference against approved inventory; flag unmanaged or out-of-compliance exposures given CISA KEV active-exploitation status and 2026-08-01 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Collection from FMC
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised attacker 'access[es] sensitive data within the impacted systems'—requires detection of credential/configuration/threat-intelligence extraction by low-privilege accounts post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk policy exports, configuration snapshots, credential-store queries, or threat-intelligence database access initiated by low-privileged accounts within 10 minutes of first successful login. Correlate with suspicious egress traffic to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Cisco FMC Version Discovery via Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is version-specific; attackers must identify vulnerable FMC builds before exploitation. Article implies version-dependent flaw but does not list patch thresholds, indicating scanner-based reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FMC administrative endpoints requesting /api/version, /admin/build, or similar version-discovery paths. Alert on scripted request patterns or repeated scanning across multiple FMC targets within short time windows.

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states INC exploits SonicWall SMA 1000 flaws. Pipeline should detect inbound exploit attempts via known CVE paths (likely HTTP/HTTPS to admin or resource endpoints). Article phrase: 'Exploiting SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaws'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances for HTTP requests targeting known vulnerability endpoints or payloads (e.g., specific URI patterns, payload signatures). Alert on any successful connection followed by unusual process spawning or file write activity on the device.

suggestion.title: INC Ransomware Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies INC Ransomware as threat actor; ransomware by definition executes data encryption. Pipeline failed to generate behavioral detection for encryption loops or mass file modification. Article phrase: 'INC Ransomware'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential file modifications with binary/unusual extensions post-exploitation. Look for high-entropy writes to user-accessible directories, process execution of encryption-stage payloads, or ransom note file creation (e.g., READ_ME.txt, RESTORE_FILES.txt variants).

suggestion.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 Post-Exploitation Persistence
suggestion.rationale: SMA 1000 devices serve as trusted network gateways; exploitation likely followed by persistence to maintain access for lateral movement or exfiltration. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection. Article context implies sustained access for ransomware deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of unauthorized admin accounts, credential changes, or cron/scheduled task creation on SonicWall appliances post-exploitation. Alert on any file modifications to appliance configuration or boot files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from SonicWall SMA 1000
suggestion.rationale: SMA 1000 is a remote-access hub with internal network visibility; exploitation enables pivot into protected networks. Article title implies network compromise but pipeline generated no lateral-movement detection. Article phrase: 'SonicWall SMA 1000' (network access point).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual egress traffic from SonicWall SMA 1000 to internal subnets post-exploitation; flag scanning activity (port sweeps, SMB probes) or unusual protocol usage (SSH, RDP) originating from the appliance. Cross-correlate with exploitation timestamp.

suggestion.title: INC Ransomware Exfiltration Before Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Modern ransomware (especially INC) typically exfiltrates sensitive data before encryption for extortion leverage. Pipeline missed data-movement phase. While article is truncated, ransomware naming implies double-extortion pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/DNS tunneling or known C2 domains/IPs associated with INC ransomware. Alert on large data transfers to external IPs not matching organization's CDN/SaaS footprint, especially if preceded by file enumeration on sensitive shares.

suggestion.title: LockBit Ransomware Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Leaked LockBit builder' as Case 01 and identifies ransomware as primary attack outcome; no detection logic generated despite this being the article's lead threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LockBit process signatures (file encryption, registry modifications to HKLM for ASR bypass), dropped PE files with LockBit-specific exports, and characteristic bulk file access patterns (reading .docx, .xls, .pdf before deletion/encryption). Correlate with prior web shell or exploitation artifacts.

suggestion.title: AnyDesk Installation and Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Case 02 explicitly states 'DragonForce deployed via AnyDesk'; article identifies AnyDesk (legitimate RMM tool) as active initial access method in educational sector compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected AnyDesk Setup executable downloads, installations to non-standard paths, execution without corresponding support ticket/user request, and subsequent cmd.exe or PowerShell spawning from AnyDesk parent process (indicates attacker shell, not user-initiated RMM session).

suggestion.title: Python Keylogger Installation and Persistence Targeting Educational Staff
suggestion.rationale: Case 03 explicitly names 'Python keylogger used by an insider'; article notes machines with multiple users and no accountability create vulnerability; keylogger targets credential harvesting from staff with database access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter spawning with pynput/keyboard library imports; monitor startup folders and registry (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) for persistence; correlate with user accounts performing unusual data queries or exfiltration immediately after keylogger installation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Student/Staff PII Extraction from Management Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exfiltration of 'social security numbers (CPF in Brazil), addresses, phone numbers, and even parents' names'—targeting of specific PII types indicates database-level extraction, not individual records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk SELECT queries against student information system databases returning 1000+ records; flag creation of large .zip/.rar archives containing CSV/database exports; detect exfiltration of multi-GB transfers to non-institutional IP space or public cloud storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unpatched Educational Management Software
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'software for managing personally identifiable information (PII) that is often insecure or insufficiently tested against known vulnerabilities'—identifies vulnerability exploitation as primary initial access vector specific to this sector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor educational institution networks for exploitation attempts against known-vulnerable student info systems, web application firewalls, and directory services; alert on suspicious process spawn or reverse shell indicators immediately following failed authentication or web server anomalies.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Credential Harvesting Targeting SIM Swap Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers can attempt phishing attacks and impersonate the victims in SIM swapping attacks, a common practice in Brazil'—post-breach phishing chain targeting stolen phone numbers and names unique to Brazilian threat landscape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exfiltration of phone numbers/names with phishing campaigns targeting same institution domain; flag credential spray or MFA bypass attempts originating from regions associated with Brazilian SIM swap fraud; detect unusual account logins post-compromise (atypical time/geography patterns).

suggestion.title: GHOSTBLADE iOS Malware Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'GHOSTBLADE on iOS'—a named malware family requiring behavioral detection on mobile endpoints. Article does not detail payload specifics, but iOS malware typically exfiltrates contacts, messages, location, or media.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iOS processes for unsigned or suspicious app execution, intercept network connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with GHOSTBLADE, and flag apps attempting excessive system API calls (contacts, photos, location, SMS).

suggestion.title: DarkSword Toolkit Installation on iOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actor 'uses leaked DarkSword Kit'—indicates tooling was repurposed or weaponized. DarkSword represents a known attack platform requiring artifact hunting on compromised iOS devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for DarkSword artifacts (installation packages, configuration files, or telemetry) on iOS endpoints; correlate with app store or phishing campaigns that may have delivered the kit.

suggestion.title: Chinese APT iOS Targeting Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Chinese Threat Actor'—does not specify family (APT10, APT40, etc.), but iOS targeting by state-sponsored groups typically aims at high-value individuals in tech, government, or journalism. Requires actor attribution and victim-profile matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing or watering-hole campaigns delivering GHOSTBLADE to iOS users; correlate with known Chinese APT infrastructure (command domains, ASNs, SSL certificates). Alert on emails or link previews matching iOS malware delivery patterns.

suggestion.title: Passkey Authentication Without User Verified Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'relying parties fail to validate the User Verified flag, reducing MFA to a single factor.' Detections should trigger when passkey authentication succeeds but the UV flag is absent or false, breaking MFA semantics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebAuthn attestation responses for missing or false User Verified flag during authentication ceremonies. Flag instances where passkey-based MFA completes but UV validation was skipped or returned false, indicating a relying party failing to enforce FIDO2 spec compliance.

suggestion.title: Rapid or Concurrent Passkey Authentication Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Once passkey MFA is degraded to single-factor (no UV check), brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks become viable. Pipeline should detect velocity anomalies: multiple passkey auths from same account in short window or from multiple IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Count passkey authentication attempts per account per 5-minute window. Alert on >5 attempts (including failures) or successful auths from 3+ distinct IPs within 10 minutes, suggesting automated attack against weakened MFA.

suggestion.title: Passkey Registered Without User Interaction Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies passkey registration can be subverted if UV flag is not checked. Detect new passkeys added to an account without evidence of user presence/interaction during registration ceremony.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a new passkey is registered under an account but the registration attestation response lacks a valid User Presence or User Verified flag. Cross-reference with account login patterns to identify suspicious new credentials added during off-hours or from unexpected locations.
