suggestion.title: Anomalous API or Direct Protocol Access to N-able N-central
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'alternate path or channel' suggests the bypass may not use normal login UI. Could be direct API calls, internal protocols, or RPC endpoints. No UC generated for non-standard access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/API requests to N-able N-central that succeed in authentication without passing through standard login endpoints (e.g., direct calls to /api/v1, /rpc, or other undocumented paths). Look for requests lacking standard session/auth headers or hitting alternate port ranges. Correlate with CVE-2026-18577 unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection — CVE-2026-18577 on N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV status (confirmed active exploitation). Primary detection vector: vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-18577 on N-central instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner identification of CVE-2026-18577 on any N-central appliance. Escalate if instance is internet-facing or externally accessible. Correlate with patch-due deadline (2026-08-06) for urgency scoring.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass — Anomalous Login Pattern Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authentication bypass' enabling 'account takeover'. Detection should capture: failed authentication attempts followed by successful login from anomalous source, or direct session establishment bypassing normal auth UI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central auth logs for multiple failed login attempts (probing) followed by successful authentication from unexpected IP/geography/time-of-day. Flag direct API/session creation bypassing web login interface if detectable.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Account Takeover — Suspicious Admin Actions in N-central
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'account takeover' implications. After auth-bypass success, attackers would perform lateral movement and data exfiltration via N-central: privilege escalation, policy changes, agent deployment, credential export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative policy changes, user account creation, or agent deployment in N-central executed by newly-compromised accounts within hours of suspected exploitation. Correlate with anomalous login detection and vulnerability scanner alerts.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Regression — CVE-2026-18556 Reactivation Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'. This signals the predecessor vulnerability may still be exploitable. Attackers may downgrade or retry the original attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all N-central instances for both CVE-2026-18577 AND CVE-2026-18556. Flag any appliance showing both as highest-risk due to incomplete patch. Prioritize for immediate re-patching.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Auth-Bypass — Process Execution on N-central
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation; auth bypass alone is credential theft. Threat actors would escalate to RCE for persistence. Article context: public-facing app → likely OS-level code execution possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central management servers for unexpected process execution (PowerShell, cmd, bash) or script deployment immediately following suspicious authentication. Correlate parent process (N-central service) with child process execution.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing N-central Instance Exposure — Attack Surface Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190). Critical: identify all N-central instances externally accessible, not just internal appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network perimeter logs for inbound connections to N-central default ports (typically 8400/8401 for web console) from untrusted external IP ranges. Cross-check asset inventory: flag any N-central with public IP, NAT exposure, or reverse-proxy internet access.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Vulnerable N-able N-central Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CISA KEV entries are 'observed exploited in the wild.' Pipeline missed the canonical UC. Substitute CVE-2026-18577 into vulnerability scanner queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for N-able N-central instances flagged with CVE-2026-18577. Even if patch status claims 'patched,' validate actual version against vendor advisory—article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Flag assets exposed on public-facing networks.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' Pipeline did not map to T1556 (Modify Authentication Process) or produce detection for alternate auth flows. This is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central application logs for unusual authentication attempts that bypass standard login endpoints (e.g., direct API calls, non-standard ports, path traversal to /admin or /api). Correlate failed auth attempts followed by successful access without corresponding credential entry in login logs.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows...account takeover.' Pipeline did not generate UC for post-compromise account activity (T1078). Critical for detecting active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful auth bypass, attackers assume valid accounts. Detect suspicious account behavior: lateral movement from N-central to managed endpoints, credential changes, policy modifications, or exfiltration of asset lists. Baseline normal N-central admin activity first.

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Validation and Re-exploitation Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article footnote: 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556.' Pipeline missed this chaining risk. Detection should validate patch completeness, not just presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify N-central version against vendor's CVE-2026-18577 fix. Incomplete patches may still expose alternate auth channels. Monitor for exploitation attempts against previously-patched CVE-2026-18556 (suggests attacker testing patch effectiveness). Flag if N-central version reports patched but still vulnerable via alternate path.

suggestion.title: Federated Due-Date Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal due-date dates...patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline ignored compliance-deadline-driven detection, which drives SOC burn-down prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert: flag any N-able N-central instance still vulnerable to CVE-2026-18577 after federal due date (2026-08-06). Cross-reference asset inventory with patch status. Alert if instance existed on due date but remains unpatched 7+ days after deadline—indicator of patch lag or evasion.

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt Detection: CVE-2026-18577 Payloads
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV means exploitation is active. Pipeline should suggest detection of exploit attempts themselves, not just vulnerability presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central endpoints for HTTP requests containing alternate-path authentication attempts (e.g., /api/auth, /admin/login, /system/auth, path traversal sequences). Spike in failed auth attempts followed by success is exploitation signature. Correlate with known public exploit PoCs if available.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secrets Exposed in Plaintext Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' This is the direct impact and should trigger immediate detection when secrets appear unencrypted in workflow logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for patterns indicating secrets (regex for API keys, tokens, PII). Alert when GitHub Actions environment variables or injected secrets appear in plaintext job output. Cross-check against repository secrets stored in GitHub settings.

suggestion.title: Release Tag Repointing to Orphaned/Suspicious Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit' and demonstrates retagging v35 to orphaned commit. This is the core distribution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when release tags (especially semantic version tags like v1, v2, v35) are moved to commits that lack branch ancestry or exist only as orphaned commits. Flag tag modifications where the new commit is not reachable from main/master.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Widely-Used GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' as deliberate obfuscation. Create branch, commit, delete branch to hide—should be detectable in public action repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repositories matching patterns of widely-used GitHub Actions (>1000 stars, >100 dependents) for commit creation followed by rapid branch deletion. Alert if commits become orphaned (no branch/tag reference) within 5 minutes of creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Write Access to High-Criticality GitHub Action Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Initial access is unexplained; anomalous write events to high-impact actions should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new write-permission grants to repositories categorized as GitHub Actions or in tj-actions namespace. Alert on unexpected commits authored by low-activity accounts or commits without PR review in high-dependency repositories.

suggestion.title: External Network Call from GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner logs for outbound network calls to non-whitelisted domains. Alert on curl/wget/Invoke-WebRequest to external hosts during workflow execution, especially in public repositories where logs are publicly visible.

suggestion.title: Repository Write Permission Change in GitHub Actions Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Core prerequisite: 'attacker with write privileges on the Action repo.' Detect when permissions escalate on critical actions repositories via team membership, collaborator additions, or GitHub app grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when write/admin permissions are granted to GitHub Actions repositories (identify by workflow-common names like 'actions', 'changed-files', 'setup-*', etc.). Flag if granted to external collaborators or service accounts with unusual access patterns.

suggestion.title: Failed SFTP authentication attempt with empty credentials to goshs
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes empty-password (-b 'admin:') and empty-username (-b ':pass') as the bypass vectors. Authentication logs or SFTP connection attempts with missing credentials are explicit attack indicators. Article states 'SFTP accepts connections without password'—detection of the accept itself (not just the command line) strengthens coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor goshs process for inbound SFTP connection attempts where SSH PublicKeyAuth or PasswordAuth failed or were skipped, correlate with empty credentials in the process command line. Absence of authentication logs or immediate session acceptance despite missing credentials indicates exploitation.

suggestion.title: goshs process spawned with incomplete credentials in basic-auth flag
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerable pattern: '-b' flag with colon-only syntax (e.g., 'user:' or ':pass'). Command-line monitoring is high-fidelity for this signature attack. Different from UC_103_2 in that it focuses on spawning goshs with ANY incomplete creds, regardless of -fkf presence or SFTP enablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with command line containing '-b' followed by a pattern matching empty-username (:[a-zA-Z0-9]) or empty-password (\w+:) variants. High confidence indicator of deliberate empty-credential configuration.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed SFTP login attempts to goshs followed by successful unauthenticated session
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass scenario where legitimate auth attempts fail but then unauthenticated access succeeds. Behavioral hunt: watch for SFTP session logs showing PasswordAuth failures or key rejection followed immediately by authenticated commands without further credential exchange. This is the ground truth of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed SFTP authentication event (PasswordAuth=no or PublicKeyAuth=no from client) within same session, followed by accepted file operations without re-authentication. Absence of valid credentials in successful session indicates bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in exposed 'N-able N-central' permitting exploitation. Initial step is asset discovery: 'Vendor / Product: N-able N-central' with federal patch due 2026-08-06 implies millions of instances need scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate N-central instances via fingerprinting (certificate CN, HTTP headers, default ports 8000-8010). Tag against vulnerability databases. Cross-reference with patched-vs-unpatched inventory as of 2026-08-06 cutoff to identify current exposure window.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Alternate Path (N-central)
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel allows for authentication bypass.' Bypass patterns should be detectable before account takeover completes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central auth logs for requests to API endpoints or alternate paths that succeed without valid credential chain. Flag: auth failures on /login followed by successful access on /api/*, or unauthenticated requests to privilege-requiring endpoints that return success.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Indicators Post-Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states bypass 'allows for...account takeover in N-central.' Successful bypass converts to account compromise; detect post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After auth bypass indicator: detect account takeover signals within N-central logs — privilege escalation without request, new API keys/credentials issued, account settings modified (email, MFA disabled), or access pattern shift (geo, time, device).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-18577 Incomplete Patch Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556' — the gap between patches is the exploit target. Identify which bypass techniques are new in 18577 vs patched in 18556.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate requests that trigger CVE-2026-18556 mitigations (e.g., requests to known-vulnerable paths now blocked) against those succeeding on unpatched systems. Differential log analysis: flag requests that fail on 2026-08-07+ (post-patch deadline) but succeed before cutoff.

suggestion.title: N-central Compromised Account Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Post-takeover via auth bypass, attacker holds valid N-central credentials. Subsequent access to downstream systems is likely: 'account takeover' without scope constraint implies persistence beyond N-central.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After accounting for auth bypass + account takeover: detect API calls enumerating connected systems, credential theft from N-central config, or access to resources outside N-central using stolen session tokens.

suggestion.title: N-able N-central Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies N-central as the target product; enterprises need asset visibility before exploitation can occur. Pipeline ignored the asset-discovery prerequisite despite article stating 'exploit public-facing application.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify and enumerate N-central instances exposed to untrusted networks via port scanning and DNS/IP discovery. Baseline discovered instances against CMDB; flag rogue or unpatched deployments. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-18577 patch status to identify exploitable assets within the organization's external footprint.

suggestion.title: N-central Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel.' Pipeline omitted detection for the exploit phase despite T1190 being explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication requests to N-central using alternate paths/channels (non-standard endpoints, unauthenticated API calls, direct database access attempts). Monitor for failed auth attempts immediately followed by successful session creation without credential submission. Correlate with exploit traffic signatures for CVE-2026-18577 bypass payloads.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via N-central Post-Auth Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack outcome: 'account takeover in N-central.' Pipeline generated zero detection rules for the post-compromise account activity phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hijacked N-central accounts for unusual activity: first-time source IPs, privilege escalations, bulk administrative actions (user creation, policy modification, credential resets). Alert when account activity post-auth-bypass diverges from historical baseline in timing, geography, or resource scope.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised N-central
suggestion.rationale: N-central is a remote administration platform; article does not explicitly describe post-compromise lateral movement but this is the logical attack continuation for a management tool compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor N-central job execution logs for suspicious automated tasks targeting unexpected endpoint groups or systems outside the compromised account's normal scope. Detect when N-central is used to deploy scripts, patches, or persistence mechanisms. Correlate suspicious N-central jobs with endpoint anomalies (process injection, privilege escalation, service installation).

suggestion.title: Incomplete Patch Vulnerability Gap Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556'—systems patched for the old CVE remain vulnerable to the new variant. Pipeline ignored this patch-escape risk despite it being the root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results to flag N-central instances where CVE-2026-18556 shows patched but CVE-2026-18577 shows vulnerable or unknown. Identify gap between patch dates; alert if older patch (CVE-2026-18556) was applied before new CVE (CVE-2026-18577) disclosure, indicating potential false-negative scan results from incomplete patches.

suggestion.title: N-central Session and Behavior Baseline Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass may not produce perfect impersonation; behavioral divergence from account baseline (login patterns, IP stability, access scope) indicates compromise post-auth-bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-account baselines for N-central sessions: typical source IP/CIDR, geographic origin, login hours, session duration, and systems accessed. Alert on deviations: concurrent sessions per account, mid-session IP changes, impossible-travel geographic jumps, or access to systems never touched by the account historically.
